title: engine.solvers.supervision
text:
engine.solvers.supervision
Responsible physical AI solvers: a detection gap in meters and joules, one assistant’s queue.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics/statistics.py and physics/serving.py; these models compose them for one stated machine and site, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




DetectionShortfallModel
A stop sized for the best-detected group, met by groups the detector sees less often.


SupervisorQueueModel
One remote assistant serving a fleet, as an M/M/1 queue.





engine.solvers.supervision.DetectionShortfallModel()
A stop sized for the best-detected group, met by groups the detector sees less often.
Each group needs N = ceil(ln p_miss / ln(1 - p_frame)) independent frame opportunities to bound the probability of missing every frame. A group needing Delta N more frames than the reference loses Delta d = v T_frame Delta N before braking begins. The reference stop sheds all of v^2 just as it reaches the person, so the late stop arrives with v_impact = sqrt(2 a Delta d) and E = m a Delta d, valid while Delta d stays below the braking travel v^2 / (2 a).





Name
Description




solve
Translate a detection-probability gap into braking distance and energy.





engine.solvers.supervision.DetectionShortfallModel.solve(
    speed,
    frame_period,
    deceleration,
    mass,
    all_miss_probability,
    reference,
    groups,
    delay=None,
)
Translate a detection-probability gap into braking distance and energy.











Name
Type
Description
Default




speed
Quantity
Positive initial approach speed, in meters per second.
required


frame_period
Quantity
Positive interval between detector frames, in seconds.
required


deceleration
Quantity
Positive constant braking-deceleration magnitude, in meters per second squared.
required


mass
Quantity
Positive moving mass, in kilograms.
required


all_miss_probability
float
Desired probability of missing every frame, between zero and one.
required


reference
float
Reference per-frame detection probability, between zero and one.
required


groups
sequence of float
Per-frame detection probabilities strictly between zero and one and no greater than reference. Higher-than-reference detection is outside the late-stop model.
required


delay
Quantity
Nonnegative extra reaction delay, in seconds. If omitted, reference brake-onset and absolute stopping distances are not calculated.
None














Name
Type
Description





DetectionShortfallResult
Per-group frame counts, extra time in ms, lost distance in meters, impact speed in m/s, and impact energy in joules. within_braking flags whether each delay distance is below the reference braking travel; impact estimates outside that regime must not be interpreted physically.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_consecutive_detection_frames : Independent miss-trial count.



Equation: N = ceil(log(all_miss_probability) / log(1 - p)); lost_distance = speed * frame_period * (N - N_reference). While lost_distance < speed**2 / (2 * deceleration), the residual impact speed is sqrt(2 * deceleration * lost_distance) and energy is mass * deceleration * lost_distance. Assumptions: independent equal-probability frame trials, a stop sized to reach the target at zero speed for the reference group, and constant deceleration after detection. Counts bound all misses, not consecutive successful detections. Excludes: correlated frames, obstacle motion, actuator saturation, collision mechanics, and validation of a detector’s group-specific probabilities.



Derivation: multiply independent miss probabilities to solve for frame count; delayed braking preserves kinetic energy m*a*lost_distance relative to the reference trajectory under constant deceleration.



A constructed group identical to the reference has no extra lost distance.
>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = DetectionShortfallModel().solve(
...     Q_(1, 'm/s'), Q_(0.01, 's'), Q_(1, 'm/s^2'), Q_(10, 'kg'),
...     0.01, 0.9, [0.9])
>>> result.rows[0].distance_lost == Q_(0, 'm')
True






engine.solvers.supervision.SupervisorQueueModel()
One remote assistant serving a fleet, as an M/M/1 queue.
Requests arrive at lambda = N r (N machines, r requests per machine-hour) and each holds the assistant for a mean s: utilization rho = lambda s, mean wait W_q = rho s / (1 - rho) (the M/G/1 wait ratio with exponential service), and the 99th-percentile wait from the Erlang C tail with one server.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate a remote assistant’s stationary request queue.





engine.solvers.supervision.SupervisorQueueModel.solve(
    request_rate,
    service_time,
    machines,
)
Estimate a remote assistant’s stationary request queue.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_rate
Quantity
Positive mean requests per machine per unit time, convertible to 1/hour.
required


service_time
Quantity
Positive mean time the assistant holds one request, in seconds.
required


machines
int
Positive number of independently requesting machines.
required














Name
Type
Description





SupervisorQueueResult
Fleet arrival rate in 1/hour, utilization as a fraction, mean and 99th-percentile queue waits in seconds, and busy minutes per hour.














Name
Type
Description





ValueError
If fleet utilization is not between zero and one.






mlsysim.physics.serving.calc_mg1_wait_ratio : Mean queue-wait ratio. mlsysim.physics.serving.calc_queue_latency_mmc : Erlang-C queue tail.



Equation: lambda = machines * request_rate; rho = lambda * service_time; mean_wait = rho * service_time / (1 - rho). The tail comes from the Erlang-C waiting-time distribution with one server. Assumptions: independent Poisson arrivals, exponentially distributed service, one always-available assistant, and stationary utilization below one. Excludes: shifts, priority queues, correlated incidents, abandonment, travel time, and any guarantee on an individual intervention deadline.



Derivation: superpose independent Poisson request streams, then apply the single-server M/M/1 specialization of the linked queueing functions.



A constructed low-load fleet yields positive finite waiting times.
>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = SupervisorQueueModel().solve(Q_(1, '1/hour'), Q_(1, 'minute'), 10)
>>> 0 < result.utilization < 1 and result.mean_wait > Q_(0, 's')
True

title: physics.retrieval
text:
physics.retrieval
Retrieval from long-term memory: the equations behind a read and its index.
Pure arithmetic (added 2026-10-20). A read stages whole serialized records inside a token allowance; a lexical index ranks candidates with BM25; an exact vector scan streams every eligible vector, so bandwidth sets its floor; a typed traversal grows with depth; and similarity between two texts counts shared words, which is all a similarity-first deduplicator sees. The solvers in engine/solvers/retrieval.py compose these.





Name
Description




calc_bandwidth_fit_through_origin
Fit bandwidth from paired scan bytes and elapsed times.


calc_bm25_idf
Calculate the nonnegative BM25 inverse document frequency variant.


calc_bm25_length_normalizer
Calculate the document-length term in the BM25 denominator.


calc_bm25_term_score
Calculate one query term’s BM25 contribution to a document score.


calc_full_tree_nodes
Count nodes in a full tree through a specified depth.


calc_interface_bandwidth
Calculate peak bandwidth from interface width and per-pin transfer rate.


calc_lsh_candidate_probability
Calculate the ideal MinHash banding candidate probability.


calc_lsh_threshold
Estimate the transition similarity of a MinHash banding curve.


calc_minhash_standard_error
Calculate standard error of an ideal MinHash similarity estimate.


calc_records_that_fit
Count whole serialized records within a token allowance.


calc_vectors_in_budget
Calculate the bandwidth-only vector count for an exact scan.


calc_word_overlap
Count distinct-word intersection and union after simple normalization.





physics.retrieval.calc_bandwidth_fit_through_origin(bytes_streamed, seconds)
Fit bandwidth from paired scan bytes and elapsed times.











Name
Type
Description
Default




bytes_streamed
sequence of float
Nonnegative bytes for each scan, with at least one positive value.
required


seconds
sequence of float
Corresponding positive elapsed seconds; must have the same length.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Fitted bandwidth in bytes per second, minimizing squared time residuals.






Equation: B = sum(x_i**2) / sum(x_i * t_i), from t_i = x_i / B. Assumptions: a zero-intercept latency model and paired sequences of equal length. The helper uses zip for cross-products and does not validate equal lengths; callers must ensure alignment. Inputs are supplied data, not measurements performed by this function. Excludes: startup intercept, uncertainty intervals, outlier removal, and weighting.



Derivation: minimize sum((t_i - a*x_i)**2) over a = 1/B. Setting its derivative to zero gives a = sum(x_i*t_i)/sum(x_i**2).



>>> calc_bandwidth_fit_through_origin([100, 200], [1, 2])
100.0




physics.retrieval.calc_bm25_idf(documents, matching_documents)
Calculate the nonnegative BM25 inverse document frequency variant.











Name
Type
Description
Default




documents
int
Positive corpus document count N.
required


matching_documents
int
Document count n containing the term, between zero and N inclusive.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless inverse document frequency, using the natural logarithm.






Equation: IDF = ln(1 + (N - n + 0.5) / (n + 0.5)). Assumptions: document-level occurrence counts and a fixed corpus. The outer addition of one is the nonnegative variant; it differs from a raw log-odds IDF. Excludes: term frequency, query weighting, corpus updates, and learned relevance.



Robertson and Zaragoza (2009), “The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond”, https://doi.org/10.1561/1500000019 (bibliography key: robertson2009bm25). The nonnegative transform is stated explicitly above rather than treated as the only BM25 IDF convention.



>>> round(calc_bm25_idf(100, 10), 6)
2.263745




physics.retrieval.calc_bm25_length_normalizer(length, average_length, k1, b)
Calculate the document-length term in the BM25 denominator.











Name
Type
Description
Default




length
float
Nonnegative document length, in tokens.
required


average_length
float
Positive corpus mean document length, in the same tokens.
required


k1
float
Positive dimensionless term-frequency saturation parameter.
required


b
float
Dimensionless length-normalization strength, normally in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless denominator offset before adding term frequency.






Equation: normalizer = k1 * (1 - b + b * length / average_length). Assumptions: document and mean lengths use the same tokenizer and units. At the average length the offset equals k1 regardless of b. Excludes: query-term frequency, IDF, field weighting, and learned length effects.



Robertson and Zaragoza (2009), “The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond”, https://doi.org/10.1561/1500000019 (bibliography key: robertson2009bm25).



>>> calc_bm25_length_normalizer(100, 100, 1.2, 0.75)
1.2




physics.retrieval.calc_bm25_term_score(
    idf,
    frequency,
    length,
    average_length,
    k1,
    b,
)
Calculate one query term’s BM25 contribution to a document score.











Name
Type
Description
Default




idf
float
Dimensionless inverse document frequency under the caller’s convention.
required


frequency
float
Nonnegative term occurrence count in this document.
required


length
float
Nonnegative document token count.
required


average_length
float
Positive corpus mean token count under the same tokenizer.
required


k1
float
Positive dimensionless term-frequency saturation parameter.
required


b
float
Dimensionless length-normalization strength, normally in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless term score; sum over terms outside this helper if desired.






Equation: score = IDF * f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * (1 - b + b * length / average_length)). Assumptions: a fixed corpus, a supplied IDF, and the denominator produced by calc_bm25_length_normalizer. A zero frequency contributes zero. Excludes: query-term repetition weights, field boosts, and ranking evaluation.



Robertson and Zaragoza (2009), “The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond”, https://doi.org/10.1561/1500000019 (bibliography key: robertson2009bm25).



>>> calc_bm25_term_score(1.0, 2, 100, 100, 1.2, 0.75)
1.375




physics.retrieval.calc_full_tree_nodes(children, depth)
Count nodes in a full tree through a specified depth.











Name
Type
Description
Default




children
int
Nonnegative branching factor c, identical at every non-leaf node.
required


depth
int
Nonnegative final depth d; the root has depth zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Number of nodes including the root and the final level.






Equation: nodes = sum(c**j for j in range(d + 1)); equivalently (c**(d + 1) - 1) / (c - 1) for c != 1, and d + 1 for c = 1. Assumptions: every branch expands fully through the same depth. Excludes: shared graph nodes, cycles, deduplication, pruning, and traversal cost.



Derivation: level j contains c**j nodes; sum the finite geometric series.



>>> calc_full_tree_nodes(2, 3)
15
>>> calc_full_tree_nodes(1, 3)
4




physics.retrieval.calc_interface_bandwidth(width, transfer_rate)
Calculate peak bandwidth from interface width and per-pin transfer rate.











Name
Type
Description
Default




width
Quantity
Positive interface width in bits, one bit per pin per transfer.
required


transfer_rate
Quantity
Positive per-pin bit rate, in bits per second.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Aggregate interface bandwidth in bytes per second.






Equation: bandwidth = width_in_bits * per_pin_bit_rate / 8 bits_per_byte. Assumptions: all data pins transfer simultaneously at the stated rate, which already includes any multiple transfers per clock cycle. Excludes: command/address pins, refresh, coding overhead, and utilization losses.



Derivation: each data pin contributes its bit rate; summing over the interface width gives aggregate bit rate, then unit conversion gives byte rate.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> calc_interface_bandwidth(Q_('64 bit'), Q_('1e9 bit/s')).m_as('GB/s')
8.0

Calculate the ideal MinHash banding candidate probability.











Name
Type
Description
Default




similarity
float
Jaccard similarity s, a dimensionless probability in [0, 1].
required


bands
int
Positive number b of bands in the signature.
required


rows
int
Positive independent hashes r per band.
required














Name
Type
Description

Fitted bandwidth in bytes per second, minimizing squared time residuals.






Equation: B = sum(x_i**2) / sum(x_i * t_i), from t_i = x_i / B. Assumptions: a zero-intercept latency model and paired sequences of equal length. The helper uses zip for cross-products and does not validate equal lengths; callers must ensure alignment. Inputs are supplied data, not measurements performed by this function. Robertson and Zaragoza (2009), “The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond”, https://doi.org/10.1561/1500000019 (bibliography key: robertson2009bm25). The nonnegative transform is stated explicitly above rather than treated as the only BM25 IDF convention.

Default

    frequency,
    length,
    average_length,
    k1,
    b,
)

title: physics.robotics.estimation
text:
physics.robotics.estimation
State estimation and belief expiry: scalar fusion, inertial coasting, and error-bound growth (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




calc_belief_error_bound
Propagate a scalar error allowance without new evidence.


calc_inertial_coast_errors
Estimate open-loop inertial error components over a duration.


calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon
Find when a growing error allowance reaches its limit.


calc_scalar_kalman_update
Compute scalar Kalman gain and posterior variance.





physics.robotics.estimation.calc_belief_error_bound(
    initial_error,
    growth_rate,
    elapsed,
    growth_acceleration=None,
)
Propagate a scalar error allowance without new evidence.











Name
Type
Description
Default




initial_error
Quantity
Initial nonnegative error allowance in length units.
required


growth_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative error-growth speed in length / time.
required


elapsed
Quantity
Nonnegative elapsed time since the last evidence update.
required


growth_acceleration
Quantity
Nonnegative error-growth acceleration in length / time**2; None omits the quadratic term.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Propagated error allowance in millimeters.






Equation: E(t) = initial_error + growth_rate*t + growth_acceleration*t**2/2.
Assumptions: Inputs bound additive scalar disturbances over the interval.
Excludes: Measurement updates, correlated error cancellation, and proof that supplied allowances are bounds.
Equation: E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2
v bounds the unobserved velocity and a the disturbance acceleration; a growth law bounded by a speed alone has a = 0.
Source: kinematics of a bounded disturbance (displacement under a velocity bound plus a constant-acceleration bound).



Derivation: Integrate a bounded velocity plus a constant acceleration allowance and add initial error.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_belief_error_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> bound = calc_belief_error_bound(1 * ureg.millimeter, 1 * ureg.millimeter / ureg.second, 2 * ureg.second)
>>> assert bound == 3 * ureg.millimeter




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_inertial_coast_errors(
    gyro_noise_density,
    gyro_bias,
    accel_noise_density,
    accel_bias,
    duration,
)
Estimate open-loop inertial error components over a duration.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gyro_noise_density
Quantity
Angular-rate white-noise density in angle / sqrt(time).
required


gyro_bias
Quantity
Constant signed gyroscope bias in angle / time.
required


accel_noise_density
Quantity
Acceleration white-noise density in length / time**1.5.
required


accel_bias
Quantity
Constant signed acceleration bias in length / time**2.
required


duration
Quantity
Positive integration duration in time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Heading_noise and heading_bias in degrees; position_noise and position_bias in millimeters.






Equation: heading_noise = N_g*sqrt(T); heading_bias = b_g*T; position_noise = N_a*sqrt(T**3/3); position_bias = b_a*T**2/2.
Assumptions: White independent rate/acceleration noise and constant biases over the interval.
Excludes: Gravity projection from attitude errors, bias drift, cross-axis coupling, and sensor fusion.
Equations: heading from white rate noise = N_g sqrt(T) heading from a constant offset = b_g T position from white accel noise = N_a sqrt(T^3 / 3) position from a constant offset = b_a T^2 / 2
Noise grows with the square root of time (a random walk, integrated once more for position); an offset grows with time, or its square for position, so offsets limit how long a robot can coast between fixes.
Source: Woodman, “An introduction to inertial navigation,” University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory Tech. Rep. UCAM-CL-TR-696 (2007), Secs. 4.2 and 4.3.



Derivation: Integrate constant biases and white-noise covariance over time; Woodman (2007), UCAM-CL-TR-696, Sections 4.2 and 4.3, supplies the existing inertial- navigation context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_inertial_coast_errors
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> errors = calc_inertial_coast_errors(0 * ureg.radian / ureg.second**0.5, 0 * ureg.radian / ureg.second, 0 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**1.5, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2, 2 * ureg.second)
>>> assert errors["position_bias"] == 2 * ureg.meter




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon(
    initial_error,
    growth_rate,
    growth_acceleration,
    error_limit,
)
Find when a growing error allowance reaches its limit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




initial_error
Quantity
Initial nonnegative error allowance in length units.
required


growth_rate
Quantity
Positive error-growth speed in length / time.
required


growth_acceleration
Quantity
Nonnegative error-growth acceleration in length / time**2.
required


error_limit
Quantity
Allowed error in length units; a spent allowance yields zero time.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
First-passage time in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: Solve a*t**2/2 + v*t + initial_error - error_limit = 0 for its nonnegative root.
Assumptions: Monotone scalar error growth; zero acceleration uses the linear horizon.
Excludes: Stochastic confidence interpretation and validation of the disturbance envelope.
Equation: a dt^2 / 2 + v dt + (E_0 - E_max) = 0 ; T_inv = the positive root
With a = 0 this is calc_linear_invalidation_horizon. A zero result means the initial error already spends the limit.
Source: first-passage time of the bound calc_belief_error_bound (definition of the invalidation horizon, T_inv = inf{dt >= 0 : E(dt) >= E_max}).



Derivation: Set calc_belief_error_bound equal to the limit and solve the resulting quadratic; the linear branch is its zero-acceleration limit.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> horizon = calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon(0 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second, 0 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2, 1 * ureg.meter)
>>> assert horizon == 1 * ureg.second




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_scalar_kalman_update(
    prior_variance,
    measurement_variance,
)
Compute scalar Kalman gain and posterior variance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




prior_variance
Quantity
Positive prior-error variance in squared state units.
required


measurement_variance
Quantity
Positive measurement-error variance with the same dimension as the prior.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Dimensionless float gain and posterior variance in the prior variance unit.






Equation: gain = P / (P + R); posterior = (1 - gain) * P.
Assumptions: A scalar direct observation with independent prior and measurement errors.
Excludes: State propagation, cross-covariance, bias, and covariance consistency checks.
Equation: g = P / (P + R) ; P+ = (1 - g) P
The gain is how far the estimate moves toward the reading, between 0 and 1; the posterior is tighter than either input. Both variances must share a unit.
Source: Kalman (1960), Trans. ASME J. Basic Eng. 82(1); Thrun, Burgard, and Fox, Probabilistic Robotics (2005), Table 3.1, in one dimension.



Derivation: Minimizing the variance of a weighted combination of independent scalar estimates yields gain P/(P+R); the existing Kalman/Thrun references give the estimator context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_scalar_kalman_update
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> gain, posterior = calc_scalar_kalman_update(1 * ureg.meter**2, 1 * ureg.meter**2)
>>> assert gain == 0.5
>>> assert posterior == 0.5 * ureg.meter**2

Nonnegative error-growth acceleration in length / time**2; None omits the quadratic term.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Propagated error allowance in millimeters.






Equation: E(t) = initial_error + growth_rate*t + growth_acceleration*t**2/2.
Assumptions: Inputs bound additive scalar disturbances over the interval.
Excludes: Measurement updates, correlated error cancellation, and proof that supplied allowances are bounds.
Equation: E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2
v bounds the unobserved velocity and a the disturbance acceleration; a growth law bounded by a speed alone has a = 0.
Source: kinematics of a bounded disturbance (displacement under a velocity bound plus a constant-acceleration bound).



Derivation: Integrate a bounded velocity plus a constant acceleration allowance and add initial error.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_belief_error_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> bound = calc_belief_error_bound(1 * ureg.millimeter, 1 * ureg.millimeter / ureg.second, 2 * ureg.second)
>>> assert bound == 3 * ureg.millimeter




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_inertial_coast_errors(
    gyro_noise_density,
    gyro_bias,
    accel_noise_density,
    accel_bias,
    duration,
)
Estimate open-loop inertial error components over a duration.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gyro_noise_density
Quantity
Angular-rate white-noise density in angle / sqrt(time).
required


gyro_bias
Quantity
Constant signed gyroscope bias in angle / time.
required


accel_noise_density
Quantity
Acceleration white-noise density in length / time**1.5.
required


accel_bias
Quantity
Constant signed acceleration bias in length / time**2.
required


duration
Quantity
Positive integration duration in time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Heading_noise and heading_bias in degrees; position_noise and position_bias in millimeters.






Equation: heading_noise = N_g*sqrt(T); heading_bias = b_g*T; position_noise = N_a*sqrt(T**3/3); position_bias = b_a*T**2/2.
Assumptions: White independent rate/acceleration noise and constant biases over the interval.
Excludes: Gravity projection from attitude errors, bias drift, cross-axis coupling, and sensor fusion.
Equations: heading from white rate noise = N_g sqrt(T) heading from a constant offset = b_g T position from white accel noise = N_a sqrt(T^3 / 3) position from a constant offset = b_a T^2 / 2
Noise grows with the square root of time (a random walk, integrated once more for position); an offset grows with time, or its square for position, so offsets limit how long a robot can coast between fixes.
Source: Woodman, “An introduction to inertial navigation,” University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory Tech. Rep. UCAM-CL-TR-696 (2007), Secs. 4.2 and 4.3.



Derivation: Integrate constant biases and white-noise covariance over time; Woodman (2007), UCAM-CL-TR-696, Sections 4.2 and 4.3, supplies the existing inertial- navigation context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_inertial_coast_errors
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> errors = calc_inertial_coast_errors(0 * ureg.radian / ureg.second**0.5, 0 * ureg.radian / ureg.second, 0 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**1.5, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2, 2 * ureg.second)
>>> assert errors["position_bias"] == 2 * ureg.meter




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon(
    initial_error,
    growth_rate,
    growth_acceleration,
    error_limit,
)
Find when a growing error allowance reaches its limit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




initial_error
Quantity
Initial nonnegative error allowance in length units.
required


growth_rate
Quantity
Positive error-growth speed in length / time.
required


growth_acceleration
Quantity
Nonnegative error-growth acceleration in length / time**2.
required


error_limit
Quantity
Allowed error in length units; a spent allowance yields zero time.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
First-passage time in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: Solve a*t**2/2 + v*t + initial_error - error_limit = 0 for its nonnegative root.
Assumptions: Monotone scalar error growth; zero acceleration uses the linear horizon.
Excludes: Stochastic confidence interpretation and validation of the disturbance envelope.
Equation: a dt^2 / 2 + v dt + (E_0 - E_max) = 0 ; T_inv = the positive root
With a = 0 this is calc_linear_invalidation_horizon. A zero result means the initial error already spends the limit.
Source: first-passage time of the bound calc_belief_error_bound (definition of the invalidation horizon, T_inv = inf{dt >= 0 : E(dt) >= E_max}).



Derivation: Set calc_belief_error_bound equal to the limit and solve the resulting quadratic; the linear branch is its zero-acceleration limit.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> horizon = calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon(0 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second, 0 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2, 1 * ureg.meter)
>>> assert horizon == 1 * ureg.second




physics.robotics.estimation.calc_scalar_kalman_update(
    prior_variance,
    measurement_variance,
)
Compute scalar Kalman gain and posterior variance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




prior_variance
Quantity
Positive prior-error variance in squared state units.
required


measurement_variance
Quantity
Positive measurement-error variance with the same dimension as the prior.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Dimensionless float gain and posterior variance in the prior variance unit.






Equation: gain = P / (P + R); posterior = (1 - gain) * P.
Assumptions: A scalar direct observation with independent prior and measurement errors.
Excludes: State propagation, cross-covariance, bias, and covariance consistency checks.
Equation: g = P / (P + R) ; P+ = (1 - g) P
The gain is how far the estimate moves toward the reading, between 0 and 1; the posterior is tighter than either input. Both variances must share a unit.
Source: Kalman (1960), Trans. ASME J. Basic Eng. 82(1); Thrun, Burgard, and Fox, Probabilistic Robotics (2005), Table 3.1, in one dimension.



Derivation: Minimizing the variance of a weighted combination of independent scalar estimates yields gain P/(P+R); the existing Kalman/Thrun references give the estimator context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.estimation import calc_scalar_kalman_update
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> gain, posterior = calc_scalar_kalman_update(1 * ureg.meter**2, 1 * ureg.meter**2)
>>> assert gain == 0.5
>>> assert posterior == 0.5 * ureg.meter**2

title: ReleaseFootprintScenario
text:
Reliability scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/reliability.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Resident copies of model that release controls hold on device.
A copy is the registry model_size, or the parameters at bytes_per_param when given; it spans accelerators_per_copy devices. A canary, shadow, A/B test, blue-green switch, and hot standby each hold one more copy whatever share of traffic they serve. Optional: the node’s node_accelerators, a retraining run of retrain_accelerators for retrain_time on the same node, the canary_share, and the staged exposure ramp (traffic shares, first stage the canary).


Equation: A copy occupies the selected model bytes; devices per copy are ceil(copy_bytes/device_capacity); copies reserve that count independently.
Assumptions: A model copy can be partitioned across the counted devices; optional retraining fields are supplied before using retraining properties.
Excludes: Communication, KV cache, allocator reserve, packing efficiencies, and proof that a distributed serving layout executes.



Derivation: A copy occupies the selected model bytes; devices per copy are ceil(copy_bytes/device_capacity); copies reserve that count independently. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One detection window every window, listening_per_day of each day, over horizon.
budget is the expected false alarms allowed per horizon. Each window with no keyword is a chance to fire, so a per-window rejection rate multiplies into a count; rejection_levels lists rates to compare against the budget.


Equation: expected alarms = listening windows * false-positive probability; allowable probability = budget / windows.
Assumptions: Listening windows tile the active listening duration. The calculation controls expected counts, not a probability of no alarms.
Excludes: Temporal dependence in alarm episodes, deduplication, and uncertainty in the supplied rejection rate.

title: ReferenceTrainingStepScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One optimizer step of a reference pretraining job, fixed once for every chapter that quotes it.
The layout is replica (tensor parallelism across one node, the shallowest pipeline that fits unsharded training state) repeated across fleet for data parallelism. One step is one optimizer update over the global batch, split into microbatches of sequences_per_microbatch sequences, so the data-parallel gradient reduction happens once per step. The global batch is the cited token batch divided by the context length, rounded down to a multiple of batch_divisor so every data-parallel degree used in the book divides it. Step time is modeled by DistributedModel, not measured.


Equation: global sequences = rounded token batch / context; data degree = fleet devices / replica devices; step time = DistributedModel.solve(…).
Assumptions: The declared replica layout and global batch admit whole microbatches. The local efficiency and communication-overlap choice are inputs.
Excludes: A measured step-time claim, convergence prediction, and incomplete replica or microbatch allocations.



Derivation: This configuration forwards its stored inputs to mlsysim.solvers.DistributedModel.solve. The solver contract records the equations and their provenance.

title: solvers.SensitivitySolver
text:
solvers.SensitivitySolver()
Identifies the binding constraint via numerical sensitivity analysis (Wall 21).
This solver computes numerical partial derivatives of performance with respect to hardware parameters to identify the ‘binding constraint.’
Literature Source: 1. Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline Model.” 2. Ofenbeck et al. (2014), “Applying the Roofline Model.”





Name
Description




solve
Solve for parameter sensitivities and identify the binding constraint.





solvers.SensitivitySolver.solve(
    model,
    hardware,
    precision='fp16',
    perturbation_pct=10.0,
    efficiency=0.5,
)
Solve for parameter sensitivities and identify the binding constraint.
Numerically perturbs each hardware parameter (peak FLOPS, memory bandwidth, memory capacity) by perturbation_pct and re-solves the single-node Roofline. Each sensitivity is the normalized latency response (T_perturbed - T_base) / T_base (dimensionless; negative means the upgrade helps). The binding constraint is the parameter with the largest absolute sensitivity — the resource whose improvement moves latency the most.











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
Workload
The workload to analyze.
required


hardware
HardwareNode
The baseline hardware configuration.
required


precision
str
Numerical precision used for both baseline and perturbed solves.
'fp16'


perturbation_pct
float
Perturbation size in percent (default 10.0, i.e. a 1.1x upgrade).
10.0


efficiency
float
Software efficiency factor in (0, 1].
0.5














Name
Type
Description





SensitivityResult
Per-parameter sensitivities, the binding constraint name, the baseline latency, and feasible. If the baseline does not fit in memory, feasible is False, binding_constraint is "memory_capacity", and constraint_trace carries the Memory Wall failure: the offload path pins latency, so the sensitivities (typically all zero) do not rank hardware levers.






mlsysim.engine.engine.Engine.solve : Baseline and perturbed evaluator.



Equation: response_j = (T(x_j*(1+p/100)) - T(x)) / T(x), where p is perturbation_pct. The reported response is a finite fractional change, not a derivative divided by the perturbation size.
Assumptions: each hardware field changes alone; all other inputs and the generic engine’s assumptions remain fixed. Use positive p for an upgrade experiment. Capacity-infeasible baselines are labeled separately. Excludes: coupled hardware costs, changes in kernel efficiency, and uncertainty intervals. Near a regime boundary the finite step matters.



Derivation: compute a finite difference in latency and normalize by the baseline; rank the absolute responses of compute, bandwidth, and capacity.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Models
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SensitivitySolver
>>> r = SensitivitySolver().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Hardware.Cloud.H100)
>>> sorted(r.sensitivities)
['memory_bandwidth', 'memory_capacity', 'peak_flops']

title: Communication Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

AllReduceScheduleScenario: One buffer reduced by ring, simple tree, and parameter server at each of group_sizes.
AllToAllDispatchScenario: One expert-parallel dispatch: total_tokens of hidden_dim values over n_devices holding n_experts.
AlphaBetaScenario: Named messages on named paths, each path an alpha startup and a beta bandwidth.
BandwidthDelayScenario: Data a link carries during delay: line rate times delay (for example, a Go-Back-N resend window).
ComponentExposureScenario: Independent components, each affected with probability (per day, or at one instant).
CompressionPaybackScenario: One synchronization compressed by compression_ratio at a codec cost of codec_time.
CompressionRunScenario: A run to a quality target with and without gradient compression on several networks.
DataParallelIntensityScenario: Communication intensity of one data-parallel worker of workload.
ErrorFeedbackScenario: A rounding compressor applied to a gradient sequence, with and without error feedback.
FatTreeScenario: A non-blocking fat-tree of radix-radix switches (Al-Fares et al. 2008).
GradientSyncScenario: A data-parallel step of workload: compute, then a ring AllReduce over each link.
HierarchicalAllReduceScenario: A buffer AllReduced over n_nodes nodes of gpus_per_node GPUs, in three phases or one flat ring.
HopPathScenario: Named paths through hops identical switch traversals of hop_latency each.
IncastScenario: n_senders at sender_bandwidth into one egress port with a buffer.
LinkBuildoutScenario: links_per_device links per accelerator of fleet, each with a price and a module power.
MessageFusionScenario: count small messages sent one by one against one fused message on the same path.
NicSharingScenario: One NIC split into n_virtual_functions rate-capped slices, and a burst at full line rate.
OverlapBudgetScenario: Layer-by-layer gradient AllReduce of workload: sequential against overlapped with backward.
OversubscriptionScenario: A ring AllReduce whose edges all cross the bisection of fleet, at 1:1 and at oversubscription_ratio.
PropagationScenario: A request sent distance over fiber and answered; optionally a budget and a measured round trip.
ResidualShareScenario: A residual equal to residual of the one-device step, on devices devices.
RingAttentionScenario: Ring attention on accelerator: the smallest chunk that hides each K/V tile, per link.
RingTraceScenario: A ring AllReduce traced step by step on one short integer vector per GPU.
SensorUplinkScenario: streams raw video streams against a shared link, and the event records that replace them.
SilentSlowdownScenario: A run on fleet slowed a few percent by a degraded link, with no alarm.
SlowdownDiagnosisScenario: A training step that slowed, and a pairwise link test that finds one link at a fraction of its rate.
SyncStrategyScenario: Data-parallel training to a fixed target under one synchronization strategy.
TensorParallelScenario: The activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel step of workload.
TorusScenario: n_endpoints as a cubic torus against a non-blocking fat-tree, at equal per-link bandwidth.
TransferScenario: copies of one payload moved at once over each named link tier.

title: CanaryScheduleScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A staged rollout that needs samples_per_variant guardrail samples per stage at request_rate; stages is the configured ladder of (traffic share, duration).
Optional (added 2026-10-20): label_delay is the time from admission to a verdict, so labeled_by_completion counts the candidate tasks whose labels exist when the ladder ends (admitted at least that long before the end).


Equation: Admission counts integrate share*rate over stages; labeled counts truncate admissions at total_time-label_delay.

Excludes: Label failures, stochastic traffic, and power calculations beyond the supplied sample target.



Derivation: Each stage contributes traffic_share*request_rate*duration admissions. Only admissions before completion-label_delay have available labels at completion, so the labeled count integrates each stage only up to that cutoff. >>> s = s.variant(label_delay=s.total / 2)
>>> s.labeled_by_completion <= s.admitted_by_completion
True

title: Serving Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

BatchCapChoiceScenario: Two batch caps at one arrival rate, batches waiting until full: throughput against formation wait.
BatchDispatchScenario: A dual-trigger batch: it may leave at timeout after its oldest arrival, then waits for a worker.
BatchEnergyPerImageScenario: Bytes, arithmetic intensity, and energy per image when a batch shares one weight read.
BatchWindowScenario: Requests arriving as a Poisson stream into a batching window of length window.
BatchingKneeScenario: Batch service time S(B) = t_0 + B t_req: where throughput turns over.
ChunkedPrefillScenario: A long prompt advanced chunk_tokens per iteration beside decode.
ColdStartScenario: A new replica: provision, fetch the weight artifact, load and warm up.
CompilationPaybackScenario: A compiled decode step and the executions that repay its build.
ContextGrowthScenario: A context window grown from base_tokens to tokens: a kept cache grows with the ratio, attention’s score work and stored scores with its square.
ContextMemoryCrossingScenario: Three memories of workload as context grows on hardware: fixed weights, a KV cache linear in tokens, and one layer’s stored scores (all heads) quadratic in tokens.
DecodeBudgetScenario: A constructed decode-step budget, cut interval by interval, against a TPOT target.
DecodeScenario: One decode step of workload on hardware (weight-streaming bound).
EmbeddingGatherScenario: One recommender request on hardware: one row of width values per categorical feature of dataset is gathered, then the rows and the bottom MLP’s output interact by pairwise dot products.
EmbeddingTableScenario: tables embedding tables of rows rows, each width values wide, against hardware.
FixedBatchScheduleScenario: Requests in one batch of fixed membership, one token per iteration.
FleetMfuScenario: Program goodput (MFU) of a training step on one node and on a fleet of fleet_devices.
GoodputScenario: ML productivity goodput of a job on a pool: scheduling, runtime, and program goodput.
KvAdmissionScenario: A replica’s KV budget against one context length (KvAdmissionModel).
KvAttentionDesignScenario: Bytes per token across registry models, with one MHA, one GQA, and one MLA reference.
KvBlockSharingScenario: Requests with an output allowance in whole blocks, with and without a shared prefix, as a turn rate.
KvDecodeBatchScenario: Batched decode on one accelerator when every sequence also reads its own KV cache.
KvFootprintScenario: workload’s KV cache for tokens kept tokens; with hardware and kv_share, how many such requests the cache’s share of the labeled device memory holds. kv_width_factor scales the key-value width (one half: half the key-value heads).
KvForkCopyScenario: Candidates forked from one prefix, each copying the prefix’s KV state without block sharing.
KvResidencyArchetypeScenario: One agent workload’s sharing gain, residency tax, and reload against recompute.
LittlesLawScenario: Requests in flight at arrival_rate, and replicas sized from a batch service time.
MM1CapacityPlanScenario: Accelerators for peak_rate when each is an M/M/1 server whose tail must meet tail_budget.
MM1ServiceSpeedupScenario: The same traffic on an M/M/1 server before and after its service time falls.
MaterializedScoresScenario: Attention scores stored in full: seq_len^2 per head, heads per layer, layers layers.
NoisyNeighborScenario: Tenants sharing a KV pool and a replica, one of them bursting, with and without quotas.
PackedQkvProjectionScenario: tokens rows through workload’s packed query-key-value projection, one d x 3d matrix.
PagedAllocationScenario: Requests under a length cap in pool’s KV pool: full-cap reservation against paged blocks.
PausedKvStateScenario: A request paused on a tool: keep, move over the host links, or drop and recompute its KV state.
PrecisionDividendScenario: Maximum batch before and after lower-precision weights and KV (PrecisionDividendModel).
PrecomputeVersusOnDemandScenario: items inputs answered one at a time on demand, or precomputed at a large-batch offline_rate.
PrefixRebuildScenario: A cached prefix on node: the prefill a miss rebuilds against one short suffix pass on a hit.
PrefixSharingScenario: KV cache for users who share one prompt prefix, stored per user or once.
QueueWaitScenario: A fleet modeled as one M/G/1 server at offered load utilization.
ReasoningLatencyScenario: Serial reasoning tokens before the answer, at a fixed time per token.
ReplicaStartupScenario: A serving replica’s startup phases; warm_path and cold_path name the phases each start pays.
RequestZonesScenario: One serialized request laid out in zones, the leading ones an invariant shared prefix.
RuntimeGoodputScenario: Runtime goodput of a job on failures.n_devices devices over a held window.
SchedulingSnapshotScenario: One snapshot of a shared pool’s in-service capacity, read at the scheduling boundary.
ServingScenario: Serving workload on hardware at a stated context and batch (ServingModel).
ServingTaxScenario: A request’s latency target split between model execution and everything outside it.
SingleAcceleratorLlmServiceScenario: An LLM chat service on one accelerator: latency, KV residency, request rate, and token cost.
SpeculativeRoundScenario: A draft proposes draft_length tokens; the target verifies them in one step.
TailEventRateScenario: How often an event of probability event_probability per request occurs at request_rate.
TensorParallelSpeedupScenario: Stated per-layer compute split tp_size ways, plus the AllReduces each layer adds.
TraceVolumeScenario: A profiler trace of window on every one of devices devices.
TrafficSurgeScenario: A service sized for normal_rate that receives surge_rate; latency in each regime.
TransformerBlockScenario: workload’s decoder blocks at a context of context_tokens: the classic block’s weights (4 d^2 attention projections, 2 x ffn_multiple d^2 MLP), its dense and attention multiply-adds, and, with hardware, the attention arithmetic of one prompt at peak.
WeightedRoutingScenario: Traffic split over server pools in proportion to each pool’s per-server capacity.

text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Eager against compiled execution: the work that repays compile_time.
Compiling pays when the time saved per item, summed over items, exceeds the compile time. An experiment of experiment_items items that changes the code recompiles times pays a compile for every change.


Equation: Compile cost divided by per-item time savings gives the breakeven item count.
Assumptions: Steady item rates and a positive compiled speed advantage; recompilation is charged once per declared code change.
Excludes: Warmup, cache effects, and rate changes during the experiment.



Derivation: Compile cost divided by per-item time savings gives the breakeven item count. Individual property contracts identify the exact accounting expression or reusable calculation. Registry entries supply the scenario inputs; this class does not turn them into measured outcomes.

title: solvers.SingleNodeModel
text:
solvers.SingleNodeModel()
Resolves single-node hardware Roofline bounds and feasibility.
This model handles the ‘Iron Law’ of machine learning systems, calculating whether a model fits in memory and predicting its throughput based on arithmetic intensity.
Literature Source: Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Floating-Point Programs and Multicore Architectures.”





Name
Description




solve
Calculate the Roofline performance profile for a single hardware node.

    model,
    hardware,
    batch_size=1,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
    raise_errors=False,
    **kwargs,
)
Calculate the Roofline performance profile for a single hardware node.
Thin wrapper that delegates to Engine.solve (the core Roofline implementation in engine/engine.py), exposing it through the resolver interface so it can participate in pipelines.

mlsysim.engine.engine.Engine.solve : Generic node calculation.



Equation: T = max(F / (eta * peak), traffic / bandwidth) + overhead. This wrapper delegates the workload lowering, memory accounting, and constraint traces to Engine.solve.
Assumptions: the generic engine’s activation-traffic convention and one forward step unless additional engine options select training. Efficiency scales compute capacity, not peak memory bandwidth. Excludes: explicit KV-aware serving and distributed collectives.



Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). Activation traffic and runtime taxes are separate modeling conventions.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Models
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SingleNodeModel
>>> r = SingleNodeModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Hardware.Cloud.H100)
>>> bool(r.feasible and r.latency.m_as("ms") > 0)
True

physics.serving.calc_batch_formation_wait(batch_size, arrival_rate)
Calculate mean delay while a fixed-size batch fills.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_size
int
Positive batch count B; no timeout or partial-batch release.
required


arrival_rate
Quantity or float
Positive stationary arrival rate lambda; output has reciprocal-rate units.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or float
Mean formation delay, excluding execution and downstream queueing.






Equation: Wform = (B-1)/(2 lambda).
Assumptions: Average interarrival gap is 1/lambda and each request position within a batch is equally represented.
Excludes: Arrival bursts correlated with batch position, timeouts, priorities, and execution delay.



Derivation: batch positions wait for B-1, B-2, …, 0 subsequent arrivals; averaging those counts and multiplying by the mean gap gives the formula.



>>> calc_batch_formation_wait(1, 2 / ureg.second) == 0 * ureg.second
True




physics.serving.calc_batch_knee(fixed_time, per_request_time)
Calculate where variable batch work equals fixed work.











Name
Type
Description
Default




fixed_time
Quantity
Nonnegative fixed duration per batch.
required


per_request_time
Quantity
Positive incremental duration per request; compatible time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Continuous batch-size knee; an integer scheduler may need rounding.






Equation: Bknee = t0/treq; throughput B/(t0+B treq) is half its asymptotic ceiling at this point.
Assumptions: Batch service duration is affine in batch size with fixed coefficients.
Excludes: Queueing, capacity limits, nonlinear kernels, and discrete batch-size rounding.



Derivation: equate the fixed term t0 and variable term B treq in the affine batch-service model and solve for B.



>>> calc_batch_knee(4 * ureg.ms, 2 * ureg.ms) == 2
True




physics.serving.calc_batch_throughput_share(
    batch_size,
    fixed_time,
    per_request_time,
)
Calculate batch throughput as a fraction of its affine-model ceiling.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_size
int or float
Nonnegative request count B, with a positive total service duration.
required


fixed_time
Quantity
Nonnegative fixed per-batch duration t0.
required


per_request_time
Quantity
Positive incremental duration treq per request.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless share of the ceiling throughput 1/treq.






Equation: share = B treq / (t0 + B treq).
Assumptions: The same affine service model holds across batch sizes.
Excludes: Queue formation, memory-capacity limits, and changes in per-request execution efficiency.



Derivation: divide B/(t0+B treq) by its large-batch limit 1/treq.



>>> calc_batch_throughput_share(2, 4 * ureg.ms, 2 * ureg.ms) == 0.5
True




physics.serving.calc_exponential_quantile_factor(quantile)
Calculate an exponential quantile relative to its mean.





Name
Type
Description
Default




quantile
float
Cumulative probability q in [0, 1).
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless quantile-to-mean ratio.






Equation: kq = -log(1-q).
Assumptions: An exponential distribution with positive finite mean.
Excludes: Other service-time distributions and mixtures with a point mass at zero.



Derivation: invert F(t)=1-exp(-t/mean) at F(t)=q, then divide by mean.



>>> calc_exponential_quantile_factor(0) == 0
True
>>> calc_exponential_quantile_factor(0.99) > calc_exponential_quantile_factor(0.5)
True




physics.serving.calc_kingman_wait_ratio(utilization, arrival_scv, service_scv)
Approximate mean G/G/1 wait relative to mean service time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




utilization
float
Busy fraction rho in [0, 1).
required


arrival_scv
float
Nonnegative squared coefficient of variation of interarrival gaps.
required


service_scv
float
Nonnegative squared coefficient of variation of service durations.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless approximate mean-wait to mean-service ratio.






Equation: Wq/E[S] approximately ((Ca**2 + Cs**2)/2) rho/(1-rho).
Assumptions: A single first-come server with independent renewal arrivals and service durations; the approximation is motivated by heavy traffic.
Excludes: Tail percentiles, correlated service/arrivals, finite buffers, and multiple-server routing.



Kingman (1961), The Single Server Queue in Heavy Traffic. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305004100036094 (bibliography key: kingman1961single).



>>> calc_kingman_wait_ratio(0.5, 1, 1) == calc_mg1_wait_ratio(0.5, 1)
True




physics.serving.calc_littles_law_occupancy(arrival_rate, time_in_system)
Calculate mean occupancy from arrival rate and residence time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrival_rate
Quantity or float
Nonnegative average arrivals per unit time; use units reciprocal to time_in_system.
required


time_in_system
Quantity or float
Nonnegative mean total residence duration, including waiting and service.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or float
Mean resident request count; units follow the product of the inputs.






Equation: L = lambda W.
Assumptions: A stable system and consistently defined boundaries for arrivals, occupancy, and residence.
Excludes: Tail occupancy, burst reserves, and admission guarantees.



Little (1961), A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = lambda W. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.9.3.383 (bibliography key: little1961).



>>> calc_littles_law_occupancy(2 / ureg.second, 3 * ureg.second).dimensionless
True




physics.serving.calc_littles_law_rate(occupied_slots, residence_time)
Calculate average turnover rate from occupied slots and residence time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




occupied_slots
Quantity or float
Nonnegative mean count L of occupied slots.
required


residence_time
Quantity or float
Positive mean duration W for which each turn holds a slot.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or float
Average turnover rate L/W, reciprocal to the residence-time unit.






Equation: lambda = L/W.
Assumptions: Stable operation and a common definition of a turn across slot and duration measurements.
Excludes: Peak throughput, tail delays, and idle capacity not represented by occupied_slots.



Little (1961), A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = lambda W. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.9.3.383 (bibliography key: little1961).



>>> calc_littles_law_rate(6, 3 * ureg.second) == 2 / ureg.second
True




physics.serving.calc_mg1_wait_ratio(utilization, service_cv)
Calculate mean M/G/1 queue wait relative to mean service time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




utilization
float
Nonnegative busy fraction rho; values at or above one return infinity.
required


service_cv
float
Nonnegative dimensionless coefficient of variation of service duration.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Mean waiting time divided by mean service time; dimensionless.






Equation: Wq/E[S] = rho (1 + Cs**2) / [2 (1-rho)].
Assumptions: Poisson arrivals, one first-come server, independent service times with finite second moment.
Excludes: Tail percentiles, correlated service, finite queue capacity, and multiple servers.



Harchol-Balter (2013), Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems: Queueing Theory in Action. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~harchol/PerformanceModeling/book.html (bibliography key: harchol-balter2013).



>>> calc_mg1_wait_ratio(0.5, 1) == 1
True
>>> calc_mg1_wait_ratio(0.5, 0) < calc_mg1_wait_ratio(0.5, 1)
True




physics.serving.calc_mm1_max_utilization(service_time, tail_budget, tail_factor)
Calculate the utilization ceiling implied by an M/M/1 tail budget.











Name
Type
Description
Default




service_time
Quantity
Positive mean service duration S.
required


tail_budget
Quantity
Positive allowed tail duration T, in compatible units.
required


tail_factor
float
Positive tail-to-mean multiplier k, normally from the exponential quantile.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Unclamped dimensionless ceiling; a negative result means even idle service misses the budget.






Equation: rho_max = 1 - k S/T.
Assumptions: M/M/1 response time is exponential, and the tail factor matches the chosen quantile.
Excludes: Admission enforcement, finite buffers, or nonexponential latency tails.



Derivation: rearrange k S/(1-rho) <= T for rho. The underlying M/M/1 mean is documented in calc_mm1_time_in_system.



>>> calc_mm1_max_utilization(2 * ureg.ms, 2 * ureg.ms, 1) == 0
True




physics.serving.calc_mm1_time_in_system(service_time, utilization)
Calculate mean M/M/1 residence time including service.











Name
Type
Description
Default




service_time
Quantity or float
Positive mean service duration S; output preserves its unit.
required


utilization
float
Dimensionless busy fraction rho in [0, 1).
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or float
Mean total residence time, in the service-time unit.






Equation: W = S/(1-rho).
Assumptions: One first-come server, Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, and steady state.
Excludes: Finite buffer loss, nonexponential service, and tail percentiles.



Harchol-Balter (2013), Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems: Queueing Theory in Action. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~harchol/PerformanceModeling/book.html (bibliography key: harchol-balter2013).



>>> calc_mm1_time_in_system(2 * ureg.ms, 0) == 2 * ureg.ms
True




physics.serving.calc_padding_waste_fraction(lengths)
Calculate idle slot share when a batch waits for its longest member.











Name
Type
Description
Default




lengths
iterable of float
Nonempty sequence of nonnegative work lengths in common units, with a positive maximum.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless fraction of reserved slot-time unused.






Equation: waste = 1 - sum(L)/(n max(L)).
Assumptions: Each member reserves one slot until the longest member finishes, and length is proportional to slot occupancy.
Excludes: Continuous replacement, variable work per token, and non-slot resource bottlenecks.



Derivation: useful slot-time is sum(L), while fixed-membership reservation consumes n max(L). Divide the unused difference by the reservation.



>>> calc_padding_waste_fraction([2, 2]) == 0
True
>>> calc_padding_waste_fraction([1, 2]) > 0
True




physics.serving.calc_queue_latency_mmc(
    arrival_rate_hz,
    service_rate_hz,
    num_servers,
)
Calculate M/M/c utilization and queue-wait percentiles.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrival_rate_hz
Quantity or float
Nonnegative request arrival rate lambda; bare numbers mean Hz.
required


service_rate_hz
Quantity or float
Positive completion rate mu per replica; bare numbers mean Hz.
required


num_servers
int
Replica count c; implementation truncates to an integer and clamps to at least one.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Dimensionless utilization, median queue wait, and p99 queue wait; waits are second quantities.






Equation: rho = lambda/(c mu); P(W > t) = ErlangC(c, rho) exp[-c mu (1-rho)t]. The returned waits invert this tail at tail probabilities 0.5 and 0.01.
Assumptions: Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, identical replicas, and a shared first-come queue. Stable operation requires lambda < c mu.
Excludes: Service duration in the returned waits, batching, admission limits, heterogeneous replicas, and burst correlations.
The Erlang C sum is evaluated in the log domain to limit overflow. Numerical breakdown falls back to rho as a proxy waiting probability, which is an approximation. At saturation or zero service rate the function returns utilization one and infinite waits; these are not finite latency estimates.



Harchol-Balter (2013), Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems: Queueing Theory in Action. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~harchol/PerformanceModeling/book.html (bibliography key: harchol-balter2013).



>>> rho, median, tail = calc_queue_latency_mmc(1, 2, 1)
>>> rho == 0.5 and median.magnitude == 0 and tail.magnitude > 0
True




physics.serving.calc_residency_factor(generation_time, wait_time)
Calculate how retaining state during a wait expands residence time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




generation_time
Quantity
Positive active generation duration.
required


wait_time
Quantity
Nonnegative additional duration for which state retains its slot.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless residence multiplier; fixed-slot turnover is divided by this factor.






Equation: factor = (Tgen + Twait)/Tgen.
Assumptions: Generation and waiting are sequential, and both reserve the same slot.
Excludes: Releasing state during waits, overlapping work, and different memory sizes across phases.



Derivation: compare total reserved duration Tgen+Twait with generation-only duration Tgen; Little’s law converts this to the inverse turnover ratio.



>>> calc_residency_factor(2 * ureg.second, 0 * ureg.second) == 1
True




physics.serving.calc_speculative_expected_tokens(acceptance, draft_length)
Calculate expected emitted tokens per speculative round.











Name
Type
Description
Default




acceptance
float
Independent per-token acceptance probability alpha in [0, 1); the alpha=1 limit is not accepted by this implementation.
required


draft_length
int
Nonnegative number K of draft proposals; caller must supply an integer count.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Expected total emitted tokens, including the target bonus or correction token.






Equation: E[tokens] = sum(alpha**i, i=0..K) = (1-alpha**(K+1))/(1-alpha).
Assumptions: Identical independent acceptance probabilities; verification stops at the first rejected draft, and the target supplies one additional token.
Excludes: Context-dependent acceptance, verification compute, draft cost, and output quality.



Leviathan, Kalman, and Matias (2023), Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/leviathan23a.html (bibliography key: leviathan2023fast).



>>> calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0, 4) == 1
True
>>> calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0.5, 4) > calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0.5, 2)
True




physics.serving.calc_speculative_round_speedup(
    accepted_per_round,
    draft_length,
    draft_cost_ratio,
)
Calculate a speculative-round decode speedup under fixed step costs.











Name
Type
Description
Default




accepted_per_round
float
Nonnegative mean number m of accepted draft tokens, excluding the target token.
required


draft_length
int
Nonnegative number gamma of draft steps per round.
required


draft_cost_ratio
float
Nonnegative draft-step duration divided by one target-step duration.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless time-per-token speedup against serial target-only decoding.






Equation: speedup = (m+1)/(gamma r + 1).
Assumptions: Draft steps execute serially and one target verification costs one target step regardless of gamma; one target token is always emitted.
Excludes: Verification compute growth, KV-cache memory, communication, and changing context or acceptance.



Leviathan, Kalman, and Matias (2023), Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/leviathan23a.html (bibliography key: leviathan2023fast).



>>> calc_speculative_round_speedup(0, 0, 0) == 1
True
>>> calc_speculative_round_speedup(1, 4, 1) < 1
True

Assumptions: One first-come server, Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, and steady state.
Excludes: Finite buffer loss, nonexponential service, and tail percentiles.



Harchol-Balter (2013), Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems: Queueing Theory in Action. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~harchol/PerformanceModeling/book.html (bibliography key: harchol-balter2013).



>>> calc_mm1_time_in_system(2 * ureg.ms, 0) == 2 * ureg.ms
True




physics.serving.calc_padding_waste_fraction(lengths)
Calculate idle slot share when a batch waits for its longest member.











Name
Type
Description
Default




lengths
iterable of float
Nonempty sequence of nonnegative work lengths in common units, with a positive maximum.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless fraction of reserved slot-time unused.






Equation: waste = 1 - sum(L)/(n max(L)).
Assumptions: Each member reserves one slot until the longest member finishes, and length is proportional to slot occupancy.
Excludes: Continuous replacement, variable work per token, and non-slot resource bottlenecks.



Derivation: useful slot-time is sum(L), while fixed-membership reservation consumes n max(L). Divide the unused difference by the reservation.



>>> calc_padding_waste_fraction([2, 2]) == 0
True
>>> calc_padding_waste_fraction([1, 2]) > 0
True




physics.serving.calc_queue_latency_mmc(
    arrival_rate_hz,
    service_rate_hz,
    num_servers,
)
Calculate M/M/c utilization and queue-wait percentiles.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrival_rate_hz
Quantity or float
Nonnegative request arrival rate lambda; bare numbers mean Hz.
required


service_rate_hz
Quantity or float
Positive completion rate mu per replica; bare numbers mean Hz.
required


num_servers
int
Replica count c; implementation truncates to an integer and clamps to at least one.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Dimensionless utilization, median queue wait, and p99 queue wait; waits are second quantities.






Equation: rho = lambda/(c mu); P(W > t) = ErlangC(c, rho) exp[-c mu (1-rho)t]. The returned waits invert this tail at tail probabilities 0.5 and 0.01.
Assumptions: Poisson arrivals, independent exponential service, identical replicas, and a shared first-come queue. Stable operation requires lambda < c mu.
Excludes: Service duration in the returned waits, batching, admission limits, heterogeneous replicas, and burst correlations.
The Erlang C sum is evaluated in the log domain to limit overflow. Numerical breakdown falls back to rho as a proxy waiting probability, which is an approximation. At saturation or zero service rate the function returns utilization one and infinite waits; these are not finite latency estimates.



Harchol-Balter (2013), Performance Modeling and Design of Computer Systems: Queueing Theory in Action. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~harchol/PerformanceModeling/book.html (bibliography key: harchol-balter2013).



>>> rho, median, tail = calc_queue_latency_mmc(1, 2, 1)
>>> rho == 0.5 and median.magnitude == 0 and tail.magnitude > 0
True




physics.serving.calc_residency_factor(generation_time, wait_time)
Calculate how retaining state during a wait expands residence time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




generation_time
Quantity
Positive active generation duration.
required


wait_time
Quantity
Nonnegative additional duration for which state retains its slot.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless residence multiplier; fixed-slot turnover is divided by this factor.






Equation: factor = (Tgen + Twait)/Tgen.
Assumptions: Generation and waiting are sequential, and both reserve the same slot.
Excludes: Releasing state during waits, overlapping work, and different memory sizes across phases.



Derivation: compare total reserved duration Tgen+Twait with generation-only duration Tgen; Little’s law converts this to the inverse turnover ratio.



>>> calc_residency_factor(2 * ureg.second, 0 * ureg.second) == 1
True




physics.serving.calc_speculative_expected_tokens(acceptance, draft_length)
Calculate expected emitted tokens per speculative round.











Name
Type
Description
Default




acceptance
float
Independent per-token acceptance probability alpha in [0, 1); the alpha=1 limit is not accepted by this implementation.
required


draft_length
int
Nonnegative number K of draft proposals; caller must supply an integer count.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Expected total emitted tokens, including the target bonus or correction token.






Equation: E[tokens] = sum(alpha**i, i=0..K) = (1-alpha**(K+1))/(1-alpha).
Assumptions: Identical independent acceptance probabilities; verification stops at the first rejected draft, and the target supplies one additional token.
Excludes: Context-dependent acceptance, verification compute, draft cost, and output quality.



Leviathan, Kalman, and Matias (2023), Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/leviathan23a.html (bibliography key: leviathan2023fast).



>>> calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0, 4) == 1
True
>>> calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0.5, 4) > calc_speculative_expected_tokens(0.5, 2)
True




physics.serving.calc_speculative_round_speedup(
    accepted_per_round,
    draft_length,
    draft_cost_ratio,
)
Calculate a speculative-round decode speedup under fixed step costs.











Name
Type
Description
Default

float
Nonnegative mean number m of accepted draft tokens, excluding the target token.
required


draft_length
int
Nonnegative number gamma of draft steps per round.
required


draft_cost_ratio
float
Nonnegative draft-step duration divided by one target-step duration.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless time-per-token speedup against serial target-only decoding.






Equation: speedup = (m+1)/(gamma r + 1).
Assumptions: Draft steps execute serially and one target verification costs one target step regardless of gamma; one target token is always emitted.
Excludes: Verification compute growth, KV-cache memory, communication, and changing context or acceptance.



Leviathan, Kalman, and Matias (2023), Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/leviathan23a.html (bibliography key: leviathan2023fast).

True

title: physics.scaling
text:
physics.scaling
Scaling-law arithmetic: power-law price lists and compute-optimal allocation.





Name
Description




calc_allocation_growth
Calculate fractional allocation growth under a compute power law.


calc_compute_optimal_allocation
Allocate a compute budget at a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio.


calc_halving_multiple
Find the resource multiple that halves a power-law loss term.


calc_loss_reduction_compute_multiple
Find the compute multiple for a fractional power-law loss reduction.


calc_power_law_factor
Calculate the remaining fraction of a resource-dependent power-law term.





physics.scaling.calc_allocation_growth(compute_multiple, exponent)
Calculate fractional allocation growth under a compute power law.











Name
Type
Description
Default




compute_multiple
float
Positive dimensionless ratio of new to old compute budget.
required


exponent
float
Dimensionless exponent relating the allocation to compute.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Fractional change in allocation; multiply by 100 only when presenting a percentage.






Equation: growth = compute_multiple**exponent - 1.
Assumptions: Allocation follows X_opt = A*C**exponent with fixed A.
Excludes: Fitting the exponent, integer rounding, and changes in optimal regime.



Derivation: divide X_new=A*C_new**exponent by X_old=A*C_old**exponent and subtract one.



>>> calc_allocation_growth(4, 0.5)
1.0




physics.scaling.calc_compute_optimal_allocation(
    budget_flops,
    tokens_per_param,
    flops_per_param_token,
)
Allocate a compute budget at a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio.











Name
Type
Description
Default




budget_flops
float
Positive training-work budget C, in FLOPs as a plain number.
required


tokens_per_param
float
Positive ratio r of training tokens to model parameters.
required


flops_per_param_token
float
Positive accounting coefficient k, FLOPs per parameter per token.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple of float
Parameter count N and training-token count D as continuous plain numbers; neither value is rounded to an implementable model shape.






Equation: N = sqrt(C/(k*r)); D = r*N, from C=k*N*D.
Assumptions: The supplied ratio is the chosen allocation rule and work is parameter dominated. The function does not estimate the optimal ratio.
Excludes: Attention work, communication, architecture constraints, and fitting a loss model to determine r.



Hoffmann et al. (2022), “Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556 (bibliography key: hoffmann2022chinchilla). Derivation: substitute the assumed D=r*N into the work budget C=k*N*D.



>>> calc_compute_optimal_allocation(600, 1, 6)
(10.0, 10.0)




physics.scaling.calc_halving_multiple(exponent)
Find the resource multiple that halves a power-law loss term.











Name
Type
Description
Default




exponent
float
Positive dimensionless power-law exponent alpha.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless resource multiplier required to halve the modeled term.






Equation: multiple = 2**(1/exponent).
Assumptions: The reducible term follows A*R**(-alpha) with fixed A and alpha.
Excludes: Irreducible loss, regime changes, and estimation of the exponent.



Derivation: solve (R_new/R_old)**(-alpha) = 1/2 for the resource ratio.



>>> calc_halving_multiple(0.5)
4.0




physics.scaling.calc_loss_reduction_compute_multiple(exponent, loss_reduction)
Find the compute multiple for a fractional power-law loss reduction.











Name
Type
Description
Default




exponent
float
Positive dimensionless alpha in L=A*C**(-alpha).
required


loss_reduction
float
Desired fractional reduction r in the modeled loss, in (0, 1).
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless new-to-old compute ratio.






Equation: multiple = (1/(1-loss_reduction))**(1/exponent).
Assumptions: The entire loss being reduced is the power-law term with fixed coefficient and exponent.
Excludes: Irreducible loss floors, model-size constraints, and fitted uncertainty.



Derivation: solve multiple**(-alpha) = 1-r for multiple. Small positive exponents can make modest loss reductions expensive.



>>> calc_loss_reduction_compute_multiple(0.5, 0.5)
4.0




physics.scaling.calc_power_law_factor(multiple, exponent)
Calculate the remaining fraction of a resource-dependent power-law term.











Name
Type
Description
Default




multiple
float
Positive dimensionless ratio of new to old resource.
required


exponent
float
Dimensionless alpha in the assumed law A*R**(-alpha).
required














Name
Type
Description





float
New term divided by old term, dimensionless; this is the remaining fraction rather than the reduction fraction.






Equation: factor = multiple**(-exponent).
Assumptions: The same coefficient and exponent hold before and after the change.
Excludes: Irreducible offsets, empirical fitting, and saturation.



Derivation: cancel A in the ratio (A*R_new**(-alpha))/(A*R_old**(-alpha)).



>>> calc_power_law_factor(4, 0.5)
0.5

title: HazardExposureScenario
text:
Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Failure-free exposure that bounds each of rates (constant hazards per hour) at one-sided confidence, against what rigs rigs or one rig over rig_time accumulate.


Equation: The zero-event Poisson relation exp(-rate*time)=1-confidence gives exposure by inversion.
Assumptions: A constant hazard, independent exposure, and no observed failures; rig exposure pools linearly.
Excludes: Changing operating conditions, reset downtime beyond the supplied duty schedule, and field-safety certification.



Derivation: The zero-event Poisson relation exp(-rate*time)=1-confidence gives exposure by inversion. Individual property contracts identify the exact accounting expression or reusable calculation. Registry entries supply the scenario inputs; this class does not turn them into measured outcomes.
