title: CodecEpochScenario
text:
Data scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/data.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
epoch_bytes decompressed on the host each epoch for epochs epochs, at each codec’s decode_rates.


Equation: decode duration = epoch bytes / codec rate; run saving = epochs * per-epoch saving.
Assumptions: Each epoch decodes the full corpus at a fixed supplied codec rate.
Excludes: Storage overlap, compression-ratio differences, and codec warm-up or parallel scaling.



Derivation: decode duration = epoch bytes / codec rate; run saving = epochs * per-epoch saving. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.GzipVersusSnappyEpochs
>>> round(float(case.decode_time('gzip').to('min').magnitude), 3)
13.889






Name
Description




decode_rates



epoch_bytes



epochs










Name
Description




decode_time
CPU decompression time for one epoch in minutes at the selected codec’s fixed


rate_ratio
Fast codec throughput divided by slow codec throughput, a dimensionless ratio.


run_time_saved
Total decompression hours saved across all epochs.


time_saved
Per-epoch minutes saved by the fast codec relative to the slow one.





engine.scenario_types.CodecEpochScenario.decode_time(codec)
CPU decompression time for one epoch in minutes at the selected codec’s fixed rate.
Equation: return (epoch_bytes / decode_rates[codec]).to('minute').



engine.scenario_types.CodecEpochScenario.rate_ratio(fast, slow)
Fast codec throughput divided by slow codec throughput, a dimensionless ratio.
Equation: return (decode_rates[fast] / decode_rates[slow]).to('').magnitude.



engine.scenario_types.CodecEpochScenario.run_time_saved(slow, fast)
Total decompression hours saved across all epochs.
Equation: return (epochs * time_saved(slow, fast)).to('hour').



engine.scenario_types.CodecEpochScenario.time_saved(slow, fast)
Per-epoch minutes saved by the fast codec relative to the slow one.
Equation: return decode_time(slow) - decode_time(fast).

Logic cost of two activation datapaths, in transistor equivalents (an illustrative budget).

title: solvers.DataModel
text:
solvers.DataModel()
Analyzes the ‘Data Wall’ — the throughput bottleneck between storage and compute.
This model simulates the data pipeline constraints, comparing the data demand of a workload (e.g., training tokens or high-resolution video frames) against the physical bandwidth of the storage hierarchy and IO interconnects.
Literature Source: 1. Janapa Reddi et al. (2025), “Machine Learning Systems,” Chapter 4 (Data Engineering). 2. Beitzel et al. (2024), “The Data Wall: Scaling Laws for Data Ingestion in AI.” 3. Mohan et al. (2022), “Analyzing and Mitigating Data Bottlenecks in Deep Learning Training.”





Name
Description




solve
Compare ingestion demand with the slowest specified data path.





solvers.DataModel.solve(workload_data_rate, hardware)
Compare ingestion demand with the slowest specified data path.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workload_data_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative required ingestion bandwidth, convertible to GB/s.
required


hardware
HardwareNode
Hardware entry with optional storage and I/O bandwidth specifications.
required














Name
Type
Description





DataResult
Demand, supply, and margin in GB/s; utilization is demand/supply. is_stalled indicates demand above supply, not an empirical probability. Missing positive paths yield zero supply and infinite utilization.






Equation: supply = min(positive specified storage and I/O bandwidths); utilization = demand/supply and margin = supply - demand.
Assumptions: each specified path carries the same steady-state byte stream. An absent or nonpositive path is omitted rather than treated as a zero-rate physical link. If all paths are absent, capacity is unknown.
Excludes: CPU transformations, buffering, burstiness, cache reuse, and concurrent clients. The stall flag alone does not predict elapsed time.



Derivation: conservation of the same byte stream across serial stages makes the smallest stage bandwidth the sustainable pipeline supply.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Q_
>>> result = DataModel().solve(Q_("1 MB/s"), Hardware.Cloud.H100)
>>> result.margin == result.supply_bw - result.demand_bw
True

Mutating calls retried once after any timeout, with independent request and reply loss.


Equation: Calls=workers*calls_per_worker; duplicate and timeout expectations come from BlindRetryModel.

title: engine.solvers.sandboxes
text:
engine.solvers.sandboxes
Agent-sandbox solvers: the cost of an isolation envelope (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated per-call, per-byte, or per-lease inputs: the system-call tax each envelope pays, setup paid per call or once per trajectory, workspace provisioning by copy or copy-on-write, and a warm pool sized by Little’s law and a Poisson reserve. None models queueing inside a host, restore contention, or a particular hypervisor.





Name
Description




EnvelopeAmortizationModel
Setup paid on every call against once per trajectory, under equal useful work.


SandboxPoolReserveModel
A warm sandbox pool under steady Poisson arrivals.


SyscallTaxModel
The added time of calls ordinary system calls under each envelope.


WorkspaceProvisioningModel
Bytes to provision workspaces by full copy or copy-on-write, and the





engine.solvers.sandboxes.EnvelopeAmortizationModel()
Setup paid on every call against once per trajectory, under equal useful work.
Fresh per call: N (T_setup + W); retained: T_setup + N W. Setup is T_setup / (T_setup + W) of a fresh call, and holding it to a share phi needs W >= T_setup (1 - phi) / phi. Serialized, no overlap.





Name
Description




solve
Compare fresh and retained envelope setup costs.





engine.solvers.sandboxes.EnvelopeAmortizationModel.solve(
    calls,
    setup,
    work_per_call,
    overhead_cap,
)
Compare fresh and retained envelope setup costs.











Name
Type
Description
Default




calls
int
Positive number of calls.
required


setup
Quantity
Nonnegative setup time quantity.
required


work_per_call
Quantity
Positive useful time per call.
required


overhead_cap
float
Allowed setup share, dimensionless and between zero and one.
required














Name
Type
Description





EnvelopeAmortizationResult
Useful work, setup and total durations, reuse speedup, setup share, and useful-work duration required by the overhead cap.






Equation: T_fresh=N(S+W); T_retained=S+NW; W_min=S(1-phi)/phi.
Assumptions: Equal useful work and serial setup across calls.
Excludes: Idle retention cost, eviction, and overlapping work.



Derivation: retaining an envelope removes all but one setup charge. Solving setup / (setup + work) <= overhead_cap for work gives the minimum useful-work duration; this is a cost-accounting identity.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = EnvelopeAmortizationModel().solve(2, Q_(1,"s"), Q_(2,"s"), 0.2)
>>> r.per_call_total > r.per_trajectory_total
True






engine.solvers.sandboxes.SandboxPoolReserveModel()
A warm sandbox pool under steady Poisson arrivals.
Active leases follow Little’s law, N = lambda T_hold. With s standby instances and a constant restore lead time T_init, a request misses when at least s earlier replacements are outstanding: P(Poisson(lambda T_init) >= s). Resident guest memory is a private image per lease, or one shared image plus dirty pages per lease and private state per standby under copy-on-write.





Name
Description




solve
Size a warm pool against a Poisson miss target.





engine.solvers.sandboxes.SandboxPoolReserveModel.solve(
    arrival_rate,
    hold,
    restore,
    guest_memory,
    dirty,
    standby,
    target_miss,
    initial_reserve,
    slow_factor,
)
Size a warm pool against a Poisson miss target.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrival_rate
Quantity
Positive arrival rate, inverse time.
required


hold
Quantity
Positive lease holding time.
required


restore
Quantity
Positive restore lead time.
required


guest_memory
Quantity
Positive private guest memory, byte quantity.
required


dirty
Quantity
Nonnegative dirty memory per active guest, byte quantity.
required


standby
Quantity
Nonnegative private state per standby, byte quantity.
required


target_miss
float
Target miss probability, between zero and one.
required


initial_reserve
int
Nonnegative initial standby count.
required


slow_factor
float
Positive multiplicative restore-time slowdown.
required














Name
Type
Description





SandboxPoolReserveResult
Mean active leases, standby counts, Poisson miss probabilities, private and shared-pool memory in GB, and restore-time ceiling in ms.






Equation: N=lambda T_hold; mu=lambda T_restore; miss=P(Poisson(mu)>=reserve).
Assumptions: Steady Poisson arrivals and constant restore lead time.
Excludes: Burst correlation, restore contention, and a guaranteed tail bound for non-Poisson arrivals.



Derivation: Little’s occupancy identity multiplies arrivals per second by lease duration. During a fixed restore interval, Poisson arrivals have mean arrival_rate * restore; calc_poisson_reserve chooses the smallest standby count meeting its upper-tail target. Pool memory adds one shared image, dirty pages for active leases, and private standby state.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = SandboxPoolReserveModel().solve(Q_(1,"1/s"), Q_(10,"s"), Q_(1,"s"), Q_(1,"GB"), Q_(0.1,"GB"), Q_(0.1,"GB"), 0.01, 1, 2)
>>> r.reserve_miss <= 0.01
True






engine.solvers.sandboxes.SyscallTaxModel()
The added time of calls ordinary system calls under each envelope.
A shared-kernel container pays a trap and an in-kernel filter per call, a microVM a native trap in its guest (device exits counted separately), and a user-space kernel a trap, emulation, and a switch to the emulator.





Name
Description




solve
Compute serialized system-call overhead.





engine.solvers.sandboxes.SyscallTaxModel.solve(
    calls,
    trap,
    filter,
    emulate,
    switch,
)
Compute serialized system-call overhead.











Name
Type
Description
Default




calls
int
Number of calls, nonnegative.
required


trap
Quantity
Native trap duration, positive time quantity.
required


filter
Quantity
Filter duration per call, nonnegative time quantity.
required


emulate
Quantity
Emulation duration per call, nonnegative time quantity.
required


switch
Quantity
Context-switch duration per call, nonnegative time quantity.
required














Name
Type
Description





SyscallTaxResult
Per-call durations, total serialized seconds, and the dimensionless userspace-to-microVM time ratio.






Equation: T_container=N(trap+filter); T_guest=N trap; T_user=N(trap+emulate+switch).
Assumptions: Each call pays the same stated cost, with no overlap.
Excludes: Device exits, scheduling contention, and measured hypervisor behavior.



Derivation: add the trap and envelope-specific costs paid by one call, then multiply that duration by the call count. The guest baseline pays only the native trap, so dividing user-space duration by trap gives its relative tax.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = SyscallTaxModel().solve(2, Q_(1,"us"), Q_(1,"us"), Q_(2,"us"), Q_(1,"us"))
>>> r.container_total > r.microvm_total
True






engine.solvers.sandboxes.WorkspaceProvisioningModel()
Bytes to provision workspaces by full copy or copy-on-write, and the first-write payload under file or block granularity.
Payload only: drive times are lower bounds at the sequential rate, and metadata, journaling, and caching add traffic.





Name
Description




solve
Compare full-copy and copy-on-write payloads.





engine.solvers.sandboxes.WorkspaceProvisioningModel.solve(
    workspaces,
    base_image,
    written,
    bandwidth,
    fixture,
    block,
    modified,
)
Compare full-copy and copy-on-write payloads.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workspaces
int
Positive workspace count.
required


base_image
Quantity
Base image size, positive byte quantity.
required


written
Quantity
Bytes written per workspace, positive byte quantity.
required


bandwidth
Quantity
Positive sequential storage bandwidth, bytes per second.
required


fixture
Quantity
File copied on first write, positive byte quantity.
required


block
Quantity
Block copied on first write, positive byte quantity.
required


modified
Quantity
Logical modification size, nonnegative byte quantity.
required














Name
Type
Description





WorkspaceProvisioningResult
Full-copy and copy-on-write byte payloads, sequential-transfer times in seconds, and file-to-block amplification ratios.






Equation: B_full=N B_image; B_cow=N B_written; T=B/bandwidth.
Assumptions: Each workspace writes the supplied payload at a constant bandwidth.
Excludes: Metadata, journaling, cache effects, and device contention.



Derivation: each workspace contributes either the whole image or its written payload. Dividing aggregate bytes by sequential bytes per second gives a transfer-time lower bound. First-write amplification divides file-size payload by block-size payload for the same logical change.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = WorkspaceProvisioningModel().solve(2, Q_(10,"GB"), Q_(1,"GB"), Q_(1,"GB/s"), Q_(1,"MB"), Q_(4,"KiB"), Q_(1,"KiB"))
>>> r.full_copy_time > r.cow_time
True

SandboxPoolReserveResult
Mean active leases, standby counts, Poisson miss probabilities, private and shared-pool memory in GB, and restore-time ceiling in ms.






Equation: N=lambda T_hold; mu=lambda T_restore; miss=P(Poisson(mu)>=reserve).
Assumptions: Steady Poisson arrivals and constant restore lead time.
Excludes: Burst correlation, restore contention, and a guaranteed tail bound for non-Poisson arrivals.



Derivation: Little’s occupancy identity multiplies arrivals per second by lease duration. During a fixed restore interval, Poisson arrivals have mean arrival_rate * restore; calc_poisson_reserve chooses the smallest standby count meeting its upper-tail target. Pool memory adds one shared image, dirty pages for active leases, and private standby state.

True

Per-call durations, total serialized seconds, and the dimensionless userspace-to-microVM time ratio.






Equation: T_container=N(trap+filter); T_guest=N trap; T_user=N(trap+emulate+switch).
Assumptions: Each call pays the same stated cost, with no overlap.

title: engine.solvers.interconnect
text:
engine.solvers.interconnect
Interconnect solvers: transfer bounds across link tiers, alpha-beta messages, bisection cuts, incast, and fits to measured collectives.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable.





Name
Description




AlphaBetaModel
Point-to-point message time under the alpha-beta model on several paths.


BisectionModel
A ring AllReduce whose every edge crosses the bisection, on a full and an oversubscribed cut.


CommunicationIntensityModel
Communication intensity of one data-parallel worker step against fabric balance.


GradientSyncModel
One data-parallel step: local compute, then a ring AllReduce of the gradients.


IncastModel
Many senders converge on one egress port (incast).


TensorParallelCommModel
Activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel training step.


TransferLadderModel
Moves one payload over each tier of a bandwidth hierarchy.





engine.solvers.interconnect.AlphaBetaModel()
Point-to-point message time under the alpha-beta model on several paths.
Each message of n bytes pays a fixed startup alpha (NIC, switch hops, error correction, software) plus n / beta on the wire. The two terms are equal at n* = alpha * beta: below it a lower alpha helps, above it only a higher beta does.
Literature Source: Hockney (1994), “The communication challenge for MPP”.





Name
Description




solve
Evaluate startup and wire time for named messages and paths.





engine.solvers.interconnect.AlphaBetaModel.solve(alphas, bandwidths, messages)
Evaluate startup and wire time for named messages and paths.











Name
Type
Description
Default




alphas
Dict[str, Quantity]
Mapping of path names to nonnegative startup times.
required


bandwidths
Dict[str, Quantity]
Mapping of path names to positive bandwidths in byte/s.
required


messages
Dict[str, Quantity]
Mapping of message names to nonnegative byte quantities.
required














Name
Type
Description





AlphaBetaResult
Per-path message times and wire times in seconds, with crossover bytes. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: time = alpha + message_bytes / bandwidth; crossover_bytes = alpha * bandwidth.
Assumptions: Every alpha path has a bandwidth entry; both terms are constant per path.
Excludes: Congestion, packetization, and throughput variation.



Derivation: time = alpha + message_bytes / bandwidth; crossover_bytes = alpha * bandwidth. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import AlphaBetaModel
>>> AlphaBetaModel().solve({'p': Q_('1 ms')}, {'p': Q_('1 GB/s')}, {'m': Q_('1 MB')}).times['p']['m'].to('ms').magnitude == 2
True






engine.solvers.interconnect.BisectionModel()
A ring AllReduce whose every edge crosses the bisection, on a full and an oversubscribed cut.
With ranks placed alternately in the two halves, each of the N/2 ring edges in one direction crosses the cut and carries 2(N-1)/N times the per-device payload (ReduceScatter then AllGather). The cut carries N/2 links, divided by the oversubscription ratio. Only the communication fraction of the step stretches, so relative throughput is 1 / ((1 - f) + f r); the lost share of a cluster’s capital cost is its equivalent idle capacity. This placement is the worst case.





Name
Description




solve
Bound collective traffic through a worst-case bisection placement.

    n_devices,
    link_bandwidth,
    oversubscription_ratio,
    payload_per_device,
    communication_fraction,
    cluster_cost,
)
Bound collective traffic through a worst-case bisection placement.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_devices
int
Even device count at least two.
required


link_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive link bandwidth in byte/s.
required


oversubscription_ratio
float
Positive full-cut to available-cut bandwidth ratio.
required


payload_per_device
Quantity

required


communication_fraction
float
Fraction of baseline step spent communicating, between zero and one.
required


cluster_cost
Quantity
Nonnegative capital cost in currency units.
required














Name
Type
Description





BisectionResult
Cut bandwidths, crossing GB, communication seconds, slowdown and throughput ratios, and idle-equivalent capital cost. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: crossing = floor(N/2) * payload * ring_factor; cut_bandwidth = floor(N/2) * link_bandwidth / oversubscription; throughput = 1 / (1-f+f*r).
Assumptions: Even device groups with alternating placement across the cut and positive traffic.
Excludes: Alternative rank placement, overlap changes, and monetary accounting beyond idle-capacity equivalence.



Derivation: crossing = floor(N/2) * payload * ring_factor; cut_bandwidth = floor(N/2) * link_bandwidth / oversubscription; throughput = 1 / (1-f+f*r). This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import BisectionModel
>>> BisectionModel().solve(4, Q_('100 GB/s'), 2, Q_('1 GB'), 0.5, Q_('100 USD')).slowdown == 2
True

engine.solvers.interconnect.GradientSyncModel()
One data-parallel step: local compute, then a ring AllReduce of the gradients.
Each worker sends about 2x the gradient bytes per step (the ring factor for large N). With no overlap the step is compute plus transfer, so the compute fraction shows how much of the step the accelerator works. Energy charges each transferred bit once at the fabric’s energy per bit.

    model,
    precision,
    links,
    compute_time,
    energy_per_bit=None,
    steps=1,
    compute_speedup=1.0,
)
Compare gradient synchronization time and energy across fabrics.

Type
Description
Default

object

required


precision
str
Weight or KV precision name; gradient synchronization also accepts bytes per element.
required

required

object

1.0














Name
Type
Description





GradientSyncResult
Synchronization bytes, transfer and step times in seconds per link, compute fractions, and per-step and total energy in joules. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: sync_bytes = ring_factor * model_bytes; step_i = compute_time / speedup + sync_bytes / bandwidth_i; energy = sync_bits * energy_per_bit.
Assumptions: The registry ring factor approximates large groups; transfers serialize after compute.

Derivation: sync_bytes = ring_factor * model_bytes; step_i = compute_time / speedup + sync_bytes / bandwidth_i; energy = sync_bits * energy_per_bit. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import GradientSyncModel
>>> GradientSyncModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 'fp16', {'link': Q_('100 GB/s')}, Q_('1 s')).transfer_times['link'].magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.interconnect.IncastModel()
Many senders converge on one egress port (incast).
The offered load is the senders’ combined rate; the buffer fills at the offered load less what the egress drains, and a full buffer holds buffer / egress of waiting. The bandwidth-delay product is the data in flight on the egress link during one feedback round trip, which is what end-to-end congestion control must absorb before it can react.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate buffer fill and drain under sustained incast.





engine.solvers.interconnect.IncastModel.solve(
    n_senders,
    sender_bandwidth,
    egress_bandwidth,
    buffer,
    feedback_rtt,
)
Estimate buffer fill and drain under sustained incast.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_senders
int
Positive number of simultaneous senders.
required


sender_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive bandwidth offered by each sender in byte/s.
required


egress_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive shared egress bandwidth in byte/s.
required


buffer
Quantity
Positive buffer capacity in bytes.
required


feedback_rtt
Quantity
Nonnegative feedback round-trip time.
required














Name
Type
Description





IncastResult
Offered and net fill bandwidths, dimensionless oversubscription, fill/drain microseconds, and bandwidth-delay product in KB. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: offered = senders * sender_bandwidth; fill_time = buffer / (offered-egress); drain_time = buffer / egress; BDP = egress * RTT.
Assumptions: Offered load exceeds positive egress bandwidth; constant rates during the burst.
Excludes: Congestion control reactions, dropped packets, and finite burst termination.



Derivation: offered = senders * sender_bandwidth; fill_time = buffer / (offered-egress); drain_time = buffer / egress; BDP = egress * RTT. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import IncastModel
>>> IncastModel().solve(2, Q_('1 GB/s'), Q_('1 GB/s'), Q_('1 MB'), Q_('1 ms')).oversubscription == 2
True






engine.solvers.interconnect.TensorParallelCommModel()
Activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel training step.
Each Transformer layer sums an activation-sized partial result across the tensor-parallel group once in the forward pass and once in the backward pass. A ring AllReduce over N devices moves 2(N-1)/N times the payload per device. The bound is bandwidth-only and assumes no overlap with the stated compute time, so the fractions are a diagnostic, not a forecast.
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (two AllReduces per layer per pass). 2. Patarasuk and Yuan (2009), ring AllReduce bandwidth factor.





Name
Description




solve
Account for repeated activation collectives in a tensor-parallel step.

    model,
    tp_size,
    microbatch,
    link_bandwidth,
    compute_time,
    seq_len=None,
    collectives_per_layer=2,
)
Account for repeated activation collectives in a tensor-parallel step.

Type

Default

Workload with parameter count, dimensions, and weight size.
required

required

int

required

Quantity
Positive link bandwidth in byte/s.
required

Nonnegative local compute time, convertible to seconds.
required


seq_len
int
Positive tokens per sequence; None uses model context length.
None


collectives_per_layer
int
Nonnegative collectives per layer per modeled step.
2














Name
Type
Description





TensorParallelCommResult
Payload and per-rank traffic in bytes; per-collective, communication, compute, and total step times in milliseconds; dimensionless time shares. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: payload = microbatch * sequence * hidden_dim * FP16_bytes; traffic = 2(N-1)/N * payload; step = compute + layers * collectives_per_layer * traffic / bandwidth.
Assumptions: FP16 activations and serialized bandwidth-only ring collectives; the caller chooses collective count.
Excludes: Startup latency, collective overlap, contention, and model residency.



Derivation: payload = microbatch * sequence * hidden_dim * FP16_bytes; traffic = 2(N-1)/N * payload; step = compute + layers * collectives_per_layer * traffic / bandwidth. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TensorParallelCommModel
>>> TensorParallelCommModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 2, 1, Q_('100 GB/s'), Q_('1 s'), seq_len=8).communication_time.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.interconnect.TransferLadderModel()
Moves one payload over each tier of a bandwidth hierarchy.
The time on each tier is the bandwidth-only lower bound, bytes / bandwidth; per-message startup latency (the alpha term) is excluded. The ratios between tiers are the bandwidth staircase that decides where each kind of parallel traffic may run.





Name
Description




solve
Evaluate bandwidth-only transfer time on each named link.





engine.solvers.interconnect.TransferLadderModel.solve(payload, links)
Evaluate bandwidth-only transfer time on each named link.











Name
Type
Description
Default




payload
Quantity
Nonnegative payload size in bytes.
required


links
Dict[str, Quantity]
Mapping of path names to positive bandwidth quantities in byte/s.
required














Name
Type
Description





TransferLadderResult
Payload bytes, bandwidths, and transfer times in milliseconds per link. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: t_i = payload / bandwidth_i.
Assumptions: Each link carries the same complete payload at constant bandwidth.
Excludes: Startup, contention, protocol overhead, and overlap.



Derivation: t_i = payload / bandwidth_i. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TransferLadderModel
>>> TransferLadderModel().solve(Q_('1 GB'), {'link': Q_('1 GB/s')}).times['link'].to('s').magnitude == 1
True

engine.solvers.interconnect.TensorParallelCommModel()
Activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel training step.
Each Transformer layer sums an activation-sized partial result across the tensor-parallel group once in the forward pass and once in the backward pass. A ring AllReduce over N devices moves 2(N-1)/N times the payload per device. The bound is bandwidth-only and assumes no overlap with the stated compute time, so the fractions are a diagnostic, not a forecast.

text:
engine.solvers.embodied
Embodied solvers: how far a machine travels before it stops, and what the floor allows.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.robotics.stopping and physics.drivetrain; these models compose them for one stated situation (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




OnsetTrialModel
One stopping trace scored against a precommitted oracle (added 2026-10-20).


RailHoldUpModel
A capacitor-backed rail that must carry the protective response from the


ShieldCoverageBillModel
The evidence a shielded hazard-rate claim needs (added 2026-10-20).


StoppingBudgetModel
The elementary stopping budget: travel during the pre-brake delay plus braking travel.


TakeoverBudgetModel
A request for a person to take over, priced against the finished stopping budget.


TractionLossModel
A drop in floor friction against the deceleration a machine’s budget assumes.





engine.solvers.embodied.OnsetTrialModel()
One stopping trace scored against a precommitted oracle (added 2026-10-20).
The oracle bounds powered-deceleration onset at onset_bound after the reference event and travel to rest at travel_bound (onset-bound travel, the resident stop, and the tracking inset). A trace that begins braking at onset travels speed * onset plus the same resident stop. Each predicate keeps its own signed margin; a combined score needs scales fixed in advance, here the bounds themselves. The trace passes only when both margins are non-negative.





Name
Description




solve
Score one observed onset against precommitted bounds.





engine.solvers.embodied.OnsetTrialModel.solve(
    onset_bound,
    onset,
    speed,
    resident_stop,
    travel_bound,
    stop_time,
)
Score one observed onset against precommitted bounds.


    onset_bound : Quantity
        Positive permitted onset delay in seconds, fixed before scoring.
    onset : Quantity
        Observed powered-braking onset in seconds after the reference event.
    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    resident_stop : Quantity
        Braking travel after onset in meters; nonnegative.
    travel_bound : Quantity
        Positive allowed total travel in meters, fixed before scoring.
    stop_time : Quantity
        Braking duration after onset in seconds; nonnegative.



    OnsetTrialResult
        Onset/time margins in milliseconds, travel margins in millimeters,
        normalized margins, and the conjunction of the two bound checks.



    Equation: travel = speed onset + resident_stop; passes = (onset <= onset_bound) and (travel <= travel_bound).

    Assumptions: The observed and reference cases share the resident braking profile; the two bounds are fixed externally.

    Excludes: Statistical confidence across trials and any inference of certified safety.



    Derivation: Each signed margin subtracts the observed quantity from its precommitted bound; normalized margins divide by that same bound.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import OnsetTrialModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = OnsetTrialModel().solve(ureg('0.2 s'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('0.5 m'), ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 s'))



r.passes True









engine.solvers.embodied.RailHoldUpModel()
A capacitor-backed rail that must carry the protective response from the loss-of-feed flag until the holding brakes are set (added 2026-10-20).
t_set = flag_path + (v/a + a/j) + t_engage: the path from the flag to powered-deceleration onset, the S-curve stop from the entry speed v (calc_scurve_stop_time), and the holding brake’s engagement. The margin is the hold-up time less t_set.





Name
Description




solve
Compare rail hold-up time with the protective stop duration.





engine.solvers.embodied.RailHoldUpModel.solve(
    flag_path,
    speed,
    deceleration,
    jerk,
    engage,
    holdup,
)
Compare rail hold-up time with the protective stop duration.


    flag_path : Quantity
        Loss-of-feed flag to brake-onset latency in seconds.
    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    jerk : Quantity
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    engage : Quantity
        Holding-brake engagement duration in seconds.
    holdup : Quantity
        Available rail hold-up duration in seconds.



    RailHoldUpResult
        Phase durations and remaining hold-up margin in milliseconds;
        a negative margin means the stated supply duration is insufficient.



    Equation: t_set = flag_path + t_scurve + engage; margin = holdup - t_set.

    Assumptions: Serial flag, stopping, and engagement phases; the supplied jerk and deceleration remain available during hold-up.

    Excludes: Rail voltage trajectories, capacitor sizing, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Serial response durations add; the S-curve stopping helper supplies the powered-stop duration.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import RailHoldUpModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = RailHoldUpModel().solve(ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('2 m/s**3'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('3 s'))



r.margin.m_as(‘s’) > 0 True









engine.solvers.embodied.ShieldCoverageBillModel()
The evidence a shielded hazard-rate claim needs (added 2026-10-20).
A fleet of fleet_units logs hours_per_day for one release cycle of cycle_days with zero hazardous proposals; the one-sided Poisson bound is -ln(1 - C) / T. The shield passes 1 - coverage of hazardous proposals (calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate), plus the common-cause rate. Against target_rate the model reports the coverage the bound would need, the proposal bound the stated coverage would need, the failure-free exposure and fleet days that bound it (calc_empirical_testing_exposure), and the seeded-hazard campaign that bounds the coverage itself (calc_zero_failure_sample_size), alone and with both bounds held jointly at 1 - alpha/2 each.





Name
Description




solve
Compute exposure and coverage requirements for a hazard-rate bound.





engine.solvers.embodied.ShieldCoverageBillModel.solve(
    fleet_units,
    cycle_days,
    hours_per_day,
    coverage,
    common_cause_rate,
    target_rate,
    confidence,
)
Compute exposure and coverage requirements for a hazard-rate bound.


    fleet_units : int
        Positive number of machines contributing exposure.
    cycle_days : Quantity
        Release-cycle duration in days; positive.
    hours_per_day : Quantity
        Logging rate in hours/day; positive.
    coverage : float
        Hazard rejection fraction, strictly between zero and one.
    common_cause_rate : Quantity
        Nonnegative common-cause hazard rate in 1/hour.
    target_rate : Quantity
        Target hazard rate in 1/hour, above the common-cause rate.
    confidence : float
        One-sided confidence in (0, 1).



    ShieldCoverageBillResult
        Exposure in hours, rate bounds in inverse hours, campaign duration
        in days, trial counts, and the comparison with the stated rate target.



    Equation: T = fleet_units cycle_days hours_per_day; lambda_upper = -log(1-confidence)/T; lambda_residual = (1-coverage) lambda_upper + common_cause_rate.

    Assumptions: Zero observed hazardous proposals under a stationary Poisson process and representative seeded coverage trials. Joint bounds split the error budget equally.

    Excludes: Nonstationary hazards, unmodeled dependence, experimental evidence collection, and safety certification.



    Derivation: For zero Poisson events, exp(-lambda T) equals the tail probability. Residual proposals multiply by the uncovered fraction; the joint bounds use a union-bound allocation.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import ShieldCoverageBillModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = ShieldCoverageBillModel().solve(10, ureg('30 day'), ureg('8 hour/day'), 0.9, ureg('0 / hour'), ureg('0.001 / hour'), 0.95)



r.exposure.m_as(‘hour’) 2400.0









engine.solvers.embodied.StoppingBudgetModel()
The elementary stopping budget: travel during the pre-brake delay plus braking travel.
d_stop = travel(delay) + v^2 / (2 a) <= D_clear. The delay travel is v * tau at constant speed, or the trapezoid between speed and speed_at_delay_end when two speeds were recorded. Braking travel and braking time are from speed, the speed when the hazard appears, as the elementary budget assumes. The crossover speed 2 a tau is where the two terms are equal; the speed ceiling is the fastest speed whose stop fits clear_distance. A localization bound and a protective margin, when stated, add to the required distance and lower the ceiling (calc_safe_stopping_distance). added_delay prices one more delay step as travel at speed. The delay ceiling is the longest constant-speed pre-brake delay whose stop, with the overhead, still fits (calc_watchdog_lease_bound): (D_clear - overhead - v^2/2a) / v.
The finished budget (added 2026-10-20) takes three optional terms. A jerk bound replaces constant-deceleration braking with the resident S-curve stop (calc_scurve_stop_distance); its extra travel over v^2/2a is the jerk-ramp travel, and above a^2/j it equals v a / (2 j), a delay of a / (2 j). A tracking_bound (the tracking inset) joins the required distance after the two allowances. An approach_speed charges a person who keeps closing the gap for the whole delay and stop (v_h (tau + T_stop)). With a jerk bound the speed ceiling is the S-curve root (calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity) and the delay ceiling is (D_clear - overhead - inset - d_S(v)) / v. The same case reports the weakest deceleration whose S-curve stop still fits the braking room, jerk fixed, and its shortfall from the stated one (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Compose delay, braking, and clearance budgets.





engine.solvers.embodied.StoppingBudgetModel.solve(
    speed,
    delay,
    deceleration,
    clear_distance=None,
    speed_at_delay_end=None,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    added_delay=None,
    jerk=None,
    tracking_bound=None,
    approach_speed=None,
)
Compose delay, braking, and clearance budgets.


    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    delay : Quantity
        Pre-braking latency in seconds; nonnegative.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    clear_distance : Optional[Quantity]
        Available clearance in meters; None omits clearance checks.
    speed_at_delay_end : Optional[Quantity]
        Recorded terminal delay speed in m/s; None uses entry speed.
    loc_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Localization allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    physical_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Protective allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    added_delay : Optional[Quantity]
        Extra delay to price as travel, in seconds; None omits that output.
    jerk : Optional[Quantity]
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    tracking_bound : Optional[Quantity]
        Tracking inset in meters; None contributes zero.
    approach_speed : Optional[Quantity]
        Closing speed of the other body in m/s; None contributes zero.



    StoppingBudgetResult
        Distances in meters, times in milliseconds, speed ceilings in m/s,
        and signed clearance margins; optional fits compares required clearance.



    Equation: d_required = (v + v_end) tau / 2 + d_brake + margins + v_approach (tau + t_stop).

    Assumptions: The constant-deceleration branch brakes from entry speed, even when the delay endpoint differs. Optional jerk selects the S-curve branch.

    Excludes: Terrain changes, controller transients outside the stated delay, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Distances are integrated over the stated delay and braking profile; inverse budgets solve the same distance inequality.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import StoppingBudgetModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = StoppingBudgetModel().solve(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'))



round(r.stop_distance.m_as(‘m’), 2) 0.6









engine.solvers.embodied.TakeoverBudgetModel()
A request for a person to take over, priced against the finished stopping budget.
The takeover T_Sigma (the human response plus the console transport) adds to the machine’s pre-brake delay tau: until the person commits, the machine keeps moving at the request speed. Four finished budgets (StoppingBudgetModel with the S-curve jerk bound and the tracking inset) are solved at that speed: the machine alone, the machine with the dispatch-to-admission allocation Delta_da charged, and each with the takeover waited out before braking. The fallback deadline T_latest is the machine-alone delay spare: the longest wait after the request before the machine’s own stop must begin,
T_latest = (D_clear - delta - d_S(v)) / v - tau.
Configured timeouts are clipped to it, T = max(0, min(T_cfg, T_latest)), and dispatched on the last whole permission tick. Once the operator holds the channel, a manual lease longer than the chunk lease adds its excess to the delay as travel at the request speed (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Charge takeover latency against the machine stopping reserve.





engine.solvers.embodied.TakeoverBudgetModel.solve(
    speed,
    delay,
    deceleration,
    clear_distance,
    takeover,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    jerk=None,
    tracking_bound=None,
    dispatch_to_admission=None,
    configured_timeout=None,
    tick=None,
    manual_lease=None,
    chunk_lease=None,
)
Charge takeover latency against the machine stopping reserve.


    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    delay : Quantity
        Pre-braking latency in seconds; nonnegative.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    clear_distance : Quantity
        Available clearance in meters; None omits clearance checks.
    takeover : Quantity
        Human response and transport duration in seconds; nonnegative.
    loc_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Localization allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    physical_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Protective allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    jerk : Optional[Quantity]
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    tracking_bound : Optional[Quantity]
        Tracking inset in meters; None contributes zero.
    dispatch_to_admission : Optional[Quantity]
        Additional admission delay in seconds; None contributes zero.
    configured_timeout : Optional[Quantity]
        Requested timeout in seconds; requires positive tick when supplied.
    tick : Optional[Quantity]
        Permission tick period in seconds; positive when timeout is supplied.
    manual_lease : Optional[Quantity]
        Manual command lease in seconds; requires chunk_lease when supplied.
    chunk_lease : Optional[Quantity]
        Reference command lease in seconds.



    TakeoverBudgetResult
        Stopping budgets, travel in millimeters, and deadlines, timeouts, and
        time reserves in milliseconds; permission counts are dimensionless.



    Equation: T_latest = (D_clear - overhead - d_brake) / v - tau; timeout = max(0, min(T_configured, T_latest)).

    Assumptions: The same speed, braking profile, and margins apply to all four compared budgets. Inputs must leave an available delay_spare on the underlying stopping result.

    Excludes: Human-response distributions, changing approach speed, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Subtract the common stopping budget from clearance and convert remaining travel into waiting time at entry speed.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import TakeoverBudgetModel

A drop in floor friction against the deceleration a machine’s budget assumes.
At the traction limit the deceleration is mu g phi, so braking distance v^2 / (2 mu g phi) scales as 1 / mu and the ratio of the two braking distances is mu_before / mu_after. The stated deceleration holds only while the lower friction still supplies it (calc_required_friction).





Name
Description




solve
Compare a friction change with required deceleration.





engine.solvers.embodied.TractionLossModel.solve(
    mu_before,
    mu_after,
    deceleration,
    drive_load_share=1.0,
)
Compare a friction change with required deceleration.


    mu_before : float
        Positive dimensionless friction coefficient before the change.
    mu_after : float
        Positive dimensionless friction coefficient after the change.

        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.

        ceiling in m/s**2, and a friction-premise comparison.

engine.solvers.embodied.OnsetTrialModel()
One stopping trace scored against a precommitted oracle (added 2026-10-20).
The oracle bounds powered-deceleration onset at onset_bound after the reference event and travel to rest at travel_bound (onset-bound travel, the resident stop, and the tracking inset). A trace that begins braking at onset travels speed * onset plus the same resident stop. Each predicate keeps its own signed margin; a combined score needs scales fixed in advance, here the bounds themselves. The trace passes only when both margins are non-negative.





Name
Description




solve
Score one observed onset against precommitted bounds.





engine.solvers.embodied.OnsetTrialModel.solve(
    onset_bound,
    onset,
    speed,
    resident_stop,
    travel_bound,
    stop_time,
)
Score one observed onset against precommitted bounds.


    onset_bound : Quantity
        Positive permitted onset delay in seconds, fixed before scoring.
    onset : Quantity
        Observed powered-braking onset in seconds after the reference event.
    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    resident_stop : Quantity
        Braking travel after onset in meters; nonnegative.
    travel_bound : Quantity
        Positive allowed total travel in meters, fixed before scoring.
    stop_time : Quantity
        Braking duration after onset in seconds; nonnegative.



    OnsetTrialResult
        Onset/time margins in milliseconds, travel margins in millimeters,
        normalized margins, and the conjunction of the two bound checks.



    Equation: travel = speed onset + resident_stop; passes = (onset <= onset_bound) and (travel <= travel_bound).

    Assumptions: The observed and reference cases share the resident braking profile; the two bounds are fixed externally.

    Excludes: Statistical confidence across trials and any inference of certified safety.



    Derivation: Each signed margin subtracts the observed quantity from its precommitted bound; normalized margins divide by that same bound.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import OnsetTrialModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = OnsetTrialModel().solve(ureg('0.2 s'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('0.5 m'), ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 s'))



r.passes True

A capacitor-backed rail that must carry the protective response from the loss-of-feed flag until the holding brakes are set (added 2026-10-20).
t_set = flag_path + (v/a + a/j) + t_engage: the path from the flag to powered-deceleration onset, the S-curve stop from the entry speed v (calc_scurve_stop_time), and the holding brake’s engagement. The margin is the hold-up time less t_set.





Name
Description




solve
Compare rail hold-up time with the protective stop duration.





engine.solvers.embodied.RailHoldUpModel.solve(
    flag_path,
    speed,
    deceleration,
    jerk,
    engage,
    holdup,
)

    flag_path : Quantity
        Loss-of-feed flag to brake-onset latency in seconds.
    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    jerk : Quantity
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    engage : Quantity

    holdup : Quantity
        Available rail hold-up duration in seconds.

        Phase durations and remaining hold-up margin in milliseconds;
        a negative margin means the stated supply duration is insufficient.



    Equation: t_set = flag_path + t_scurve + engage; margin = holdup - t_set.

    Assumptions: Serial flag, stopping, and engagement phases; the supplied jerk and deceleration remain available during hold-up.

    Excludes: Rail voltage trajectories, capacitor sizing, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Serial response durations add; the S-curve stopping helper supplies the powered-stop duration.

r.margin.m_as(‘s’) > 0 True









engine.solvers.embodied.ShieldCoverageBillModel()
The evidence a shielded hazard-rate claim needs (added 2026-10-20).
A fleet of fleet_units logs hours_per_day for one release cycle of cycle_days with zero hazardous proposals; the one-sided Poisson bound is -ln(1 - C) / T. The shield passes 1 - coverage of hazardous proposals (calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate), plus the common-cause rate. Against target_rate the model reports the coverage the bound would need, the proposal bound the stated coverage would need, the failure-free exposure and fleet days that bound it (calc_empirical_testing_exposure), and the seeded-hazard campaign that bounds the coverage itself (calc_zero_failure_sample_size), alone and with both bounds held jointly at 1 - alpha/2 each.





Name
Description




solve
Compute exposure and coverage requirements for a hazard-rate bound.





engine.solvers.embodied.ShieldCoverageBillModel.solve(
    fleet_units,
    cycle_days,
    hours_per_day,
    coverage,
    common_cause_rate,
    target_rate,
    confidence,
)
Compute exposure and coverage requirements for a hazard-rate bound.


    fleet_units : int
        Positive number of machines contributing exposure.
    cycle_days : Quantity
        Release-cycle duration in days; positive.
    hours_per_day : Quantity
        Logging rate in hours/day; positive.
    coverage : float
        Hazard rejection fraction, strictly between zero and one.
    common_cause_rate : Quantity
        Nonnegative common-cause hazard rate in 1/hour.
    target_rate : Quantity
        Target hazard rate in 1/hour, above the common-cause rate.
    confidence : float
        One-sided confidence in (0, 1).



    ShieldCoverageBillResult
        Exposure in hours, rate bounds in inverse hours, campaign duration
        in days, trial counts, and the comparison with the stated rate target.



    Equation: T = fleet_units cycle_days hours_per_day; lambda_upper = -log(1-confidence)/T; lambda_residual = (1-coverage) lambda_upper + common_cause_rate.

    Assumptions: Zero observed hazardous proposals under a stationary Poisson process and representative seeded coverage trials. Joint bounds split the error budget equally.

    Excludes: Nonstationary hazards, unmodeled dependence, experimental evidence collection, and safety certification.



    Derivation: For zero Poisson events, exp(-lambda T) equals the tail probability. Residual proposals multiply by the uncovered fraction; the joint bounds use a union-bound allocation.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import ShieldCoverageBillModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = ShieldCoverageBillModel().solve(10, ureg('30 day'), ureg('8 hour/day'), 0.9, ureg('0 / hour'), ureg('0.001 / hour'), 0.95)



r.exposure.m_as(‘hour’) 2400.0









engine.solvers.embodied.StoppingBudgetModel()
The elementary stopping budget: travel during the pre-brake delay plus braking travel.
d_stop = travel(delay) + v^2 / (2 a) <= D_clear. The delay travel is v * tau at constant speed, or the trapezoid between speed and speed_at_delay_end when two speeds were recorded. Braking travel and braking time are from speed, the speed when the hazard appears, as the elementary budget assumes. The crossover speed 2 a tau is where the two terms are equal; the speed ceiling is the fastest speed whose stop fits clear_distance. A localization bound and a protective margin, when stated, add to the required distance and lower the ceiling (calc_safe_stopping_distance). added_delay prices one more delay step as travel at speed. The delay ceiling is the longest constant-speed pre-brake delay whose stop, with the overhead, still fits (calc_watchdog_lease_bound): (D_clear - overhead - v^2/2a) / v.
The finished budget (added 2026-10-20) takes three optional terms. A jerk bound replaces constant-deceleration braking with the resident S-curve stop (calc_scurve_stop_distance); its extra travel over v^2/2a is the jerk-ramp travel, and above a^2/j it equals v a / (2 j), a delay of a / (2 j). A tracking_bound (the tracking inset) joins the required distance after the two allowances. An approach_speed charges a person who keeps closing the gap for the whole delay and stop (v_h (tau + T_stop)). With a jerk bound the speed ceiling is the S-curve root (calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity) and the delay ceiling is (D_clear - overhead - inset - d_S(v)) / v. The same case reports the weakest deceleration whose S-curve stop still fits the braking room, jerk fixed, and its shortfall from the stated one (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Compose delay, braking, and clearance budgets.





engine.solvers.embodied.StoppingBudgetModel.solve(
    speed,
    delay,
    deceleration,
    clear_distance=None,
    speed_at_delay_end=None,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    added_delay=None,
    jerk=None,
    tracking_bound=None,
    approach_speed=None,
)
Compose delay, braking, and clearance budgets.


    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    delay : Quantity
        Pre-braking latency in seconds; nonnegative.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    clear_distance : Optional[Quantity]
        Available clearance in meters; None omits clearance checks.
    speed_at_delay_end : Optional[Quantity]
        Recorded terminal delay speed in m/s; None uses entry speed.
    loc_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Localization allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    physical_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Protective allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    added_delay : Optional[Quantity]
        Extra delay to price as travel, in seconds; None omits that output.
    jerk : Optional[Quantity]
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    tracking_bound : Optional[Quantity]
        Tracking inset in meters; None contributes zero.
    approach_speed : Optional[Quantity]
        Closing speed of the other body in m/s; None contributes zero.



    StoppingBudgetResult
        Distances in meters, times in milliseconds, speed ceilings in m/s,
        and signed clearance margins; optional fits compares required clearance.



    Equation: d_required = (v + v_end) tau / 2 + d_brake + margins + v_approach (tau + t_stop).

    Assumptions: The constant-deceleration branch brakes from entry speed, even when the delay endpoint differs. Optional jerk selects the S-curve branch.

    Excludes: Terrain changes, controller transients outside the stated delay, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Distances are integrated over the stated delay and braking profile; inverse budgets solve the same distance inequality.



    >>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.embodied import StoppingBudgetModel
    >>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
    >>> r = StoppingBudgetModel().solve(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'))



round(r.stop_distance.m_as(‘m’), 2) 0.6









engine.solvers.embodied.TakeoverBudgetModel()
A request for a person to take over, priced against the finished stopping budget.
The takeover T_Sigma (the human response plus the console transport) adds to the machine’s pre-brake delay tau: until the person commits, the machine keeps moving at the request speed. Four finished budgets (StoppingBudgetModel with the S-curve jerk bound and the tracking inset) are solved at that speed: the machine alone, the machine with the dispatch-to-admission allocation Delta_da charged, and each with the takeover waited out before braking. The fallback deadline T_latest is the machine-alone delay spare: the longest wait after the request before the machine’s own stop must begin,
T_latest = (D_clear - delta - d_S(v)) / v - tau.
Configured timeouts are clipped to it, T = max(0, min(T_cfg, T_latest)), and dispatched on the last whole permission tick. Once the operator holds the channel, a manual lease longer than the chunk lease adds its excess to the delay as travel at the request speed (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Charge takeover latency against the machine stopping reserve.





engine.solvers.embodied.TakeoverBudgetModel.solve(
    speed,
    delay,
    deceleration,
    clear_distance,
    takeover,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    jerk=None,
    tracking_bound=None,
    dispatch_to_admission=None,
    configured_timeout=None,
    tick=None,
    manual_lease=None,
    chunk_lease=None,
)
Charge takeover latency against the machine stopping reserve.


    speed : Quantity
        Entry speed in m/s; positive for inverse budgets.
    delay : Quantity
        Pre-braking latency in seconds; nonnegative.
    deceleration : Quantity
        Available braking magnitude in m/s**2; positive.
    clear_distance : Quantity
        Available clearance in meters; None omits clearance checks.
    takeover : Quantity
        Human response and transport duration in seconds; nonnegative.
    loc_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Localization allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    physical_margin : Optional[Quantity]
        Protective allowance in meters; None contributes zero.
    jerk : Optional[Quantity]
        Positive acceleration slew limit in m/s**3; None uses constant deceleration.
    tracking_bound : Optional[Quantity]
        Tracking inset in meters; None contributes zero.
    dispatch_to_admission : Optional[Quantity]
        Additional admission delay in seconds; None contributes zero.
    configured_timeout : Optional[Quantity]
        Requested timeout in seconds; requires positive tick when supplied.
    tick : Optional[Quantity]
        Permission tick period in seconds; positive when timeout is supplied.
    manual_lease : Optional[Quantity]
        Manual command lease in seconds; requires chunk_lease when supplied.
    chunk_lease : Optional[Quantity]
        Reference command lease in seconds.



    TakeoverBudgetResult
        Stopping budgets, travel in millimeters, and deadlines, timeouts, and
        time reserves in milliseconds; permission counts are dimensionless.



    Equation: T_latest = (D_clear - overhead - d_brake) / v - tau; timeout = max(0, min(T_configured, T_latest)).

    Assumptions: The same speed, braking profile, and margins apply to all four compared budgets. Inputs must leave an available delay_spare on the underlying stopping result.

    Excludes: Human-response distributions, changing approach speed, and safety certification.



    Derivation: Subtract the common stopping budget from clearance and convert remaining travel into waiting time at entry speed.

physics.power.calc_dynamic_power_ratio(
    frequency_ratio,
    voltage_tracks_frequency=True,
)
Estimate the dynamic-power ratio after clock scaling.











Name
Type
Description
Default




frequency_ratio
float
Positive new frequency divided by reference frequency.
required

bool
If True, voltage scales by the same ratio; otherwise voltage stays fixed.
True














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless new dynamic power divided by reference dynamic power.






Equation: P_new/P_old = (V_new/V_old)^2 (f_new/f_old), giving r^3 when voltage tracks frequency and r at fixed voltage. Assumptions: identical switched capacitance and activity factor; voltage proportional to frequency is an optional modeling assumption. Excludes: leakage, clock gating changes, transition energy, and physical voltage-frequency operating limits.



Derivation: take the ratio of the capacitive switching-power relation P = activity * capacitance * V^2 * f at two operating points.



>>> calc_dynamic_power_ratio(1.0)
1.0
>>> calc_dynamic_power_ratio(2.0, voltage_tracks_frequency=False) == 2.0
True

Estimate loop-inductance voltage during a linear current ramp.

Type

Default

required

Quantity or float
Positive edge duration; bare numbers mean seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Signed inductive voltage in volts; a rising current gives positive droop.






Equation: delta_V = L delta_I/delta_t. Assumptions: constant lumped inductance and a linear current ramp. Excludes: resistance, decoupling capacitance, distributed parasitics, and converter response. The edge duration must be positive.



Derivation: apply the inductor terminal relation V = L dI/dt to a linear ramp.



>>> calc_inductive_droop(1e-9, 0, 1e-6).m_as('V')

required

Equation: delta_I = delta_P/V. Assumptions: constant rail voltage during the calculation and power measured at that rail rather than upstream of conversion losses. Excludes: converter efficiency, voltage droop feedback, and transient storage.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Peak compute against memory bandwidth across accelerators, first to last.
The ridge point of each is its peak over its bandwidth; the gap growth is how far the ridge rose from the first to the last.

Assumptions: Input order defines the first and last generations; compute and bandwidth are peak specifications.
Excludes: Sustained utilization, kernel dispatch, capacity, and workload-specific traffic.

>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios

>>> value = case.gap_growth
>>> print(f"{value:.3g}")
2.02

accelerators

Dimensionless last-to-first memory bandwidth growth.

Dimensionless last-to-first peak compute growth for the ordered series.


gap_growth
Compute growth divided by bandwidth growth, equal to ridge-point growth.

Sustainability scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/sustainability.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Joules per generated token: node power over aggregate token rate, well used and poorly used.
The node draws the accelerator’s power plus a host share whether a step carries one sequence or many. concurrent_requests at per_request_rate set the well-used token rate; at low_use_fraction of that rate the accelerator still draws low_use_accelerator_power.


Equation: Per-token energy is attributed node watts divided by aggregate tokens per second, then multiplied by response token count for response joules.
Assumptions: Power and throughput are steady within each declared utilization regime; host power is attributed equally to both regimes.
Excludes: Idle transitions, a power trace, other tenants, and prediction of low-use power from throughput.



Derivation: Per-token energy is attributed node watts divided by aggregate tokens per second, then multiplied by response token count for response joules. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.

A residual per-step rate of violating proposals over horizon steps, for a day’s trajectories.


Equation: Trajectory violation probability is 1-(1-step_violation)**horizon; multiplying by daily trajectories gives an expected count.
Assumptions: Per-step violation events are independent with a fixed rate.
Excludes: Correlated violations, event severity, and distinction between proposed and executed harmful actions.



Derivation: the scenario composes mlsysim.physics.agents.calc_unchecked_success. Their contracts supply the underlying equations; property equations show the remaining unit conversions and accounting.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.ResidualViolationsFiftyTurns
>>> value = scenario.trajectory_violation
>>> round(float(value), 3)
0.049

Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Bytes, arithmetic intensity, and energy per image when a batch shares one weight read.
Each image moves the weights divided by the batch plus its own activations activation_passes times (written once, read once), at byte_energy; its arithmetic costs flop_energy per FLOP.


Equation: The calculation members below define weights, weight_per_image, bytes_per_image, intensity, movement_energy, compute_energy, energy, movement_share.
Assumptions: One weight read is shared by the batch; each image pays the stated activation passes and arithmetic work.
Excludes: Cache retention across batches, leakage, and utilization-dependent device power.



Derivation: Bytes, arithmetic intensity, and energy per image when a batch shares one weight read. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.ResNet50BatchEnergyPerImage
>>> value = case.energy(1)
>>> print(f"{value:.3g~}")

title: solvers.TrainingMemoryModel
text:
solvers.TrainingMemoryModel()
Decomposes per-accelerator training memory into teachable components.
This model answers a different question than SingleNodeModel. Roofline feasibility asks whether a workload’s inference weights fit; training feasibility must also account for gradients, optimizer state, activations, and communication buffers. The accounting follows the common mixed-precision state breakdown used by Megatron-LM and ZeRO.
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (tensor/pipeline parallel state). 2. Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO” (data-parallel state sharding). 3. Korthikanti et al. (2023), activation recomputation accounting.
Formula contract: - parameter states are sharded by TP * PP * EP before ZeRO sharding. - ZeRO-1 shards optimizer state, ZeRO-2 also shards gradients, and ZeRO-3 also shards weights across DP. - activation memory is based on local microbatch, layers per pipeline stage, hidden dimension, and the actual bytes per element for the precision.

Description

Estimate per-accelerator training memory from local state and activations.

)

Name
Type
Description





TrainingMemoryResult
Weights, gradients, optimizer state, activations, buffers, and total memory in GB. feasible compares that modeled total with device capacity; it excludes unmodeled runtime reserves.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_activation_memory : Activation retention model. mlsysim.physics.memory.optimizer_state_bytes : Optimizer storage convention.



Equation: total = weights + gradients + optimizer + activations + communication_buffers. Parameter state first divides by TP * PP * EP; ZeRO then divides selected terms by DP. Local microbatch is max(1, ceil(global_batch / (DP * accumulation_steps))). Layers per stage are max(1, ceil(layers / PP)). Activation bytes follow calc_activation_memory and divide by TP when sequence parallelism is enabled. Buffers contain a gradient fraction plus send/receive pipeline boundary activations.
Assumptions: balanced parameter sharding and uniform layer geometry. The precision byte count rescales the activation model’s FP16 baseline. ZeRO stages are cumulative. Trainable fraction affects gradients and optimizer state but not resident weights.
Excludes: allocator reserves, implementation workspaces, fragmentation, uneven expert placement, and detailed interleaved pipeline lifetimes. A capacity pass does not guarantee a runnable deployment.



Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models.” https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054 (bibliography key: rajbhandari2020). Korthikanti et al. (2023), “Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05198 (bibliography key: korthikanti2023).



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Hardware
>>> result = TrainingMemoryModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
...     Hardware.Cloud.H100, batch_size=1, seq_len=128)
>>> result.total_memory.to("GB").magnitude > 0
True
>>> result.feasible == (result.total_memory <= result.available_memory)
True
