title: engine.solvers.perception
text:
engine.solvers.perception
Sensor-perception solvers: capture timing, observation age, and measured error scales (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics/robotics/sensing.py, physics/robotics/control.py, and physics/statistics.py; these models compose them for one stated camera, lidar, stereo rig, or loop, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic.





Name
Description




ClockConversionModel
A free-running clock’s drift between syncs, and the dispatch limit a conversion bound sets.


ConformalInsetModel
The calibration rank behind a split-conformal bound on residuals.


DelayPhaseMarginModel
The delay a loop’s phase margin can absorb, and the share a stated delay spends.


LidarSweepAgeModel
One spinning-lidar sweep’s motion distortion, and a forward sector’s age.


ObservationAgeModel
A camera observation’s age, stage by stage, from the exposure midpoint to dispatch.


RollingShutterSkewModel
Row timing and skew of a rolling-shutter camera on a moving base.


StereoDepthErrorModel
One-sigma stereo depth error against range, and where it spends each clearance.


ThermalExpansionModel
Length change of a uniformly heated member, alpha L dT.


TimingAttitudeErrorModel
Position errors from a timing error and an angle error, for a target at distance.


VisibilityRangeModel
Range at which fog with extinction beta drops a black target’s contrast to the threshold (Koschmieder).





engine.solvers.perception.ClockConversionModel()
A free-running clock’s drift between syncs, and the dispatch limit a conversion bound sets.
Drift accumulates as rate x interval; a producer refuses to dispatch an observation older than its budgeted age plus the conversion bound, whose own uncertainty is travel at speed.





Name
Description




solve
Convert clock drift and conversion uncertainty into age and travel budgets.





engine.solvers.perception.ClockConversionModel.solve(
    drift_rate,
    sync_interval,
    conversion_bound,
    observation_age,
    speed,
)
Convert clock drift and conversion uncertainty into age and travel budgets.











Name
Type
Description
Default




drift_rate
Quantity
Clock offset accumulation rate, such as microseconds per second.
required


sync_interval
Quantity
Nonnegative time between clock synchronizations.
required


conversion_bound
Quantity
Nonnegative timestamp-conversion uncertainty, in time units.
required


observation_age
Quantity
Nonnegative nominal observation-age budget, in time units.
required


speed
Quantity
Translation speed, convertible to meters per second.
required














Name
Type
Description





ClockConversionResult
Accumulated drift in microseconds, dispatch age limit in milliseconds, and travel associated with the conversion bound in millimeters.






Equation: drift_per_interval = drift_rate*sync_interval; dispatch_age_limit = observation_age+conversion_bound; bound_travel = speed*conversion_bound.
Assumptions: Constant drift rate and speed over the supplied interval. The conversion bound is an externally justified input, not estimated here.
Excludes: Oscillator-temperature variation, synchronization protocol failures, stochastic timestamp error, and an enforced dispatch policy.



Derivation: Integrate a constant offset rate over time, add an uncertainty allowance to the nominal age budget, and convert that time allowance to travel by multiplying by speed.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = ClockConversionModel().solve(Q_("10 us/s"), Q_("2 s"), Q_("1 ms"), Q_("5 ms"), Q_("1 m/s"))
>>> r.drift_per_interval == Q_("20 us") and r.bound_travel == Q_("1 mm")
True






engine.solvers.perception.ConformalInsetModel()
The calibration rank behind a split-conformal bound on residuals.
The bound is the ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest of n residuals, which exists only from n = ceil((1 - alpha) / alpha).





Name
Description




solve
Locate the finite-sample order statistic for a split-conformal bound.





engine.solvers.perception.ConformalInsetModel.solve(alpha, calibration_count)
Locate the finite-sample order statistic for a split-conformal bound.











Name
Type
Description
Default




alpha
float
Desired miscoverage fraction, strictly between zero and one.
required


calibration_count
int
Positive number of held-out calibration residuals; large enough for the requested order statistic to exist.
required














Name
Type
Description





ConformalInsetResult
Dimensionless miscoverage, calibration count, minimum count, one-based ascending rank, and one-based rank counted down from the largest residual. No residual values are inspected and no physical inset is calculated.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_rank : Finite-sample rank. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_min_count : Minimum sample count.



Equation: rank = ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)); min_count = ceil((1-alpha)/alpha); rank_from_top = n-rank+1.
Assumptions: Calibration and future examples are exchangeable and use the same fixed score. A finite observed rank must not exceed the calibration count.
Excludes: Distribution-shift protection, score construction, conditional coverage guarantees, and computation of the residual quantile itself.



Derivation: The split-conformal finite-sample rank uses the n+1 possible positions of a future exchangeable score. Requiring ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) <= n gives the minimum calibration-count expression. The rank itself is implemented by the referenced statistics helpers.



>>> r = ConformalInsetModel().solve(0.1, 19)
>>> r.rank + r.rank_from_top == r.calibration_count + 1
True






engine.solvers.perception.DelayPhaseMarginModel()
The delay a loop’s phase margin can absorb, and the share a stated delay spends.
A pure delay removes omega_c tau of phase at crossover, so the margin is gone at tau_max = PM / omega_c (calc_delay_phase_margin_ceiling).





Name
Description




solve
Compute the pure-delay budget implied by a phase margin.





engine.solvers.perception.DelayPhaseMarginModel.solve(
    phase_margin,
    crossover,
    delay,
)
Compute the pure-delay budget implied by a phase margin.











Name
Type
Description
Default




phase_margin
Quantity
Positive available phase margin, convertible to radians.
required


crossover
Quantity
Positive loop crossover angular frequency, in radians per second.
required


delay
Quantity
Nonnegative additional pure delay, in time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





DelayPhaseMarginResult
Phase margin in radians, crossover in hertz, delay and delay ceiling in milliseconds, and the dimensionless fraction of the ceiling consumed.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.control.calc_delay_phase_margin_ceiling : Pure-delay ceiling.



Equation: delay_ceiling = phase_margin/crossover, after expressing margin in radians and crossover in radians per second. share_used = delay/ceiling; crossover_frequency = crossover/(2*pi).
Assumptions: A fixed crossover and a pure transport-delay phase contribution. The margin refers to the loop before adding this delay.
Excludes: Changes to gain crossover, other plant dynamics, sampling and jitter distributions, and a complete closed-loop stability proof.



Derivation: The frequency response of a delay is exp(-j*omega*tau), whose phase is -omega*tau. Set that phase loss equal to the available phase margin.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = DelayPhaseMarginModel().solve(Q_("1 rad"), Q_("10 rad/s"), Q_("50 ms"))
>>> r.delay_ceiling == Q_("100 ms") and r.share_used == 0.5
True






engine.solvers.perception.LidarSweepAgeModel()
One spinning-lidar sweep’s motion distortion, and a forward sector’s age.
A sweep lasts one rotation, during which the base travels v T and turns omega T. A sector of width w at distance d is swept in T phi / 360 deg; streaming it as it arrives ages it by that sector time plus the sensor’s data latency and its time-sync bound, waiting for the full sweep by the whole rotation plus the same two terms.





Name
Description




solve
Compare full-sweep and sector-streaming observation ages.





engine.solvers.perception.LidarSweepAgeModel.solve(
    scan_rate,
    data_latency,
    sync_accuracy,
    sector_width,
    sector_distance,
    speed,
    yaw_rate,
    reference_age,
)
Compare full-sweep and sector-streaming observation ages.











Name
Type
Description
Default




scan_rate
Quantity
Positive rotational scan frequency, convertible to hertz.
required


data_latency
Quantity
Nonnegative sensor delivery latency, in time units.
required


sync_accuracy
Quantity
Nonnegative time-synchronization uncertainty bound.
required


sector_width
Quantity
Positive lateral width of the sector, in length units.
required


sector_distance
Quantity
Positive distance to the center of the sector.
required


speed
Quantity
Platform translation speed, convertible to meters per second.
required


yaw_rate
Quantity
Platform angular velocity, convertible to radians per second.
required


reference_age
Quantity
Nonnegative observation-age budget, in time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





LidarSweepAgeResult
Sweep and sector times and ages in milliseconds, travel in millimeters, rotation in milliradians, sector angle in degrees, and streamed-age slack. Negative slack means the supplied budget is exceeded.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_scan_sector_angle : Sector geometry.



Equation: T = 1/scan_rate; phi = 2*atan(sector_width/(2*sector_distance)); sector_time = T*phi/(2*pi). Streamed age adds data_latency and sync_accuracy to sector_time; full age adds those terms to T.
Assumptions: Uniform rotation, constant platform speed and yaw, and serial addition of the stated latency and synchronization bounds.
Excludes: Scan deskewing, nonuniform firing patterns, dropped returns, network-delay distributions, and object motion.



Derivation: A uniformly rotating scanner spends the angular fraction phi/(2*pi) of one revolution on the sector. Age and travel follow by adding serial intervals and integrating constant speed.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = LidarSweepAgeModel().solve(Q_("10 Hz"), Q_("1 ms"), Q_("1 ms"), Q_("1 m"), Q_("5 m"), Q_("1 m/s"), Q_("0 rad/s"), Q_("20 ms"))
>>> r.age_streamed < r.age_full and r.sweep_period == Q_("100 ms")
True






engine.solvers.perception.ObservationAgeModel()
A camera observation’s age, stage by stage, from the exposure midpoint to dispatch.
The capture epoch is the exposure midpoint, so the age starts at half the exposure, then adds readout, link transport, DMA and queueing, the image signal processor, the vision backbone, and dispatch. A stamp taken at DMA completion (arrival) misdates the frame by the age up to that stage; a trigger stamp at exposure start misdates it by half the exposure. Batching batch_frames successive frames holds the oldest n - 1 frame periods. Every interval is also priced as travel at speed.





Name
Description




solve
Accumulate observation age from exposure midpoint to dispatch.





engine.solvers.perception.ObservationAgeModel.solve(
    exposure,
    readout,
    transport,
    dma,
    isp,
    backbone,
    dispatch,
    frame_rate,
    speed,
    batch_frames=1,
)
Accumulate observation age from exposure midpoint to dispatch.











Name
Type
Description
Default




exposure
Quantity
Nonnegative exposure duration, in time units.
required


readout
Quantity
Nonnegative sensor readout duration, in time units.
required


transport
Quantity
Nonnegative link-transfer duration, in time units.
required


dma
Quantity
Nonnegative DMA and queue delay, in time units.
required


isp
Quantity
Nonnegative image-signal-processing duration, in time units.
required


backbone
Quantity
Nonnegative vision-model execution duration, in time units.
required


dispatch
Quantity
Nonnegative dispatch duration, in time units.
required


frame_rate
Quantity
Positive capture frequency, convertible to hertz.
required


speed
Quantity
Travel speed, convertible to meters per second.
required


batch_frames
int
Number of successive frames accumulated; at least one. The default one-frame batch adds no frame-collection wait.
1














Name
Type
Description





ObservationAgeResult
Stage and cumulative ages in milliseconds; travel in millimeters; dimensionless age and stage shares. These are timing accounts, not a prediction of perception accuracy.






Equation: age = exposure/2 + readout + transport + dma + isp + backbone + dispatch. The oldest frame in an n-frame batch waits (n-1)/frame_rate; distance traveled during any interval t is speed*t.
Assumptions: Stages execute serially with the supplied durations. Exposure midpoint represents capture time; frame arrivals are evenly spaced. Inputs must describe nonnegative intervals and a positive total age.
Excludes: Pipeline overlap, jitter distributions, variable frame spacing, object motion, and a collision-safety determination.



Derivation: Elapsed time along a serial path is the sum of its intervals. Changing the timestamp from the capture midpoint to arrival hides the elapsed capture/readout/transport/DMA intervals; batching adds arrival periods.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> durations = [Q_("2 ms")] * 7
>>> one = ObservationAgeModel().solve(*durations, Q_("10 Hz"), Q_("1 m/s"))
>>> two = ObservationAgeModel().solve(*durations, Q_("10 Hz"), Q_("1 m/s"), batch_frames=2)
>>> two.batched_age - one.age == Q_("100 ms")
True






engine.solvers.perception.RollingShutterSkewModel()
Row timing and skew of a rolling-shutter camera on a moving base.
Rows are read one after another over the readout time, so the last row sees the scene from v t_readout farther along, and a turn at omega shifts a target at range d sideways by d omega t_readout. Each row also blurs over its own exposure, v t_exp.





Name
Description




solve
Translate rolling-shutter readout time into motion skew.





engine.solvers.perception.RollingShutterSkewModel.solve(
    rows,
    readout,
    exposure,
    speed,
    yaw_rate,
    target_range,
    along_allowance,
    side_clearance,
)
Translate rolling-shutter readout time into motion skew.











Name
Type
Description
Default




rows
int
Positive number of uniformly timed sensor rows.
required


readout
Quantity
Nonnegative full-image readout time.
required


exposure
Quantity
Nonnegative per-row exposure duration.
required


speed
Quantity
Translational speed, convertible to meters per second.
required


yaw_rate
Quantity
Angular velocity, convertible to radians per second.
required


target_range
Quantity
Nonnegative distance to the target.
required


along_allowance
Quantity
Positive longitudinal error allowance, in length units.
required


side_clearance
Quantity
Positive lateral clearance used to normalize angular skew.
required














Name
Type
Description





RollingShutterSkewResult
Row interval in microseconds, exposure-midpoint lag in milliseconds, motion displacements in millimeters, and dimensionless allowance shares.






Equation: row_interval = readout/rows; longitudinal skew = speed*readout; lateral skew = target_range*yaw_rate*readout, with yaw in radians. Exposure travel is speed*exposure.
Assumptions: Constant translation and yaw during capture, uniform row timing, and small angular displacement. Allowances are supplied comparisons.
Excludes: Acceleration, lens distortion, rolling-shutter correction, scene-depth variation, and safety certification.



Derivation: Uniformly partition the readout interval among rows, integrate constant translational velocity over that interval, and apply the small-angle arc-length relation d*theta to yaw motion.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RollingShutterSkewModel().solve(100, Q_("10 ms"), Q_("2 ms"), Q_("1 m/s"), Q_("0 rad/s"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("20 mm"), Q_("20 mm"))
>>> r.skew == Q_("10 mm") and r.lateral_skew == Q_("0 mm")
True






engine.solvers.perception.StereoDepthErrorModel()
One-sigma stereo depth error against range, and where it spends each clearance.
sigma_z = z^2 sigma_d / (f b) grows with squared range; the range at which one sigma equals a clearance C is sqrt(C f b / sigma_d). Adding one sigma to a clearance kept along the viewing ray is the shortcut inset; an unmodeled baseline change db biases depth by z db / b.





Name
Description




solve
Propagate stereo disparity uncertainty into range-dependent depth error.





engine.solvers.perception.StereoDepthErrorModel.solve(
    baseline,
    focal_length_px,
    disparity_sigma_px,
    near_range,
    far_range,
    target_range,
    ray_clearance,
    loc_allowance,
    side_clearance,
    baseline_change,
    bias_range,
)
Propagate stereo disparity uncertainty into range-dependent depth error.











Name
Type
Description
Default




baseline
Quantity
Positive camera separation, in length units.
required


focal_length_px
float
Positive rectified-camera focal length, in pixels.
required


disparity_sigma_px
float
Positive disparity standard deviation, in pixels.
required


near_range
Quantity
Positive near comparison depth, in length units.
required


far_range
Quantity
Positive far comparison depth, in length units.
required


target_range
Quantity
Positive depth of the target whose uncertainty is reported.
required


ray_clearance
Quantity
Nonnegative clearance added to one standard deviation along the ray.
required


loc_allowance
Quantity
Positive localization allowance used to invert the uncertainty equation.
required


side_clearance
Quantity
Positive second error allowance used for range comparisons.
required


baseline_change
Quantity
Nonnegative magnitude of unmodeled baseline change.
required


bias_range
Quantity
Positive depth at which baseline-change bias is evaluated.
required














Name
Type
Description





StereoDepthErrorResult
One-sigma errors, clearance-plus-sigma insets, and baseline bias in millimeters; inverse-error ranges in meters; dimensionless growth ratios. One sigma is not a guaranteed containment interval.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_depth_sigma : Disparity propagation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_range_for_sigma : Inverse error relation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_baseline_bias : Baseline sensitivity.



Equation: sigma_z = z**2*sigma_d/(f*b); z_at_allowance = sqrt(allowance*f*b/sigma_d); baseline bias = bias_range*baseline_change/b. The near and far insets add ray_clearance to their respective sigma_z.
Assumptions: Rectified pinhole stereo, small disparity errors, fixed f and b, and the same disparity variance across all evaluated depths.
Excludes: Occlusions, matching outliers, lens/calibration covariance, correlated errors, and any claimed collision-risk probability.



Derivation: Differentiate z=f*b/disparity with respect to disparity to propagate one standard deviation; invert that expression for a chosen error allowance. Baseline enters linearly at fixed disparity.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = StereoDepthErrorModel().solve(Q_("0.1 m"), 1000, 1, Q_("1 m"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("1 m"), Q_("1 mm"), Q_("10 mm"), Q_("20 mm"), Q_("0 mm"), Q_("1 m"))
>>> r.sigma_far == 4 * r.sigma_near and r.baseline_bias == Q_("0 mm")
True






engine.solvers.perception.ThermalExpansionModel()
Length change of a uniformly heated member, alpha L dT.





Name
Description




solve
Calculate linear expansion of a uniformly heated member.





engine.solvers.perception.ThermalExpansionModel.solve(
    coefficient,
    length,
    temperature_rise,
)
Calculate linear expansion of a uniformly heated member.











Name
Type
Description
Default




coefficient
Quantity
Linear expansion coefficient, in inverse kelvin or inverse temperature difference units; treated as constant over the interval.
required


length
Quantity
Positive initial member length, in length units.
required


temperature_rise
Quantity
Signed temperature difference, in kelvin or delta-degrees Celsius; not an absolute Celsius temperature.
required














Name
Type
Description





ThermalExpansionResult
Signed length change in millimeters. Positive values denote expansion; negative values denote contraction under the supplied coefficient.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_thermal_expansion : Linear thermal expansion.



Equation: expansion = coefficient*length*temperature_rise.
Assumptions: Uniform temperature change, unconstrained expansion, constant linear coefficient, and small strain.
Excludes: Thermal gradients, anisotropy, mechanical restraint, temperature- dependent coefficients, stress, and buckling.



Derivation: The linear thermal-expansion coefficient is fractional length change per temperature change; multiplying it by initial length and the uniform temperature increment gives the first-order length change.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> a = ThermalExpansionModel().solve(Q_("1e-5 / K"), Q_("1 m"), Q_("10 K"))
>>> b = ThermalExpansionModel().solve(Q_("1e-5 / K"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("10 K"))
>>> b.expansion == 2 * a.expansion
True






engine.solvers.perception.TimingAttitudeErrorModel()
Position errors from a timing error and an angle error, for a target at distance.
A timestamp off by dt places the target v dt along the travel and, while turning at omega, misorients the view by omega dt, which at range is d omega dt sideways. An angle error theta moves the target d theta sideways (calc_lever_arm_error, small angle).





Name
Description




solve
Separate translation and angular displacement caused by timestamp error.





engine.solvers.perception.TimingAttitudeErrorModel.solve(
    speed,
    yaw_rate,
    distance,
    timing_error,
    angle_error,
    reference=None,
)
Separate translation and angular displacement caused by timestamp error.











Name
Type
Description
Default




speed
Quantity
Translation speed, convertible to meters per second.
required


yaw_rate
Quantity
Angular velocity, convertible to radians per second.
required


distance
Quantity
Nonnegative target range, in length units.
required


timing_error
Quantity
Signed timestamp offset, in time units.
required


angle_error
Quantity
Signed small orientation error, convertible to radians.
required


reference
Quantity
Positive length used to normalize the angle-induced displacement; omit to return no normalized share.
None














Name
Type
Description





TimingAttitudeErrorResult
Translation and lateral errors in millimeters, timestamp-induced orientation error in milliradians, and an optional dimensionless share.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_lever_arm_error : Small-angle displacement.



Equation: translation = speed*timing_error; misorientation = yaw_rate* timing_error; timing lateral error = distance*misorientation; independent angle error produces distance*angle_error.
Assumptions: Translation and yaw remain constant over the timestamp offset. Angular errors are small; signs of supplied errors are retained.
Excludes: Error covariance, sensor fusion, acceleration, and a combined probabilistic error bound.



Derivation: Integrate constant velocity and angular velocity over the time offset, then multiply each angular error in radians by its lever arm.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = TimingAttitudeErrorModel().solve(Q_("1 m/s"), Q_("0 rad/s"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("10 ms"), Q_("0 rad"))
>>> r.timing_travel == Q_("10 mm") and r.angle_lateral == Q_("0 mm")
True






engine.solvers.perception.VisibilityRangeModel()
Range at which fog with extinction beta drops a black target’s contrast to the threshold (Koschmieder).





Name
Description




solve
Find the distance at which atmospheric attenuation reaches a contrast threshold.





engine.solvers.perception.VisibilityRangeModel.solve(
    extinction,
    contrast_threshold,
)
Find the distance at which atmospheric attenuation reaches a contrast threshold.











Name
Type
Description
Default




extinction
Quantity
Positive homogeneous extinction coefficient, in inverse length units.
required


contrast_threshold
float
Detection contrast fraction, strictly between zero and one.
required














Name
Type
Description





VisibilityRangeResult
Modeled visibility range in meters for a black target against the assumed background. This is not a sensor detection guarantee.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_contrast_visibility_range : Contrast attenuation.



Equation: visibility_range = log(1/contrast_threshold)/extinction, from contrast(d) = exp(-extinction*d).
Assumptions: Homogeneous attenuation, unit initial contrast of a black target, and a fixed detection threshold supplied by the caller.
Excludes: Illumination variation, finite target size, sensor noise, scattering geometry, and learned-detector performance.



Derivation: Solve the exponential contrast-attenuation relation for distance at the chosen contrast threshold; the sensing helper documents the Koschmieder model underlying that relation.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> a = VisibilityRangeModel().solve(Q_("0.1 / m"), 0.1)
>>> b = VisibilityRangeModel().solve(Q_("0.2 / m"), 0.1)
>>> a.visibility_range == 2 * b.visibility_range
True

Accumulated drift in microseconds, dispatch age limit in milliseconds, and travel associated with the conversion bound in millimeters.






Equation: drift_per_interval = drift_rate*sync_interval; dispatch_age_limit = observation_age+conversion_bound; bound_travel = speed*conversion_bound.
Assumptions: Constant drift rate and speed over the supplied interval. The conversion bound is an externally justified input, not estimated here.

engine.solvers.perception.ConformalInsetModel()
The calibration rank behind a split-conformal bound on residuals.
The bound is the ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest of n residuals, which exists only from n = ceil((1 - alpha) / alpha).





Name
Description

Type

Default

float

required

int

required

Type
Description

Dimensionless miscoverage, calibration count, minimum count, one-based ascending rank, and one-based rank counted down from the largest residual. No residual values are inspected and no physical inset is calculated.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_rank : Finite-sample rank. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_min_count : Minimum sample count.



Equation: rank = ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)); min_count = ceil((1-alpha)/alpha); rank_from_top = n-rank+1.
Assumptions: Calibration and future examples are exchangeable and use the same fixed score. A finite observed rank must not exceed the calibration count.
Excludes: Distribution-shift protection, score construction, conditional coverage guarantees, and computation of the residual quantile itself.



Derivation: The split-conformal finite-sample rank uses the n+1 possible positions of a future exchangeable score. Requiring ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) <= n gives the minimum calibration-count expression. The rank itself is implemented by the referenced statistics helpers.



>>> r = ConformalInsetModel().solve(0.1, 19)
>>> r.rank + r.rank_from_top == r.calibration_count + 1
True

The delay a loop’s phase margin can absorb, and the share a stated delay spends.
A pure delay removes omega_c tau of phase at crossover, so the margin is gone at tau_max = PM / omega_c (calc_delay_phase_margin_ceiling).

A sweep lasts one rotation, during which the base travels v T and turns omega T. >>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_

engine.solvers.perception.ObservationAgeModel()
A camera observation’s age, stage by stage, from the exposure midpoint to dispatch.
The capture epoch is the exposure midpoint, so the age starts at half the exposure, then adds readout, link transport, DMA and queueing, the image signal processor, the vision backbone, and dispatch. A stamp taken at DMA completion (arrival) misdates the frame by the age up to that stage; a trigger stamp at exposure start misdates it by half the exposure. Batching batch_frames successive frames holds the oldest n - 1 frame periods. Every interval is also priced as travel at speed.





Name
Description




solve

    exposure,
    readout,
    transport,
    dma,
    isp,
    backbone,
    dispatch,
    frame_rate,
    speed,
    batch_frames=1,
)

1














Name
Type
Description





ObservationAgeResult
Stage and cumulative ages in milliseconds; travel in millimeters; dimensionless age and stage shares. These are timing accounts, not a prediction of perception accuracy.






Equation: age = exposure/2 + readout + transport + dma + isp + backbone + dispatch. The oldest frame in an n-frame batch waits (n-1)/frame_rate; distance traveled during any interval t is speed*t.
Assumptions: Stages execute serially with the supplied durations. Exposure midpoint represents capture time; frame arrivals are evenly spaced. Inputs must describe nonnegative intervals and a positive total age.
Excludes: Pipeline overlap, jitter distributions, variable frame spacing, object motion, and a collision-safety determination.



Derivation: Elapsed time along a serial path is the sum of its intervals. Changing the timestamp from the capture midpoint to arrival hides the elapsed capture/readout/transport/DMA intervals; batching adds arrival periods.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> durations = [Q_("2 ms")] * 7
>>> one = ObservationAgeModel().solve(*durations, Q_("10 Hz"), Q_("1 m/s"))
>>> two = ObservationAgeModel().solve(*durations, Q_("10 Hz"), Q_("1 m/s"), batch_frames=2)
>>> two.batched_age - one.age == Q_("100 ms")
True

Rows are read one after another over the readout time, so the last row sees the scene from v t_readout farther along, and a turn at omega shifts a target at range d sideways by d omega t_readout. Each row also blurs over its own exposure, v t_exp.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RollingShutterSkewModel().solve(100, Q_("10 ms"), Q_("2 ms"), Q_("1 m/s"), Q_("0 rad/s"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("20 mm"), Q_("20 mm"))
>>> r.skew == Q_("10 mm") and r.lateral_skew == Q_("0 mm")
True

mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_depth_sigma : Disparity propagation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_range_for_sigma : Inverse error relation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_baseline_bias : Baseline sensitivity.



Equation: sigma_z = z**2*sigma_d/(f*b); z_at_allowance = sqrt(allowance*f*b/sigma_d); baseline bias = bias_range*baseline_change/b. The near and far insets add ray_clearance to their respective sigma_z.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_

title: engine.solvers.recovery
text:
engine.solvers.recovery
Failure-recovery solvers: what the runtime does once an effect has failed (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated inputs: one bounded repair priced against unwinding and rebuilding to the same endpoint, the expected irreversible loss of a plan whose checks run before or after its pivot, an append-only loop run to its turn ceiling or stopped early, retries multiplied through nested layers, a capped dependency under one burst of blocking calls, a retry cohort synchronized or jittered, a cleanup graph against a reverse stack, a breaker window classified two ways, and the incidents a published table lists as sustained by retries. None models a particular framework, provider, or queueing burst beyond what it states.





Name
Description




BulkheadAdmissionModel
One burst of blocking calls to a stalled dependency, before any completes.


IrreversibleLossModel
Expected irreversible loss of a plan with its check after, or before, the pivot.


RepairBreakEvenModel
One bounded repair attempt against compensating and rebuilding to the same endpoint.


RetryAmplificationModel
Attempts one failing logical operation sends when each layer retries on its own allowance.


RetryJitterModel
A cohort of retries released together: all inside a burst window, or jittered.


UndetectedLoopModel
An append-only loop run to its turn ceiling, or stopped after an earlier turn.





engine.solvers.recovery.BulkheadAdmissionModel()
One burst of blocking calls to a stalled dependency, before any completes.
Uncapped, every call takes a worker until the pool is full. Capped, at most worker_cap occupy workers and queue_cap wait without one; the rest are rejected at admission, and the cap protects the remaining workers however long the stall lasts. Worker slots only: not CPU, storage, or remote jobs that outlive a timeout.





Name
Description




solve
Partition a burst among occupied, queued, and rejected calls.





engine.solvers.recovery.BulkheadAdmissionModel.solve(
    arrivals,
    workers,
    worker_cap,
    queue_cap,
)
Partition a burst among occupied, queued, and rejected calls.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrivals
int
Nonnegative burst arrival count.
required


workers
int
Positive total worker count.
required


worker_cap
int
Dependency worker cap between zero and workers.
required


queue_cap
int
Nonnegative waiting-queue capacity.
required














Name
Type
Description





BulkheadAdmissionResult
Occupied, queued, rejected, and protected-worker counts for the burst, together with the uncapped occupancy comparison.






Equation: occupied=min(arrivals,cap); queued=min(arrivals-occupied,queue_cap).
Assumptions: All arrivals precede completion and queued calls hold no worker.
Excludes: CPU load, remote jobs surviving timeouts, and service-time distributions.



Derivation: assign burst calls first to dependency worker slots, then to waiting slots, then reject the remainder. Subtract occupied workers from the whole pool to count protected workers. The comparison repeats this partition with the entire pool available and no waiting queue.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = BulkheadAdmissionModel().solve(10, 8, 3, 2)
>>> r.occupied + r.queued + r.rejected == 10
True






engine.solvers.recovery.IrreversibleLossModel()
Expected irreversible loss of a plan with its check after, or before, the pivot.
Without a check ahead of the pivot nothing recovers: L = P(bad) I. A check that catches a fraction v and reverts with fidelity rho leaves P(bad) v I (1 - rho) from caught changes and P(bad) (1 - v) I from missed ones, which sum to P(bad) I (1 - v rho). Raising v by one step dv removes P(bad) I rho dv.





Name
Description




solve
Split expected loss into caught and missed defects.

    defect_probability,
    consequence,
    catch_rate,
    revert_fidelity,
    attempt_cost,
    catch_step,
)
Split expected loss into caught and missed defects.











Name
Type
Description
Default

float
Defect probability in [0, 1].
required


consequence
Quantity
Positive consequence per defect, USD.
required


catch_rate
float
Check catch probability in [0, 1].
required


revert_fidelity
float
Fraction recovered after a caught defect, in [0, 1].
required


attempt_cost
Quantity
Positive per-attempt cost, USD.
required


catch_step
float
Nonnegative catch-rate increment; catch_rate + catch_step <= 1.
required














Name
Type
Description





IrreversibleLossResult
Caught and missed expected losses in USD, recovery benefit ratios, and marginal loss reduction for the supplied catch-rate increment.






Equation: L=p I(1-v rho); delta_L=p I rho delta_v.
Assumptions: Consequence and recovery fidelity are fixed conditional on a defect.
Excludes: Estimated detection accuracy, correlated harms, and risk certification.



Derivation: partition defective attempts into caught and missed events. Caught defects retain fraction 1 - revert_fidelity of their consequence; missed defects retain all of it. Summing the two mutually exclusive contributions gives defect_probability * consequence  (1 - catch_rate  revert_fidelity).



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = IrreversibleLossModel().solve(0.1, Q_(100,"USD"), 0.5, 0.5, Q_(1,"USD"), 0.1)
>>> r.loss_with_check < r.loss_without_check
True






engine.solvers.recovery.RepairBreakEvenModel()
One bounded repair attempt against compensating and rebuilding to the same endpoint.
The fallback costs the compensation and rebuild times and the rebuild’s model tokens; one repair costs its pre-output startup, its output at the decode rate, local validation, and its whole isolated request. If a failed attempt leaves the fallback unchanged, E[C] = C_repair + (1 - p) C_fallback and repair first pays when p > p* = C_repair / C_fallback, per axis.





Name
Description

    unwind_time,
    rebuild_time,
    rebuild_input,
    rebuild_output,
    repair_input,
    repair_output,
    startup_time,
    output_rate,
    validation_time,
    input_price,
    output_price,
    assumed_success,
)

Type
Description
Default

Nonnegative compensation time.
required


rebuild_time

required

int
Nonnegative rebuild input-token count.
required

required

required


repair_output
int
Nonnegative repair output-token count.
required


startup_time
Quantity
Nonnegative startup time.
required

required


validation_time

required


input_price

required


output_price
Quantity
Positive output price, USD per token.
required


assumed_success
float
Assumed repair success probability in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





RepairBreakEvenResult
Repair and fallback costs in USD and seconds, break-even success probabilities per axis, expected costs, and fractional savings.






Equation: E[C]=C_repair+(1-p)C_fallback; p_star=C_repair/C_fallback.
Assumptions: A failed repair leaves the same fallback available; costs are additive.
Excludes: Success-rate estimation, retries after repair, and correlated failures.



Derivation: a repair charge is paid on every trial, whereas fallback is paid only on the failure branch with probability 1 - assumed_success. Comparing this expected charge with unconditional fallback yields the repair-to-fallback cost ratio as the success threshold, independently for time and money.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RepairBreakEvenModel().solve(Q_(1,"s"), Q_(10,"s"), 100, 10, 10, 2, Q_(1,"s"), Q_(2,"token/s"), Q_(1,"s"), Q_(1,"USD/token"), Q_(1,"USD/token"), 0.9)
>>> r.repair_time < r.fallback_time
True






engine.solvers.recovery.RetryAmplificationModel()
Attempts one failing logical operation sends when each layer retries on its own allowance.
Every attempt of a layer drives a full set of attempts in the layer below, so a attempts per layer over L layers reach the dependency a^L times; one retry owner with the same allowance sends a (Brooker 2019).





Name
Description




solve
Count attempts amplified through nested retry layers.





engine.solvers.recovery.RetryAmplificationModel.solve(
    attempts_per_layer,
    layers,
)
Count attempts amplified through nested retry layers.











Name
Type
Description
Default




attempts_per_layer
int
Positive integer attempt allowance per layer.
required


layers
int
Nonnegative number of nested layers.
required














Name
Type
Description





RetryAmplificationResult
Attempt counts by depth, total layered attempts, and coordinated attempts; these are counts rather than latency predictions.






Equation: A_layered=a**L; A_coordinated=a.
Assumptions: Every attempt fails and consumes the full downstream allowance.
Excludes: Early success, backoff timing, and overlapping requests.



Derivation: every parent attempt invokes attempts_per_layer child attempts. Repeating this branching for layers levels multiplies the allowance once per level. A single retry owner invokes the dependency directly and therefore spends only one allowance.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RetryAmplificationModel().solve(2, 3)
>>> r.layered > r.coordinated
True






engine.solvers.recovery.RetryJitterModel()
A cohort of retries released together: all inside a burst window, or jittered.
Synchronized, the window average is N / w; each drawing its arrival uniformly over the span J, the expected rate is N / J and a window of length w expects N w / J arrivals. Expectations only: one window can still receive every retry, so only an admission rate limiter bounds the peak.





Name
Description




solve
Compare synchronized and uniformly jittered retry rates.





engine.solvers.recovery.RetryJitterModel.solve(
    retries,
    burst_window,
    jitter_span,
)
Compare synchronized and uniformly jittered retry rates.











Name
Type
Description
Default




retries
int
Nonnegative retry count.
required


burst_window
Quantity
Positive observation-window duration.
required


jitter_span
Quantity
Positive uniform-jitter span, at least the window duration.
required














Name
Type
Description





RetryJitterResult
Synchronized and jittered mean rates in inverse seconds, their ratio, and the expected count in the observation window.






Equation: rate_sync=N/w; rate_jitter=N/J; E[arrivals_in_window]=N w/J.
Assumptions: Each retry chooses an independent uniform arrival within the jitter span.
Excludes: A deterministic peak-rate guarantee or admission rate limiting.



Derivation: a uniform arrival has probability burst_window / jitter_span of falling in the observation window. Linearity of expectation multiplies that probability by retries. Dividing the cohort by its release interval gives each mean rate; this calculation does not bound a realized burst.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RetryJitterModel().solve(10, Q_(1,"s"), Q_(10,"s"))
>>> r.jittered_mean_rate < r.synchronized_rate
True






engine.solvers.recovery.UndetectedLoopModel()
An append-only loop run to its turn ceiling, or stopped after an earlier turn.
Each turn appends its output and an observation and resends the whole history, so h turns send h s0 + delta h (h - 1) / 2 input tokens (calc_append_only_context) and h k_out output tokens; every turn takes the same time. The avoided charge is gross: detector cost, false alarms, and cleanup are not debited.





Name
Description




solve
Account for an append-only loop stopped early.

    first_input,
    output_per_turn,
    observation_per_turn,
    turn_time,
    ceiling,
    stop_after,
    context_window,
    input_price,
    output_price,
)
Account for an append-only loop stopped early.











Name
Type
Description
Default




first_input
int
Positive initial prompt-token count.
required


output_per_turn
int
Nonnegative output tokens per turn.
required


observation_per_turn
int
Nonnegative observation tokens per turn.
required


turn_time
Quantity
Positive fixed duration per turn.
required


ceiling
int
Turn ceiling, integer at least two.
required


stop_after
int
Positive stop turn no larger than the ceiling.
required


context_window
int
Positive context capacity in tokens.
required


input_price
Quantity
Positive input price, USD per token.
required


output_price
Quantity
Positive output price, USD per token.
required














Name
Type
Description





UndetectedLoopResult
Input/output token accounting, costs in USD, durations in seconds, context-fit flag, and avoided gross spend from early stopping.






Equation: I(h)=h s0+delta h(h-1)/2; C(h)=I(h)p_in+h k_out p_out.
Assumptions: Each turn appends the same token counts and resends all history.
Excludes: Detector overhead, false alarms, cleanup, and prefix-cache discounts.



Derivation: prompt lengths form an arithmetic progression beginning with first_input and increasing by output_per_turn + observation_per_turn. Summing that progression prices all resent input; multiplying the fixed output count and fixed duration by turns gives output spend and elapsed time. The stopped trajectory truncates the same progression.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = UndetectedLoopModel().solve(10, 2, 3, Q_(1,"s"), 4, 2, 100, Q_(1,"USD/token"), Q_(1,"USD/token"))
>>> r.stop_cost < r.ceiling_cost
True

title: solvers.FailureTriageModel
text:
solvers.FailureTriageModel()
Failures that counterfactual probes remove below the weights, and the price of training on all of them.
runs x failure_rate failures; each probe removes its share (rounded to whole failures), and the rest survive every probe. Training on every failure for epochs epochs of sequence_tokens costs 6PD FLOPs, run on devices at peak_rate x utilization and billed per device-hour.





Name
Description




solve
Account for training work on all failures versus probe-surviving failures.





solvers.FailureTriageModel.solve(
    runs,
    failure_rate,
    probe_shares,
    parameters,
    sequence_tokens,
    epochs,
    devices,
    peak_rate,
    utilization,
    hourly_price,
)
Account for training work on all failures versus probe-surviving failures.











Name
Type
Description
Default




runs
int
Positive number of observed runs.
required


failure_rate
float
Failure fraction in (0, 1], yielding a positive rounded failure count.
required


probe_shares
Mapping[str, float]
Disjoint attributed fractions of all failures, nonnegative and summing to at most one.
required


parameters
Quantity
Model parameter count, convertible to param.
required


sequence_tokens
int
Positive training tokens per failed run.
required


epochs
int
Positive number of passes over the failure corpus.
required


devices
int
Positive number of identical training devices.
required


peak_rate
Quantity
Positive compute rate per device in flop/s.
required


utilization
float
Supplied sustained-compute fraction in (0, 1].
required


hourly_price
Quantity
Nonnegative price per device-hour, convertible to USD/hour.
required














Name
Type
Description





FailureTriageResult
Rounded failure counts; tokens and FLOPs; wall time in hours, device-hours, and costs in USD.






mlsysim.physics.transformer.calc_transformer_training_flops : Parameter-dominated training work per processed token.



Equation: F = round(runs*failure_rate); residual = F - round(F*sum(probe_shares)); training work = 6*parameters*F*sequence_tokens*epochs; time = work/(devices*peak_rate*utilization).
Assumptions: Probe categories are mutually exclusive. Each removed category and the sum are rounded separately, so their integer counts need not add exactly. The training FLOP convention excludes recomputation.
Excludes: Overlapping attribution, causal identification of probe effects, communication, memory feasibility, and optimizer overhead.



Derivation: corpus token counts feed the parameter-dominated training accounting in calc_transformer_training_flops; divide work by aggregate sustained rate and multiply device-hours by the caller-supplied price.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = FailureTriageModel().solve(100, 0.2, {"runtime": 0.5}, Q_("1000 param"), 10, 1, 1, Q_("1e9 flop/s"), 0.5, Q_("1 USD/hour"))
>>> result.residual_cost < result.cost
True

title: Robotics Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

Contact

ForceTailScenario: A contact force over trials trials with a benign mean_force and a p99_force tail, against site’s tripwire and structural limit.
HeadingDriftScenario: A persistent heading_offset at machine’s drive limit in site’s aisle: the angular error an open-loop replay scores, and where the closed loop spends the side clearance (y = v sin(eps) t).
StiffContactScenario: A stiff contact of stiffness (a linear spring, F = k x): the force a residual penetration commands, and the penetrations at site’s latch tripwire and limit.



Control

CycleBudgetScenario: Stage sub-budgets of one permission check against site’s declared WCET and deadline.
GravityBiasedJointStopScenario: One loaded arm joint at joint_speed braking with machine’s peak torque while gravity holds bias_fraction of that peak along (descending) or against (ascending) the motion.
HoldIntervalDriftScenario: Drift while a drive holds the last command for one period: travel at speed plus the half acceleration period^2 an independent acceleration bound allows.
TorqueHalfSpaceProjectionScenario: A torque proposal against one barrier half-space normal . u <= bound: the least-change projection (calc_cbf_qp_orthogonal_projection) against a per-axis clamp.



Demonstrations

ContactGridScenario: A contact task binned by contact angle and normal force, and the cells each archive occupies.
CorrelatedLogScenario: duration of records logged at rate whose adjacent records have lag-one correlation lag1_correlation: how few independent samples the record count holds.
DemonstrationCampaignScenario: Scheduled sessions of attempt-and-reset cycles: demonstrations kept per session, the campaign that keeps target_kept of them, and the wear it puts on a gear and a cable.
GripperTransferScenario: A normalized gripper command from a donor gripper replayed on a target with a shorter stroke and a lower continuous force rating, against a part of part_width.
ImitationBoundScenario: Worst-case imitation cost over one episode at control_rate with per-step error per_step_error: open loop, behavioral cloning, and aggregation with recoverability u.
PairingLagScenario: An observation paired with an action lag later, against a clearance, at a transit speed and at site’s guarded and fast latch approaches.
ScenarioTableCoverageScenario: A scenario table of offsets by speeds joined against an archive demonstrated within logged_offset at demonstrated_speed, plus recovery collections at added_offsets.
StateGridScenario: A state space of state_components axes cut into bins per axis, against the records fleet robots log at log_rate for duration.
TeleopIngestionScenario: Raw telemetry of one teleoperated session on machine: its navigation and wrist cameras, external_cameras RGB-D cameras, and the kinematic record at the permission tick.
TeleopLoopScenario: One teleoperated correction: display, human, command transport, and mechanical response.



Diagnostics

DiagnosticCoverageScenario: Fault-rate strata (FIT) to be left at most target FIT unmitigated, shown at confidence.
ExponentialRareEventScenario: An exponential delay of mean that fails past the delay spare of budget (or threshold).
OnsetTrialScenario: A stopping trace that begins braking at onset after the reference event of oracle.
RailHoldUpScenario: site.machine’s backed permission rail, its feed lost during the longest admitted stop.



Estimation

BeliefExpiryScenario: A belief with initial error, growth law, and task tolerance; optionally admitted at use_age under age_bound.
ClearanceQueryScenario: Sphere-hull clearance queries on site.machine’s permission controller, and a snapshot of the stopping corridor.
EncoderRateScenario: An encoder of flop_per_frame on every site.machine navigation frame, against the host SoC’s dense FP16 peak.
EpochGapScenario: Named acquisition epochs in one cycle; the pair to fuse is projected across its gap at speed.
EstimatorConsistencyScenario: A qualification campaign of runs scalar estimates, and single-update gates against fusion’s misdated update.
FreeSpaceExpiryScenario: site’s rack end: free space ahead (clear distance) and abreast (side clearance) eroding at the walking speed.
FrozenTransformScenario: site’s conveyor object tracked by a camera lost at loss_time; its last transform republished every republish_period.
HostMapSizingScenario: A workcell of extent mapped at pitch: dense grid against a hashed band of band_half_width around surface_area.
InertialCoastScenario: site.machine’s IMU coasting duration without a fix, seen at the rack-end distance.
OdometryDriftScenario: A square-path odometry benchmark’s return errors, priced against site’s localization bound at its aisle speed and length.
RangeFusionScenario: The range to site’s rack-end upright, predicted over one lidar sweep and updated by the lidar, then stereo; the stereo update misdated by age’s arrival stamp at speed.
RaymarchTrafficScenario: One depth stream ray-marched into a map on site.machine’s host SoC.
ReplayBufferScenario: A rewind buffer at site.machine’s IMU rate reaching back one observation age.
SensorBiasDriftScenario: A steady reading whose sensor bias drifts at drift_rate for span, while the estimator reports reported_sigma.
SkewedRecordsScenario: Two records skew apart, compared at site: the base at its drive limit and a person at the walking speed close on each other.
StaleTransformScenario: belief’s cached camera edge composed with the current wrist pose, one site.machine wrist-camera frame old.



Grounding

ConfidenceRegionScenario: A Gaussian position estimate with principal standard deviations sigmas: its coverage region against site’s grasp tolerance.
DynamicReachScenario: A target target_distance from the gripper at cadence.machine’s TCP speed ceiling, against the cadence scenario’s evidence windows.
ForwardOccupancyScenario: A coworker’s forward occupancy set at cadence.site’s design approach speed, screened over the cadence scenario’s evidence windows and over a forecast horizon, against the aisle.
GoalSetMembershipScenario: Terminal TCP offsets along one axis tested against a goal set whose semi-axes all equal site’s grasp tolerance: the normalized ellipsoidal distance, inside when at most one.
IntentCadenceScenario: site’s conveyor target proposed by machine’s intent model: evidence horizons against the model’s cadence, a host stall of stall, and the stop onset after expiry.
IntentLeaseExpiryScenario: The intent lease for the cadence scenario’s target: its evidence horizons, an administrative_lease, and the stopping deadline from clearance at the TCP speed ceiling, with the arm’s credible deceleration from its handbook worst-case stop.
ReferentSetScenario: Raw per-box scores of retained candidates screened by a conformal threshold calibrated on calibration_count scenes at miss rate alpha, whose calibration score is threshold_score.



Learning

ContactDeadlineScenario: A constant-speed drive into site’s latch plate: when the force ramp k v t reaches the tripwire and the limit, when braking can begin, and the time left, at both approaches.
DiscountHorizonScenario: One rollout of decisions step apart under discount discount: how far the return reaches, in decisions and in seconds, and the discount that keeps retained_weight of the final reward at the first decision.
ForceRiseGapScenario: An illustrative linear drive regulating target_force against a surface, in simulation and on hardware, with one stated discrepancy in each reality-gap channel: dynamics (force-rise rate and drive delay), timing (p99 actuation delay against the simulator’s), sensing (range bias and dropout), and appearance (pixel difference hiding a contact-patch shift).
IterativeDecoderBudgetScenario: machine’s one-pass chunk decoder against an iterative head that encodes once and runs denoising_steps dependent evaluations in denoising_latency, and a flow_steps head at the same cost per evaluation, on the setpoint step and the renewal period with renewal_jitter held free.
OnRobotFineTuneScenario: interaction_steps setpoints step apart collected on the machine to absorb a plate_offset, of which exceed_fraction cross the contact tripwire.
ParallelSimRunScenario: A GPU-parallel on-policy run: robots environments each stepping steps_per_update times per update for updates updates within training_time, at policy_rate.
SoftContactExploitScenario: machine’s arm coasting into site’s latch plate at the fast approach: the peak force a penalty spring that lets the gripper sink penalty_penetration reports, the peak the real plate imposes on a rigid arm, and the arm stiffness at which the series chain reaches the limit. The moving mass is the arm’s effective contact mass without its payload capacity (the gripper holds no object at the door).
TrialCampaignScenario: trials hardware trials of rollout each, decisions decision_step apart, with automated and manual resets, on one machine and on a farm; what a demonstration-seeded seeded_budget allows; and the same trials in simulator at its published throughput.



Perception

ClockConversionScenario: A sensor clock drifting at drift_rate between syncs every sync_interval, converted under site’s bound.
ConformalInsetScenario: A split-conformal bound at miss rate alpha from calibration_count residuals.
DelayPhaseMarginScenario: A loop with phase_margin at crossover, closed through a pure delay.
LidarSweepAgeScenario: site.machine’s spinning lidar at speed: sweep motion and the age of the aisle sector at the rack end.
ObservationAgeScenario: site.machine’s navigation-camera observation age at speed, with a batch_frames comparison.
RollingShutterScenario: site.machine’s rolling-shutter navigation camera at speed, turning at the site’s yaw rate toward the rack end.
StereoDepthErrorScenario: A stereo rig’s depth error at two ranges and at site’s rack end, against the site’s clearances.
ThermalExpansionScenario: A member of length and expansion coefficient warmed by temperature_rise.
TimingAttitudeErrorScenario: A timing_error and an angle_error on a target at distance, priced against reference.
VisibilityRangeScenario: Fog of extinction coefficient extinction against a contrast threshold.



Placement

RailDroopScenario: A current step delta_i in rise_time through a package’s inductance and resistance, and the alpha-power gate-delay stretch at the drooped rail.
SharedDramReadScenario: site’s permission tick placed on the machine’s application SoC, its snapshot read queued behind backlogs on the shared DRAM controller.
StallShareScenario: site’s unloaded permission tick with a share of it slowed slowdown times.
ThermalThrottleScenario: site’s permission tick on a cluster whose clock a thermal governor halves.
TickTraceScenario: Percentiles of a permission tick’s execution time over a trace of ticks periods, cold and warm, against site’s declared WCET and deadline.



Planning

ChunkReplacementScenario: Replacing machine’s admitted chunk at site: capture-to-admission latency against the renewal period and the chunk lease, with an interference_tail on the inference pass.
DynamicWindowScenario: machine’s base over one chunk renewal at site: its dynamic window and the classical admissible speed against the site’s clear distance and credible deceleration.
HandoffExposureScenario: A replanner at replan_rate over mission_time whose handoffs are each late with late_probability, held to mission_budget for the whole mission.
JerkLimitedStopScenario: A machine at speed that stops along an S-curve at deceleration after delay.
SeamBridgeScenario: A velocity_gap at a chunk seam on joint, closed in one tick or by a quintic bridge over bridge_duration, against machine’s arm torque-rate limit. loaded_inertia (optional) prices the one-tick step with the payload’s inertia added.
ShoulderSwingScenario: machine’s shoulder holding its rated payload at full planar reach, with joint’s reflected rotor inertia, swinging swing rest to rest inside its datasheet limits.
SpillLimitedStopScenario: The free_stop scenario’s machine carrying an open container of inner_radius filled freeboard below the rim: the deceleration the liquid allows, that stop, and the carry speed.
StaleAnchorScenario: A joint of machine’s arm turning at joint_speed while a replacement takes delay, anchored at the pose sampled at the request; the lever arm is the planar reach.
TrajectoryDeadlinesScenario: A trajectory record for machine’s arm at site: a replacement requested at request_delay with a latency_target and schedule_slack, a blend deadline, the commit instant when stop (a JerkLimitedStopScenario) must begin, and a late_wait.
TwoLinkJointRateScenario: machine’s arm as a planar two-link chain at elbow_angle: the joint rates its TCP speed limit asks in the weakest direction, exact and with damped least squares at damping.



Plant

BrakingCeilingsScenario: The ceilings on site’s credible deceleration for its loaded machine at the drive limit.
ContinuousDeratingScenario: A catalog continuous rating carried to a hotter ambient and a worse heat path.
DriveBusScenario: site.machine’s shared drive bus: a coincident load step, and a stop from the drive limit into it.
FreshnessProfileScenario: A target moving at site’s conveyor speed, grasped through a staged capture-to-onset pipeline.
GearRatioCostScenario: motor in joint holding output_torque through each of ratios.
GearedRotorScenario: A rotor seen through a gear_ratio reduction, beside a link of load_inertia.
HubDriveElectricalScenario: Current rise and phase-short braking of site.machine’s hub drives on a depleted bus.
StallDeratingScenario: joint holding hold_torque at stall with copper’s resistance rising with temperature.
ThermalBurstScenario: A burst_factor times rated-current burst in joint, first-order lumped, fixed resistance.
ThrottledStageScenario: site’s vision backbone at clock_ratio of full clock, paid as travel at speed.
ZeroFailureScenario: trials failure-free trials, bounded at one-sided confidence.



Proposers

DecoderFamiliesScenario: One fresh machine.chunk_horizon-step chunk from backbone, per decoder family.
EvidenceHorizonScenario: site’s conveyor target tracked by machine’s chunk policy: evidence horizon against renewal.
KvHistoryScenario: Key-value cache for history_window of retained context at history_rate beside machine’s weights.
ProposerTrafficScenario: machine’s intent model and chunk policy sharing its memory bus (weight traffic only).
RateTargetScenario: evaluation held against a target_rate: one fresh evaluation per period, not pipelined.
VlaEvaluationScenario: One fresh evaluation of machine’s intent model on its application processor.
VlaTokenBudgetScenario: Tokens a VLA backbone reads from views square camera frames, and their memory per token.
WeightOnlyQuantizationScenario: One backbone priced at several weight formats against measurements of the same formats.



Realtime

CanFdBusScenario: num_axes servo axes on one CAN FD bus, frames_per_axis frames each per cycle.
EtherCatCycleScenario: num_axes drives on one EtherCAT chain, bytes_per_axis of process data each per cycle.
LeaseBudgetScenario: site.machine’s chunk lease at speed: its stopping-budget cost and the lease rule’s bounds.
PhaseLagBudgetScenario: A loop with crossover crossover sampled every sample_period, with compute and transport delays.
ResponseTimeScenario: site’s permission check as a periodic task: R = C + B + I against its deadline.



Site Limits

LatchSeriesSpringScenario: A series spring sized so machine’s arm stays under site’s declared latch floor.
PackagingCellScenario: A packaging cell’s carriage that must stop before a fixed stop line.
RestrictedTransitScenario: site’s aisle leg at restricted_speed against its normal aisle speed.
ShieldCoverageBillScenario: A fleet’s zero-event proposal log and a shield’s tested coverage against a hazard target.



Stopping

SpeedStepScenario: Raising the speed setpoint from base to raised (two stopping budgets at one deceleration).
StoppingBudgetScenario: A machine at speed that must stop: travel during delay, then braking at deceleration.
TractionLossScenario: Floor friction falls from mu_before to mu_after under a machine that assumes deceleration.
TravelDuringLatencyScenario: Distance a vehicle at speed covers during latency; optionally a remote-path delay range.



Supervision

BrakingBlendScenario: A bumpless transfer into braking on a site’s base at speed, and an arm joint’s blend.
CommandAuthenticationScenario: Remote commands authenticated on a machine’s permission processor, priced against a takeover budget.
DecisionChainScenario: links independently kept decision records behind one admitted action, each retrievable with probability p; the whole chain resolves with p^links for each p in link_probabilities.
DetectionShortfallScenario: site.machine at speed with a stop sized for a group detected in reference of frames, met by groups detected less often; misses allowed in every frame with probability all_miss_probability, frames independent.
EventRetentionScenario: Event-triggered retention: pre_trigger before and post_trigger after each of events_per_day events, against keeping the whole operating_day.
ExposureConcentrationScenario: encounter_share of a site’s machine-person encounters fall on user_share of its people: their per-person exposure against the site average, and everyone else’s.
OversightTimeScenario: A person asked to act through budget (a TakeoverBudgetScenario) against the time the hazard at its site leaves: the clear distance at the request speed.
SubgroupSampleScenario: An evaluation set of total people with a group of small_share, both detected at recall: exact intervals for each group, and the people per group a two-sided test at significance with power needs to tell rate_a from rate_b.
SupervisorQueueScenario: One remote assistant serving machines, each asking for help at request_rate, each request holding the assistant for service_time; utilization_cap sizes the largest fleet.
TakeoverBudgetScenario: A machine at speed at a site asks a person to take over within takeover.
TakeoverCeilingLadderScenario: One takeover budget per sourced human response, each plus the same console transport.

title: DiurnalLendingScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A fleet split between a serving reservation and a training base, static against lent.
The reservation is the forecast serving peak plus surge_buffer. Lending gives training whatever the reservation holds above average demand plus the buffer; the GPUs left after the reservation and the training base are maintenance headroom.


Equation: lent devices = serving reservation - average demand - surge buffer; dynamic active = static active + lent.
Assumptions: Demand and reservation counts describe one common fleet and the average lent capacity can be reclaimed.
Excludes: A time-series demand simulation, reclaim delay, and preemption losses.



Derivation: lent devices = serving reservation - average demand - surge buffer; dynamic active = static active + lent. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.DiurnalServingLending1K
>>> round(float(case.peak_demand), 3)
283.0

title: FleetMfuScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Program goodput (MFU) of a training step on one node and on a fleet of fleet_devices.
Useful work per step is the model’s training arithmetic for the tokens in the step (6 x parameters x tokens); MFU divides it by every device’s peak over the measured step time. Their ratio is the scaling efficiency measured from the node.


Equation: MFU = useful training FLOPs / (device count * peak FLOP/s * step time); scaling ratio = fleet MFU / node MFU.
Assumptions: Supplied step times are comparable and training work follows the parameter-dominated helper without full recomputation.
Excludes: Predicting step latency, identifying causes of scaling loss, and correcting measurement uncertainty.



Derivation: mFU = useful training FLOPs / (device count * peak FLOP/s * step time); scaling ratio = fleet MFU / node MFU. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.Llama2_70BFleetMfu128
>>> round(float(case.node_useful_work.to('flop').magnitude), 3)
925680000000000.0

engine.scenario_types.FleetMfuScenario.fleet_peak_work
Fleet peak FLOPs over the supplied fleet step duration, the MFU denominator.
Equation: return fleet_devices * hardware.compute.peak_flops * fleet_step_time.

Equation: return (fleet_useful_work / fleet_peak_work).to('').magnitude.

Fleet MFU divided by node MFU, a dimensionless per-device scaling ratio.
Equation: return fleet_mfu / node_mfu.

Fleet step duration minus node step duration, in milliseconds.

physics.robotics.perception.calc_3dgs_memory_footprint(
    num_gaussians,
    bytes_per_gaussian=56,
)
Count Gaussian-state storage under an explicit packing.











Name
Type
Description
Default




num_gaussians
int
Positive count of Gaussian state records.
required


bytes_per_gaussian
int
Positive bytes per record; default 56 is an assumed packing, not a universal 3DGS layout.
56









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Packed state storage in bytes.






Equation: memory = num_gaussians * bytes_per_gaussian.
Assumptions: Each record uses the same caller-specified packing.
Excludes: Optimizer state, allocator overhead, renderer workspaces, and additional harmonic coefficients.
Equation: Memory = K_gaussians * bytes_per_gaussian



Derivation: Count records and multiply by storage per record; the packing is an input convention.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_3dgs_memory_footprint
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> small = calc_3dgs_memory_footprint(10)
>>> large = calc_3dgs_memory_footprint(20)
>>> assert large == 2 * small




physics.robotics.perception.calc_free_space_expiry(
    free_depth,
    loc_bound,
    protective_clearance,
    approach_speed,
)
Compute a free-space claim’s erosion horizon.











Name
Type
Description
Default




free_depth
Quantity
Observed free depth in length units.
required


loc_bound
Quantity
Nonnegative localization allowance in length units.
required


protective_clearance
Quantity
Nonnegative clearance reserved before an approaching object reaches the task region.
required


approach_speed
Quantity
Positive assumed approach speed in length / time; supplied by the caller.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Expiry time in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: expiry = max(free_depth - loc_bound - protective_clearance, 0) / approach_speed.
Assumptions: An unseen object enters from the free-space boundary at a bounded constant speed.
Excludes: Occlusion geometry beyond a scalar depth, braking, speed-bound validation, and standards compliance.
Equation: T_inv = max(0, (d_free - delta_loc - delta_margin) / v_h)
The free region erodes from its unobserved boundary at the approach speed v_h; localization error delta_loc and the protective clearance delta_margin are spent up front. It is calc_linear_invalidation_horizon with E_0 = delta_loc, r = v_h, and E_max = d_free - delta_margin.
Source: linear invalidation horizon applied to occluded free space; the walking-speed bound v_h is ISO 13855’s K (1.6 m/s).



Derivation: Apply the linear invalidation horizon with initial_error = loc_bound and error_limit = free_depth - protective_clearance.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_free_space_expiry
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_free_space_expiry(3 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second)
>>> assert h == 1 * ureg.second




physics.robotics.perception.calc_linear_invalidation_horizon(
    initial_error,
    error_growth_rate,
    error_limit,
)
Find the first passage of a linearly growing error allowance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




initial_error
Quantity
Initial error allowance in length units.
required


error_growth_rate
Quantity
Positive error-growth rate in length / time.
required


error_limit
Quantity
Allowed error in length units; a spent limit returns zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Invalidation horizon in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: horizon = max(error_limit - initial_error, 0) / error_growth_rate.
Assumptions: Monotone constant-rate growth of a scalar error allowance.
Excludes: Acceleration, new evidence, stopping capability, and confidence calibration.
Equation: E(dt) = E_0 + r * dt ; T_inv = max(0, (E_max - E_0) / r)
A zero result means the belief never supported the task: its initial error already consumes the tolerance. Unlike calc_target_evidence_horizon this does not raise when E_0 >= E_max; it floors the deadline at zero.
Source: first-passage time of a linear error bound (definition of the invalidation horizon, T_inv = inf{dt >= 0 : E(dt) >= E_max}); the reachable-set lineage for occluded free space is Orzechowski, Meyer, and Lauer 2018 (IEEE ITSC).



Derivation: Set a linear error envelope equal to the limit; clamp past crossings to time zero.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_linear_invalidation_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_linear_invalidation_horizon(2 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second, 1 * ureg.meter)
>>> assert h.magnitude == 0




physics.robotics.perception.calc_octree_depth(map_edge, pitch)
Count halvings from a map edge to a target voxel edge.











Name
Type
Description
Default




map_edge
Quantity
Positive cubic map edge; the intended hierarchy has map_edge >= pitch.
required


pitch
Quantity
Positive target leaf edge in the same length dimension.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Ceiling of the base-two edge ratio; can be negative for out-of-regime pitch > map_edge.






Equation: depth = ceil(log2(map_edge / pitch)).
Assumptions: Each level halves an edge and a query descends the full hierarchy.
Excludes: Allocation sparsity, early termination, memory latency, and automatic clamping of out-of-regime input.
Equation: depth = ceil(log2(L / r))
Each level is one dependent read in a point query.
Source: Hornung et al., “OctoMap,” Autonomous Robots 34(3), 2013, Sec. III.



Derivation: After d binary subdivisions the edge is map_edge/2**d; choose the least integer d attaining pitch.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_octree_depth
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> assert calc_octree_depth(8 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter) == 3




physics.robotics.perception.calc_spatial_information_age_displacement(
    velocity,
    information_age,
)
Compute displacement during a perception delay.











Name
Type
Description
Default




velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative constant translational speed in length / time.
required


information_age
Quantity
Positive sensor-to-use age in time units.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Displacement in meters.






Equation: displacement = velocity * information_age.
Assumptions: The supplied speed remains constant over the age interval.
Excludes: Acceleration, object motion not included in velocity, and collision assessment.
Equation: Delta_x = v * tau_age
Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.1. Physical AI perception pipeline waterfall (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, IPC).



Derivation: Integrate constant velocity over the elapsed perception age.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_spatial_information_age_displacement
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> distance = calc_spatial_information_age_displacement(1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second, 1 * ureg.second)
>>> assert distance == 1 * ureg.meter




physics.robotics.perception.calc_sphere_scan_cells(reach, pitch)
Estimate voxel reads from a spherical query volume.











Name
Type
Description
Default




reach
Quantity
Positive sphere radius including any clearance allowance.
required


pitch
Quantity
Positive cubic voxel edge length.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless continuum estimate of cells, not an integer enumeration.






Equation: cells = (4*pi/3) * (reach / pitch)**3.
Assumptions: A dense read of every voxel within the spherical volume.
Excludes: Boundary-cell rounding, early exits, spatial indexes, and clearance certification.
Equation: N = (4/3) pi (reach / r)^3
reach is the sphere radius plus the protective clearance; every cell within it must be read, because an occupancy cell answers only whether that one cell is occupied.
Source: volume of a sphere in units of the voxel volume r^3.



Derivation: Divide sphere volume by cubic voxel volume.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_sphere_scan_cells
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> small = calc_sphere_scan_cells(1 * ureg.meter, 0.1 * ureg.meter)
>>> large = calc_sphere_scan_cells(2 * ureg.meter, 0.1 * ureg.meter)
>>> assert large == 8 * small




physics.robotics.perception.calc_target_evidence_horizon(
    tolerance_radius,
    sensor_noise,
    drift_velocity,
)
Find when constant target drift consumes an error margin.











Name
Type
Description
Default




tolerance_radius
Quantity
Positive spatial tolerance in length units.
required


sensor_noise
Quantity
Positive initial error allowance below tolerance_radius; a quantile is not a hard bound.
required


drift_velocity
Quantity
Positive drift-speed allowance in length / time.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Target-evidence validity horizon in milliseconds.






Equation: horizon = (tolerance_radius - sensor_noise) / drift_velocity.
Assumptions: An initial scalar error plus constant bounded drift; interpretation follows the supplied allowances.
Excludes: Braking, fallback feasibility, clearance checks, and safety certification.
This is not a stopping-time or stopping-distance bound. Motion admission also needs current clearance, total pre-brake delay, achievable deceleration, and a feasible fallback after this evidence expires.
Equation: tau = (r_tol - e_0) / v_drift



Derivation: Solve initial error + drift*time = tolerance for time.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_target_evidence_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_target_evidence_horizon(2 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second)
>>> assert h == 1 * ureg.second
