    num_cameras,
    rgb_width,
    rgb_height,
    rgb_fps,
    rgb_bytes_per_pixel=3,
    depth_width=0,
    depth_height=0,
    depth_fps=0.0,
    depth_bytes_per_pixel=2,
    kinematics_bytes_per_sec=None,
    tactile_bytes_per_sec=None,
)
Count uncompressed teleoperation traffic and hourly storage.











Name
Type
Description
Default




num_cameras
int
Positive count of identical camera streams.
required


rgb_width
int
Positive RGB image width in pixels.
required


rgb_height
int
Positive RGB image height in pixels.
required


rgb_fps
float
Positive RGB frame frequency in frames per second.
required


rgb_bytes_per_pixel
int
Positive RGB bytes per pixel; default 3.
3


depth_width
int
Depth width in pixels; default zero disables depth.
0


depth_height
int
Depth height in pixels; default zero disables depth.
0


depth_fps
float
Depth frames per second; depth is enabled only when width, height, and frequency are positive.
0.0


depth_bytes_per_pixel
int
Positive depth bytes per pixel; default 2.
2


kinematics_bytes_per_sec
Quantity
Nonnegative kinematics bandwidth in bytes / time; None means zero.
None


tactile_bytes_per_sec
Quantity
Nonnegative tactile bandwidth in bytes / time; None means zero.
None














Name
Type
Description





dict
RGB, depth, vision, kinematics, tactile, and total bandwidth in MB/s; storage_per_hour in TB.






Equation: camera bandwidth = cameras*width*height*bytes_per_pixel*fps; total = RGB + depth + kinematics + tactile; hourly storage = total*3600 seconds.
Assumptions: Identical continuous camera streams and uncompressed fixed-size payloads.
Excludes: Compression, transport headers, indexes, replication, and storage write amplification.
Equation: BW_rgb = num_cameras * (W_rgb * H_rgb * Bpp_rgb) * FPS_rgb BW_depth = num_cameras * (W_depth * H_depth * Bpp_depth) * FPS_depth BW_kinematics = bytes_per_sec_kinematics BW_tactile = bytes_per_sec_tactile BW_total = BW_rgb + BW_depth + BW_kinematics + BW_tactile Storage_1hr = BW_total * 3600 s



Derivation: Multiply pixels per frame by bytes per pixel and frames per second, sum independent streams, and integrate over one hour.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_teleop_ingestion_budget
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> budget = calc_teleop_ingestion_budget(1, 10, 10, 1)
>>> assert budget["bw_depth"].magnitude == 0
>>> assert budget["storage_per_hour"] == (budget["bw_total"] * ureg.hour).to("terabyte")




physics.robotics.perception.calc_tracked_evidence_horizon(
    tolerance_radius,
    initial_error,
    slip_acceleration,
)
Find when residual acceleration consumes a tracked error margin.











Name
Type
Description
Default




tolerance_radius
Quantity
Positive spatial tolerance in length units.
required


initial_error
Quantity
Nonnegative initial error below tolerance_radius.
required


slip_acceleration
Quantity
Positive residual relative acceleration in length / time**2.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Tracked-evidence horizon in milliseconds.






Equation: horizon = sqrt(2*(tolerance_radius - initial_error)/slip_acceleration).
Assumptions: Tracking removes initial relative velocity; residual acceleration is bounded by the input.
Excludes: Velocity-estimation error, braking, and proof of an acceleration bound.
A tracker that follows a moving target removes its steady velocity, so the remaining error growth comes from a bounded residual acceleration a_slip. A segment executed open-loop for a time T then drifts by a_slip T^2 / 2; setting that drift equal to the error margin r_tol - e_0 gives
Equation: tau_ev = sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip)
This is the constant-acceleration counterpart of calc_target_evidence_horizon (constant drift velocity, a_slip = 0). Like that function it is not a stopping-time bound.
Source: first-passage time of a constant-acceleration displacement (d = a T^2 / 2, solved for T at d = r_tol - e_0); kinematics, derived here.



Derivation: Integrate constant acceleration from zero residual velocity, then solve displacement = remaining margin.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_tracked_evidence_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_tracked_evidence_horizon(2 * ureg.meter, 0 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2)
>>> assert h == 2 * ureg.second

physics.robotics.perception.calc_free_space_expiry(
    free_depth,
    loc_bound,
    protective_clearance,
    approach_speed,
)
Compute a free-space claim’s erosion horizon.











Name
Type
Description
Default




free_depth
Quantity
Observed free depth in length units.
required


loc_bound
Quantity
Nonnegative localization allowance in length units.
required


protective_clearance
Quantity
Nonnegative clearance reserved before an approaching object reaches the task region.
required


approach_speed
Quantity
Positive assumed approach speed in length / time; supplied by the caller.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Expiry time in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: expiry = max(free_depth - loc_bound - protective_clearance, 0) / approach_speed.
Assumptions: An unseen object enters from the free-space boundary at a bounded constant speed.
Excludes: Occlusion geometry beyond a scalar depth, braking, speed-bound validation, and standards compliance.
Equation: T_inv = max(0, (d_free - delta_loc - delta_margin) / v_h)
The free region erodes from its unobserved boundary at the approach speed v_h; localization error delta_loc and the protective clearance delta_margin are spent up front. It is calc_linear_invalidation_horizon with E_0 = delta_loc, r = v_h, and E_max = d_free - delta_margin.
Source: linear invalidation horizon applied to occluded free space; the walking-speed bound v_h is ISO 13855’s K (1.6 m/s).



Derivation: Apply the linear invalidation horizon with initial_error = loc_bound and error_limit = free_depth - protective_clearance.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_free_space_expiry
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_free_space_expiry(3 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second)
>>> assert h == 1 * ureg.second




physics.robotics.perception.calc_linear_invalidation_horizon(
    initial_error,
    error_growth_rate,
    error_limit,
)
Find the first passage of a linearly growing error allowance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




initial_error
Quantity
Initial error allowance in length units.
required


error_growth_rate
Quantity
Positive error-growth rate in length / time.
required


error_limit
Quantity
Allowed error in length units; a spent limit returns zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Invalidation horizon in milliseconds, floored at zero.






Equation: horizon = max(error_limit - initial_error, 0) / error_growth_rate.
Assumptions: Monotone constant-rate growth of a scalar error allowance.
Excludes: Acceleration, new evidence, stopping capability, and confidence calibration.
Equation: E(dt) = E_0 + r * dt ; T_inv = max(0, (E_max - E_0) / r)
A zero result means the belief never supported the task: its initial error already consumes the tolerance. Unlike calc_target_evidence_horizon this does not raise when E_0 >= E_max; it floors the deadline at zero.
Source: first-passage time of a linear error bound (definition of the invalidation horizon, T_inv = inf{dt >= 0 : E(dt) >= E_max}); the reachable-set lineage for occluded free space is Orzechowski, Meyer, and Lauer 2018 (IEEE ITSC).



Derivation: Set a linear error envelope equal to the limit; clamp past crossings to time zero.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_linear_invalidation_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_linear_invalidation_horizon(2 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second, 1 * ureg.meter)
>>> assert h.magnitude == 0

Equation: depth = ceil(log2(map_edge / pitch)).

Excludes: Allocation sparsity, early termination, memory latency, and automatic clamping of out-of-regime input.

Type

Default

physics.robotics.perception.calc_tracked_evidence_horizon(
    tolerance_radius,
    initial_error,
    slip_acceleration,
)
Find when residual acceleration consumes a tracked error margin.











Name
Type
Description
Default




tolerance_radius
Quantity
Positive spatial tolerance in length units.
required


initial_error
Quantity
Nonnegative initial error below tolerance_radius.
required


slip_acceleration
Quantity
Positive residual relative acceleration in length / time**2.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Tracked-evidence horizon in milliseconds.






Equation: horizon = sqrt(2*(tolerance_radius - initial_error)/slip_acceleration).
Assumptions: Tracking removes initial relative velocity; residual acceleration is bounded by the input.
Excludes: Velocity-estimation error, braking, and proof of an acceleration bound.
A tracker that follows a moving target removes its steady velocity, so the remaining error growth comes from a bounded residual acceleration a_slip. A segment executed open-loop for a time T then drifts by a_slip T^2 / 2; setting that drift equal to the error margin r_tol - e_0 gives
Equation: tau_ev = sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip)
This is the constant-acceleration counterpart of calc_target_evidence_horizon (constant drift velocity, a_slip = 0). Like that function it is not a stopping-time bound.
Source: first-passage time of a constant-acceleration displacement (d = a T^2 / 2, solved for T at d = r_tol - e_0); kinematics, derived here.



Derivation: Integrate constant acceleration from zero residual velocity, then solve displacement = remaining margin.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.perception import calc_tracked_evidence_horizon
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> h = calc_tracked_evidence_horizon(2 * ureg.meter, 0 * ureg.meter, 1 * ureg.meter / ureg.second**2)
>>> assert h == 2 * ureg.second

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Accuracy measured separately on each traffic segment; traffic_shares and accuracies are keyed by segment name.


Equation: Overall accuracy sums traffic_share[k]*accuracy[k]; the worst segment minimizes the declared accuracy mapping.

title: solvers.MoERoutingModel
text:
solvers.MoERoutingModel()
Models first-order MoE routing imbalance and expert-parallel all-to-all cost.
Sparse models decouple memory from compute, but routing is rarely perfectly balanced. This model keeps the abstraction small: a single imbalance factor inflates the effective active experts and the routed-token communication volume. It does not simulate a router or token dispatcher.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate effective active parameters and optional EP all-to-all latency.





solvers.MoERoutingModel.solve(
    model,
    batch_size,
    seq_len,
    precision='fp16',
    ep_size=1,
    routing_imbalance_factor=1.0,
    fleet=None,
)
Estimate effective active parameters and optional EP all-to-all latency.
Single-factor imbalance model: a router that overloads hot experts behaves as if each token activated top_k * routing_imbalance_factor experts (capped at the model’s expert count), inflating active parameters and routed traffic by the same multiplier. The routed payload per step is batch * seq_len * hidden_dim * bytes_per_param * top_k * multiplier bytes, of which the fraction (ep_size - 1) / ep_size crosses ranks (a token’s target expert is local with probability 1/ep_size under uniform placement).











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
SparseTransformerWorkload
MoE workload (experts, active_experts_per_token, hidden_dim, active_parameters).
required


batch_size
int
Sequences per step (>= 1).
required


seq_len
int
Tokens per sequence (>= 1).
required


precision
str
Numerical precision; sets bytes per routed activation element.
'fp16'


ep_size
int
Expert-parallel group size (1 = no expert parallelism, no all-to-all cost).
1


routing_imbalance_factor
float
>= 1.0; 1.0 is perfectly balanced routing, larger values approximate hot experts.
1.0


fleet
Fleet
If given (and ep_size > 1), prices the all-to-all exchange over the fleet fabric (bandwidth deflated by oversubscription).
None














Name
Type
Description





MoERoutingResult
Effective active experts/parameters, the dispatch volume (MB), and the all-to-all latency (ms) when a fleet is provided.






Equation: effective experts are min(experts, top_k * imbalance); routed bytes are B * S * H * bytes * effective_experts * (EP-1)/EP. Assumptions: uniform expert placement and one scalar imbalance multiplier applied to both active work and dispatch traffic. Excludes: per-expert queues, token dropping, capacity-factor admission, and measured routing distributions. No fleet means latency is unset, not a zero-cost exchange.



Derivation: count hidden-state elements dispatched per token and multiply by the fraction of destinations outside the local expert-parallel rank.



>>> from mlsysim.models.types import SparseTransformerWorkload
>>> model = SparseTransformerWorkload(name="example", architecture="transformer", parameters=Q_(1000, "count"),
...     active_parameters=Q_(250, "count"), experts=4,
...     active_experts_per_token=1, layers=1, hidden_dim=16, heads=1)
>>> result = MoERoutingModel().solve(model, batch_size=1, seq_len=8)
>>> result.token_dispatch_bytes.m_as("byte") == 0
True

title: solvers.ErrorFeedbackModel
text:
solvers.ErrorFeedbackModel()
A compressor that sends each value rounded to a whole unit, with error feedback.
Without a residual, every value below half a unit is lost. With error feedback the worker adds the carried residual e_t to the gradient, sends the rounded v_t, and keeps e_{t+1} = g_t + e_t - v_t; what is sent plus the last residual equals the true sum at every step.
Literature Source: Karimireddy et al. (2019), “Error Feedback Fixes SignSGD”.





Name
Description




solve
Track rounding residuals across gradient transmissions.





solvers.ErrorFeedbackModel.solve(gradients)
Track rounding residuals across gradient transmissions.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gradients
Sequence[float]
Scalar gradient sequence in consistent arbitrary units.
required














Name
Type
Description





ErrorFeedbackResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: v_t = round(g_t + e_t); e_(t+1) = g_t + e_t - v_t.
Assumptions: Scalar whole-unit compressor with ties rounded away from zero.
Excludes: Optimizer convergence and vector compression costs.



Derivation: v_t = round(g_t + e_t); e_(t+1) = g_t + e_t - v_t. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = ErrorFeedbackModel().solve([0.25, 0.25])
>>> r.total_sent + r.final_error == r.true_total
True

title: solvers.ServingModel
text:
solvers.ServingModel()
Analyzes the two-phase LLM serving lifecycle: Pre-fill vs. Decoding.
LLM inference is not a single mathematical operation; it is a stateful process with two phases. Prefill is modeled with a compute bound; decode compares compute and memory bounds because the limiting resource depends on batch size and context length.
Literature Source: 1. Pope et al. (2023), “Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference.” 2. Agrawal et al. (2024), “Sarathi-Serve” (chunked prefill scheduling). 3. Patel et al. (2024), “Splitwise” and Zhong et al. (2024), “DistServe” (prefill/decode disaggregation).
Formula contract: - TTFT is prefill compute over new prompt tokens plus dispatch overhead and, for disaggregated serving, KV-transfer time. - ITL is max(decode compute time, weight/KV memory time), plus the configured framework layer tax. Efficiency derates compute only. - KV memory always covers the full sequence, even when prompt caching skips part of the prefill computation.





Name
Description




solve
Solve for LLM serving performance.





solvers.ServingModel.solve(
    model,
    hardware,
    seq_len,
    batch_size=1,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
    decode_hardware=None,
    network_bandwidth=Q_('100 GB/s'),
    draft_model=None,
    draft_acceptance_rate=0.7,
    cached_prefix_len=0,
    prefill_chunk_tokens=None,
)
Solve for LLM serving performance.











Name
Type
Description
Default

TransformerWorkload
The primary model to be served.
required

HardwareNode
The hardware node for serving (or pre-fill node in disaggregated serving).
required

int

required

'fp16'

0.5


decode_hardware
HardwareNode
If provided, models Disaggregated Serving where ‘hardware’ does pre-fill and ‘decode_hardware’ does decoding. KV-cache is transferred over the network.
None


network_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive transfer rate in bytes/time between prefill and decode nodes.
Q_('100 GB/s')


draft_model
TransformerWorkload
If provided, models Speculative Decoding using this smaller draft model.
None


draft_acceptance_rate
float
Expected acceptance rate (0.0 to 1.0) of draft tokens per step.
0.7


cached_prefix_len
int
Nonnegative count of tokens with precomputed KV cache (prefix caching). When > 0, the prefill phase only processes (seq_len - cached_prefix_len) new tokens, reducing TTFT proportionally. The full KV-cache (including cached prefix) still occupies memory. Must be < seq_len.
0


prefill_chunk_tokens
int
If provided, split new prefill tokens into chunks of at most this size. This estimates a Sarathi-Serve-style chunked-prefill stall proxy: total TTFT keeps the same compute work plus one dispatch tax per chunk, while decode_stall_bound reports the slowest single chunk that can interfere with ongoing decode iterations. It is not a full scheduler simulation.
None














Name
Type
Description





ServingResult
TTFT and ITL in time units, required memory, and constraint traces. Feasibility checks modeled resident storage on each device; it does not guarantee a serving engine can deploy the configuration.






Equation: T_step = max(F_step / (eta * peak), (W + KV) / BW) + T_layer. F_step includes linear work and both attention matrix products; W is resident weight storage and KV covers all requests. The helper shared with ContinuousBatchingModel implements this bound.
Assumptions: peak memory bandwidth, one weight read per decode step, and ideal compute/memory overlap. Efficiency eta changes compute only. The per-layer tax is a separate runtime assumption. Excludes: runtime workspaces, allocator reserve, and tensor-parallel collectives. Speculation adds draft weights and KV storage; disaggregation checks prefill and decode capacities independently. For K draft proposals, target verification evaluates K+1 query positions, including the bonus-token distribution, before amortizing by expected output tokens. Prefill remains a compute-time approximation, not a kernel schedule.



Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). Pope et al. (2023), “Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.05102 (bibliography key: pope2023efficiently). Leviathan et al. (2023), “Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding,” Algorithm 1 (bibliography key: leviathan2023fast). https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192. These sources motivate the bounds; the layer tax and feasibility conventions above are MLSysIM modeling choices.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Models
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel
>>> result = ServingModel().solve(
...     Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Hardware.Cloud.H100, seq_len=2048)
>>> bool(result.feasible and result.itl.m_as("ms") > 0)
True

title: TeleopLoopScenario
text:
Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/demonstrations.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One teleoperated correction: display, human, command transport, and mechanical response.


Equation: Loop delay=display+human+command+mechanical.
Assumptions: Serial additive delays supplied for the same correction path.
Excludes: Overlapped stages and statistical tail composition.



Derivation: The correction path is explicitly serial, so its display, human, command, and mechanical intervals add. Dividing one interval by their sum yields its contribution to total delay.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.TeleopCorrectionLoop
>>> round((scenario.loop).to('ms').magnitude, 6)
340

title: solvers.CompressionModel
text:
solvers.CompressionModel()
Analyzes model compression trade-offs (Accuracy vs. Efficiency).
This model simulates the ‘Compression Tax’ — the accuracy degradation that occurs when reducing model size via quantization or pruning, balanced against the gains in memory footprint and inference latency.
Literature Source: 1. Han et al. (2015), “Deep Compression: Compressing Deep Neural Networks with Pruning, Trained Quantization and Huffman Coding.” 2. Gholami et al. (2021), “A Survey of Quantization Methods for Efficient Neural Network Inference.” 3. Blalock et al. (2020), “What is the State of Neural Network Pruning?”





Name
Description




candidate
Apply declared size, quality, speed, and support constraints to a candidate.


solve
Estimate compression storage, speed, and assumed quality trade-offs.


sweep
Evaluate compression configurations and identify nondominated candidates.

    hardware,
    *,
    label=None,
    method='quantization',
    target_bitwidth=8,
    sparsity=0.0,
    sparsity_type='unstructured',
    size_limit=None,
    max_accuracy_drop=None,
    min_speedup=None,
    require_hardware_support=False,
    baseline_precision='fp32',
)

CompressionModel.solve : Compression estimates and their assumptions.

The compression method (‘quantization’, ‘pruning’, ‘distillation’).
'quantization'

int
Target numerical precision in bits (e.g., 8 for INT8/FP8, 4 for INT4). At 8-bit, accuracy delta uses the FP8 estimate (near-lossless) by default.
8


sparsity
float
Target sparsity ratio (0.0 to 1.0) for pruning.
0.0


sparsity_type
str
Type of sparsity pattern: ‘unstructured’, ‘structured’, or ‘n_m’ (2:4). - unstructured: storage savings only, no inference speedup - structured: both storage and compute savings - n_m: hardware 2:4 sparsity with 2x speedup at 50% sparsity (Ampere+)
'unstructured'


baseline_precision
str
Configurable precision of the uncompressed model that ratios and sizes are measured against, resolved through core.units.PRECISION_MAP. Defaults to "fp32" (INT8 is 4x, INT4 is 8x). Pass "fp16" for models trained and served from FP16/BF16 weights, such as most LLMs, where INT4 is quoted as 4x.
'fp32'














Name
Type
Description





CompressionResult
Compression metrics including memory savings, inference speedup, and estimated accuracy delta, plus the baseline_precision they are relative to.






mlsysim.physics.performance.calc_bottleneck : Weight-only Roofline regime.



Equation: quantization ratio = baseline_bits/target_bitwidth; pruning ratio = 1/(1-sparsity); compressed_bytes = original_bytes/ratio. Fully sparse pruning uses a finite 100x convention instead of infinity.
Assumptions: quality deltas are model-independent defaults. The baseline weight-only Roofline regime determines the quantization speed branch; structured sparsity is assumed to translate storage savings into speed.
Excludes: measured task accuracy, retraining, sparse index storage, dequantization overhead, and kernel/allocator effects. distillation is documented as an accepted name but currently follows the no-op branch.
Conventions and branch logic:

Sizes are measured against the configurable baseline_precision (FP32 by default, 4 bytes/param), so quantization’s compression_ratio = b_base / target_bitwidth (32/4 = 8x for INT4 by default; 16/4 = 4x with baseline_precision="fp16"). A target wider than the baseline is an upcast and yields a ratio < 1.
estimated_accuracy_delta is a signed fraction (e.g. -0.005 = -0.5 percentage points top-1), selected from illustrative defaults in engine/calibration.py. These are not a measurement of this workload. The pruning branch uses an exponential penalty beyond its declared sparsity threshold.
inference_speedup depends on the Roofline regime: memory-bound workloads gain the full compression ratio (less data to move); compute-bound workloads gain only what the hardware’s low-precision path provides (1.0 when unsupported). For pruning, only structured and 2:4 N:M sparsity translate into compute speedup; unstructured sparsity saves storage only.
Unknown method values fall through to a no-op result (ratio 1.0, delta 0.0).




Derivation: storage changes in proportion to bits per element or the surviving weight fraction. Speed and quality branches are declared implementation assumptions, not consequences of that storage identity.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Hardware
>>> result = CompressionModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
...     Hardware.Cloud.H100, target_bitwidth=8, baseline_precision="fp16")
>>> result.compression_ratio == 2
True

    model,
    hardware,
    candidate_configs,
    *,
    size_limit=None,
    max_accuracy_drop=None,
    min_speedup=None,
    require_hardware_support=False,
    objective='min_size_max_speed_preserve_quality',
    baseline_precision='fp32',
)

required

Require the candidate support heuristic; default False.
False

Descriptive result label only; changing it does not change the selection algorithm. Default min_size_max_speed_preserve_quality.
'min_size_max_speed_preserve_quality'

str

'fp32'














Name
Type
Description





CompressionSweepResult
Candidate records, frontier/dominated labels, and a selected label among feasible frontier candidates, or None when none exist. Sizes are in GB; quality and speed comparisons are dimensionless modeled quantities.






CompressionModel.candidate : Constraint checks and support heuristics.



Equation: A dominates B if A has no larger size, no lower speed, and no lower quality (1 + accuracy_delta), with at least one strict improvement. Among feasible frontier entries, selection minimizes the tuple (abs(accuracy_delta), size/max(speedup, 1e-9)).
Assumptions: each candidate uses the same workload, hardware, and baseline. Dominance is evaluated across all candidates, including infeasible ones; feasibility is applied afterward when choosing the returned best label.
Excludes: global optimization outside the supplied candidate list, measured accuracy/performance, uncertainty intervals, and runtime memory feasibility.



Derivation: Pareto dominance is the componentwise ordering of storage cost, speed benefit, and assumed quality. The lexicographic tie-break is an explicit implementation policy, not a learned or universally optimal preference.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Hardware
>>> result = CompressionModel().sweep(Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
...     Hardware.Cloud.H100, [{"target_bitwidth": 8, "label": "int8"}])
>>> result.frontier_labels
['int8']

Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Attempt cost by term for several workloads, and three levers on cost per accepted task.
Each workload gives acceptance, environment, assessment in dollars, and either human (fixed per attempt) or handoff (charged per rejected attempt). The model term is model dollars, or the bill’s cached trajectory cost, or token_multiple chats of chat_input/chat_output tokens at the stated tariff.

title: physics.coordination
text:
physics.coordination
Coordination of several agents: partitions, schedules, shared writes, and correlated votes.
Added 2026-10-20. Each function is the arithmetic of one coordination relation: the elapsed time of a work partition with a per-worker overhead, the deliveries of a full mesh against a supervisor, the earliest schedule of a dependency graph, the chance that independent write sets stay disjoint, the binomial and beta-binomial tails of a vote, and the beta mass above a threshold that floors a correlated majority.





Name
Description




calc_beta_binomial_pmf
Calculate beta-binomial masses for a correlated Bernoulli panel.


calc_beta_mixture_shape
Recover beta shape parameters from Bernoulli mean and correlation.


calc_beta_tail
Calculate beta propensity mass above a threshold.


calc_binomial_tail
Calculate a binomial upper-tail probability by summing masses.


calc_disjoint_writes
Calculate the probability that uniform write sets are disjoint.


calc_disjoint_writes_approx
Approximate disjoint write-set probability in the sparse regime.


calc_earliest_schedule
Compute earliest starts and finishes for an acyclic dependency graph.


calc_full_mesh_deliveries
Count directed deliveries in one full-mesh exchange.


calc_partition_elapsed
Estimate partition elapsed time relative to serial execution.


calc_supervisor_deliveries
Count deliveries in one supervisor request-and-receipt round.





physics.coordination.calc_beta_binomial_pmf(trials, mean, correlation)
Calculate beta-binomial masses for a correlated Bernoulli panel.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trials
int
Nonnegative number n of Bernoulli outcomes.
required


mean
float
Marginal success probability, greater than zero and less than one.
required


correlation
float
Pairwise intraclass correlation, greater than zero and less than one.
required














Name
Type
Description





list of float
Dimensionless masses ordered by success count k=0,…,n.






Equation: P(X=k) = C(n,k) B(k+a,n-k+b)/B(a,b), where a and b come from calc_beta_mixture_shape. Beta-function ratios are evaluated with log gamma.
Assumptions: draw one propensity per panel from the beta law, then sample conditionally independent outcomes using that same propensity. Input ranges are caller preconditions.
Excludes: arbitrary dependence structures and uncertainty in fitted mixture parameters. Large binomial coefficients can still limit numerical range.



Derivation: integrate the conditional binomial mass against the beta density; the resulting integral is B(k+a,n-k+b)/B(a,b).



>>> [round(p, 6) for p in calc_beta_binomial_pmf(2, 0.5, 0.5)]
[0.375, 0.25, 0.375]




physics.coordination.calc_beta_mixture_shape(mean, correlation)
Recover beta shape parameters from Bernoulli mean and correlation.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean
float
Marginal success probability mu, greater than zero and less than one.
required


correlation
float
Intraclass correlation rho, greater than zero and less than one.
required














Name
Type
Description




a
float
Positive dimensionless first beta shape parameter.


b
float
Positive dimensionless second beta shape parameter.






Equation: a = mu(1/rho-1) and b = (1-mu)(1/rho-1).
Assumptions: Bernoulli outcomes share one beta-distributed propensity and are independent conditional on that propensity. Input ranges are caller preconditions; independent trials require the rho -> 0 limiting model.
Excludes: negative correlation, deterministic propensities at the domain boundaries, and estimation uncertainty in the supplied mean and correlation.



Derivation: a beta mixture has mean a/(a+b) and Bernoulli intraclass correlation 1/(a+b+1). Solve these two equations for a and b.



>>> calc_beta_mixture_shape(0.5, 0.5)
(0.5, 0.5)




physics.coordination.calc_beta_tail(mean, correlation, threshold)
Calculate beta propensity mass above a threshold.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean
float
Mean propensity, greater than zero and less than one.
required


correlation
float
Bernoulli intraclass correlation, greater than zero and less than one.
required


threshold
float
Propensity threshold between zero and one.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless beta probability mass above the threshold.






Equation: P(theta > t) = 1 - I_t(a,b), where I is the regularized incomplete beta function and shapes come from calc_beta_mixture_shape.
Assumptions: one beta-distributed propensity is shared by all conditionally independent members of a panel. As the panel grows, its success share converges to that propensity. If success denotes an error and t=1/2, the returned mass is the limiting majority-error probability.
Excludes: finite-panel voting corrections, arbitrary correlations, and parameter-estimation uncertainty. Subtracting from one can lose precision in very small upper tails. SciPy is required at call time.



Derivation: integrate the beta density above t, or subtract its cumulative mass I_t(a,b) from one. The conditional law of large numbers gives the infinite-panel interpretation.



>>> round(calc_beta_tail(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 6)
0.5




physics.coordination.calc_binomial_tail(trials, probability, at_least)
Calculate a binomial upper-tail probability by summing masses.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trials
int
Nonnegative number n of independent trials.
required


probability
float
Common success probability p, between zero and one.
required


at_least
int
Inclusive success threshold k, from zero through n+1.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless probability of at least k successes.






Equation: P(X >= k) = sum from j=k to n of C(n,j)p**j(1-p)**(n-j). A threshold of n+1 produces an empty sum, which is zero.
Assumptions: independent Bernoulli trials with a common fixed probability. Valid input ranges are caller preconditions.
Excludes: correlated or unequal-probability trials. Direct summation is not a numerically stabilized large-n survival-function implementation.



Derivation: there are C(n,j) success-position subsets for j successes; each has probability p**j(1-p)**(n-j). Sum the disjoint events above k.



>>> calc_binomial_tail(2, 0.5, 1)
0.75




physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes(workers, files, writes_per_worker)
Calculate the probability that uniform write sets are disjoint.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workers
int
Number N of independent workers, at least one.
required


files
int
Positive number F of available files.
required


writes_per_worker
int
Number w of distinct files chosen by each worker, with 0 <= w <= F. If N*w exceeds F, disjoint placement is impossible and probability is zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless probability that all worker write sets are pairwise disjoint.






Equation: product over k=1,…,N-1 of C(F-kw,w)/C(F,w). Worker k+1 must avoid the kw files already selected by earlier workers.
Assumptions: each worker independently chooses a uniformly distributed w-element subset; selections within a worker are without replacement. Counts must be integers in the documented ranges.
Excludes: hot-file skew, coordinated partitioning, and write ordering.



Derivation: condition each successive worker on all earlier write sets being disjoint, count allowed subsets, and multiply conditional probabilities.



>>> calc_disjoint_writes(2, 4, 1)
0.75




physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes_approx(
    workers,
    files,
    writes_per_worker,
)
Approximate disjoint write-set probability in the sparse regime.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workers
int
Number N of workers, at least one.
required


files
int
Positive number F of available files.
required


writes_per_worker
int
Nonnegative number w of distinct files selected per worker, at most F.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless approximate probability of no cross-worker collision.






Equation: probability approximately exp(-N(N-1)w**2/(2F)).
Assumptions: independent uniform file selection and sparse collisions, so a Poisson approximation to the number of pairwise collisions is useful.
Excludes: hot-file skew and higher-order dependence among collisions. It need not match the exact probability near capacity; use calc_disjoint_writes for its supported exact-combinatorial domain.



Derivation: N(N-1)/2 worker pairs each have approximately w**2/F shared files in expectation; approximate the zero-collision probability by the zero mass of a Poisson variable with that mean.

physics.coordination.calc_beta_binomial_pmf(trials, mean, correlation)
Calculate beta-binomial masses for a correlated Bernoulli panel.











Name
Type
Description
Default

int
Nonnegative number n of Bernoulli outcomes.
required

float
Marginal success probability, greater than zero and less than one.
required


correlation
float
Pairwise intraclass correlation, greater than zero and less than one.
required














Name
Type
Description





list of float
Dimensionless masses ordered by success count k=0,…,n.






Equation: P(X=k) = C(n,k) B(k+a,n-k+b)/B(a,b), where a and b come from calc_beta_mixture_shape. Beta-function ratios are evaluated with log gamma.
Assumptions: draw one propensity per panel from the beta law, then sample conditionally independent outcomes using that same propensity. Input ranges are caller preconditions.
Excludes: arbitrary dependence structures and uncertainty in fitted mixture parameters. Large binomial coefficients can still limit numerical range.



Derivation: integrate the conditional binomial mass against the beta density; the resulting integral is B(k+a,n-k+b)/B(a,b).



>>> [round(p, 6) for p in calc_beta_binomial_pmf(2, 0.5, 0.5)]

Type

Default

required

float
Intraclass correlation rho, greater than zero and less than one.
required

Type
Description




a
float
Positive dimensionless first beta shape parameter.


b
float
Positive dimensionless second beta shape parameter.






Equation: a = mu(1/rho-1) and b = (1-mu)(1/rho-1).
Assumptions: Bernoulli outcomes share one beta-distributed propensity and are independent conditional on that propensity. Input ranges are caller preconditions; independent trials require the rho -> 0 limiting model.
Excludes: negative correlation, deterministic propensities at the domain boundaries, and estimation uncertainty in the supplied mean and correlation.



Derivation: a beta mixture has mean a/(a+b) and Bernoulli intraclass correlation 1/(a+b+1). Solve these two equations for a and b.

physics.coordination.calc_beta_tail(mean, correlation, threshold)
Calculate beta propensity mass above a threshold.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean
float
Mean propensity, greater than zero and less than one.
required


correlation
float
Bernoulli intraclass correlation, greater than zero and less than one.
required

float
Propensity threshold between zero and one.
required

Type
Description





float
Dimensionless beta probability mass above the threshold.






Equation: P(theta > t) = 1 - I_t(a,b), where I is the regularized incomplete beta function and shapes come from calc_beta_mixture_shape.
Assumptions: one beta-distributed propensity is shared by all conditionally independent members of a panel. As the panel grows, its success share converges to that propensity. If success denotes an error and t=1/2, the returned mass is the limiting majority-error probability.
Excludes: finite-panel voting corrections, arbitrary correlations, and parameter-estimation uncertainty. Subtracting from one can lose precision in very small upper tails. SciPy is required at call time.



Derivation: integrate the beta density above t, or subtract its cumulative mass I_t(a,b) from one. The conditional law of large numbers gives the infinite-panel interpretation.



>>> round(calc_beta_tail(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 6)

physics.coordination.calc_binomial_tail(trials, probability, at_least)
Calculate a binomial upper-tail probability by summing masses.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trials
int
Nonnegative number n of independent trials.
required


probability
float
Common success probability p, between zero and one.
required


at_least
int
Inclusive success threshold k, from zero through n+1.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless probability of at least k successes.






Equation: P(X >= k) = sum from j=k to n of C(n,j)p**j(1-p)**(n-j). A threshold of n+1 produces an empty sum, which is zero.
Assumptions: independent Bernoulli trials with a common fixed probability. Valid input ranges are caller preconditions.
Excludes: correlated or unequal-probability trials. Direct summation is not a numerically stabilized large-n survival-function implementation.



Derivation: there are C(n,j) success-position subsets for j successes; each has probability p**j(1-p)**(n-j). Sum the disjoint events above k.



>>> calc_binomial_tail(2, 0.5, 1)
0.75




physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes(workers, files, writes_per_worker)
Calculate the probability that uniform write sets are disjoint.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workers
int
Number N of independent workers, at least one.
required


files
int
Positive number F of available files.
required


writes_per_worker
int
Number w of distinct files chosen by each worker, with 0 <= w <= F. If N*w exceeds F, disjoint placement is impossible and probability is zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless probability that all worker write sets are pairwise disjoint.






Equation: product over k=1,…,N-1 of C(F-kw,w)/C(F,w). Worker k+1 must avoid the kw files already selected by earlier workers.
Assumptions: each worker independently chooses a uniformly distributed w-element subset; selections within a worker are without replacement. Counts must be integers in the documented ranges.
Excludes: hot-file skew, coordinated partitioning, and write ordering.



Derivation: condition each successive worker on all earlier write sets being disjoint, count allowed subsets, and multiply conditional probabilities.



>>> calc_disjoint_writes(2, 4, 1)
0.75




physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes_approx(
    workers,
    files,
    writes_per_worker,
)

Description
Default

files

required


writes_per_worker
int

required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless approximate probability of no cross-worker collision.






Equation: probability approximately exp(-N(N-1)w**2/(2F)).
Assumptions: independent uniform file selection and sparse collisions, so a Poisson approximation to the number of pairwise collisions is useful.
Excludes: hot-file skew and higher-order dependence among collisions. It need not match the exact probability near capacity; use calc_disjoint_writes for its supported exact-combinatorial domain.



Derivation: N(N-1)/2 worker pairs each have approximately w**2/F shared files in expectation; approximate the zero-collision probability by the zero mass of a Poisson variable with that mean.



>>> round(calc_disjoint_writes_approx(2, 100, 1), 6)

title: Data Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

AcceleratorInputFeedScenario: accelerators copies of hardware training workload at sustained_rate samples a second each, fed from supply with encoded_sample bytes stored per sample and decoded_sample bytes after decode.
ActiveLearningBudgetScenario: Active learning against a fixed label budget when scoring the pool is charged to the same budget.
ActiveLearningRoundsScenario: Active learning from initial_labels adding labels_per_round for rounds rounds, each round paying round_scoring_cost to score the pool, against random labeling that needs random_labels at the same label_price.
AdmissionOrderScenario: Independent admission checks (pass probability, slot time) run in each of orders.
AllocationGrowthScenario: A compute-optimal allocation X_opt ~ C^exponent when compute grows by compute_multiple.
AlwaysOnDetectorTargetsScenario: An always-on detector’s product contract: what it must catch, how rarely it may wake falsely, what it may occupy on the device, and the data budget and schedule that must deliver it.
AttemptGroupContrastScenario: attempts independent attempts per fixture at each of pass_rates.
BatchVersusStreamingIngestScenario: One event stream ingested by always-on streaming cores or by a batch job each hour.
BudgetMatchedLabelingScenario: A pool to label at label_price under budget: random labeling spends the budget, active learning reaches the same quality with active_labels.
CheckpointStormScenario: Every one of replicas writes workload’s full resumable state through one ingest path.
CodecEpochScenario: epoch_bytes decompressed on the host each epoch for epochs epochs, at each codec’s decode_rates.
CohortDispositionScenario: A finite cohort of attempts by disposition at a cutoff, its total cost, and the disposition that emits a learning artifact.
ColumnProjectionScenario: A model that uses columns_used of columns_total equal-size columns, read from a row or a columnar file.
CompressedReadScenario: Compressed shards read at read_bandwidth, decoded on CPU cores at each codec’s output rate.
CoresetRunScenario: workload trained for epochs over dataset on one hardware at utilization, against a keep_fraction coreset scored by one forward pass of workload or proxy.
CorpusDenominatorsScenario: A retained pool of record classes (records, stored tokens per record, selected target tokens per record); focus is the class whose shares are read, admitted the classes a route admits.
CorpusRepetitionScenario: A training run (ClusterTrainingTimeScenario) set against the unique tokens of its workload’s own corpus.
CorpusTierScenario: An audio corpus (dataset) kept on storage tiers at storage_rates and read at read_bandwidths.
CoverageFloorScenario: A keep_fraction coreset drawn without regard to class from pool examples, of which rare_share belong to a rare class that needs at least floor examples.
CurriculumScheduleScenario: A curriculum that reaches target in curriculum_epochs against baseline_epochs shuffled, with an optional linear warmup of warmup_epochs (epoch j serves j/W of the data).
DataBudgetScenario: A data budget split into shares by category; the labeling share buys labels at label_price plus review_overhead for quality review.
DataCostBreakdownScenario: A supervised dataset’s bill: acquisition, labels at label_price, storage_bytes kept for storage_duration at storage_rate, and runs training runs of run_time each on accelerators at accelerator_rate.
DataEchoingScenario: A host that prepares host_rate samples a second feeding an accelerator that consumes accelerator_rate, over epochs of examples, with each prepared sample used echo_factor times.
DataScalingReturnScenario: Growing a dataset from base_examples to scaled_examples for accuracy_gain points.
DataStallScenario: A batch delivered in io_time against compute_time of compute, in sequence or overlapped.
DesignTradeoffScenario: One design-space move of a knob from baseline to alternative, with an illustrative quality gain from gain_low to gain_high (fractions); costs scale by ratio.
DuplicateRemovalScenario: Near-duplicate shares removed from run’s corpus: the training time and energy each share returns, against one read of the corpus and the MinHash signatures of its documents.
FailureTriageScenario: runs trajectories a month failing at failure_rate, each probe’s attributed share, and a fine-tuning run on every failure of workload on devices x hardware.
FeatureLookupScenario: An online service at request_rate that reads reads_per_request stored features per request.
HostIoCpuScenario: devices each consuming requests_per_device reads per second, at each path’s CPU service time.
InformationComputeRatioScenario: Accuracy gained per training FLOP for one epoch over all of dataset and over a keep_fraction subset, with gain_full and gain_subset points of gain.
InputDemandScenario: consumers each read samples_per_step samples per step_time of compute.
LabelGranularityScenario: Label entries for one image: a per-pixel mask against boxes boxes of coords_per_box.
LabelingVersusTrainingScenario: A labeling budget against one training run: epochs over dataset_examples at throughput_per_accelerator on accelerators, priced at a low and a high hourly rate.
LaborEffortScenario: items labeled by hand at time_per_item each: total hours and full-time person-years.
MinHashBandingScenario: A MinHash signature cut into bands bands of rows hashes over shingle_words-word shingles.
ObjectStorageBillScenario: A dataset kept in object storage for a billing period and read reads times across a boundary.
PrefetchDepthScenario: Ready batches that cover each tier’s tail read, and host memory at a safety depth.
PretrainingAmortizationScenario: tasks tasks trained from scratch at scratch_compute each against one pretraining run of pretrain_compute plus finetune_compute per task, with the labels each path needs.
RunAmortizationScenario: A one-time investment of build_cost plus operating_cost that saves saving_per_run on every training run that reuses its output.
RunSplitLeakageScenario: attempts runs per task, each assigned to training with probability train_fraction.
SelectionBudgetScenario: Selection that takes selection_time and leaves a subset that trains in subset_time, against full training in full_time (the selection inequality in hours).
SemiSupervisedCostScenario: A supervised baseline with supervised_labels and supervised_compute against a semi-supervised run with ssl_labels and ssl_compute, labels at label_price.
ShardPackagingScenario: files samples packaged into shards large files on a file system rated at rated_bandwidth.
StagingBurstScenario: A collector of rollouts concurrent rollouts feeding slots verifiers, whose checks stall at timeout, with records charged at record_ceiling against store.
StorageFootprintScenario: What a training run of workload reads once, saves every interval, and archives.
StreamVsStageScenario: Stream every epoch from remote object storage, or stage the dataset locally once per run.
SyntheticFootprintScenario: Generated samples with provenance metadata, read once per verification pass.
TieredCacheScenario: A fast tier in front of a slow one: a stated hit rate, or capacity over a uniformly sampled corpus.
TieredCheckpointScenario: One save of workload’s state on fleet: local write per node, then a durable drain.
UtilizationLossScenario: fleet’s accelerators billed at device_hour_rate while utilization falls.

title: ElasticResizeScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Three ways to run one job over window: start small, wait for the full size, or step up.
Start small runs small_gpus for the whole window. Wait queues queue_wait for full_gpus. Step up starts on small_gpus and, when the full allocation would free, pauses rescale_overhead and grows to step_up_gpus, leaving the rest to queued jobs. Throughputs are epochs per hour at each size. GPU-hours count the step-up size through its resize pause.


Equation: epochs = throughput * productive hours for each phase; efficiency = epochs / reserved device-hours.
Assumptions: Throughputs are fixed epochs per hour and enough window remains for each chosen phase. The larger reservation includes the resize pause.
Excludes: Convergence differences, variable scaling efficiency, and a scheduler that predicts future queue availability.



Derivation: epochs = throughput * productive hours for each phase; efficiency = epochs / reserved device-hours. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.ElasticResizeDecision
>>> round(float(case.window_h), 3)
24.0

engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.step_up_phase1_epochs
Epochs completed on the small allocation before resizing begins.
Equation: return wait_h * small_throughput.



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.step_up_phase2_h
Productive hours remaining after both queue delay and resize pause.
Equation: return window_h - wait_h - rescale_h.



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.step_up_phase2_epochs

Equation: return step_up_phase2_h * step_up_throughput.

Equation: return step_up_phase1_epochs + step_up_phase2_epochs.

Equation: return step_up_epochs / start_small_epochs.



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.rescale_break_even_h
Resize pause in hours at which step-up completes as many epochs as staying small.
Equation: return window_h - wait_h - (start_small_epochs - step_up_phase1_epochs) / step_up_throughput.



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.step_up_efficiency
Throughput scaling relative to ideal linear growth from the small allocation, as a ratio.
Equation: return step_up_throughput / (step_up_gpus / small_gpus * small_throughput).



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.full_efficiency
Full-allocation throughput divided by linear scaling of the small allocation’s throughput.
Equation: return full_throughput / (full_gpus / small_gpus * small_throughput).



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.gpu_hours
Device-hours by policy; step-up reserves the larger allocation during its resize pause.
Equation: return {'start_small': small_gpus * window_h, 'wait': full_gpus * wait_run_h, 'step_up': small_gpus * wait_h + step_up_gpus * wait_run_h}.



engine.scenario_types.ElasticResizeScenario.epochs_per_gpu_hour
Completed epochs per reserved device-hour for each policy, including idle reservations.
Equation: epochs = {'start_small': start_small_epochs, 'wait': wait_epochs, 'step_up': step_up_epochs}; return {k: epochs[k] / h for k, h in gpu_hours.items()}.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One rollout of decisions step apart under discount discount: how far the return reaches, in decisions and in seconds, and the discount that keeps retained_weight of the final reward at the first decision.


Equation: Terminal weight=discount**decisions; effective horizon=1/(1-discount); time horizon=steps*step.

Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/demonstrations.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A contact task binned by contact angle and normal force, and the cells each archive occupies.
archives maps a name to (angle_low, angle_high, force_low, force_high, held-out RMS action error); each archive’s occupied region is a rectangle of whole bins.


Equation: Cells=angle_bins*force_bins; archive support is its rectangular bin span.
Assumptions: Archive boundaries align with angle/force bins and the supplied RMS errors are external inputs.
Excludes: Interpolation accuracy or probability mass within occupied bins.



Derivation: Aligned angular and force bins form a Cartesian product. Each archive is represented by a rectangle whose angular count times force count gives occupied cells; the RMS error is carried from the input and is not inferred from occupancy.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.

>>> scenario = Scenarios.ContactAngleCoverage
>>> scenario.cells

title: WeightReadScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Every weight of workload read once from hardware’s memory at bytes_per_weight.
The weight-streaming floor of one batch-one pass: per frame for a vision model, per token for a decoder. Unlike DecodeScenario it assumes no FLOP count, so it serves convolutional networks as well as decoders. energy_per_byte (optional) prices the reads.


Equation: read_time is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: Weights and optional full KV state stream once at the registered peak memory bandwidth.
Excludes: Compute, runtime overhead, cache reuse, interdevice communication, and serving-latency validation.



Derivation: The equations below follow the stated counts, geometric relations, or accounting definitions; scenario inputs are supplied assumptions or observations, not fitted predictions.



Execute the registered worked inputs; this is a modeled calculation.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.Llama2_7BTokenOnFlagshipPhone
>>> value = case.read_time
>>> print(f"{value:.3f~P}")
273.438 ms

engine.solvers.orchestration
Cluster orchestration and queueing solvers.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable.





Name
Description




OrchestrationModel
Analyzes Cluster Orchestration and Queueing (Little’s Law).


PreemptionTaxModel
The cost of forced preemptions to the job that is stopped.





engine.solvers.orchestration.OrchestrationModel()
Analyzes Cluster Orchestration and Queueing (Little’s Law).
Caveat: This model uses a pedagogical M/D/1 queue (single server, deterministic service) to establish macroscopic wait-time bounds for dedicated, monolithic cluster workloads. For detailed multi-tenant job packing and preemption, a discrete-event M/G/c scheduler simulation would be required.
This model simulates the ‘Wait Wall’ in shared research clusters, calculating job completion times and researcher wait times based on cluster utilization and arrival rates.
Literature Source: 1. Little (1961), “A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW.” 2. Barroso et al. (2018), “The Datacenter as a Computer” (Cluster Mgmt). 3. Jeon et al. (2019), “Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters.”





Name
Description




solve
Estimate waiting time for a whole-fleet M/D/1 queue.





engine.solvers.orchestration.OrchestrationModel.solve(
    fleet,
    arrival_rate_jobs_per_day,
    avg_job_duration_days,
)
Estimate waiting time for a whole-fleet M/D/1 queue.











Name
Type
Description
Default




fleet
Fleet
Fleet context for the query; its device count does not enter this single-server queue equation.
required


arrival_rate_jobs_per_day
float
Nonnegative Poisson arrival rate in jobs/day.
required


avg_job_duration_days
float
Positive deterministic service duration in days; one job occupies the whole fleet.
required














Name
Type
Description





OrchestrationResult
Dimensionless utilization, mean waiting time in days, queue length in jobs, and is_stable. Waiting time and queue length are infinite when utilization is at least one.






Equation: mu = 1 / service_days; rho = arrival_rate / mu; Wq = rho / (2 mu (1-rho)); Lq = rho^2 / (2(1-rho)) for rho < 1.
Assumptions: Poisson arrivals, deterministic service, one logical server, and steady state for rho < 1.
Excludes: Multi-tenant packing, job-size variation, scheduling priorities, and preemption.



Derivation: The M/G/1 mean-wait identity Wq = lambda E[S^2] / (2(1-rho)) becomes the stated M/D/1 expression when S is constant. Little’s identity Lq = lambda Wq gives queue length.



>>> from mlsysim import Systems
>>> r = OrchestrationModel().solve(Systems.Clusters.Research_256, 0.5, 1.0)
>>> r.is_stable and r.avg_wait_time_days.m_as("day") == 0.5
True






engine.solvers.orchestration.PreemptionTaxModel()
The cost of forced preemptions to the job that is stopped.
One forced preemption discards the work since the last durable checkpoint and then pays the cold-restart steps of the recovery budget: restart, checkpoint reload, and warmup. There is no detection term, because the scheduler itself stopped the job. A preempted job and a failed job therefore pay the same relaunch.





Name
Description




solve
Calculate discarded work and relaunch cost from forced preemption.





engine.solvers.orchestration.PreemptionTaxModel.solve(
    n_devices,
    checkpoint_bytes,
    lost_work,
    preemption_rate,
    recovery,
    device_hour_rate,
)
Calculate discarded work and relaunch cost from forced preemption.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_devices
int
Nonnegative number of devices reserved by the preempted job.
required


checkpoint_bytes
Quantity
Nonnegative checkpoint size in bytes.
required


lost_work
Quantity
Nonnegative time discarded since the last checkpoint.
required


preemption_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative preemption frequency in inverse time.
required


recovery
RecoveryProfile
Restart, checkpoint bandwidth, and warmup profile; bandwidth must be positive.
required


device_hour_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative device-hour cost in USD/hour.
required














Name
Type
Description





PreemptionTaxResult
Per-event loss and relaunch components, USD cost per event, events/day, lost time/day, and device-hours/day.






Equation: relaunch = restart + checkpoint_bytes / bandwidth + warmup; per_event = lost_work + relaunch; daily_loss = preemption_rate * one_day * per_event.
Assumptions: Each forced stop incurs the same lost-work and restart budget; all reserved devices remain charged.
Excludes: Failure detection time because the scheduler initiates the stop; overlapping recovery, migration, and time-varying prices.



Derivation: Serial restart phases add in time. Multiplying event loss by the expected event count gives daily loss, and multiplying device-hours by the rate gives cost.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.systems.reliability import Reliability
>>> r = PreemptionTaxModel().solve(4, Q_(1, "GB"), Q_(1, "min"),
...     Q_(1, "1/day"), Reliability.Recovery, Q_(2, "USD/hour"))
>>> r.lost_per_day == r.per_event
True

title: solvers.DistributedModel
text:
solvers.DistributedModel()
Resolves fleet-wide communication, synchronization, and pipelining constraints.
This model analyzes the constraints of distributed scale for distributed training. It decomposes a workload across a cluster using 3D Parallelism (DP, TP, PP) and calculates the resulting communication overheads and idle times (bubbles) that determine the Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU).
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism.” (3D Parallelism Framework) 2. Narayanan et al. (2019), “PipeDream: Efficient Pipeline Parallelism for Training Large Models.” (1F1B Pipeline Bubble Model) 3. Patarasuk & Mueller (2009), “Bandwidth-Optimal All-Reduce Algorithms for Clusters of Workstations.” (Ring All-Reduce)
Formula contract: - split total accelerators into TP * PP * EP model-parallel groups and DP replicas; the split must be exact. - local step time is one model-parallel replica’s training step on the per-DP local batch (_replica_profile): step FLOPs shared across the replica’s TP * PP * EP accelerators, with per-accelerator sharded training state deciding feasibility. - exposed communication = DP gradient collective + TP activation collectives (4 AllReduces per layer per training step: 2 forward, 2 backward) + EP token all-to-all, optionally reduced by overlap. - total step latency = local compute + exposed communication + pipeline bubble, adjusted by explicit congestion and straggler multipliers.





Name
Description




solve

TrainingMemoryModel.solve : Per-device state and activation accounting.



Equation: step time adds replica Roofline latency, pipeline idle time T_replica * bubble / (1 - bubble), and exposed DP/TP/EP communication. Data parallelism is N / (TP * PP * EP); transformer work counts tokens. Assumptions: homogeneous accelerators, ideal model partitioning, analytic collective traffic, and declared overlap/congestion factors. LoRA traffic uses a fixed fraction independently of the rank-based memory approximation. Excludes: measured kernel scheduling, interleaved activation deallocation, and network contention traces. topology_override is currently accepted but does not alter the calculation. Inspect node_profile.feasible; a latency returned for spilled state is not an in-HBM deployment claim.



Derivation: sum the resource-specific times after sharding the workload; subtract the permitted overlap window and add pipeline idle time.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Systems
>>> result = DistributedModel().solve(Models.Vision.ResNet50,
...     Systems.Clusters.Research_256, batch_size=256)
>>> result.step_latency_total.m_as("second") > 0
True

title: fmt.fmt
text:
fmt.fmt
fmt.fmt(
    quantity,
    unit=None,
    precision=1,
    commas=True,
    prefix='',
    suffix='',
    approx=False,
    lower_bound=False,
    upper_bound=False,
    trim_trailing_zeros=False,
)
Format a Pint Quantity (or plain number) for narrative text. Returns a MarkdownStr so Quarto inserts the value verbatim (no escape).
The prefix and suffix arguments collapse the old MarkdownStr(f”…“) escape-hatch idiom into a single canonical helper. Common uses:
fmt(value, precision=0, approx=True)       # "~1,000"
fmt(value, precision=0, lower_bound=True)  # "> 1,000"
fmt_percent(rate, precision=1, style="symbol")  # "12.4%"
fmt_qty(bandwidth, unit=MB/second)         # "2.4 MB/s"
fmt_multiple(speedup)                      # "3.2×"
Safety: Raises ValueError if formatting would hide meaningful magnitude: non-zero values displayed as 0, non-integers displayed with precision=0, or integer-like values shown with spurious decimals (512.0). Use fmt_int(...) when integer display is intentional.

A dependency graph on interchangeable slots: aggregate work, the critical path, and both bounds.
The schedule starts each node when its last predecessor finishes. No schedule on slots slots ends before max(W / slots, L).


Equation: The calculation members below define schedule, start, finish, work, makespan, work_bound, speedup, peak_slots, free_float.
Assumptions: Dependencies form a nonempty acyclic graph and tasks execute without preemption; earliest starts ignore slot scarcity.
Excludes: Claiming the critical-path schedule is feasible on the configured finite slot count.



Derivation: A dependency graph on interchangeable slots: aggregate work, the critical path, and both bounds. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.

>>> case = Scenarios.InterfaceMigrationSchedule
>>> value = case.makespan
>>> print(f"{value:.3g~}")

Description

Mapping from node identifier to earliest-finish time quantity, the schedule’s second component.


free_float
Per-node duration slack before delaying its earliest successor; sink nodes omitted.

Dependency critical-path duration, the latest earliest finish; not a slot-constrained schedule.

Maximum concurrently active nodes in the earliest-start schedule; endpoints are half open.

slots

engine.scenario_types.DependencyScheduleScenario.finish

Equation: schedule[1].



engine.scenario_types.DependencyScheduleScenario.work
Total serial work as a duration quantity, summing every node duration.
Equation: sum(durations.values(), 0 * next(iter(durations.values()))).

Dependency critical-path duration, the latest earliest finish; not a slot-constrained schedule.
The critical path: the latest earliest finish.

Aggregate-work duration divided by slot count, a capacity lower bound.

Serial time over the makespan.

Maximum concurrently active nodes in the earliest-start schedule; endpoints are half open.
Most nodes running at once in the earliest schedule.

For each node with successors, how long it can slip before delaying the earliest one.

Equation: The calculation members below define schedule, start, finish, work, makespan, work_bound, speedup, peak_slots, free_float.
Assumptions: Dependencies form a nonempty acyclic graph and tasks execute without preemption; earliest starts ignore slot scarcity.
Excludes: Claiming the critical-path schedule is feasible on the configured finite slot count.

title: engine.solvers.operations
text:
engine.solvers.operations
Agent-operations solvers: traces, retention, and staged release (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated inputs: the elapsed time one trial’s spans explain along its critical path, and what shortening one span saves; the diagnostic trace bodies head sampling and verdict-aware selection keep; and a Wald sequential test run as a canary monitor, in labeled tasks, calendar time, and excess failures. None models a particular tracing system, collector, or rollout controller.





Name
Description




SequentialCanaryModel
A Wald SPRT on task acceptance run as a canary monitor.


SpanCriticalPathModel
One trial’s spans on a shared clock: what they explain, and what one shorter span saves.


TraceRetentionModel
Diagnostic trace bodies kept over a window under three selections.





engine.solvers.operations.SequentialCanaryModel()
A Wald SPRT on task acceptance run as a canary monitor.
The log-likelihood ratio favors the degraded acceptance p_degraded over p_base: a failure adds ln((1 - p1)/(1 - p0)) and a success ln(p1/p0) (the negated increments of calc_sprt_increments on the failure probabilities). Wald’s boundaries come from the false-hold target alpha and the missed-degradation target beta (calc_sprt_boundaries). Under the degraded hypothesis the walk ends at the upper boundary with probability 1 - beta; neglecting overshoot, calc_sprt_expected_samples gives the expected labeled tasks. Labels arrive label_delay after admission at fraction of the eligible arrival_rate, so calendar time scales as 1/fraction while the measured regression’s excess failures change only through the tasks admitted while labels are pending.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate a sequential canary decision budget under a degraded hypothesis.





engine.solvers.operations.SequentialCanaryModel.solve(
    p_base,
    p_degraded,
    alpha,
    beta,
    arrival_rate,
    fraction,
    label_delay,
)
Estimate a sequential canary decision budget under a degraded hypothesis.











Name
Type
Description
Default




p_base
float
Baseline acceptance probability strictly between zero and one.
required


p_degraded
float
Degraded acceptance probability strictly between zero and p_base.
required


alpha
float
False-hold probability target strictly between zero and one.
required


beta
float
Missed-degradation probability target strictly between zero and one; alpha + beta should be below one.
required


arrival_rate
Quantity
Positive eligible-task arrival rate in inverse time.
required


fraction
float
Candidate exposure fraction in (0, 1].
required


label_delay
Quantity
Nonnegative fixed delay between task admission and label availability.
required














Name
Type
Description





SequentialCanaryResult
Log-likelihood increments and thresholds, expected labeled-task count, candidate rate, admission/decision time in hours, pending labels, and expected excess failures.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_sprt_boundaries : Set log-likelihood stopping boundaries. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_sprt_expected_samples : Estimate stopping samples from evidence drift.



Equation: success_step = log(p_degraded/p_base); failure_step = log((1-p_degraded)/(1-p_base)); drift is their degraded-probability weighted mean. Expected samples = ((1-beta)*upper + beta*lower)/drift; admission_time = expected_samples/(arrival_rate*fraction).
Assumptions: Independent Bernoulli verdicts, fixed simple hypotheses, steady task arrivals, and Wald’s no-overshoot expected-stopping approximation.
Excludes: Threshold overshoot corrections, correlated verdicts, time-varying acceptance, and queueing in the labeling service. No trial labels are generated by this solver.



Derivation: The Bernoulli likelihood ratio adds one log increment per observed verdict. Dividing approximate terminal log evidence by expected drift estimates sample count; arrivals during label delay add exposure.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = SequentialCanaryModel().solve(0.9, 0.8, 0.05, 0.1,
...     Q_(100,"1/hour"), 0.1, Q_(1,"hour"))
>>> r.expected_samples > 0 and r.decision_time > r.admission_time
True






engine.solvers.operations.SpanCriticalPathModel()
One trial’s spans on a shared clock: what they explain, and what one shorter span saves.
Each span has an observed interval and the spans it waits for. Summing every span counts overlapping work twice; the critical path (calc_cleanup_critical_path) counts the longest dependent chain once. The elapsed segment less that path is time no span explains. For an intervention, every span keeps its observed wait after its predecessors (the unexplained gap stays where it was) and takes its new duration.





Name
Description




solve
Explain elapsed time using dependent spans and a duration intervention.





engine.solvers.operations.SpanCriticalPathModel.solve(
    intervals,
    depends_on,
    intervention,
)
Explain elapsed time using dependent spans and a duration intervention.











Name
Type
Description
Default




intervals
mapping of str to sequence of Quantity
Nonempty mapping from span names to (start, end) times on a shared clock; end must not precede start.
required


depends_on
mapping of str to sequence of str
Acyclic predecessor graph using known span names; observed starts must respect dependencies.
required


intervention
mapping of str to Quantity
Replacement nonnegative durations for selected spans; omitted spans keep their observed duration.
required














Name
Type
Description





SpanCriticalPathResult
Sum of span durations, dependency critical path, observed elapsed time, unexplained gap, intervened elapsed time, and saving in seconds; changed_critical lists the limiting span chain.






mlsysim.physics.agents.calc_cleanup_critical_path : Evaluate the longest dependent span chain.



Equation: path[k] = duration[k] + max(path[p] for predecessors p); gap[k] = start[k] - max(end[p], default=global_start); changed_finish[k] = max(changed_finish[p], default=0) + gap[k] + new_duration[k].
Assumptions: Observed predecessor waits remain fixed after intervention; durations change without altering the dependency graph.
Excludes: Resource contention, new dependencies, and causal effects of an intervention on other spans. The result is an accounting counterfactual, not a measured speedup.



Derivation: The longest-path recurrence counts overlapping branches once on the completion path. Retaining each observed dependency gap isolates the stated duration change.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = SpanCriticalPathModel().solve({"a": (Q_(0,"s"), Q_(2,"s"))}, {}, {"a": Q_(1,"s")})
>>> r.saving == Q_(1, "s")
True






engine.solvers.operations.TraceRetentionModel()
Diagnostic trace bodies kept over a window under three selections.
Keeping every body stores the whole cohort. Head sampling keeps each trial with one probability, decided before its outcome, so it keeps that share of the failures too. Verdict-aware (tail) selection keeps every failed and unresolved trial and a random control share of the ordinary ones; its volume is a floor set by the failure-plus-unresolved rate plus a term linear in the control share. Classes are disjoint and every body has the same size.





Name
Description




solve
Compare trace storage under full, head, and verdict-aware selection.





engine.solvers.operations.TraceRetentionModel.solve(
    failed,
    unresolved,
    ordinary,
    cohort_period,
    trace_size,
    window,
    head_probability,
    control_probability,
    control_step,
)
Compare trace storage under full, head, and verdict-aware selection.











Name
Type
Description
Default




failed
float
Nonnegative failed-trial count per cohort.
required


unresolved
float
Nonnegative unresolved-trial count per cohort; disjoint from failed.
required


ordinary
float
Nonnegative ordinary-trial count per cohort; disjoint from both other classes.
required


cohort_period
Quantity
Positive duration of one cohort.
required


trace_size
Quantity
Nonnegative bytes per retained trace body.
required


window
Quantity
Nonnegative retention-window duration.
required


head_probability
float
Probability in [0, 1] of keeping a trial independently of verdict.
required


control_probability
float
Probability in [0, 1] of retaining an ordinary control under tail selection.
required


control_step
float
Nonnegative increment in control probability used for marginal storage accounting.
required














Name
Type
Description





TraceRetentionResult
Expected retained counts, storage volumes in GB, full-to-tail ratio, verdict-required storage floor, and volume for control_step.






Equation: trials = failed + unresolved + ordinary; head_count = trials  head_probability; tail_count = failed + unresolved + ordinary  control_probability; volume = count * window/cohort_period * trace_size.
Assumptions: Disjoint verdict classes, identical body size, stationary cohort rates, and positive tail volume for the reported ratio.
Excludes: Trace compression, indexing metadata, variable body sizes, and verdict errors.



Derivation: Expected sampled counts are population counts times retention probabilities. Storage is expected count times body size across the number of cohorts in the retention window.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = TraceRetentionModel().solve(2, 1, 7, Q_(1,"day"), Q_(1,"MB"),
...     Q_(1,"day"), 0.5, 0.0, 0.1)
>>> r.tail_count == 3 and r.tail_volume == r.floor_volume
True

Type
Description

Sum of span durations, dependency critical path, observed elapsed time, unexplained gap, intervened elapsed time, and saving in seconds; changed_critical lists the limiting span chain.






mlsysim.physics.agents.calc_cleanup_critical_path : Evaluate the longest dependent span chain.



Equation: path[k] = duration[k] + max(path[p] for predecessors p); gap[k] = start[k] - max(end[p], default=global_start); changed_finish[k] = max(changed_finish[p], default=0) + gap[k] + new_duration[k].
Assumptions: Observed predecessor waits remain fixed after intervention; durations change without altering the dependency graph.
Excludes: Resource contention, new dependencies, and causal effects of an intervention on other spans. The result is an accounting counterfactual, not a measured speedup.



Derivation: The longest-path recurrence counts overlapping branches once on the completion path. Retaining each observed dependency gap isolates the stated duration change.

>>> r = SpanCriticalPathModel().solve({"a": (Q_(0,"s"), Q_(2,"s"))}, {}, {"a": Q_(1,"s")})

True






engine.solvers.operations.TraceRetentionModel()
Diagnostic trace bodies kept over a window under three selections.
Keeping every body stores the whole cohort. Head sampling keeps each trial with one probability, decided before its outcome, so it keeps that share of the failures too. Verdict-aware (tail) selection keeps every failed and unresolved trial and a random control share of the ordinary ones; its volume is a floor set by the failure-plus-unresolved rate plus a term linear in the control share. Classes are disjoint and every body has the same size.





Name
Description




solve
Compare trace storage under full, head, and verdict-aware selection.

    control_probability,
    control_step,
)

required

required
