required














Name
Type
Description





TraceRetentionResult
Expected retained counts, storage volumes in GB, full-to-tail ratio, verdict-required storage floor, and volume for control_step.






Equation: trials = failed + unresolved + ordinary; head_count = trials  head_probability; tail_count = failed + unresolved + ordinary  control_probability; volume = count * window/cohort_period * trace_size.
Assumptions: Disjoint verdict classes, identical body size, stationary cohort rates, and positive tail volume for the reported ratio.
Excludes: Trace compression, indexing metadata, variable body sizes, and verdict errors.



Derivation: Expected sampled counts are population counts times retention probabilities. Storage is expected count times body size across the number of cohorts in the retention window.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = TraceRetentionModel().solve(2, 1, 7, Q_(1,"day"), Q_(1,"MB"),
...     Q_(1,"day"), 0.5, 0.0, 0.1)
>>> r.tail_count == 3 and r.tail_volume == r.floor_volume
True

title: models.types.Workload
text:
models.types.Workload()
Layer A (Workload Demand): Base representation of an ML model or task.
A Workload defines the computational requirements of a task without any knowledge of the hardware it will run on. It must implement lower() to project its architectural definition down into a ComputationGraph.
inference_flops semantics — the unit of work DIFFERS BY MODEL FAMILY (documented 2026-06-06; the field is dimensioned only as flop, so the family convention is the contract):

Autoregressive LMs (TransformerWorkload decoder-only, SparseTransformerWorkload): FLOPs per generated token, following the 2 x params convention — 2 x TOTAL params for dense models, 2 x ACTIVE params for MoE.
Encoder models (BERT-family): FLOPs per sequence at the reference sequence length recorded in the entry’s provenance (BERT-Base: 22 GFLOP at seq=128).
Vision / CNN / recommendation models: FLOPs per input (one image / one query forward pass).

NEVER compare inference_flops across families without normalizing — the magnitudes differ by orders of magnitude purely from the work unit.





Name
Description




lower
Project stored workload facts into a computation graph.


size_in_bytes
Calculate stored model weights at the requested precision.





models.types.Workload.lower(precision=BYTES_FP16)
Project stored workload facts into a computation graph.











Name
Type
Description
Default




precision
Quantity or str
Bytes per stored element, or a registered format such as ‘fp16’. A byte quantity specifies the width directly; it must be positive.
BYTES_FP16














Name
Type
Description





ComputationGraph
Work in FLOPs, resident weight bytes, parameter count, arithmetic intensity in FLOP/byte, and the available layer count.






Equation: W = P * b and I = F / W. F uses inference_flops when supplied; otherwise F = 2 * P. If P is absent but model_size exists, W = model_size, P = 0, and missing FLOPs become zero.
Assumptions: one graph represents the work unit described by the workload family. With parameter count present, this base implementation computes W from P and b rather than preferring model_size. A zero-byte size-only workload has zero arithmetic intensity by convention.
Excludes: activation or cache storage, backward work, hardware efficiency, and precision-dependent operation counts. The 2P fallback is an approximation, not a graph trace.



Derivation: multiply parameter count by storage width to obtain weight bytes, then divide the declared or approximated work by those bytes. This is a demand-accounting projection; it does not predict device time.



>>> from mlsysim.models.types import Workload
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> model = Workload(name='Example', architecture='dense', parameters=Q_(100, 'count'))
>>> graph = model.lower('fp16')
>>> graph.weight_bytes == model.parameters.magnitude * Q_(2, 'byte')
True




models.types.Workload.size_in_bytes(precision=BYTES_FP16)
Calculate stored model weights at the requested precision.











Name
Type
Description
Default




precision
Quantity or str
Bytes per stored element, or a registered format such as ‘fp16’. A byte quantity specifies the width directly; it must be positive.
BYTES_FP16














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Resident weight size with data units, normally bytes. A supplied model_size retains its original compatible units when returned.






Equation: W = P * b when parameter count P is available. A supplied model_size takes precedence at FP16/BF16; if P is missing it is used at every precision because there is no count from which to rescale.
Assumptions: all parameters use one element width. An explicit model_size is an authoritative footprint at the default storage format. Without parameters or model_size, the method raises NotImplementedError.
Excludes: gradients, optimizer states, activations, KV caches, quantization scales, packing alignment, and allocator reserve.



Derivation: multiply the number of stored elements by bytes per element. The model_size precedence is an implementation convention for workloads whose stored footprint is known but whose parameter inventory is absent.



>>> from mlsysim.models.types import Workload
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> model = Workload(name='Example', architecture='dense', parameters=Q_(100, 'count'))
>>> model.size_in_bytes('fp16') == 2 * model.size_in_bytes('int8')
True

title: engine.solvers.durability
text:
engine.solvers.durability
Durable-execution solvers: what a runtime pays to survive a crash (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated inputs: one group commit’s work and waits, the bytes full snapshots and deltas write, checkpoint strides priced on a fixed crash trace with Young’s balance in turns, and the cost of keeping a trajectory’s recovery and replay data. None models a particular storage engine or workflow runtime.





Name
Description




CheckpointTraceModel
Checkpoint strides priced on one fixed crash trace, against Young’s balance in turns.


GroupCommitModel
Storage work per record against the wait each record sees in one group commit.


RetentionCostModel
What keeping one trajectory’s recovery and replay data costs, against one attempt.


SnapshotVolumeModel
Bytes written by full snapshots and by deltas over one monotonically growing trajectory.





engine.solvers.durability.CheckpointTraceModel()
Checkpoint strides priced on one fixed crash trace, against Young’s balance in turns.
A policy checkpoints at every multiple of its stride (and at the final turn). A crash after turn c restores the last checkpoint and rebuilds the c mod stride turns since it from the log; the policy’s total is its checkpoint pauses plus the restores plus the rebuilt turns. The balance stride sqrt(2 pause / (rate * cost)) uses the trace’s crash rate, once with the cost of rebuilding a logged turn and once with the cost of re-executing an unlogged one.





Name
Description




solve
Price checkpoint strides on a supplied crash trace.





engine.solvers.durability.CheckpointTraceModel.solve(
    turns,
    crashes,
    strides,
    pause,
    restore,
    rebuild_per_turn,
    reexecute_per_turn,
)
Price checkpoint strides on a supplied crash trace.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Positive trajectory length in turns.
required


crashes
sequence of int
Nonempty crash positions in [0, turns], interpreted after the indicated turn.
required


strides
sequence of int
Nonempty positive checkpoint spacings to compare.
required


pause
Quantity
Positive pause to capture one checkpoint.
required


restore
Quantity
Nonnegative fixed restore time per crash.
required


rebuild_per_turn
Quantity
Positive time to rebuild one lost turn from a log.
required


reexecute_per_turn
Quantity
Positive time to re-execute one lost turn without the log.
required














Name
Type
Description





CheckpointTraceResult
Per-stride pause/recovery/total seconds and lost-turn counts, cheapest candidate, and continuous balance strides in turns.






mlsysim.physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_stride : Compute the continuous pause/rework balance.



Equation: Lost turns at crash c for stride k = c mod k. Total time equals checkpoint_count*pause + crash_count*restore + lost_turns*rebuild. Continuous balance stride = sqrt(2*pause/(crash_rate*turn_cost)).
Assumptions: Every candidate sees the same trace; capture occurs at stride multiples and at the final turn. The balance uses crashes/turns as a rate.
Excludes: Failures during checkpoint or recovery, checkpoint corruption, and a probabilistic guarantee about future traces.



Young (1974), “A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval.” https://doi.org/10.1145/361147.361115 (bibliography key: young1974). The continuous balance minimizes pause/k + crash_rate*turn_cost*k/2.
Derivation: Count every scheduled pause, fixed restore, and rebuilt turn on the supplied trace. For the continuous comparison, minimizing pause/k + crash_rate*turn_cost*k/2 gives the square-root balance; this is a separate expected-loss approximation, not the discrete trace optimum.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import CheckpointTraceModel
>>> r = CheckpointTraceModel().solve(8, [3], [1, 2], Q_(1, "s"),
...     Q_(1, "s"), Q_(1, "s"), Q_(2, "s"))
>>> assert r.best_stride in r.total_time






engine.solvers.durability.GroupCommitModel()
Storage work per record against the wait each record sees in one group commit.
One flush acknowledges batch_size records; the work charged to each falls as flush / batch_size, but every record still waits the whole flush, and the first arrival also waits the batch timer. Amortization raises throughput; it never shortens one record’s wait.





Name
Description




solve
Separate amortized flush work from the first and last record waits.





engine.solvers.durability.GroupCommitModel.solve(
    batch_timer,
    flush_time,
    batch_size,
)
Separate amortized flush work from the first and last record waits.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_timer
Quantity
Nonnegative collection interval before the flush begins.
required


flush_time
Quantity
Nonnegative duration of one synchronous flush.
required


batch_size
int
Positive record count acknowledged by the flush.
required














Name
Type
Description





GroupCommitResult
Amortized work per record and first/last record waits, all time quantities.






mlsysim.physics.reliability.calc_group_commit_waits : Compute the amortized work and per-arrival waits.



Equation: Work per record = flush_time/batch_size; first wait = timer + flush; last wait = flush_time.
Assumptions: The first record arrives when collection starts and the last arrives when the flush begins; one flush acknowledges the whole batch.
Excludes: Queueing between groups, variable flush duration, and partial acknowledgments.



Derivation: Divide the shared flush work among the acknowledged records. The first arrival waits for collection and flushing; the last arrival waits only for flushing, independent of that amortized work.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import GroupCommitModel
>>> r = GroupCommitModel().solve(Q_(1, "ms"), Q_(2, "ms"), 4)
>>> assert r.first_wait >= r.last_wait >= r.work_per_record






engine.solvers.durability.RetentionCostModel()
What keeping one trajectory’s recovery and replay data costs, against one attempt.
The log is turns * (envelope + payload); one workspace snapshot is added; the total is priced at an object-storage rate for the retention period and compared with the cost of one attempt.





Name
Description




solve
Price recovery logs and one workspace snapshot over a retention period.





engine.solvers.durability.RetentionCostModel.solve(
    turns,
    envelope,
    payload,
    workspace,
    rate,
    period,
    attempt_cost,
)
Price recovery logs and one workspace snapshot over a retention period.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Nonnegative number of retained trajectory turns.
required


envelope
Quantity
Nonnegative metadata bytes per turn.
required


payload
Quantity
Nonnegative payload bytes per turn.
required


workspace
Quantity
Nonnegative bytes in one workspace snapshot; total retained bytes must be positive.
required


rate
Quantity
Nonnegative storage price in currency/(byte*time).
required


period
Quantity
Nonnegative retention duration.
required


attempt_cost
Quantity
Positive cost of one attempt, in currency.
required














Name
Type
Description





RetentionCostResult
Log and total bytes, USD cost quantities, and dimensionless cost and workspace shares.






Equation: Log bytes = turns*(envelope+payload); total = log + workspace; cost = total*rate*period; attempt share = cost/attempt_cost.
Assumptions: All retained bytes live for the full period at a uniform rate. One workspace snapshot accompanies the per-turn log.
Excludes: Replication, retrieval charges, tier changes, and deletion overhead.



Derivation: Add per-turn envelope and payload bytes across the trajectory, then add the single workspace snapshot. Byte-time times unit storage price gives the retention cost; divide by attempt cost to express its share.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import RetentionCostModel
>>> r = RetentionCostModel().solve(2, Q_(1, "byte"), Q_(2, "byte"),
...     Q_(3, "byte"), Q_(1, "USD/GB/day"), Q_(1, "day"), Q_(1, "USD"))
>>> assert r.total_bytes >= r.log_bytes






engine.solvers.durability.SnapshotVolumeModel()
Bytes written by full snapshots and by deltas over one monotonically growing trajectory.
turns // stride checkpoints; full snapshots grow with the square of the checkpoint count, deltas linearly, so the ratio is (n + 1) / 2.





Name
Description




solve
Compare full-snapshot and incremental-delta checkpoint write volume.





engine.solvers.durability.SnapshotVolumeModel.solve(turns, stride, state_growth)
Compare full-snapshot and incremental-delta checkpoint write volume.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Nonnegative completed trajectory turns; must contain at least one stride.
required


stride
int
Positive checkpoint spacing in turns.
required


state_growth
Quantity
Positive added state bytes per turn.
required














Name
Type
Description





SnapshotVolumeResult
Checkpoint count, full and incremental byte totals, and their dimensionless ratio.






mlsysim.physics.reliability.calc_snapshot_write_volume : Sum full snapshots and incremental deltas.



Equation: N = floor(turns/stride); full = growth*stride*N*(N+1)/2; delta = growth*stride*N.
Assumptions: State starts empty and grows by equal bytes every turn. Only complete strides are checkpointed; no final partial-stride save is added.
Excludes: State deletion, compression, metadata, and checkpoint service time.



Derivation: Full snapshots contain one, two, and then up to N strides of new state; summing this arithmetic progression gives N*(N+1)/2 strides. Deltas contain one stride each, for N strides in total.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SnapshotVolumeModel
>>> r = SnapshotVolumeModel().solve(4, 2, Q_(1, "MB"))
>>> assert r.full_bytes >= r.delta_bytes

mlsysim.physics.reliability.calc_snapshot_write_volume : Sum full snapshots and incremental deltas.



Equation: N = floor(turns/stride); full = growth*stride*N*(N+1)/2; delta = growth*stride*N.
Assumptions: State starts empty and grows by equal bytes every turn. Only complete strides are checkpointed; no final partial-stride save is added.
Excludes: State deletion, compression, metadata, and checkpoint service time.



Derivation: Full snapshots contain one, two, and then up to N strides of new state; summing this arithmetic progression gives N*(N+1)/2 strides. Deltas contain one stride each, for N strides in total.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SnapshotVolumeModel
>>> r = SnapshotVolumeModel().solve(4, 2, Q_(1, "MB"))
>>> assert r.full_bytes >= r.delta_bytes

One recommender request on hardware: one row of width values per categorical feature of dataset is gathered, then the rows and the bottom MLP’s output interact by pairwise dot products.

title: engine.solvers.kv_cache
text:
engine.solvers.kv_cache
KV cache management solvers: what retained attention state costs a serving node.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on a model’s KV geometry and a node’s registry specs: the per-token payload and the pool left after the weights, the bytes per token each attention design keeps, full-cap reservation against paged blocks, the prefill a prefix hit avoids, chunked prefill against a monolithic one, keeping, moving, or dropping a paused request’s state, and block-rounded resident fit turned into a turn rate by Little’s law. None models attention traffic during a pass, link contention, or an engine’s scheduler; every rate is a memory-only or weight-only bound.





Name
Description




ChunkedPrefillModel
The decode gap a new prompt causes, run whole or in chunks.


KvAttentionDesignModel
Bytes each token keeps under multi-head, grouped-query, and latent attention.


KvBlockSharingModel
Block-rounded resident fit with and without a shared prefix, as a turn rate.


KvResidencyArchetypeModel
Sharing gain, residency tax, and resume cost for one agent workload.


PagedAllocationModel
Full-cap reservation against fixed-size blocks allocated on demand.


PausedKvStateModel
Keep, move, or drop a paused request’s KV state during a tool wait.


PrefixRebuildModel
The prefill a prefix-cache hit avoids, against one short suffix pass.





engine.solvers.kv_cache.ChunkedPrefillModel()
The decode gap a new prompt causes, run whole or in chunks.
T(N) = max(T_weights, 2 P N / R)
Run whole, the prompt sits between two decode steps, so every ongoing stream waits T(decodes) + T(prompt). Chunked, each iteration runs one chunk beside the decodes, so the gap is T(chunk + decodes) and the prompt finishes after prompt / chunk iterations. Weight work only.





Name
Description




solve
Compare monolithic and chunked weight-only prefill intervals.





engine.solvers.kv_cache.ChunkedPrefillModel.solve(
    n_params,
    sustained_rate,
    weight_read_time,
    decodes,
    prompt_tokens,
    chunk_tokens,
)
Compare monolithic and chunked weight-only prefill intervals.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_params
Quantity
Positive model parameter count in param.
required


sustained_rate
Quantity
Positive declared sustained compute rate in FLOP/s.
required


weight_read_time
Quantity
Nonnegative time to read model weights once.
required


decodes
int
Nonnegative active decode tokens per iteration.
required


prompt_tokens
int
Positive prompt length, evenly divisible by chunk_tokens.
required


chunk_tokens
int
Positive prefill chunk length in tokens.
required














Name
Type
Description





ChunkedPrefillResult
Decode and prefill time quantities, complete chunk count, total chunked duration, and monolithic-to-chunked gap ratio. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: T(n) = max(weight_read_time, 2P*n / rate); chunks = prompt_tokens // chunk_tokens; done = chunks * T(chunk_tokens+decodes).
Assumptions: Prompt tokens divide evenly into positive chunks; each iteration shares weight reads.
Excludes: Attention work, residual partial chunks, dispatch overhead, and scheduling variation.



Derivation: T(n) = max(weight_read_time, 2P*n / rate); chunks = prompt_tokens // chunk_tokens; done = chunks * T(chunk_tokens+decodes). This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ChunkedPrefillModel
>>> ChunkedPrefillModel().solve(Q_('1000 param'), Q_('1 GFLOP/s'), Q_('1 ms'), 1, 16, 4).chunks == 4
True

Bytes each token keeps under multi-head, grouped-query, and latent attention.
The design is fixed in pretraining: MHA stores a key and value per query head, GQA shares each stored head among a group, and MLA stores one compressed latent per layer. Parameter count does not enter.





Name
Description

    gqa,
    mla,
    precision,

)

KvAttentionDesignResult
Bytes per token and attention-design labels keyed by workload name, dimensionless comparison ratios, and session-state byte quantities. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: session_bytes = per_token_bytes * session_tokens; ratios divide MHA or GQA per-token bytes by MLA bytes.
Assumptions: Named comparison models are present in models and their KV geometry is defined.
Excludes: Weights, activations, allocator reserve, and attention execution time.



Derivation: session_bytes = per_token_bytes * session_tokens; ratios divide MHA or GQA per-token bytes by MLA bytes. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.

engine.solvers.kv_cache.KvBlockSharingModel()
Block-rounded resident fit with and without a shared prefix, as a turn rate.
B = floor(N_blocks / N_req),   B_shared = floor((N_blocks - N_common) / N_private)
lambda = B / W,   W = T_gen (+ T_wait if the state is kept)
Each request reserves its input and output allowance in whole blocks; a fraction of the pool is withheld as headroom. The gain from sharing approaches 1 / (1 - f) in a large pool.





Name
Description




solve
Turn block-rounded KV residency into a memory-limited turn rate.





engine.solvers.kv_cache.KvBlockSharingModel.solve(
    bytes_per_token,
    pool,
    headroom,
    context,
    output,
    common,
    block_tokens,
    generation,
    wait,
)
Turn block-rounded KV residency into a memory-limited turn rate.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive bytes retained per token across all layers.
required


pool
Quantity
Positive bytes available for KV state.
required

float
Pool fraction withheld, between zero and one (exclusive of one).
required

required

required

required

required

Quantity

required














Name
Type
Description





KvBlockSharingResult
Block-rounded byte counts and resident counts, retained duration, turn rates, and dimensionless residency and sharing factors. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: fit = usable_blocks // request_blocks; shared_fit = (usable_blocks-common_blocks) // private_blocks; rate = fit / residence_time.
Assumptions: Common prefix stored once, positive private state and generation time, and sufficient pool for one request.
Excludes: Actual serving throughput, scheduler contention, and fragmentation beyond block rounding.



Derivation: fit = usable_blocks // request_blocks; shared_fit = (usable_blocks-common_blocks) // private_blocks; rate = fit / residence_time. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import KvBlockSharingModel
>>> KvBlockSharingModel().solve(Q_('1 KB'), Q_('1 GB'), 0.1, 16, 8, 4, 4, Q_('1 s'), Q_('1 s')).fit_shared >= 1

Sharing gain, residency tax, and resume cost for one agent workload.
Unrounded resident fit with a shared prefix stored once; the residency tax 1 + T_wait / T_gen; and the two resume paths for a dropped or moved state, recompute 2 P S / R against reload S m_token / B_link.

Type

Default

required

KvResidencyArchetypeResult
Resident counts, sharing and residency factors, cycle/recompute seconds, reload milliseconds, and retained/released turn rates. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: fit_shared = floor((pool-shared_prefix*bytes_per_token)/((context-shared_prefix)*bytes_per_token)); cycle = generation+wait; recompute = 2P*context/rate.
Assumptions: Shared prefix shorter than context, positive rates, and enough pool for one request.
Excludes: Block rounding, attention recomputation, contention, and execution-capacity limits.



Derivation: fit_shared = floor((pool-shared_prefix*bytes_per_token)/((context-shared_prefix)*bytes_per_token)); cycle = generation+wait; recompute = 2P*context/rate. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.

engine.solvers.kv_cache.PagedAllocationModel()
Full-cap reservation against fixed-size blocks allocated on demand.
A reservation holds S_max slots from admission; a request ending at a mean of S_mean tokens fills S_mean / S_max of it. Paged blocks waste at most the unused tail of the last block; under capped exponential final lengths (a modeling assumption, calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens) the expected allocation sets a final-length snapshot count, not a live admission capacity.





Name
Description




solve
Compare full-context reservation with expected block allocation.





engine.solvers.kv_cache.PagedAllocationModel.solve(
    bytes_per_token,
    pool,
    cap,
    mean_final,
    small_block,
    large_block,
)
Compare full-context reservation with expected block allocation.











Name
Type
Description
Default




bytes_per_token
Quantity
Positive bytes retained per token across all layers.
required


pool
Quantity
Positive bytes available for KV state.
required


cap
int
Positive maximum request length in tokens.
required


mean_final
int
Positive mean final token count below the cap.
required


small_block
int
Positive smaller allocation block size in tokens.
required


large_block
int
Positive larger allocation block size in tokens.
required














Name
Type
Description





PagedAllocationResult
Reserved bytes and request counts, expected allocated token counts, wasted fractions, block-tail bytes, and dimensionless residency gain. Bounds are conditional on the stated assumptions, not deployment guarantees.






Equation: reservation = cap * bytes_per_token; fit = floor(pool / allocation_bytes); efficiency = mean_final / cap.
Assumptions: Capped exponential final lengths and positive blocks; pool holds at least one full reservation.
Excludes: Live scheduler admission, fragmentation between requests, and transient growth.



Derivation: reservation = cap * bytes_per_token; fit = floor(pool / allocation_bytes); efficiency = mean_final / cap. This combines the supplied quantities by conservation of traffic or residence time; it is an analytical accounting model.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import PagedAllocationModel
>>> PagedAllocationModel().solve(Q_('1 KB'), Q_('1 GB'), 128, 32, 8, 16).reservations > 0
True






engine.solvers.kv_cache.PausedKvStateModel()
Keep, move, or drop a paused request’s KV state during a tool wait.
T_reload = M / (n B_link),   T_recompute = 2 P S / R
Both grow linearly with the context, so their ratio does not depend on length. Keeping holds M x T_wait of memory time; moving frees the memory for the wait less the copy-out (on demand) or less the round trip (prefetch). Correlated returns serialize on the shared links.





Name
Description




solve
Compare keeping, copying, and rebuilding paused KV state.

    bytes_per_token,
    n_params,
    sustained_rate,
    link,
    context_tokens,
    block_tokens,

engine.solvers.kv_cache.ChunkedPrefillModel()
The decode gap a new prompt causes, run whole or in chunks.
T(N) = max(T_weights, 2 P N / R)
Run whole, the prompt sits between two decode steps, so every ongoing stream waits T(decodes) + T(prompt). Chunked, each iteration runs one chunk beside the decodes, so the gap is T(chunk + decodes) and the prompt finishes after prompt / chunk iterations. Weight work only.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A shared platform costing platform_cost per month that saves each of models model teams hours_saved per month at engineer_rate.


Equation: Gross monthly value is models*hours_saved*engineer_rate; net benefit subtracts platform_cost.

title: solvers.InferenceScalingModel
text:
solvers.InferenceScalingModel()
Models inference-time compute scaling (Wall 12: Reasoning/CoT Cost).
This model quantifies the cost of ‘System-2 thinking’ — inference-time compute scaling via chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, where the model generates K intermediate reasoning steps before producing the final answer. Each step incurs the full cost of autoregressive decoding.
Literature Source: 1. Wei et al. (2022), “Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models.” 2. Snell et al. (2024), “Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective Than Scaling Model Parameters.” 3. OpenAI (2024), “Learning to Reason with LLMs.” (o1 reasoning model.)

Total reasoning time, TDP-based energy per query in joules, and token counts.






ServingModel.solve : Prefill, decode, and memory feasibility.



Equation: generated_tokens = K*N_step; T = TTFT + K*N_step*ITL; energy = TDP*T when TDP is available, otherwise zero is returned. N_step is the declared TOKENS_PER_REASONING_STEP calibration default.
Assumptions: nonnegative reasoning-step count, fixed context for every decode step, and the batch-one ServingModel assumptions. Excludes: reasoning-quality prediction, growing contexts, verification work, measured power, and price. Feasibility is inherited from serving; a computed duration for an infeasible configuration is not deployable.



Derivation: multiply a supplied step count by an assumed token budget and per-token latency, then add one prefill. Energy uses a TDP-time proxy; neither token budget nor power is a measured workload trace.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Models
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import InferenceScalingModel

>>> a = solver.solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Hardware.Cloud.H100, reasoning_steps=1)
>>> b = solver.solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Hardware.Cloud.H100, reasoning_steps=2)
>>> bool(b.tokens_generated == 2*a.tokens_generated and b.total_reasoning_time > a.total_reasoning_time)
True

title: DenseLayerScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One dense layer: in_features inputs to out_features outputs, bytes_per_weight each.


Equation: A matrix with n inputs and m outputs has n*m weights; a batch costs 2*B*n*m FLOPs.
Assumptions: Dense multiplication, one weight read shared by the batch, and one read/write of activations in the traffic variant.
Excludes: Cache hierarchy, bias/activation FLOPs, and kernel scheduling; target-intensity inversions require a positive denominator.



Derivation: Every output dot product reads n weights, so m outputs require n*m weights and MACs per example. Counting one multiply and one add per MAC gives 2*B*n*m FLOPs. The traffic variant separately counts input reads, shared weight reads, and output writes.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.MnistMlpFirstLayer
>>> s.variant(batch_size=2*s.batch_size).flops == 2*s.flops
True

title: DenseLayerScenario
text:
Equation: A matrix with n inputs and m outputs has n*m weights; a batch costs 2*B*n*m FLOPs.
Assumptions: Dense multiplication, one weight read shared by the batch, and one read/write of activations in the traffic variant.
Excludes: Cache hierarchy, bias/activation FLOPs, and kernel scheduling; target-intensity inversions require a positive denominator.

title: DenseLayerScenario
text: Derivation: Every output dot product reads n weights, so m outputs require n*m weights and MACs per example. Counting one multiply and one add per MAC gives 2*B*n*m FLOPs. The traffic variant separately counts input reads, shared weight reads, and output writes.

>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.MnistMlpFirstLayer
>>> s.variant(batch_size=2*s.batch_size).flops == 2*s.flops
True

title: engine.solvers.estimation
text:
engine.solvers.estimation
Spatial-memory solvers: state estimation, estimator consistency, drift, and belief expiry (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. The equations live in physics/robotics/estimation.py, physics/robotics/perception.py, physics/robotics/sensing.py, and physics/statistics.py; these models compose them for one stated estimator, sensor, benchmark, or belief, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic.





Name
Description




BeliefExpiryModel
A belief’s error bound E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2, its invalidation horizon, and an admission check.


EpochGapModel
Travel across the gap between two acquisition epochs, speed x \|t2 - t1\|.


EstimatorConsistencyModel
The band a campaign’s mean NEES or NIS must fall in, and what single-update gates catch.


FreeSpaceExpiryModel
Occluded free space eroding inward at the approach speed v_h, ahead and abreast of an occluder.


FrozenTransformModel
A last transform republished every republish_period with fresh stamps while the object moves.


InertialCoastModel
An IMU integrated open loop for duration, with the heading offset seen at target_range.


OdometryDriftModel
A benchmark’s return error over its path as a drift rate, before and after calibration.


RangeFusionModel
One scalar predict and two updates of a range, and the same second update misdated.


ReplayBufferModel
Slots of a rewind buffer sampled at sample_rate that reach back horizon: ceil(horizon / dt).


SensorBiasDriftModel
A bias drifting at drift_rate for span under a steady reading: the true value is the reading less the shift.


StaleTransformModel
A cached sensor-to-target edge, one interval old, composed with the current wrist pose.





engine.solvers.estimation.BeliefExpiryModel()
A belief’s error bound E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2, its invalidation horizon, and an admission check.
The horizon is calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon; dropping the acceleration term gives the constant-velocity horizon, at which the true bound has already overrun the tolerance. With use_age, the consumer’s age bound is use_age + age_bound (the clock-conversion bound), and the belief is admitted if the error there is within tolerance; the latest admissible use age is the horizon less age_bound.

Description

)

Type

BeliefExpiryResult
Initial error and tolerance in millimeters, growth rates in millimeters per second, expiry times in milliseconds, and dimensionless overshoot. Use-time fields remain absent when use_age is None.






calc_belief_error_bound : Composed numerical primitive. calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: The horizon is calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon; dropping the acceleration term gives the constant-velocity horizon, at which the true bound has already overrun the tolerance. With use_age, the consumer’s age bound is use_age + age_bound (the clock-conversion bound), and the belief is admitted if the error there is within tolerance; the latest admissible use age is the horizon less age_bound.
Assumptions: Nonnegative error-growth terms bound the full interval; optional clock uncertainty is an additive upper bound on observation age.
Excludes: Stochastic cancellation, abrupt changes in motion, and measurement updates that would reset the initial error.



Derivation: Integrate a constant growth rate and acceleration to obtain E0+v*t+a*t*t/2; solve its first crossing of tolerance and subtract the clock-age bound for latest admissible use.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.estimation import BeliefExpiryModel
>>> result = BeliefExpiryModel().solve(initial_error=Q_('1 mm'), growth_rate=Q_('1 mm/s'), tolerance=Q_('2 mm'))
>>> bool(result.horizon.to("s").magnitude == 1)
True

calc_chi2_gate : Composed numerical primitive. calc_chi2_mean_band : Composed numerical primitive. calc_noncentral_gate_detection : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: calc_chi2_mean_band gives the band for runs statistics of dimension dimension; each gate is calc_chi2_gate at its confidence, and a biased update with mean NIS nis_expected exceeds it with calc_noncentral_gate_detection (noncentrality nis_expected - dimension).
Assumptions: Independent campaign statistics with the stated chi-square dimension; biased single-update statistics have the stated noncentrality.
Excludes: Temporal correlation, distribution misspecification, and guarantees that a finite campaign detects every inconsistent estimator.



Derivation: Independent chi-square statistics add their degrees of freedom. Divide sum-statistic quantiles by runs for the mean band; evaluate noncentral chi-square upper tails for biased gate exceedance.

>>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.estimation import EstimatorConsistencyModel
>>> result = EstimatorConsistencyModel().solve(runs=100, dimension=1, confidence=0.95, gate_confidences=[0.95], nis_expected=2)
>>> bool(result.band_low < result.band_high)
True

calc_free_space_expiry : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: Each horizon is calc_free_space_expiry; the observation age spends part of it before memory receives the frame. A walker approaching during a stop at speed covers v_h (tau_delay + v / a_brake).
Assumptions: Constant approach speed erodes free depth; localization and protective clearance are reserved before assigning an expiry time.
Excludes: Occluder shape changes, approach acceleration, and safety certification from a single free-space observation.



Derivation: Subtract localization and clearance from observed depth, floor remaining depth at zero, then divide by approach speed. During robot delay plus speed/braking stop time, a walker advances at the supplied approach speed.

calc_scalar_kalman_update : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: Prediction adds (sigma_v dt)^2; each update applies calc_scalar_kalman_update. A reading paired with the wrong pose is off by misdating_bias; the update moves the estimate g b while the reported spread, which uses only the modeled noise, is unchanged. Its innovation’s NIS has mean 1 + b^2 / S. comparison_scale reruns the second update with that sensor’s spread scaled.
Assumptions: Scalar linear observations with independent Gaussian noises; velocity uncertainty contributes independent variance during prediction.
Excludes: Correlated sensors, nonlinear range geometry, and changes in bias during the update sequence.



Derivation: Add independent variances for prediction, then apply K=P/(P+R) and P_post=(1-K)P. A deterministic observation bias shifts the posterior by Kb and adds b squared over innovation variance to NIS.

>>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.estimation import RangeFusionModel
>>> result = RangeFusionModel().solve(prior_sigma=Q_('2 mm'), speed_sigma=Q_('1 mm/s'), interval=Q_('1 s'), first_sigma=Q_('1 mm'), second_sigma=Q_('1 mm'), misdating_bias=Q_('1 mm'))
>>> bool(result.second_gain > 0)

calc_lever_arm_error : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: The finger error is the initial error, plus the unobserved drift over the interval v dt, plus the lever-arm swing l omega dt of the rotation the cached edge never saw. Composing the edge with the wrist pose of its own epoch removes the lever term and leaves the belief’s own bound.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.global_batch
Samples processed in one global iteration. Equation: workers * per_worker_batch. Units: samples; every worker contributes a full local batch.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.ideal_iterations
Iteration count under perfect sample-efficiency scaling. Equation: base_iterations / workers. Units: iterations; no quality degradation is assumed for this reference.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.iteration_time
Per-iteration time after the stated communication overhead. Equation: base_iteration_time * (1 + communication_overhead). Units: time; overhead is relative to base iteration time.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.speedup
Time-to-target speedup against the single-worker baseline. Equation: base_iterations / (iterations * (1 + communication_overhead)). Units: dimensionless; both runs use the same base iteration duration.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.sample_efficiency
Ideal iteration count divided by actual target-reaching iteration count. Equation: ideal_iterations / iterations. Units: dimensionless; target-reaching iterations are supplied, not predicted.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.cost
Rental bill for the modeled run. Equation: iterations times iteration duration times worker count times device-hour price. Units: USD returned as a scalar; workers are billed throughout the run.

title: SyncStrategyScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SyncStrategyScenario.stale_lr_factor
Illustrative learning-rate reduction for stale gradients. Equation: 1 / sqrt(1 + staleness). Units: dimensionless; this prescribed heuristic is not a convergence guarantee.

physics.economics.calc_detection_delay_loss(
    annual_value,
    quality_drop,
    delay,
    year_length=None,
)
Value lost while a quality drop goes undetected: V_year * drop * (delay / year).











Name
Type
Description
Default




annual_value
float or Quantity
Value produced in one reference year, in currency.
required


quality_drop
float
Fraction of value lost, in [0, 1].
required


delay
Quantity
Nonnegative detection delay, in time units.
required


year_length
Quantity
Positive reference-year duration; defaults to DAYS_PER_YEAR days.
None














Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Currency value lost during detection delay.






Equation: loss = annual_value * quality_drop * delay / year_length.
Assumptions: Value accrues uniformly and the quality loss is constant until detection.
Excludes: Recovery time after detection, seasonality, and nonlinear effects of quality.



Derivation: Prorate annual value by elapsed time and multiply by the lost fraction.



>>> calc_detection_delay_loss(100, 0.5, 365 * ureg.day)
50.0




physics.economics.calc_fleet_tco(unit_cost, power_w, quantity, years, kwh_price)
Total Cost of Ownership (CapEx + energy OpEx) for a hardware fleet.
Calculates the combined capital expenditure (hardware purchase) and operational expenditure (electricity) over a given lifespan.











Name
Type
Description
Default




unit_cost
Quantity
The purchase price of a single hardware unit (e.g., USD).
required


power_w
Quantity
The average active power consumption per unit (e.g., Watts).
required


quantity
int
The total number of units in the fleet.
required


years
Quantity or float
The total operating lifespan to cost out (NOT annualized — full CapEx is charged up front, no straight-line amortization). Bare floats are years of 365 days (8,760 hours, the convention every book LEGO cell uses).
required


kwh_price
Quantity
The local cost of electricity (e.g., $/kWh).
required









Name
Type
Description





float
The total cost of ownership in USD.






Equation: TCO = N * unit_cost + N * power * duration * electricity_price.
Assumptions: All devices draw the supplied average power throughout the duration; a year has 365 days.
Excludes: PUE, cooling, maintenance, discounting, and amortization. Use EconomicsModel for facility accounting.



Derivation: Capital and energy expenditures add; energy is power integrated over time.



>>> calc_fleet_tco(100, 0, 2, 1, 0.1)
200.0




physics.economics.calc_monthly_egress_cost(bytes_per_sec, cost_per_gb)
Calculate the monthly cloud egress cost for sustained bandwidth usage.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
The sustained continuous data transfer rate (e.g., Bytes/s).
required


cost_per_gb
Quantity
The egress pricing tier from the cloud provider (e.g., $/GB).
required









Name
Type
Description





float
The total monthly cost in USD.






Equation: C = bandwidth * (30 days) * price per byte.
Assumptions: Constant transfer rate and linear pricing for a 30-day month.
Excludes: Calendar-month length, free tiers, and tiered discounts.



Derivation: Multiplying transferred volume by a per-volume price gives cost.



>>> calc_monthly_egress_cost(0, 1)
0.0




physics.economics.calc_optimal_retraining_interval(run_cost, staleness_slope)
Interval that minimizes calc_retraining_cost_rate: T* = sqrt(2 C / s).











Name
Type
Description
Default




run_cost
float or Quantity
Positive currency cost of one retraining run.
required


staleness_slope
float or Quantity
Positive growth of loss rate, in currency/time squared.
required














Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Optimal cycle length, in the time units implied by the inputs.






Equation: T = sqrt(2 * run_cost / staleness_slope).
Assumptions: Positive run cost and slope; training restores the reference quality each cycle.
Excludes: Operational scheduling constraints, downtime, and nonlinear drift.



Derivation: Set the derivative of C/T + sT/2 to zero; the positive stationary point minimizes the cost.



>>> calc_optimal_retraining_interval(4, 2)
2.0

    upfront_cost,
    fixed_cost_per_year,
    rent_per_year_full,
    years,
    use_cost_per_year_full=0.0,
)
Sustained utilization at which owning and renting cost the same over years.











Name
Type
Description
Default

required


fixed_cost_per_year
float

required


rent_per_year_full
float
Annual rental cost at full utilization.
required


years

required

float

Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless utilization at equal cumulative cost.






Equation: u = (C + Y * F) / (Y * (R - E)).
Assumptions: Constant sustained utilization, positive duration, and a nonzero rent-minus-use-cost gap.

physics.economics.calc_payback_period(upfront_cost, annual_savings)
Calculate the time for running-cost savings to repay an up-front cost.
t = C_upfront / (savings per year), undiscounted (added 2026-10-20).











Name
Type
Description
Default




upfront_cost
Quantity
One-time capital cost (USD).
required


annual_savings
Quantity
Running cost avoided per year (USD/year); must be positive.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Payback period in years.






Equation: t = upfront_cost / annual_savings.
Assumptions: Positive savings continue at a constant annual rate.
Excludes: Discounting, taxes, depreciation, and changes in savings.



Derivation: Accumulated savings equal rate times time; solve that equality for time.



>>> calc_payback_period(100, 50).m_as("year")
2.0




physics.economics.calc_rent_crossover(
    upfront_cost,
    owned_cost_rate,
    rent_cost_rate,
)
Time at which cumulative rent overtakes owning: t = C_up / (r_rent - r_own).











Name
Type
Description
Default




upfront_cost
Quantity
Nonnegative initial purchase cost, in currency.
required


owned_cost_rate
Quantity
Owned running cost per time, in currency/time.
required


rent_cost_rate
Quantity
Rental cost per time, in currency/time.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or None
Crossover time; None if rent does not overtake ownership.






Equation: t = upfront_cost / (rent_cost_rate - owned_cost_rate).
Assumptions: Both cost rates are constant and use compatible time units.
Excludes: Discounting and variable utilization; no crossover is returned when the rate gap is nonpositive.



Derivation: Equate upfront cost plus owned running cost to accumulated rent.



>>> calc_rent_crossover(100 * ureg.dollar, 2 * ureg.dollar / ureg.hour, 12 * ureg.dollar / ureg.hour).m_as("hour")
10.0




physics.economics.calc_retraining_cost_rate(interval, run_cost, staleness_slope)
Cost per unit time of retraining every interval: C / T + (1/2) s T.











Name
Type
Description
Default




interval
float or Quantity
Positive time between retraining runs.
required


run_cost
float or Quantity
Nonnegative currency cost per run.
required


staleness_slope
float or Quantity
Nonnegative growth of loss rate, in currency/time squared.
required









Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Average total cost per time.






Equation: rate = run_cost / interval + staleness_slope * interval / 2.
Assumptions: Positive cycle length, constant training cost, and linear staleness growth reset after each run.
Excludes: Training downtime, discrete scheduling, and nonlinear drift.



Derivation: Divide run cost plus the triangular integrated staleness loss by the cycle length.



>>> calc_retraining_cost_rate(2, 4, 2)
4.0




physics.economics.calc_skew_cost(skew_rate, query_rate, cost_per_error)
Cost rate of training-serving skew: Rate_skew * Q * C_error.











Name
Type
Description
Default




skew_rate
float
Fraction of queries made wrong by skew, in [0, 1].
required


query_rate
float or Quantity
Nonnegative queries per unit time.
required


cost_per_error
float or Quantity
Expected currency loss per erroneous query.
required









Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Expected currency loss per unit time.






Equation: loss_rate = skew_rate * query_rate * cost_per_error.
Assumptions: Each affected query incurs the same supplied expected cost.
Excludes: Correlated downstream losses and nonlinear business impact.



Derivation: Multiply query volume by error fraction and loss per error.



>>> calc_skew_cost(0.5, 100, 2)
100.0




physics.economics.calc_staleness_slope(
    query_rate,
    value_per_query,
    initial_accuracy,
    decay_rate,
)
Growth of value lost per unit time since the last retraining run: Q V A0 gamma.











Name
Type
Description
Default




query_rate
float or Quantity
Queries per time, nonnegative.
required


value_per_query
float or Quantity
Currency value per query.
required


initial_accuracy
float
Reference correct fraction, in [0, 1].
required


decay_rate
float or Quantity
Nonnegative exponential decay rate in inverse time.
required














Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Loss-rate growth, in currency/time squared.






Equation: s = query_rate * value_per_query * initial_accuracy * decay_rate.
Assumptions: Exponential accuracy decay is linearized near zero age, where decay_rate * age is small.
Excludes: Long-horizon nonlinear decay and changing query volume.



Derivation: The first-order expansion of A0 exp(-gamma t) gives an accuracy loss A0 gamma t.



>>> calc_staleness_slope(100, 2, 0.5, 0.1)
10.0

Description





Quantity
Reserve use in millimeters.






Equation:
At each permission tick i of a blend of length T from cruise into braking, u = min(i * tick / T, 1); the blended speed and travel follow from the once- and twice-integrated smoothstep:
A1(u) = u^6 - 3 u^5 + 2.5 u^4,   A2(u) = u^7 / 7 - u^6 / 2 + u^5 / 2
v(u) = v0 - a T A1(u),            x(u) = v0 T u - a T^2 A2(u)
use = max_i [ x(u_i) + d_S(v(u_i)) ] - d_S(v0)
where d_S is the resident jerk-limited stop (calc_scurve_stop_distance). The resident stop from each blended speed is charged from zero acceleration, which overstates it while the blend is already decelerating, so the bound is conservative (added 2026-10-20).
Assumptions: Positive window and tick define a finite permission grid; positive deceleration and jerk define the resident stop, and blended speed stays nonnegative.
Excludes: Between-tick maxima, acceleration-aware resident stopping, tracking error, and safety certification.



Derivation: At each sampled permission time, integrate the blend and add the resident zero- acceleration stop; subtract the original stop distance and take the largest sampled growth.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_blend_reserve_use
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_blend_reserve_use(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('0.01 s')).check('[length]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_braking_time(velocity, max_deceleration)
Time to brake from velocity to rest at constant deceleration.











Name
Type
Description
Default




velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative forward speed in m/s.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration bound in m/s^2.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Braking time in seconds.






Equation: t_brake = v / a
Assumptions: Speed is nonnegative and the positive braking deceleration is constant.
Excludes: Reaction time, jerk ramps, and speed-dependent braking.



The constant-acceleration relation v = v0 + a * t is evaluated at rest (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.12).
Derivation: Integrate dv/dt = -a to rest to get elapsed time v/a.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_braking_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_braking_time(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('1 s')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_c2_stop_suffix(entry_velocity, peak_deceleration)
Calculate the duration and distance of a C2-continuous stop from cruise.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Cruise velocity at the start of the stop (e.g. m/s).
required


peak_deceleration
Quantity
Credible peak deceleration the stop may reach (e.g. m/s^2).
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Duration (ms), distance (m), and peak_jerk (m/s^3).






Equation:
A stop that begins and ends at zero acceleration, entered from constant velocity v_c, follows the minimum-order polynomial
q(u) = q_c + v_c * T * (u - u^3 + u^4 / 2),  u = t / T in [0, 1],
whose peak deceleration is 1.5 * v_c / T and whose distance is v_c * T / 2. Setting the peak equal to the credible deceleration a gives
T = 1.5 * v / a,    d = 0.75 * v^2 / a,
which is 1.5 times the constant-deceleration distance v^2 / (2 * a). The factor belongs to this polynomial, not to smooth stopping in general: its jerk q’’’ = -(6 v_c / T^2)(1 - 2u) peaks in magnitude at the ends,
j_peak = 6 * v / T^2 = (8 / 3) * a^2 / v,
and a jerk-limited S-curve with the same a and j_peak stops shorter (calc_scurve_stop_distance).
Assumptions: Positive entry speed begins at zero acceleration; the specified quartic position polynomial stops with zero final acceleration.
Excludes: An independent jerk bound, actuator tracking, and an optimality claim across other smooth profiles.



This polynomial construction satisfies q’ = v_c, q’’ = 0 at u = 0 and q’ = 0, q’’ = 0 at u = 1; peak |q’‘| occurs at u = 1/2 (minimum of q’‘(u) = v_c / T * (-6u + 6u^2)); peak |q’’’| occurs at u = 0 and u = 1.
Derivation: Differentiate the displayed quartic to locate its peak deceleration at normalized time one-half, then solve for duration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_c2_stop_suffix
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_c2_stop_suffix(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'))['distance'].check('[length]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile(
    approach_velocity=None,
    tripwire_force=None,
    latch_stiffness=None,
    response_time=None,
    force_limit=None,
    *,
    scenario=None,
)
Calculate force rise and required braking after latch contact.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Arm approach speed (e.g. m/s). If omitted and scenario is given, defaults to scenario.v_latch_approach.
None


tripwire_force
Quantity
Tripwire threshold force (e.g. N). Defaults to scenario.f_latch_tripwire if scenario is given.
None


latch_stiffness
Quantity
Spring stiffness of the latch mechanism (e.g. N/m). Defaults to scenario.k_latch.
None


response_time
Quantity
Contact-loop response latency from tripwire detection to brake onset (e.g. ms). Defaults to scenario.t_contact_response.
None


force_limit
Quantity
Maximum permissible contact force limit (e.g. N). Defaults to scenario.f_latch_limit.
None


scenario
EmbodiedSiteScenario
Site scenario supplying default latch physical parameters.
None














Name
Type
Description





dict
- “f_at_brake_onset”: Force at brake command onset (Quantity in N). - “x_remaining”: Remaining allowable displacement (Quantity in mm). - “a_arm_needed”: Required arm deceleration to honor force limit (Quantity in m/s^2). - “t_arm_stop”: Arm stopping duration (Quantity in ms). - “df_dt”: Force rate of rise during contact (Quantity in N/s).






Equation:
When a robot manipulator contacts a compliant latch or strike plate: 1. Force accumulation rate: df/dt = k_latch * v_approach 2. Force at brake command onset (tripwire force + accumulation during response time): f_cmd = f_tripwire + k_latch * v_approach * t_response 3. Remaining allowable deflection before exceeding contact limit f_limit: x_remaining = (f_limit - f_cmd) / k_latch 4. Required constant arm deceleration to halt within x_remaining: a_arm_needed = v_approach^2 / (2 * x_remaining) 5. Duration of the arm stopping phase: t_arm_stop = v_approach / a_arm_needed
Assumptions: Positive approach speed remains constant until brake onset; a positive linear stiffness sets force and braking deceleration is constant afterward. Brake-onset force must remain below the limit.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, damping, actuator limits, and contact safety certification.



Derivation: Use Hooke’s law for the remaining compression and solve v squared/(2 a) = remaining compression for required deceleration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 N'), ureg('1 N/m'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('10 N'))['a_arm_needed'].check('[length]/[time]**2')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_max_permitted_velocity(
    d_clear,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
)
Calculate the forward-velocity ceiling in the delayed stopping model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




d_clear
Quantity
Detected clearance distance to obstacle along travel vector (e.g. m).
required


total_latency
Quantity
End-to-end sense-to-actuation latency tau_delay (e.g. s or ms).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Maximum braking deceleration capacity a_brake (e.g. m/s^2).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization uncertainty bound (e.g. cm or m).
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Physical clearance safety buffer (e.g. cm or m).
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled forward-velocity ceiling in meters/second.






Equation:
Solves the quadratic inequality: v * tau + v^2 / (2 * a) <= D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin for the maximum non-negative velocity root: v_max = -a * tau + sqrt((a * tau)^2 + 2 * a * D_eff) where D_eff = D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin. If D_eff <= 0, v_max = 0.
Assumptions: Clearance is nonnegative; the delay and constant braking deceleration are positive. Margins consume clearance before solving.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, approaching obstacles, changing traction, and certified safe-speed determination.



The speed ceiling follows from the positive root of the calc_safe_stopping_distance quadratic, so it rests on the same kinematics (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14) and the same additive-margin modeling assumption.
Derivation: Take the nonnegative root of v tau + v squared/(2 a) = effective clearance, clamping to zero when no clearance remains.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_max_permitted_velocity
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_max_permitted_velocity(ureg('0 m'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('0 m/s')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_safe_stopping_distance(
    velocity,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
)
Calculate dynamic stopping distance under non-zero control latency.











Name
Type
Description
Default




velocity
Quantity
Current operational velocity (e.g. m/s).
required


total_latency
Quantity
End-to-end perception-to-brake latency (e.g. ms or s).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Maximum braking deceleration available (e.g. m/s^2).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization uncertainty bound (e.g. cm or m).
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Physical obstacle clearance safety margin (e.g. cm or m).
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Total stopping distance in meters.






Equation: d_stop = v * tau_latency + (v^2) / (2 * a_max) + delta_loc + delta_margin
Assumptions: Forward speed is nonnegative, delay and available constant deceleration are positive, and optional nonnegative margins add linearly.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, changing traction, moving obstacles, and safety certification.



Reaction distance v * tau adds to constant-deceleration braking distance v^2 / (2 * a), from v^2 = v0^2 + 2 * a * (x - x0) (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14; Example 3.10 adds reaction-time travel to braking distance the same way). The additive localization and clearance margins are a modeling assumption.
Derivation: Integrate constant speed during the delay and constant deceleration during braking, then add clearance margins.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_safe_stopping_distance
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_safe_stopping_distance(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('0 m')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
    d_clear,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    approach_velocity=None,
)
Highest cruise speed whose delayed S-curve stop fits the clearance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




d_clear
Quantity
Clear distance to the obstacle (e.g. m).
required


total_latency
Quantity
Pre-brake delay tau (e.g. ms).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Stop limits a_max (m/s^2) and j_max (m/s^3).
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Stop limits a_max (m/s^2) and j_max (m/s^3).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization bound and protective clearance subtracted from d_clear.
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Localization bound and protective clearance subtracted from d_clear.
None


approach_velocity
Quantity
Speed at which the obstacle closes during delay and stop (e.g. m/s).
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Speed ceiling in m/s (zero if the margins consume the clearance).






Equation:
Solves for the largest v with
v * tau + d_S(v) + v_h * (tau + T_S(v)) <= D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin,
where d_S and T_S are the S-curve stop distance and time (calc_scurve_stop_distance, calc_scurve_stop_time) and v_h is an optional obstacle approach speed (zero for a static obstacle). The left side is continuous and strictly increasing in v, so bisection finds the root. Because d_S is not a single quadratic in v, no one closed form covers both stop regimes; for v_h = 0 in the trapezoidal regime the result equals calc_max_permitted_velocity with delay tau + a / (2 j).
Assumptions: Clearance, delay, margins, and obstacle approach speed are nonnegative; deceleration and jerk limits are positive and the obstacle approaches at constant speed.
Excludes: Obstacle acceleration, curved motion, tracking error, and safety certification.



This inverse uses calc_scurve_stop_distance (Biagiotti and Melchiorri 2008, ch. 3) and the additive delay-plus-braking budget of calc_safe_stopping_distance.
Derivation: Find the largest root of delay travel plus S-curve travel plus obstacle closure minus available clearance by bisection.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(ureg('0 m'), ureg('0 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 m/s')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time(
    distance,
    max_acceleration,
    max_jerk,
)
Calculate the duration of a jerk-limited rest-to-rest move with no cruise phase.











Name
Type
Description
Default




distance
Quantity
Positive linear distance in m or angular distance in rad.
required


max_acceleration
Quantity
Positive acceleration limit in distance-units per second squared.
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Positive jerk bound in m/s^3.
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Duration in s, peak_velocity in distance-units/s, and Boolean reaches_max_acceleration.






Equation:
A symmetric double-S profile that accelerates, then immediately decelerates. With t_j = a/j and x the time from the start of the jerk ramp to the end of the constant-acceleration plateau minus t_j (peak speed a*x):
plateau reached (x >= t_j):  D = a * x * (x + t_j),  T = 2 (x + t_j)
no plateau (D < 2 a^3 / j^2): D = 2 j tau^3,           T = 4 tau
Returns a dict with duration, peak_velocity, and reaches_max_acceleration. Works for linear or angular moves (distance in m or rad, rates to match).
Assumptions: Distance and both limits are positive; the symmetric profile has no speed limit or cruise phase, with matching linear or angular units.
Excludes: Velocity ceilings, tracking error, and asymmetric acceleration limits.



Biagiotti and Melchiorri, Trajectory Planning for Automatic Machines and Robots (Springer, 2008), ch. 3, double-S velocity profile.
Derivation: Integrate the symmetric double-S profile; solve a quadratic when the acceleration plateau exists and a cubic otherwise.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time(ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3'))['duration'].check('[time]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_stop_distance(
    entry_velocity,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
)
Distance of a jerk-limited S-curve stop entered from zero-acceleration cruise.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Cruise velocity at stop onset (e.g. m/s); zero gives zero distance.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Deceleration bound a_max (e.g. m/s^2).
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Jerk bound j_max (e.g. m/s^3).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Stopping distance in meters.






Equation:
The stop drives acceleration from zero to -a at the jerk limit j, holds -a, and returns acceleration to zero at the jerk limit as velocity reaches zero (trapezoidal acceleration, the “double S” velocity profile). The profile is C2: position, velocity, and acceleration are continuous and jerk is piecewise constant.
if v >= a^2 / j:   d = (v / 2) * (v / a + a / j)
                     = v^2 / (2 a) + v * a / (2 j)
else:              d = v * sqrt(v / j)     (a is never reached)
In the first case the stop equals constant-deceleration braking at a plus cruise over half of one jerk ramp, a / (2 j). Under the bounds |a| <= a_max and |j| <= j_max this is the time-optimal stop, and for a stop that does not reverse it is also the shortest.
Assumptions: Entry speed is nonnegative, acceleration and jerk limits are positive, and both boundary accelerations are zero.
Excludes: Reaction delay, traction variation, tracking error, and safety certification.



Biagiotti, L. and Melchiorri, C., Trajectory Planning for Automatic Machines and Robots, Springer (2008; DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-85629-0), ch. 3, trajectory with double S velocity profile, specialized here to a stop from v to rest with zero boundary accelerations. Formula re-derived and checked against a discretized minimum-distance linear program.
Derivation: Integrate symmetric jerk ramps with an optional constant-deceleration plateau; symmetry makes distance v T/2.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_stop_distance
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_stop_distance(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 m')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_stop_time(
    entry_velocity,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
)
Duration of the jerk-limited S-curve stop of calc_scurve_stop_distance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative speed at onset in m/s.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration bound in m/s^2.
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Positive jerk bound in m/s^3.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Stopping time in milliseconds.






Equation:
if v >= a^2 / j: T = v / a + a / j else: T = 2 * sqrt(v / j)
Assumptions: The stop has the same nonnegative entry speed, positive limits, and zero boundary accelerations as calc_scurve_stop_distance.
Excludes: Pre-brake delay, tracking error, and dynamics beyond the acceleration and jerk bounds.

Derivation: Sum the two jerk-ramp durations and the plateau, when present; otherwise solve the triangular acceleration area for duration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_stop_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_stop_time(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 ms')

physics.robotics.stopping.calc_smoothstep_braking_blend(
    entry_velocity,
    deceleration,
    window,
)
Exit speed and travel of a fixed-endpoint smoothstep blend from cruise into braking.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative speed at onset in m/s.
required


deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration in m/s^2.
required


window
Quantity
Positive blend duration in s.
required









Name
Type
Description





dict
exit_speed (m/s) and travel (m).






Equation: a(t) = -a_b alpha(t / T), alpha(s) = 10 s^3 - 15 s^4 + 6 s^5 v_exit = v0 - a_b T / 2 (the integral of alpha over [0, 1] is 1/2) d_blend = v0 T - a_b T^2 / 7 (the integral of (1 - s) alpha over [0, 1] is 1/7)
The quintic smoothstep has zero first and second derivatives at both ends, so the commanded deceleration rises from zero to a_b with continuous jerk (added 2026-10-20).
Assumptions: Entry speed is nonnegative; positive deceleration rises through a quintic smoothstep over a positive window. The intended regime avoids reversing before the window ends.
Excludes: A zero-speed clamp and subsequent stop. An overlong window can return a negative exit speed.



Derivation: Integrate the quintic once for velocity and twice for displacement; the full- window integrals are one-half and one-seventh.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_smoothstep_braking_blend
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_smoothstep_braking_blend(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 s'))['exit_speed'].check('[length]/[time]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_stopping_crossover_speed(
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
)
Speed at which travel during the pre-brake delay equals braking travel.











Name
Type
Description
Default




total_latency
Quantity
Pre-brake delay tau (e.g. ms or s); zero gives v* = 0.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Braking deceleration a (e.g. m/s^2).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Crossover speed in m/s.






Equation: v * tau = v^2 / (2 * a) => v* = 2 * a * tau
Below v*, delay travel is the larger term of the elementary stopping budget; above it, braking travel is.
Assumptions: Delay is nonnegative and braking deceleration is positive and constant.
Excludes: Margins, jerk ramps, and moving obstacles.



The crossover equates the two terms of calc_safe_stopping_distance (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14 and Example 3.10).
Derivation: Equate v tau to v squared/(2 a) and select the nonzero crossover branch v = 2 a tau.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_stopping_crossover_speed
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_stopping_crossover_speed(ureg('0 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('0 m/s')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_travel_between_speeds(
    start_velocity,
    end_velocity,
    duration,
)
Distance covered while speed changes uniformly between two recorded values.











Name
Type
Description
Default




start_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative initial speed in m/s.
required


end_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative final speed in m/s.
required


duration
Quantity
Nonnegative elapsed time in s.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Distance in meters.






Equation: x = (v_start + v_end) / 2 * t
With equal speeds this is the delay travel v * tau of the stopping budget; with two recorded speeds it is the trapezoid estimate of the distance covered between them.
Assumptions: Both endpoint speeds and duration are nonnegative; speed varies linearly between endpoints.
Excludes: Unobserved nonlinear speed changes and reverse travel.



Constant-acceleration travel is x = (v0 + v) / 2 * t (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.11 with Eq. 3.12).
Derivation: Integrate the linear velocity interpolation: mean endpoint speed times elapsed duration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_travel_between_speeds
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_travel_between_speeds(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 s')) == ureg('1 m')
True

Excludes: Between-tick maxima, acceleration-aware resident stopping, tracking error, and safety certification.



Derivation: At each sampled permission time, integrate the blend and add the resident zero- acceleration stop; subtract the original stop distance and take the largest sampled growth.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_blend_reserve_use
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_blend_reserve_use(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3'), ureg('0.1 s'), ureg('0.01 s')).check('[length]')
True

Time to brake from velocity to rest at constant deceleration.

Type
Description
Default

Nonnegative forward speed in m/s.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration bound in m/s^2.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Braking time in seconds.






Equation: t_brake = v / a
Assumptions: Speed is nonnegative and the positive braking deceleration is constant.
Excludes: Reaction time, jerk ramps, and speed-dependent braking.



The constant-acceleration relation v = v0 + a * t is evaluated at rest (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.12).

>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_braking_time

physics.robotics.stopping.calc_c2_stop_suffix(entry_velocity, peak_deceleration)
Calculate the duration and distance of a C2-continuous stop from cruise.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Cruise velocity at the start of the stop (e.g. m/s).
required


peak_deceleration
Quantity
Credible peak deceleration the stop may reach (e.g. m/s^2).
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Duration (ms), distance (m), and peak_jerk (m/s^3).






Equation:
A stop that begins and ends at zero acceleration, entered from constant velocity v_c, follows the minimum-order polynomial
q(u) = q_c + v_c * T * (u - u^3 + u^4 / 2),  u = t / T in [0, 1],
whose peak deceleration is 1.5 * v_c / T and whose distance is v_c * T / 2. Setting the peak equal to the credible deceleration a gives
T = 1.5 * v / a,    d = 0.75 * v^2 / a,
which is 1.5 times the constant-deceleration distance v^2 / (2 * a). The factor belongs to this polynomial, not to smooth stopping in general: its jerk q’’’ = -(6 v_c / T^2)(1 - 2u) peaks in magnitude at the ends,
j_peak = 6 * v / T^2 = (8 / 3) * a^2 / v,
and a jerk-limited S-curve with the same a and j_peak stops shorter (calc_scurve_stop_distance).
Assumptions: Positive entry speed begins at zero acceleration; the specified quartic position polynomial stops with zero final acceleration.
Excludes: An independent jerk bound, actuator tracking, and an optimality claim across other smooth profiles.



This polynomial construction satisfies q’ = v_c, q’’ = 0 at u = 0 and q’ = 0, q’’ = 0 at u = 1; peak |q’‘| occurs at u = 1/2 (minimum of q’‘(u) = v_c / T * (-6u + 6u^2)); peak |q’’’| occurs at u = 0 and u = 1.
Derivation: Differentiate the displayed quartic to locate its peak deceleration at normalized time one-half, then solve for duration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_c2_stop_suffix
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_c2_stop_suffix(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'))['distance'].check('[length]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile(
    approach_velocity=None,
    tripwire_force=None,
    latch_stiffness=None,
    response_time=None,
    force_limit=None,
    *,
    scenario=None,
)
Calculate force rise and required braking after latch contact.











Name
Type
Description
Default
