Quantity
Arm approach speed (e.g. m/s). If omitted and scenario is given, defaults to scenario.v_latch_approach.
None


tripwire_force
Quantity
Tripwire threshold force (e.g. N). Defaults to scenario.f_latch_tripwire if scenario is given.
None


latch_stiffness
Quantity
Spring stiffness of the latch mechanism (e.g. N/m). Defaults to scenario.k_latch.
None


response_time
Quantity
Contact-loop response latency from tripwire detection to brake onset (e.g. ms). Defaults to scenario.t_contact_response.
None


force_limit
Quantity
Maximum permissible contact force limit (e.g. N). Defaults to scenario.f_latch_limit.
None


scenario
EmbodiedSiteScenario
Site scenario supplying default latch physical parameters.
None














Name
Type
Description





dict
- “f_at_brake_onset”: Force at brake command onset (Quantity in N). - “x_remaining”: Remaining allowable displacement (Quantity in mm). - “a_arm_needed”: Required arm deceleration to honor force limit (Quantity in m/s^2). - “t_arm_stop”: Arm stopping duration (Quantity in ms). - “df_dt”: Force rate of rise during contact (Quantity in N/s).






Equation:
When a robot manipulator contacts a compliant latch or strike plate: 1. Force accumulation rate: df/dt = k_latch * v_approach 2. Force at brake command onset (tripwire force + accumulation during response time): f_cmd = f_tripwire + k_latch * v_approach * t_response 3. Remaining allowable deflection before exceeding contact limit f_limit: x_remaining = (f_limit - f_cmd) / k_latch 4. Required constant arm deceleration to halt within x_remaining: a_arm_needed = v_approach^2 / (2 * x_remaining) 5. Duration of the arm stopping phase: t_arm_stop = v_approach / a_arm_needed
Assumptions: Positive approach speed remains constant until brake onset; a positive linear stiffness sets force and braking deceleration is constant afterward. Brake-onset force must remain below the limit.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, damping, actuator limits, and contact safety certification.



Derivation: Use Hooke’s law for the remaining compression and solve v squared/(2 a) = remaining compression for required deceleration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_latch_contact_stopping_profile(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 N'), ureg('1 N/m'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('10 N'))['a_arm_needed'].check('[length]/[time]**2')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_max_permitted_velocity(
    d_clear,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
)
Calculate the forward-velocity ceiling in the delayed stopping model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




d_clear
Quantity
Detected clearance distance to obstacle along travel vector (e.g. m).
required


total_latency
Quantity
End-to-end sense-to-actuation latency tau_delay (e.g. s or ms).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Maximum braking deceleration capacity a_brake (e.g. m/s^2).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization uncertainty bound (e.g. cm or m).
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Physical clearance safety buffer (e.g. cm or m).
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled forward-velocity ceiling in meters/second.






Equation:
Solves the quadratic inequality: v * tau + v^2 / (2 * a) <= D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin for the maximum non-negative velocity root: v_max = -a * tau + sqrt((a * tau)^2 + 2 * a * D_eff) where D_eff = D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin. If D_eff <= 0, v_max = 0.
Assumptions: Clearance is nonnegative; the delay and constant braking deceleration are positive. Margins consume clearance before solving.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, approaching obstacles, changing traction, and certified safe-speed determination.



The speed ceiling follows from the positive root of the calc_safe_stopping_distance quadratic, so it rests on the same kinematics (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14) and the same additive-margin modeling assumption.
Derivation: Take the nonnegative root of v tau + v squared/(2 a) = effective clearance, clamping to zero when no clearance remains.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_max_permitted_velocity
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_max_permitted_velocity(ureg('0 m'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('0 m/s')
True

    velocity,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
)
Calculate dynamic stopping distance under non-zero control latency.











Name
Type
Description
Default




velocity
Quantity
Current operational velocity (e.g. m/s).
required


total_latency
Quantity
End-to-end perception-to-brake latency (e.g. ms or s).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Maximum braking deceleration available (e.g. m/s^2).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization uncertainty bound (e.g. cm or m).
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Physical obstacle clearance safety margin (e.g. cm or m).
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Total stopping distance in meters.






Equation: d_stop = v * tau_latency + (v^2) / (2 * a_max) + delta_loc + delta_margin
Assumptions: Forward speed is nonnegative, delay and available constant deceleration are positive, and optional nonnegative margins add linearly.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, changing traction, moving obstacles, and safety certification.



Reaction distance v * tau adds to constant-deceleration braking distance v^2 / (2 * a), from v^2 = v0^2 + 2 * a * (x - x0) (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14; Example 3.10 adds reaction-time travel to braking distance the same way). The additive localization and clearance margins are a modeling assumption.
Derivation: Integrate constant speed during the delay and constant deceleration during braking, then add clearance margins.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_safe_stopping_distance
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_safe_stopping_distance(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('0 m')

physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
    d_clear,
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
    loc_margin=None,
    physical_margin=None,
    approach_velocity=None,
)
Highest cruise speed whose delayed S-curve stop fits the clearance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




d_clear
Quantity
Clear distance to the obstacle (e.g. m).
required


total_latency
Quantity
Pre-brake delay tau (e.g. ms).
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Stop limits a_max (m/s^2) and j_max (m/s^3).
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Stop limits a_max (m/s^2) and j_max (m/s^3).
required


loc_margin
Quantity
Localization bound and protective clearance subtracted from d_clear.
None


physical_margin
Quantity
Localization bound and protective clearance subtracted from d_clear.
None


approach_velocity
Quantity
Speed at which the obstacle closes during delay and stop (e.g. m/s).
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Speed ceiling in m/s (zero if the margins consume the clearance).






Equation:
Solves for the largest v with
v * tau + d_S(v) + v_h * (tau + T_S(v)) <= D_clear - delta_loc - delta_margin,
where d_S and T_S are the S-curve stop distance and time (calc_scurve_stop_distance, calc_scurve_stop_time) and v_h is an optional obstacle approach speed (zero for a static obstacle). The left side is continuous and strictly increasing in v, so bisection finds the root. Because d_S is not a single quadratic in v, no one closed form covers both stop regimes; for v_h = 0 in the trapezoidal regime the result equals calc_max_permitted_velocity with delay tau + a / (2 j).
Assumptions: Clearance, delay, margins, and obstacle approach speed are nonnegative; deceleration and jerk limits are positive and the obstacle approaches at constant speed.
Excludes: Obstacle acceleration, curved motion, tracking error, and safety certification.



This inverse uses calc_scurve_stop_distance (Biagiotti and Melchiorri 2008, ch. 3) and the additive delay-plus-braking budget of calc_safe_stopping_distance.
Derivation: Find the largest root of delay travel plus S-curve travel plus obstacle closure minus available clearance by bisection.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(ureg('0 m'), ureg('0 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 m/s')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time(
    distance,
    max_acceleration,
    max_jerk,
)
Calculate the duration of a jerk-limited rest-to-rest move with no cruise phase.











Name
Type
Description
Default




distance
Quantity
Positive linear distance in m or angular distance in rad.
required


max_acceleration
Quantity
Positive acceleration limit in distance-units per second squared.
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Positive jerk bound in m/s^3.
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Duration in s, peak_velocity in distance-units/s, and Boolean reaches_max_acceleration.






Equation:
A symmetric double-S profile that accelerates, then immediately decelerates. With t_j = a/j and x the time from the start of the jerk ramp to the end of the constant-acceleration plateau minus t_j (peak speed a*x):
plateau reached (x >= t_j):  D = a * x * (x + t_j),  T = 2 (x + t_j)
no plateau (D < 2 a^3 / j^2): D = 2 j tau^3,           T = 4 tau
Returns a dict with duration, peak_velocity, and reaches_max_acceleration. Works for linear or angular moves (distance in m or rad, rates to match).
Assumptions: Distance and both limits are positive; the symmetric profile has no speed limit or cruise phase, with matching linear or angular units.
Excludes: Velocity ceilings, tracking error, and asymmetric acceleration limits.



Biagiotti and Melchiorri, Trajectory Planning for Automatic Machines and Robots (Springer, 2008), ch. 3, double-S velocity profile.
Derivation: Integrate the symmetric double-S profile; solve a quadratic when the acceleration plateau exists and a cubic otherwise.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_rest_to_rest_time(ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3'))['duration'].check('[time]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_stop_distance(
    entry_velocity,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
)
Distance of a jerk-limited S-curve stop entered from zero-acceleration cruise.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Cruise velocity at stop onset (e.g. m/s); zero gives zero distance.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Deceleration bound a_max (e.g. m/s^2).
required


max_jerk
Quantity
Jerk bound j_max (e.g. m/s^3).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Stopping distance in meters.






Equation:
The stop drives acceleration from zero to -a at the jerk limit j, holds -a, and returns acceleration to zero at the jerk limit as velocity reaches zero (trapezoidal acceleration, the “double S” velocity profile). The profile is C2: position, velocity, and acceleration are continuous and jerk is piecewise constant.
if v >= a^2 / j:   d = (v / 2) * (v / a + a / j)
                     = v^2 / (2 a) + v * a / (2 j)
else:              d = v * sqrt(v / j)     (a is never reached)
In the first case the stop equals constant-deceleration braking at a plus cruise over half of one jerk ramp, a / (2 j). Under the bounds |a| <= a_max and |j| <= j_max this is the time-optimal stop, and for a stop that does not reverse it is also the shortest.
Assumptions: Entry speed is nonnegative, acceleration and jerk limits are positive, and both boundary accelerations are zero.
Excludes: Reaction delay, traction variation, tracking error, and safety certification.



Biagiotti, L. and Melchiorri, C., Trajectory Planning for Automatic Machines and Robots, Springer (2008; DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-85629-0), ch. 3, trajectory with double S velocity profile, specialized here to a stop from v to rest with zero boundary accelerations. Formula re-derived and checked against a discretized minimum-distance linear program.
Derivation: Integrate symmetric jerk ramps with an optional constant-deceleration plateau; symmetry makes distance v T/2.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_stop_distance
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_stop_distance(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 m')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_scurve_stop_time(
    entry_velocity,
    max_deceleration,
    max_jerk,
)

Name
Type
Description
Default

Nonnegative speed at onset in m/s.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration bound in m/s^2.
required


max_jerk

Positive jerk bound in m/s^3.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Stopping time in milliseconds.






Equation:
if v >= a^2 / j: T = v / a + a / j else: T = 2 * sqrt(v / j)
Assumptions: The stop has the same nonnegative entry speed, positive limits, and zero boundary accelerations as calc_scurve_stop_distance.
Excludes: Pre-brake delay, tracking error, and dynamics beyond the acceleration and jerk bounds.



Biagiotti and Melchiorri (2008), ch. 3, double S velocity profile; see calc_scurve_stop_distance.
Derivation: Sum the two jerk-ramp durations and the plateau, when present; otherwise solve the triangular acceleration area for duration.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_scurve_stop_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_scurve_stop_time(ureg('0 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 ms')

physics.robotics.stopping.calc_smoothstep_braking_blend(
    entry_velocity,
    deceleration,
    window,
)
Exit speed and travel of a fixed-endpoint smoothstep blend from cruise into braking.











Name
Type
Description
Default




entry_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative speed at onset in m/s.
required


deceleration
Quantity
Positive braking deceleration in m/s^2.
required


window
Quantity
Positive blend duration in s.
required









Name
Type
Description





dict
exit_speed (m/s) and travel (m).






Equation: a(t) = -a_b alpha(t / T), alpha(s) = 10 s^3 - 15 s^4 + 6 s^5 v_exit = v0 - a_b T / 2 (the integral of alpha over [0, 1] is 1/2) d_blend = v0 T - a_b T^2 / 7 (the integral of (1 - s) alpha over [0, 1] is 1/7)
The quintic smoothstep has zero first and second derivatives at both ends, so the commanded deceleration rises from zero to a_b with continuous jerk (added 2026-10-20).
Assumptions: Entry speed is nonnegative; positive deceleration rises through a quintic smoothstep over a positive window. The intended regime avoids reversing before the window ends.
Excludes: A zero-speed clamp and subsequent stop. An overlong window can return a negative exit speed.



Derivation: Integrate the quintic once for velocity and twice for displacement; the full- window integrals are one-half and one-seventh.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping import calc_smoothstep_braking_blend
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_smoothstep_braking_blend(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'), ureg('1 s'))['exit_speed'].check('[length]/[time]')
True




physics.robotics.stopping.calc_stopping_crossover_speed(
    total_latency,
    max_deceleration,
)
Speed at which travel during the pre-brake delay equals braking travel.











Name
Type
Description
Default




total_latency
Quantity
Pre-brake delay tau (e.g. ms or s); zero gives v* = 0.
required


max_deceleration
Quantity
Braking deceleration a (e.g. m/s^2).
required









Name
Type

Quantity
Crossover speed in m/s.






Equation: v * tau = v^2 / (2 * a) => v* = 2 * a * tau
Below v*, delay travel is the larger term of the elementary stopping budget; above it, braking travel is.
Assumptions: Delay is nonnegative and braking deceleration is positive and constant.
Excludes: Margins, jerk ramps, and moving obstacles.



The crossover equates the two terms of calc_safe_stopping_distance (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.14 and Example 3.10).
Derivation: Equate v tau to v squared/(2 a) and select the nonzero crossover branch v = 2 a tau.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg

physics.robotics.stopping.calc_travel_between_speeds(
    start_velocity,
    end_velocity,
    duration,
)
Distance covered while speed changes uniformly between two recorded values.











Name
Type
Description
Default




start_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative initial speed in m/s.
required


end_velocity
Quantity
Nonnegative final speed in m/s.
required


duration
Quantity
Nonnegative elapsed time in s.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Distance in meters.






Equation: x = (v_start + v_end) / 2 * t
With equal speeds this is the delay travel v * tau of the stopping budget; with two recorded speeds it is the trapezoid estimate of the distance covered between them.
Assumptions: Both endpoint speeds and duration are nonnegative; speed varies linearly between endpoints.
Excludes: Unobserved nonlinear speed changes and reverse travel.

Derivation: Integrate the linear velocity interpolation: mean endpoint speed times elapsed duration.

>>> calc_travel_between_speeds(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 s')) == ureg('1 m')
True

title: FrameRateHeadroomScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
workload at frame_rate on an accelerator of peak_rate that sustains a utilization_low to utilization_high share of peak; alternative_flops is a heavier model per frame.


Equation: Stream demand is frame_rate*work_per_frame; sustained supply is peak_rate*utilization.
Assumptions: Constant frame complexity and declared utilization, with no frame dropping.
Excludes: Memory limits, input preprocessing, deadline jitter, and measured sustained efficiency.



Derivation: A stream of equally costly frames requires frames/second times FLOPs/frame. Multiplying peak FLOP/s by a declared utilization gives the assumed sustained supply; dividing supply by demand gives dimensionless headroom.

Exposure needed, with zero events observed, to bound a rate of budget per horizon at one-sided confidence, and the size of recording that exposure at sample_rate.


Equation: zero-event bound = -log(1-confidence); required exposure = bound / target event rate.
Assumptions: Events follow the stationary Poisson model used by the exposure helper and confidence lies between zero and one.
Excludes: Nonstationary hazards, correlated events, and a guarantee of zero failures after testing.

Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
The same fixed job on base_devices and on scaled_devices: speedup, ideal time, and efficiency.
Strong-scaling efficiency is base time over (device ratio times scaled time).


Equation: The calculation members below define device_ratio, speedup, ideal_time, efficiency.
Assumptions: Both durations describe the same fixed job; ideal scaling divides time by device-count growth.
Excludes: Weak scaling, changed accuracy targets, and attribution of overhead to specific mechanisms.



Derivation: The same fixed job on base_devices and on scaled_devices: speedup, ideal time, and efficiency. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.

title: ColdStartScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A new replica: provision, fetch the weight artifact, load and warm up.


Equation: Start time=provisioning_time+artifact_bytes/fetch_bandwidth+load_warmup_time.
Assumptions: Sequential startup phases and constant available transfer bandwidth; peak replica counts are supplied.
Excludes: Overlap, network contention, and forecasting the predictive fleet size.



Derivation: Nonoverlapping startup phases add in elapsed time. The fetch phase is artifact bytes divided by available bandwidth. Replica saving is an arithmetic comparison of two supplied peak counts, not a predictive scaling model.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.

>>> round((scenario.cold_start_time).to('s').magnitude, 6)

title: physics.tool_calls
text:
physics.tool_calls
Tool calling: the equations behind a mediated call, its retry, and its catalog.
Pure arithmetic (added 2026-10-20). A call whose request or reply may be lost times out with one probability and, under one blind retry, executes twice with another; a model that polls a pending job makes one status call per interval before completion; a tool catalog staged on every call costs its descriptors, and selection pays once the descriptors it leaves out exceed its own overhead; a shared protocol turns pairwise adapters into one per party. The solvers in engine/solvers/tool_calls.py compose these.





Name
Description




calc_blind_retry_duplicate_probability
Return the unconditional probability of a duplicate effect after one retry.


calc_bulkhead_admission
Partition a burst into active, queued, and rejected calls.


calc_integration_adapters
Count pairwise and shared-protocol integration adapters.


calc_jitter_expected_arrivals
Estimate retries arriving inside a uniform-jitter window.


calc_layered_retry_attempts
Count downstream attempts under nested retry allowances.


calc_pending_polls
Count polling calls that occur before job completion.


calc_selection_break_even
Return the number of descriptors that offsets tool-selection overhead.


calc_timeout_probability
Return timeout probability for independently lost request and reply.





physics.tool_calls.calc_blind_retry_duplicate_probability(
    request_loss,
    reply_loss,
)
Return the unconditional probability of a duplicate effect after one retry.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_loss
float
Loss probability of each request transmission; between zero and one.
required


reply_loss
float
Loss probability of the original reply; between zero and one.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Probability that the original and retry both execute the effect.






Equation: P(duplicate) = (1 - request_loss)*reply_loss*(1 - request_loss).
Assumptions: A timeout causes one blind retry; requests are independent and lost messages never arrive later.
Excludes: Deduplication, idempotent effects, delayed messages, and further retries.



Derivation: Multiply the probabilities of original delivery, lost original reply, and retry delivery.



>>> calc_blind_retry_duplicate_probability(0.0, 0.5) == 0.5
True
>>> calc_blind_retry_duplicate_probability(1.0, 0.5) == 0.0
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_bulkhead_admission(
    arrivals,
    workers,
    worker_cap,
    queue_cap,
)
Partition a burst into active, queued, and rejected calls.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrivals
int
Number of calls arriving in one burst; nonnegative.
required


workers
int
Total worker count; nonnegative.
required


worker_cap
int
Maximum workers allocated to this dependency; nonnegative.
required


queue_cap
int
Queue slots that hold calls without occupying workers; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Occupied workers, queued calls, rejected calls, and remaining free workers.






Equation: occupied = min(arrivals, worker_cap, workers); queued = min(arrivals - occupied, queue_cap).
Assumptions: No call finishes during admission; each active call occupies one worker.
Excludes: Service duration, queue waiting time, cancellations, and future arrivals.



Derivation: Allocate the worker budget first, then queue capacity, and reject the unallocated remainder; subtract occupied workers from total workers.



>>> occupied, queued, rejected, free = calc_bulkhead_admission(8, 4, 2, 3)
>>> occupied + queued + rejected == 8 and occupied + free == 4
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_integration_adapters(hosts, services)
Count pairwise and shared-protocol integration adapters.











Name
Type
Description
Default




hosts
int
Number of client hosts; nonnegative.
required


services
int
Number of services reached by every host; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Pairwise adapter count and shared-protocol endpoint adapter count.






Equation: pairwise = hosts*services; shared = hosts + services.
Assumptions: Every host connects to every service; each protocol endpoint needs one adapter.
Excludes: Adapter complexity, protocol gateways, compatibility testing, and partial connectivity.



Derivation: Count edges in a complete bipartite integration graph, then count its endpoint adapters.



>>> calc_integration_adapters(2, 3) == (2 * 3, 2 + 3)
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_jitter_expected_arrivals(retries, window, jitter_span)
Estimate retries arriving inside a uniform-jitter window.











Name
Type
Description
Default




retries
float
Nonnegative number of independently jittered retries.
required


window
Quantity or float
Observation-window duration, from zero to jitter_span; use compatible time units.
required


jitter_span
Quantity or float
Positive width of the uniform retry-time distribution.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Expected retry count in the specified window.






Equation: E[arrivals] = retries*window/jitter_span.
Assumptions: The window lies entirely inside the uniform jitter support; float durations share one unit.
Excludes: Realized burst size, nonuniform jitter, dependence, and windows outside the support.
An expectation is not a capacity bound: a realized window can contain every retry.



Derivation: Multiply retry count by the fraction of uniform timing mass within the observation window.



>>> calc_jitter_expected_arrivals(10, 1, 2) == 10 / 2
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_layered_retry_attempts(attempts_per_layer, layers)
Count downstream attempts under nested retry allowances.











Name
Type
Description
Default




attempts_per_layer
int
Attempts allowed per invocation at each layer, including the initial attempt; positive.
required


layers
int
Number of independently retrying layers; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Worst-case downstream attempt count for one logical operation.






Equation: attempts = attempts_per_layer ** layers.
Assumptions: Every attempt fails and exhausts all lower-layer allowances before an outer retry.
Excludes: Early success, shared retry budgets, deadlines, and deduplication.



Derivation: Multiply equal allowances across each nested layer of the retry tree.



>>> calc_layered_retry_attempts(3, 2) == 3 * 3
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_pending_polls(job_duration, poll_interval)
Count polling calls that occur before job completion.











Name
Type
Description
Default




job_duration
Quantity
Positive duration of the job, with time units.
required


poll_interval
Quantity
Positive interval between polls, with compatible time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Number of polls returning a pending status before completion.






Equation: pending = ceil(job_duration / poll_interval) - 1.
Assumptions: Polling starts one interval after dispatch; a poll at completion sees a completed result.
Excludes: Polling latency, timer jitter, adaptive intervals, and zero-duration jobs.



Derivation: Count positive interval multiples strictly less than the completion time.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> calc_pending_polls(Q_("3 s"), Q_("1 s")) == 2
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_selection_break_even(
    selection_overhead,
    descriptor_tokens,
)
Return the number of descriptors that offsets tool-selection overhead.











Name
Type
Description
Default




selection_overhead
float
Nonnegative token overhead of selecting tools.
required


descriptor_tokens
float
Positive serialized token count per omitted tool descriptor.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Omitted-descriptor count at equal token cost; savings require a larger count.






Equation: break_even = selection_overhead / descriptor_tokens.
Assumptions: Descriptor sizes are uniform and selection overhead is paid once per request.
Excludes: Selection accuracy, invocation latency, heterogeneous descriptor sizes, and integer rounding.



Derivation: Solve omitted_count*descriptor_tokens = selection_overhead for omitted_count.



>>> calc_selection_break_even(100, 20) == 100 / 20
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_timeout_probability(request_loss, reply_loss)
Return timeout probability for independently lost request and reply.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_loss
float
Probability that a request is lost; between zero and one.
required


reply_loss
float
Probability that the reply is lost after delivery; between zero and one.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Probability of a timeout on one attempt.






Equation: P(timeout) = 1 - (1 - request_loss)*(1 - reply_loss).
Assumptions: Delivery succeeds only if both messages arrive; message losses are independent.
Excludes: Finite timeout thresholds, delayed arrival, server failures, and retries.



Derivation: Take the complement of joint request-and-reply delivery under independence.



>>> calc_timeout_probability(0.0, 0.5) == 0.5
True

    request_loss,
    reply_loss,
)
Return the unconditional probability of a duplicate effect after one retry.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_loss
float
Loss probability of each request transmission; between zero and one.
required


reply_loss
float
Loss probability of the original reply; between zero and one.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Probability that the original and retry both execute the effect.






Equation: P(duplicate) = (1 - request_loss)*reply_loss*(1 - request_loss).
Assumptions: A timeout causes one blind retry; requests are independent and lost messages never arrive later.
Excludes: Deduplication, idempotent effects, delayed messages, and further retries.



Derivation: Multiply the probabilities of original delivery, lost original reply, and retry delivery.

physics.tool_calls.calc_bulkhead_admission(
    arrivals,
    workers,
    worker_cap,
    queue_cap,
)
Partition a burst into active, queued, and rejected calls.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrivals
int
Number of calls arriving in one burst; nonnegative.
required


workers
int
Total worker count; nonnegative.
required


worker_cap
int
Maximum workers allocated to this dependency; nonnegative.
required


queue_cap
int
Queue slots that hold calls without occupying workers; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Occupied workers, queued calls, rejected calls, and remaining free workers.






Equation: occupied = min(arrivals, worker_cap, workers); queued = min(arrivals - occupied, queue_cap).
Assumptions: No call finishes during admission; each active call occupies one worker.
Excludes: Service duration, queue waiting time, cancellations, and future arrivals.



Derivation: Allocate the worker budget first, then queue capacity, and reject the unallocated remainder; subtract occupied workers from total workers.



>>> occupied, queued, rejected, free = calc_bulkhead_admission(8, 4, 2, 3)
>>> occupied + queued + rejected == 8 and occupied + free == 4
True

Count pairwise and shared-protocol integration adapters.











Name
Type
Description
Default

int

required


services
int
Number of services reached by every host; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Pairwise adapter count and shared-protocol endpoint adapter count.






Equation: pairwise = hosts*services; shared = hosts + services.
Assumptions: Every host connects to every service; each protocol endpoint needs one adapter.
Excludes: Adapter complexity, protocol gateways, compatibility testing, and partial connectivity.



Derivation: Count edges in a complete bipartite integration graph, then count its endpoint adapters.



>>> calc_integration_adapters(2, 3) == (2 * 3, 2 + 3)
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_jitter_expected_arrivals(retries, window, jitter_span)
Estimate retries arriving inside a uniform-jitter window.











Name
Type
Description
Default




retries
float
Nonnegative number of independently jittered retries.
required


window
Quantity or float
Observation-window duration, from zero to jitter_span; use compatible time units.
required


jitter_span
Quantity or float
Positive width of the uniform retry-time distribution.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Expected retry count in the specified window.






Equation: E[arrivals] = retries*window/jitter_span.
Assumptions: The window lies entirely inside the uniform jitter support; float durations share one unit.
Excludes: Realized burst size, nonuniform jitter, dependence, and windows outside the support.
An expectation is not a capacity bound: a realized window can contain every retry.



Derivation: Multiply retry count by the fraction of uniform timing mass within the observation window.



>>> calc_jitter_expected_arrivals(10, 1, 2) == 10 / 2
True




physics.tool_calls.calc_layered_retry_attempts(attempts_per_layer, layers)
Count downstream attempts under nested retry allowances.











Name
Type
Description
Default

int

required

int
Number of independently retrying layers; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Worst-case downstream attempt count for one logical operation.






Equation: attempts = attempts_per_layer ** layers.
Assumptions: Every attempt fails and exhausts all lower-layer allowances before an outer retry.
Excludes: Early success, shared retry budgets, deadlines, and deduplication.



Derivation: Multiply equal allowances across each nested layer of the retry tree.



>>> calc_layered_retry_attempts(3, 2) == 3 * 3
True

Count polling calls that occur before job completion.

Type
Description
Default

required

Quantity
Positive interval between polls, with compatible time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Number of polls returning a pending status before completion.






Equation: pending = ceil(job_duration / poll_interval) - 1.
Assumptions: Polling starts one interval after dispatch; a poll at completion sees a completed result.
Excludes: Polling latency, timer jitter, adaptive intervals, and zero-duration jobs.



Derivation: Count positive interval multiples strictly less than the completion time.

Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A human reviews an AI’s output; the human accepts miss_acceptance of the AI’s misses.
The best case assumes the reviewer catches every other miss and never overturns a correct detection, so team sensitivity is at most one minus the accepted misses.

Excludes: Correlated human errors, false positives, and an empirically validated team model.

title: SchedulingSnapshotScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One snapshot of a shared pool’s in-service capacity, read at the scheduling boundary.
Capacity assigned to jobs includes gangs still waiting for members; only complete allocations can run a synchronous step, so scheduling goodput is the assigned share less the incomplete-gang share. Capacity in complete allocations waiting for input crosses this boundary and is a runtime loss.


Equation: scheduling goodput = assigned share - incomplete-gang share; executing share subtracts input waits.
Assumptions: Shares use offered capacity as the same denominator and incomplete gangs cannot perform a synchronous step.
Excludes: A time-integrated scheduler trace, queueing predictions, and removal of runtime loss by a scheduling-only change.



Derivation: scheduling goodput = assigned share - incomplete-gang share; executing share subtracts input waits. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.SharedPoolSchedulingSnapshot
>>> round(float(case.scheduling_goodput), 3)
0.65

title: ClusterExpansionScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A synchronous job grown from n_devices to factor times as many on the same checkpoint tier.
checkpoint supplies the write path; at each size its MTBF is replaced by the GPU-only interval component_mtbf / N and the overhead is the checkpoint-and-rework waste at the Young-Daly optimum. For fixed work, run time is proportional to step time over the retained fraction (one minus that overhead), so the larger job shortens the run only when its step speedup exceeds breakeven_speedup.


Equation: breakeven_speedup is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: GPU failures are independent and fixed work experiences the checkpoint solver’s steady-state waste.
Excludes: Non-GPU failures, changing failure distributions, and prediction of the supplied step speedup.



Derivation: The scenario binds declared inputs to calc_mtbf_cluster. Those implementations document their derivations and sources.



Execute the registered worked inputs; this is a modeled calculation.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.Gpt3ClusterDoubling1K
>>> value = case.breakeven_speedup
>>> round(value, 3)
1.007

title: DenseScalingSweepScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Dense networks between a fixed input and output, swept in hidden width and in depth.
Width sweep: hidden_layers hidden layers, each of every width in widths. Depth sweep: 1 to max_depth hidden layers of fixed_width. Each doubling factor compares the last setting with the one half its size.


Equation: Width and depth sweeps call calc_dense_macs; saved state calls calc_dense_saved_activations.
Assumptions: The width list contains its final width halved; max_depth is at least two for doubling comparisons.
Excludes: Runtime, hardware saturation, and accuracy changes with model size.



Derivation: Calls mlsysim.physics.neural.calc_dense_macs for each constructed width sequence and calc_dense_saved_activations for the corresponding training-state count. Ratios compare already evaluated settings; they do not assume exact quadratic or linear scaling for the fixed input/output layers.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.DenseWidthDepthSweep
>>> len(s.width_sweep_macs) == len(s.widths)
True

Hidden depth used as the denominator of the final depth-doubling comparison.

Equation: a = depth_sweep_saved_activations; a[-1] / a[depth_doubled_from - 1].

title: GravityBiasedJointStopScenario
text:
Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/control.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One loaded arm joint at joint_speed braking with machine’s peak torque while gravity holds bias_fraction of that peak along (descending) or against (ascending) the motion.
Braking deceleration is net torque over inertia; the joint stops in w^2 / (2 alpha) and the tool at lever travels that angle times the lever. The kinetic barrier h = theta - w^2 / (2 alpha_net) (descending) bounds the next torque by tau <= -tau_bias + I alpha_net (gamma h / w - 1); its negative is the braking torque the barrier demands at a tool clearance. With site, the protective separation distance prices a person at the site’s approach speed over the site’s pre-brake delay plus the descending joint stop, the tool’s reaction travel, and the tool’s stop.


Equation: tool_stop_descending is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: Single-joint inertia, lever arm, gravity bias, and available braking torque stay constant.
Excludes: Multibody dynamics, torque slew, brake onset variation, and safety certification.



Derivation: The equations below follow the stated counts, geometric relations, or accounting definitions; scenario inputs are supplied assumptions or observations, not fitted predictions.

engine.scenario_types.GravityBiasedJointStopScenario.barrier_margin(clearance)
Kinetic barrier margin in radians at the supplied tool clearance.
Kinetic barrier h = theta - w^2 / (2 alpha_net) at a tool clearance (radians).
Equation: return (clearance / self.lever).to(’’).magnitude - self.stop_angle(self.alpha_descending)



engine.scenario_types.GravityBiasedJointStopScenario.barrier_torque_demand(
    clearance,
)
Required braking torque in N m from the stated kinetic-barrier inequality.
Braking torque the barrier demands at a tool clearance (the bound’s negative).
Equation: h = self.barrier_margin(clearance) bound = (-self.bias + self.inertia * self.alpha_descending * (self.barrier_gain * h / self.joint_speed - 1)).to(‘N*m’) return (-bound).to(‘N*m’)



engine.scenario_types.GravityBiasedJointStopScenario.stop_angle(alpha)
Joint stopping angle in radians at supplied positive angular deceleration.
Joint stop angle in radians at deceleration alpha.
Equation: return (self.joint_speed ** 2 / (2 * alpha)).to(’’).magnitude



engine.scenario_types.GravityBiasedJointStopScenario.tool_stop(alpha)
Tool stopping arc length in mm at supplied angular deceleration.
Equation: return (self.lever * self.stop_angle(alpha)).to(‘mm’)

Person’s travel over the reaction (pre-brake delay) and the descending joint stop.

Total human, reaction, and stopping travel in mm before additional margins.
Protective separation before intrusion and position margins.

engine.scenario_types.GravityBiasedJointStopScenario.separation_person_share
Dimensionless human-travel share of the separation total.
Equation: return (self.separation_person / self.separation_total).to(’’).magnitude

title: engine.solvers.plant
text:
engine.solvers.plant
Physical-plant solvers: the stopping, actuation, heat, and power budgets of an embodied machine (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). Each model takes stated inputs and returns every intermediate a budget quotes, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic. The equations themselves live in physics/ (robotics/stopping.py, drivetrain.py, motors.py); these models only compose them into the budgets of one machine.





Name
Description




BrakingCeilingsModel
The three ceilings on a credible deceleration (traction, tip-over, drive torque) and back-EMF headroom.


ContinuousDeratingModel
Installed continuous torque relative to the catalog rating.


DiagnosticCoverageModel
Diagnostic coverage that leaves at most target of a raw fault rate


DriveBusModel
A shared drive bus: sustained sag under a coincident load step, and the regenerative surge of a stop.


ExponentialRareEventModel
One rare exponential tail estimated by plain Monte Carlo, a zero-failure


FreshnessProfileModel
A moving target’s freshness deadline against a capture-to-onset age profile.


GearRatioCostModel
Holding heat and reflected inertia of one motor holding one joint torque, per gear ratio.


GearedRotorModel
Reflected rotor inertia N^2 J_rotor, sized as a solid flywheel, and the inertia match.


HubDriveElectricalModel
Electrical time constant, voltage-limited current ramp, and phase-short braking peak of a hub drive.


SpeedStepModel
Braking travel added by raising the speed setpoint, and the delay that costs the same distance.


StallDeratingModel
Steady stall temperature with copper’s resistance feedback, and the hold the winding can sustain.


ThermalBurstModel
Burst horizons from a cold and a heat-soaked start, the average-power duty screen, and the periodic peak.


ThrottledStageModel
A compute-bound stage at a fraction of full clock: its time scales by the inverse clock ratio,


ZeroFailureModel
Upper bound on the per-trial failure rate after a failure-free campaign.





engine.solvers.plant.BrakingCeilingsModel()
The three ceilings on a credible deceleration (traction, tip-over, drive torque) and back-EMF headroom.
Composes calc_braking_limits for a wheeled base driven by direct-drive hub motors at a configured current limit, adds the rated-current torque ceiling and the inspected-floor traction ceiling (all weight on the driven wheels), and checks the terminal voltage braking and driving need at speed.





Name
Description




solve
The three ceilings on a credible deceleration (traction, tip-over, drive torque) and back-EMF headroom.





engine.solvers.plant.BrakingCeilingsModel.solve(
    mass,
    deceleration,
    speed,
    hub,
    n_wheels,
    current_limit,
    drive_load_share,
    mu_dry,
    mu_inspected,
    bus_low,
    cg_height=None,
    tip_arm=None,
)
The three ceilings on a credible deceleration (traction, tip-over, drive torque) and back-EMF headroom.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive translated mass (kg).
required


deceleration
Quantity
Requested positive deceleration (m/s^2).
required


speed
Quantity
Forward speed (m/s).
required


hub
object
Motor specification with wheel radius, torque constant, rotating mass bound, rated torque, back-EMF constant, and line resistance.
required


n_wheels
int
Positive driven wheel count.
required


current_limit
Quantity
Per-wheel current limit (A).
required


drive_load_share
float
Fraction of normal load carried by driven wheels, in (0, 1].
required


mu_dry
float
Positive dry-floor friction coefficient.
required


mu_inspected
float
Positive inspected-floor friction coefficient.
required


bus_low
Quantity
Available bus voltage (V).
required


cg_height
Optional[Quantity]
Optional positive center-of-gravity height (m).
None


tip_arm
Optional[Quantity]
Optional positive support-polygon tipping arm (m).
None














Name
Type
Description





BrakingCeilingsResult
Forces in N, deceleration ceilings in m/s^2, wheel torque in N*m, voltage headroom in V.






Equation: Per-wheel torque is Kt*current_limit. Effective mass is mass+n_wheels*rotating_mass_bound; torque-limited deceleration is n_wheels*torque/(radius*effective_mass). Traction limits are mu*g*drive_load_share. Tip-over and voltage checks compose calc_braking_limits and calc_drive_voltage_headroom.
Assumptions: Quasistatic traction and rigid-body torque limits; identical wheel drives.
Excludes: Dynamic load transfer, tire dynamics, and safety certification.



Derivation: Wheel torque divided by radius gives longitudinal force; dividing by effective mass gives deceleration. Friction bounds that force by normal load times friction coefficient. See mlsysim.physics.drivetrain.calc_braking_limits for the tipping constraint and mlsysim.physics.drivetrain.calc_drive_voltage_headroom for the electrical convention.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> hub = SimpleNamespace(wheel_radius=Q("0.1 m"), torque_constant=Q("1 N*m/A"), rotating_mass_bound=Q("1 kg"), rated_torque=Q("1 N*m"), peak_torque=Q("2 N*m"), back_emf_constant=Q("1 V*s/rad"), line_resistance=Q("1 ohm"), line_inductance=Q("0.001 H"), peak_current=Q("20 A"), pole_pairs=10)
>>> BrakingCeilingsModel().solve(Q("100 kg"), Q("1 m/s^2"), Q("1 m/s"), hub, 2, Q("10 A"), 1.0, 0.8, 0.6, Q("48 V")).force.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.ContinuousDeratingModel()
Installed continuous torque relative to the catalog rating.
Continuous torque scales as sqrt((T_max - T_amb) / theta): a hotter ambient and a larger installed thermal resistance each cut it.





Name
Description




solve
Installed continuous torque relative to the catalog rating.





engine.solvers.plant.ContinuousDeratingModel.solve(
    ceiling,
    catalog_ambient,
    installed_ambient,
    thermal_resistance_factor,
)
Installed continuous torque relative to the catalog rating.











Name
Type
Description
Default




ceiling
Quantity
Absolute winding temperature ceiling (K).
required


catalog_ambient
Quantity
Catalog ambient below ceiling (K).
required


installed_ambient
Quantity
Installed ambient below ceiling (K).
required


thermal_resistance_factor
float
Positive installed/catalog thermal resistance ratio.
required














Name
Type
Description





ContinuousDeratingResult
Dimensionless installed/catalog torque shares for ambient alone and combined thermal effects.






Equation: Ambient-only torque share is sqrt((ceiling-installed_ambient)/(ceiling-catalog_ambient)); combined share divides this by sqrt(thermal_resistance_factor).
Assumptions: Torque proportional to current and copper loss proportional to current squared.
Excludes: Temperature-dependent electrical resistance and transient bursts.



Derivation: At equilibrium, allowable copper power is temperature headroom divided by thermal resistance. Fixed resistance makes allowable current proportional to the square root of this power, and fixed torque constant makes torque proportional to current.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> ContinuousDeratingModel().solve(Q("350 K"), Q("300 K"), Q("320 K"), 2).combined_share < 1
True






engine.solvers.plant.DiagnosticCoverageModel()
Diagnostic coverage that leaves at most target of a raw fault rate unmitigated, and the zero-miss injection campaign that demonstrates it (added 2026-10-20).
Rates are in FIT (faults per 10^9 hours). The raw rate is the sum of the strata; coverage C_diag = 1 - target / raw. Each injection misses with probability 1 - C_diag, so n zero-miss injections bound it at confidence C when n >= ln(1 - C) / ln(C_diag); the rule of three approximates n by 3 / (1 - C_diag). Drawn in proportion to the rates, each stratum receives its share of the n injections.





Name
Description




solve
Diagnostic coverage that leaves at most target of a raw fault rate unmitigated, and the zero-miss injection campaign that demonstrates it (added 2026-10-20).





engine.solvers.plant.DiagnosticCoverageModel.solve(strata, target, confidence)
Diagnostic coverage that leaves at most target of a raw fault rate unmitigated, and the zero-miss injection campaign that demonstrates it (added 2026-10-20).











Name
Type
Description
Default




strata
Dict[str, float]
Mapping from stratum names to nonnegative fault rates (FIT), positive total.
required


target
float
Positive residual rate below the total, in FIT.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence level in (0, 1).
required














Name
Type
Description





DiagnosticCoverageResult
Fault-rate total in FIT, dimensionless coverage and shares, and injection counts.






Equation: Raw rate is sum(strata.values()); required coverage = 1-target/raw_rate. The exact real-valued trial threshold is ln(1-confidence)/ln(coverage), rounded upward for injections. Stratum share = stratum_rate/raw_rate; allocation = injections*share.
Assumptions: Independent representative injection trials and proportional stratum allocation.
Excludes: Unequal detection probability by stratum, common-cause dependencies, and certification.



Derivation: Residual faults are the raw rate times the missed fraction. For independent representative injections, observing no misses has probability coverage^n. Inverting that probability gives the trial threshold. Proportional allocations are expected counts, not a rounded stratified test design.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> DiagnosticCoverageModel().solve({"sensor": 100.0}, 1.0, 0.95).injections > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.DriveBusModel()
A shared drive bus: sustained sag under a coincident load step, and the regenerative surge of a stop.
Sag Delta V = Delta I R_bus against the converter lockout; the step current that would spend the depleted pack’s headroom is (V_low - V_uvlo) / R_bus. A stop from speed v returns a share of (1/2) m v^2; into the bus capacitance alone, V_final = sqrt(V_full^2 + 2 E / C). Speed falls linearly at constant deceleration, so regenerated power falls linearly from 2 E / t_stop, and a chopper resistor at the clamp must satisfy R <= V_clamp^2 / P_peak.





Name
Description




solve
A shared drive bus: sustained sag under a coincident load step, and the regenerative surge of a stop.

    mass,
    speed,
    deceleration,
    step_current,
    bus_resistance,
    full,
    nominal,
    depleted,
    lockout,
    compute_power,
    converter_efficiency,
    capacitance,
    clamp,
    regen_fraction,
)
A shared drive bus: sustained sag under a coincident load step, and the regenerative surge of a stop.











Name
Type
Description
Default

required


speed
Quantity
Positive entry speed (m/s).
required


deceleration
Quantity
Positive constant deceleration (m/s^2).
required


step_current
Quantity
Positive coincident current increase (A).
required


bus_resistance
Quantity
Positive supply-path resistance (ohm).
required

Quantity
Full-pack voltage (V).
required


nominal
Quantity
Nominal voltage (V).
required


depleted
Quantity
Depleted-pack voltage (V).
required


lockout
Quantity
Converter undervoltage lockout (V).
required


compute_power
Quantity
Compute load power (W).
required


converter_efficiency
float
Converter efficiency in (0, 1].
required


capacitance
Quantity
Positive bus capacitance (F).
required


clamp
Quantity
Regeneration clamp voltage (V).
required


regen_fraction
float
Fraction of kinetic energy recovered, in (0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





DriveBusResult
Bus voltages in V, currents in A, energies in J, stop time in ms, peak power in W, and resistor bound in ohm.






Equation: Compute current = compute_power/(converter_efficiency*nominal); sag = step_current*bus_resistance. Recovered energy E = regen_fraction*mass*speed^2/2 gives capacitor-only endpoint sqrt(full^2+2*E/capacitance). Stop duration = speed/deceleration, peak regenerative power = 2*E/stop_duration, and resistor ceiling = clamp^2/peak_power.
Assumptions: Constant deceleration, resistive sustained sag, and stated energy-recovery fraction.
Excludes: Inductive transients, battery absorption, and chopper switching dynamics.



Derivation: Ohm’s law gives sustained sag. Equating recovered kinetic energy to the increase in capacitor energy gives the endpoint voltage. Constant deceleration makes recovery power triangular in time, so its peak is twice its mean. This treats the capacitor-only case separately from battery absorption.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> DriveBusModel().solve(Q("100 kg"), Q("1 m/s"), Q("1 m/s^2"), Q("10 A"), Q("0.1 ohm"), Q("48 V"), Q("44 V"), Q("40 V"), Q("36 V"), Q("100 W"), 0.9, Q("1 F"), Q("50 V"), 0.5).regenerated.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.ExponentialRareEventModel()
One rare exponential tail estimated by plain Monte Carlo, a zero-failure campaign, and cross-entropy importance sampling (added 2026-10-20).
The operational variable is exponential with mean; failure is a draw past threshold, so p = exp(-threshold / mean). Plain Monte Carlo needs (1 - p) / (p r^2) runs for relative error r; a zero-failure campaign needs ceil(ln(1 - C) / ln(1 - p)) clean runs to bound p. The cross-entropy method with elite_share reaches the threshold in a few levels; its exponential proposal gives the per-draw relative variance, the weighted runs for r, the share of proposal draws that fail, and the effective sample size.





Name
Description




solve
One rare exponential tail estimated by plain Monte Carlo, a zero-failure campaign, and cross-entropy importance sampling (added 2026-10-20).





engine.solvers.plant.ExponentialRareEventModel.solve(
    threshold,
    mean,
    elite_share,
    relative_error,
    confidence,
)
One rare exponential tail estimated by plain Monte Carlo, a zero-failure campaign, and cross-entropy importance sampling (added 2026-10-20).











Name
Type
Description
Default




threshold
Quantity
Positive failure threshold, in the same units as mean.
required


mean
Quantity
Positive operational exponential mean.
required


elite_share
float
Cross-entropy elite fraction in (0, 1).
required


relative_error
float
Positive target relative standard error.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence level in (0, 1).
required














Name
Type
Description





ExponentialRareEventResult
Analytic failure probabilities, dimensionless variances, effective counts, and proposal mean in the input units.






Equation: Failure probability p = exp(-threshold/mean). Plain Monte Carlo requires (1-p)/(p*relative_error^2) draws; importance sampling requires relative_variance/relative_error^2. Proposal means and variances come from the analytic exponential cross-entropy and importance-sampling helpers.
Assumptions: Exponential operational and proposal families with analytic importance weights.
Excludes: Empirical sampling, distribution misspecification, and device measurements.



Derivation: The exponential survival function gives p. Bernoulli variance divided by squared target absolute error gives the ordinary sample budget. Applying the same variance-to-error calculation to likelihood-weighted draws yields the importance budget; see mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_importance_sampling_exponential and calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> ExponentialRareEventModel().solve(Q("5 s"), Q("1 s"), 0.1, 0.1, 0.95).failure_probability < 1
True






engine.solvers.plant.FreshnessProfileModel()
A moving target’s freshness deadline against a capture-to-onset age profile.
The deadline is the tolerance left after the initial error, divided by the target speed: Delta t_fresh = (r_tol - e_0) / v. Stage percentiles are summed per percentile; the target’s travel at the median chain and at the system tail age is compared with the allowed error.





Name
Description




solve
A moving target’s freshness deadline against a capture-to-onset age profile.





engine.solvers.plant.FreshnessProfileModel.solve(
    target_speed,
    tolerance,
    initial_error,
    stages,
    focus_stage,
    tail_age,
)
A moving target’s freshness deadline against a capture-to-onset age profile.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_speed
Quantity
Positive target speed (m/s).
required


tolerance
Quantity
Allowed position error (m).
required


initial_error
Quantity
Position error before motion (m).
required


stages
Sequence[Tuple[str, Quantity, Quantity, Quantity]]
Sequence of (name, median, p99, maximum), with times in seconds.
required


focus_stage
str
Name present in stages whose median is inspected.
required


tail_age
Quantity
Separately supplied end-to-end tail age (s).
required














Name
Type
Description





FreshnessProfileResult
Allowed error and travel in mm, age/deadline in ms, and focus rate in Hz.






Equation: Remaining position allowance r = tolerance-initial_error gives deadline r/target_speed. Each stage column is summed separately. Travel at age t is target_speed*t; slack is r-travel.
Assumptions: Constant target speed; stage quantiles are added as a budgeting convention, not as a probabilistic convolution.
Excludes: Correlation modeling and a guarantee that summed p99 values equal end-to-end p99.



Derivation: A constant-speed target consumes position allowance linearly with age. Stage-quantile sums are a declared budget construction, while tail_age is a separate end-to-end input; summing marginal quantiles does not derive a joint quantile.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> FreshnessProfileModel().solve(Q("1 m/s"), Q("1 m"), Q("0.1 m"), [("sensor", Q("0.01 s"), Q("0.02 s"), Q("0.03 s"))], "sensor", Q("0.04 s")).deadline.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.GearRatioCostModel()
Holding heat and reflected inertia of one motor holding one joint torque, per gear ratio.
Motor torque tau_m = tau_out / (eta N); copper loss (tau_m / K_m)^2 with K_m = K_t / sqrt(R_loss); reflected inertia N^2 J_in. Their product is tau_out^2 J_in / (eta^2 K_m^2), independent of N.





Name
Description




solve
Holding heat and reflected inertia of one motor holding one joint torque, per gear ratio.





engine.solvers.plant.GearRatioCostModel.solve(
    motor,
    loss_resistance,
    input_inertia,
    output_torque,
    gear_efficiency,
    ratios,
)
Holding heat and reflected inertia of one motor holding one joint torque, per gear ratio.











Name
Type
Description
Default




motor
object
Motor specification with torque constant, peak torque, and rated torque.
required


loss_resistance
Quantity
Positive equivalent copper-loss resistance (ohm).
required


input_inertia
Quantity
Positive input-side inertia (kg*m^2).
required


output_torque
Quantity
Required joint holding torque (N*m).
required


gear_efficiency
float
Transmission efficiency in (0, 1].
required


ratios
Iterable[int]
Iterable of positive integer reduction ratios.
required














Name
Type
Description





GearRatioCostResult
Per-ratio dictionaries of torque (Nm), copper loss (W), and reflected inertia (kgm^2).






Equation: For reduction N, motor torque is output_torque/(gear_efficiency*N), motor constant Km = torque_constant/sqrt(loss_resistance), copper loss = (motor_torque/Km)^2, and reflected inertia = N^2*input_inertia.
Assumptions: Constant torque constant, loss resistance, and efficiency across ratios.
Excludes: Motion losses, gear mass, and temperature feedback.



Derivation: Combining torque = Kt*current with Joule loss current^2*R gives the torque-squared loss expression. Reflection increases inertia quadratically while required motor torque decreases inversely with reduction; their loss-inertia product therefore cancels N under fixed efficiency.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> hub = SimpleNamespace(wheel_radius=Q("0.1 m"), torque_constant=Q("1 N*m/A"), rotating_mass_bound=Q("1 kg"), rated_torque=Q("1 N*m"), peak_torque=Q("2 N*m"), back_emf_constant=Q("1 V*s/rad"), line_resistance=Q("1 ohm"), line_inductance=Q("0.001 H"), peak_current=Q("20 A"), pole_pairs=10)
>>> GearRatioCostModel().solve(hub, Q("1 ohm"), Q("0.01 kg*m^2"), Q("10 N*m"), 0.9, [10, 20]).copper_loss[10].magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.GearedRotorModel()
Reflected rotor inertia N^2 J_rotor, sized as a solid flywheel, and the inertia match.
A solid disk of radius r has J = m r^2 / 2, so m = 2 J / r^2. Joint acceleration for a fixed motor torque peaks at N* = sqrt(J_load / J_rotor); at N it is 2x / (1 + x^2) of that peak, x = N / N*.





Name
Description




solve
Reflected rotor inertia N^2 J_rotor, sized as a solid flywheel, and the inertia match.





engine.solvers.plant.GearedRotorModel.solve(
    gear_ratio,
    rotor_mass,
    rotor_inertia,
    flywheel_radius,
    load_inertia,
)
Reflected rotor inertia N^2 J_rotor, sized as a solid flywheel, and the inertia match.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gear_ratio
float
Positive output reduction ratio.
required


rotor_mass
Quantity
Positive rotor mass (kg).
required


rotor_inertia
Quantity
Positive rotor inertia (kg*m^2).
required


flywheel_radius
Quantity
Positive equivalent solid-disk radius (m).
required


load_inertia
Quantity
Positive output load inertia (kg*m^2).
required














Name
Type
Description





GearedRotorResult
Reflected inertia in kg*m^2, equivalent mass in kg, radius in mm, and dimensionless response share.






Equation: Reflected inertia is gear_ratio^2*rotor_inertia. Equivalent disk mass is 2*reflected_inertia/flywheel_radius^2. Matched ratio Nstar = sqrt(load_inertia/rotor_inertia); normalized acceleration is 2*x/(1+x^2), x = gear_ratio/Nstar.
Assumptions: Ideal rigid transmission and solid-disk equivalent flywheel.
Excludes: Gear compliance, friction, and efficiency losses.



Derivation: Conservation of rotational kinetic energy reflects inertia through the square of the speed ratio. The disk equivalent uses J = m*r^2/2. Maximizing acceleration at fixed motor torque over reduction ratio gives the inertia match; see mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_inertia_matched_ratio.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> GearedRotorModel().solve(10, Q("1 kg"), Q("0.01 kg*m^2"), Q("0.1 m"), Q("1 kg*m^2")).reflected_inertia.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.HubDriveElectricalModel()
Electrical time constant, voltage-limited current ramp, and phase-short braking peak of a hub drive.
tau_e = L / R (line quantities, the same ratio as per phase for a star winding); at stall the back-EMF is zero, so the full bus voltage ramps the current at V / L: t = L I / V. Shorted windings brake hardest where the winding reactance equals its resistance: omega_e = R / L, which is omega_e / p at the wheel for p pole pairs. The same R / L, divided by 2 pi, is the winding’s current pole in hertz.





Name
Description




solve
Electrical time constant, voltage-limited current ramp, and phase-short braking peak of a hub drive.





engine.solvers.plant.HubDriveElectricalModel.solve(
    hub,
    current_limit,
    bus_voltage,
    brake_onset,
)
Electrical time constant, voltage-limited current ramp, and phase-short braking peak of a hub drive.











Name
Type
Description
Default




hub
object
Motor specification with line inductance/resistance, peak current, and pole pairs.
required


current_limit
Quantity
Positive target current (A).
required


bus_voltage
Quantity
Positive applied voltage (V).
required


brake_onset
Quantity
Positive allotted electrical onset time (s).
required














Name
Type
Description





HubDriveElectricalResult
Electrical times in ms, currents in A, electrical speed in rad/s, wheel speed in rpm, and pole frequency in Hz.






Equation: Electrical time constant is L/R; initial ramp time is L*current_limit/bus_voltage. Full-step current is bus_voltage/R. The short-braking peak electrical speed is R/L, wheel speed is (R/L)/pole_pairs, and pole frequency is R/(2*pi*L).
Assumptions: Linear winding inductance/resistance; zero back-EMF during current-ramp calculation.
Excludes: PWM switching, magnetic saturation, and inverter dynamics.



Derivation: The series RL circuit equation at zero back-EMF gives the initial current slope V/L and steady current V/R. The short-braking speed estimate equates winding reactance and resistance; it assumes the linear sinusoidal electrical model.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> hub = SimpleNamespace(wheel_radius=Q("0.1 m"), torque_constant=Q("1 N*m/A"), rotating_mass_bound=Q("1 kg"), rated_torque=Q("1 N*m"), peak_torque=Q("2 N*m"), back_emf_constant=Q("1 V*s/rad"), line_resistance=Q("1 ohm"), line_inductance=Q("0.001 H"), peak_current=Q("20 A"), pole_pairs=10)
>>> HubDriveElectricalModel().solve(hub, Q("10 A"), Q("48 V"), Q("0.01 s")).time_constant.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.SpeedStepModel()
Braking travel added by raising the speed setpoint, and the delay that costs the same distance.
Braking travel grows as v^2; the added travel divided by the base speed is the pre-brake delay that would cost the same distance at the base speed.





Name
Description




solve
Braking travel added by raising the speed setpoint, and the delay that costs the same distance.





engine.solvers.plant.SpeedStepModel.solve(
    base_speed,
    raised_speed,
    deceleration,
)
Braking travel added by raising the speed setpoint, and the delay that costs the same distance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




base_speed
Quantity
Positive initial speed (m/s).
required


raised_speed
Quantity
Comparison speed (m/s).
required


deceleration
Quantity
Positive constant braking magnitude (m/s^2).
required














Name
Type
Description





SpeedStepResult
Added braking distance in mm and equivalent delay in ms; fractional growth is dimensionless.






Equation: For speeds v0 and v1 and positive deceleration a, d0 = v0^2/(2a), d1 = v1^2/(2a), added = d1-d0, growth = d1/d0-1, and equivalent delay = added/v0.
Assumptions: Fixed deceleration at both speeds.
Excludes: Brake ramps, tire slip, and controller delay.



Derivation: Integrating constant deceleration gives stopping time v/a and mean speed v/2. Their product is the stopping distance; divide the difference of two distances by the original speed to express it as delay.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> SpeedStepModel().solve(Q("1 m/s"), Q("2 m/s"), Q("1 m/s^2")).braking_added.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.StallDeratingModel()
Steady stall temperature with copper’s resistance feedback, and the hold the winding can sustain.
Steady state: dT = I^2 R_0 [1 + alpha (T_amb - T_0 + dT)] theta, linear in dT, so dT = c / (1 - g) with loop gain g = I^2 R_0 theta alpha (runaway if g >= 1). The sustainable loss at the limit is (T_limit - T_amb) / theta at the hot resistance R(T_limit).





Name
Description




solve
Steady stall temperature with copper’s resistance feedback, and the hold the winding can sustain.





engine.solvers.plant.StallDeratingModel.solve(
    hold_torque,
    gear_ratio,

StallDeratingResult
Steady thermal rise in K, current in A, resistance in ohm, loss in W, and sustainable torque in N*m.






Equation: Motor current I = hold_torque/(gear_efficiency*gear_ratio*torque_constant). With copper coefficient alpha, cold resistance R0, and thermal resistance theta, feedback gain g = I^2*R0*theta*alpha. Steady rise is I^2*R0*theta*(1+alpha*(ambient-T0))/(1-g). Sustainable current is sqrt((limit-ambient)/(theta*R(limit))).
Assumptions: Linear copper resistance feedback; finite stable equilibrium requires feedback_gain < 1.
Excludes: Nonlinear heat transfer and runaway transient dynamics; algebraic output above unit gain is not a stable equilibrium.



Derivation: Substitute the linear copper resistance-temperature relation into steady Joule heating and collect terms in temperature rise. The resulting denominator exposes the unit-gain instability. See mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_copper_resistance_factor for the reference-temperature convention.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> StallDeratingModel().solve(Q("1 N*m"), 10, 0.9, Q("1 N*m/A"), Q("1 ohm"), Q("1 K/W"), Q("300 K"), Q("350 K")).sustainable_current.magnitude > 0
True

Derivation: The lumped thermal energy balance gives exponential heating toward ambient+power*thermal_resistance. Inverting this exponential yields cold and hot horizons. See mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_first_order_time_to_temperature and calc_periodic_burst_peak_rise; average-power screening alone does not bound the periodic peak.

Equation: For n trials and confidence C, approximate upper failure probability is -ln(1-C)/n; exact upper probability is 1-(1-C)^(1/n). A target p requires ceil(ln(1-C)/ln(1-p)) failure-free trials.
Assumptions: Independent identically distributed Bernoulli trials; approximate rate uses the zero-event Poisson bound.
Excludes: Nonstationarity, correlated failures, and proof of absence of failures.



Derivation: For independent Bernoulli trials, the probability of zero failures is (1-p)^n. Invert this probability at tail mass 1-C to obtain the exact one-sided bound. Replacing ln(1-p) by -p yields the Poisson approximation; see mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance.calc_zero_failure_sample_size.

>>> ZeroFailureModel().solve(100, 0.95).rate_upper_exact < 1
True

Equation: Per-wheel torque is Kt*current_limit. Effective mass is mass+n_wheels*rotating_mass_bound; torque-limited deceleration is n_wheels*torque/(radius*effective_mass). Traction limits are mu*g*drive_load_share. Tip-over and voltage checks compose calc_braking_limits and calc_drive_voltage_headroom.
Assumptions: Quasistatic traction and rigid-body torque limits; identical wheel drives.
Excludes: Dynamic load transfer, tire dynamics, and safety certification.



Derivation: Wheel torque divided by radius gives longitudinal force; dividing by effective mass gives deceleration. Friction bounds that force by normal load times friction coefficient. engine.solvers.plant.DiagnosticCoverageModel()
Diagnostic coverage that leaves at most target of a raw fault rate unmitigated, and the zero-miss injection campaign that demonstrates it (added 2026-10-20).
Rates are in FIT (faults per 10^9 hours). The raw rate is the sum of the strata; coverage C_diag = 1 - target / raw. Each injection misses with probability 1 - C_diag, so n zero-miss injections bound it at confidence C when n >= ln(1 - C) / ln(C_diag); the rule of three approximates n by 3 / (1 - C_diag). Drawn in proportion to the rates, each stratum receives its share of the n injections.

Equation: Raw rate is sum(strata.values()); required coverage = 1-target/raw_rate. The exact real-valued trial threshold is ln(1-confidence)/ln(coverage), rounded upward for injections. Stratum share = stratum_rate/raw_rate; allocation = injections*share.
Assumptions: Independent representative injection trials and proportional stratum allocation.
Excludes: Unequal detection probability by stratum, common-cause dependencies, and certification.



Derivation: Residual faults are the raw rate times the missed fraction. For independent representative injections, observing no misses has probability coverage^n. Inverting that probability gives the trial threshold. Proportional allocations are expected counts, not a rounded stratified test design.

>>> DiagnosticCoverageModel().solve({"sensor": 100.0}, 1.0, 0.95).injections > 0

engine.solvers.plant.DriveBusModel()
A shared drive bus: sustained sag under a coincident load step, and the regenerative surge of a stop.
Sag Delta V = Delta I R_bus against the converter lockout; the step current that would spend the depleted pack’s headroom is (V_low - V_uvlo) / R_bus. A stop from speed v returns a share of (1/2) m v^2; into the bus capacitance alone, V_final = sqrt(V_full^2 + 2 E / C). Speed falls linearly at constant deceleration, so regenerated power falls linearly from 2 E / t_stop, and a chopper resistor at the clamp must satisfy R <= V_clamp^2 / P_peak.

Stop duration = speed/deceleration, peak regenerative power = 2*E/stop_duration, and resistor ceiling = clamp^2/peak_power.

Derivation: Ohm’s law gives sustained sag. Equating recovered kinetic energy to the increase in capacitor energy gives the endpoint voltage. Constant deceleration makes recovery power triangular in time, so its peak is twice its mean. This treats the capacitor-only case separately from battery absorption.

engine.solvers.plant.ExponentialRareEventModel()
One rare exponential tail estimated by plain Monte Carlo, a zero-failure campaign, and cross-entropy importance sampling (added 2026-10-20).
The operational variable is exponential with mean; failure is a draw past threshold, so p = exp(-threshold / mean). Plain Monte Carlo needs (1 - p) / (p r^2) runs for relative error r; a zero-failure campaign needs ceil(ln(1 - C) / ln(1 - p)) clean runs to bound p. The cross-entropy method with elite_share reaches the threshold in a few levels; its exponential proposal gives the per-draw relative variance, the weighted runs for r, the share of proposal draws that fail, and the effective sample size.

Equation: Failure probability p = exp(-threshold/mean). Plain Monte Carlo requires (1-p)/(p*relative_error^2) draws; importance sampling requires relative_variance/relative_error^2. Proposal means and variances come from the analytic exponential cross-entropy and importance-sampling helpers.
Assumptions: Exponential operational and proposal families with analytic importance weights.
Excludes: Empirical sampling, distribution misspecification, and device measurements.



Derivation: The exponential survival function gives p. Bernoulli variance divided by squared target absolute error gives the ordinary sample budget. Applying the same variance-to-error calculation to likelihood-weighted draws yields the importance budget; see mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_importance_sampling_exponential and calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> ExponentialRareEventModel().solve(Q("5 s"), Q("1 s"), 0.1, 0.1, 0.95).failure_probability < 1
True

Equation: For reduction N, motor torque is output_torque/(gear_efficiency*N), motor constant Km = torque_constant/sqrt(loss_resistance), copper loss = (motor_torque/Km)^2, and reflected inertia = N^2*input_inertia.

Derivation: Combining torque = Kt*current with Joule loss current^2*R gives the torque-squared loss expression. Reflection increases inertia quadratically while required motor torque decreases inversely with reduction; their loss-inertia product therefore cancels N under fixed efficiency.

engine.solvers.plant.GearedRotorModel()
Reflected rotor inertia N^2 J_rotor, sized as a solid flywheel, and the inertia match.
A solid disk of radius r has J = m r^2 / 2, so m = 2 J / r^2. Joint acceleration for a fixed motor torque peaks at N* = sqrt(J_load / J_rotor); at N it is 2x / (1 + x^2) of that peak, x = N / N*.

Description

Equation: Reflected inertia is gear_ratio^2*rotor_inertia. Equivalent disk mass is 2*reflected_inertia/flywheel_radius^2. Matched ratio Nstar = sqrt(load_inertia/rotor_inertia); normalized acceleration is 2*x/(1+x^2), x = gear_ratio/Nstar.
Assumptions: Ideal rigid transmission and solid-disk equivalent flywheel.
Excludes: Gear compliance, friction, and efficiency losses.



Derivation: Conservation of rotational kinetic energy reflects inertia through the square of the speed ratio. The disk equivalent uses J = m*r^2/2. Maximizing acceleration at fixed motor torque over reduction ratio gives the inertia match; see mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_inertia_matched_ratio.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> GearedRotorModel().solve(10, Q("1 kg"), Q("0.01 kg*m^2"), Q("0.1 m"), Q("1 kg*m^2")).reflected_inertia.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.HubDriveElectricalModel()
Electrical time constant, voltage-limited current ramp, and phase-short braking peak of a hub drive.
tau_e = L / R (line quantities, the same ratio as per phase for a star winding); at stall the back-EMF is zero, so the full bus voltage ramps the current at V / L: t = L I / V. Shorted windings brake hardest where the winding reactance equals its resistance: omega_e = R / L, which is omega_e / p at the wheel for p pole pairs. The same R / L, divided by 2 pi, is the winding’s current pole in hertz.

Description




solve

)
