Equation: Electrical time constant is L/R; initial ramp time is L*current_limit/bus_voltage. Full-step current is bus_voltage/R. The short-braking peak electrical speed is R/L, wheel speed is (R/L)/pole_pairs, and pole frequency is R/(2*pi*L).
Assumptions: Linear winding inductance/resistance; zero back-EMF during current-ramp calculation.
Excludes: PWM switching, magnetic saturation, and inverter dynamics.



Derivation: The series RL circuit equation at zero back-EMF gives the initial current slope V/L and steady current V/R. The short-braking speed estimate equates winding reactance and resistance; it assumes the linear sinusoidal electrical model.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> hub = SimpleNamespace(wheel_radius=Q("0.1 m"), torque_constant=Q("1 N*m/A"), rotating_mass_bound=Q("1 kg"), rated_torque=Q("1 N*m"), peak_torque=Q("2 N*m"), back_emf_constant=Q("1 V*s/rad"), line_resistance=Q("1 ohm"), line_inductance=Q("0.001 H"), peak_current=Q("20 A"), pole_pairs=10)
>>> HubDriveElectricalModel().solve(hub, Q("10 A"), Q("48 V"), Q("0.01 s")).time_constant.magnitude > 0
True

engine.solvers.plant.StallDeratingModel()
Steady stall temperature with copper’s resistance feedback, and the hold the winding can sustain.
Steady state: dT = I^2 R_0 [1 + alpha (T_amb - T_0 + dT)] theta, linear in dT, so dT = c / (1 - g) with loop gain g = I^2 R_0 theta alpha (runaway if g >= 1). The sustainable loss at the limit is (T_limit - T_amb) / theta at the hot resistance R(T_limit).

StallDeratingResult
Steady thermal rise in K, current in A, resistance in ohm, loss in W, and sustainable torque in N*m.






Equation: Motor current I = hold_torque/(gear_efficiency*gear_ratio*torque_constant). With copper coefficient alpha, cold resistance R0, and thermal resistance theta, feedback gain g = I^2*R0*theta*alpha. Steady rise is I^2*R0*theta*(1+alpha*(ambient-T0))/(1-g). Sustainable current is sqrt((limit-ambient)/(theta*R(limit))).
Assumptions: Linear copper resistance feedback; finite stable equilibrium requires feedback_gain < 1.
Excludes: Nonlinear heat transfer and runaway transient dynamics; algebraic output above unit gain is not a stable equilibrium.



Derivation: Substitute the linear copper resistance-temperature relation into steady Joule heating and collect terms in temperature rise. The resulting denominator exposes the unit-gain instability. See mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_copper_resistance_factor for the reference-temperature convention.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> StallDeratingModel().solve(Q("1 N*m"), 10, 0.9, Q("1 N*m/A"), Q("1 ohm"), Q("1 K/W"), Q("300 K"), Q("350 K")).sustainable_current.magnitude > 0
True






engine.solvers.plant.ThermalBurstModel()
Burst horizons from a cold and a heat-soaked start, the average-power duty screen, and the periodic peak.
First-order lumped winding at fixed resistance: tau = theta C; the burst drives the winding toward T_amb + P theta; the duty screen holds the average loss to (T_ceiling - T_amb) / theta; the off-time is rounded up to 0.1 s and the resulting schedule’s periodic peak is checked against the ceiling.

Type

Thermal horizons in s, temperatures in K, losses in W, burst current in A, and dimensionless duty.






Equation: Thermal time constant is thermal_resistance*thermal_capacitance. Burst loss is (burst_factor*rated_current)^2*loss_resistance; asymptotic temperature is ambient+burst_loss*thermal_resistance. Duty = (ceiling-ambient)/(thermal_resistance*burst_loss); off-time is burst_on*(1-duty)/duty, rounded upward to tenths of a second for the periodic check.
Assumptions: Single thermal pole and fixed resistance; choose limits below the burst asymptote for finite heating horizons.
Excludes: Temperature-dependent resistance, spatial hot spots, and thermal protection certification.



Derivation: The lumped thermal energy balance gives exponential heating toward ambient+power*thermal_resistance. Inverting this exponential yields cold and hot horizons. See mlsysim.physics.motors.calc_first_order_time_to_temperature and calc_periodic_burst_peak_rise; average-power screening alone does not bound the periodic peak.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> ThermalBurstModel().solve(Q("1 A"), Q("1 ohm"), Q("10 J/K"), Q("1 K/W"), Q("300 K"), Q("303 K"), Q("302 K"), 2, Q("1 s")).burst_loss.magnitude > 0

engine.solvers.plant.ZeroFailureModel()
Upper bound on the per-trial failure rate after a failure-free campaign.
Poisson (rule of three):  p_upper = -ln(1 - C) / n
exact binomial:           p_upper = 1 - (1 - C)^(1/n)
With target_rate, also the clean trials that bound the rate at the target: ceil(ln(1 - C) / ln(1 - target)), and its rule-of-three estimate -ln(1 - C) / target (exact form and target added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve

    trials,
    confidence,
    target_rate=None,
)

Type

Default

int

required

float

required

Optional[float]

None














Name
Type
Description





ZeroFailureResult
Dimensionless approximate/exact failure bounds and trial counts; optional target counts are None when no target is supplied.






Equation: For n trials and confidence C, approximate upper failure probability is -ln(1-C)/n; exact upper probability is 1-(1-C)^(1/n). A target p requires ceil(ln(1-C)/ln(1-p)) failure-free trials.
Assumptions: Independent identically distributed Bernoulli trials; approximate rate uses the zero-event Poisson bound.
Excludes: Nonstationarity, correlated failures, and proof of absence of failures.



Derivation: For independent Bernoulli trials, the probability of zero failures is (1-p)^n. Invert this probability at tail mass 1-C to obtain the exact one-sided bound. Replacing ln(1-p) by -p yields the Poisson approximation; see mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance.calc_zero_failure_sample_size.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_ as Q
>>> ZeroFailureModel().solve(100, 0.95).rate_upper_exact < 1
True

physics.memory.calc_activation_memory(
    n_layers,
    seq_len,
    batch_size,
    hidden_dim,
    n_heads=None,
    precision_bytes=2,
    strategy='selective',
)
Estimate saved Transformer training activations per device.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_layers
int
Positive number of layers resident on the device after pipeline partitioning.
required


seq_len
int
Positive tokens per sequence.
required


batch_size
int
Positive microbatch sequence count per device.
required


hidden_dim
int
Positive hidden width in elements.
required


n_heads
int
Positive attention-head count; required for strategy=“none” and otherwise unused.
None


precision_bytes
float
Positive bytes per activation element; default 2 scales the FP16 accounting.
2


strategy
str
Saved-state policy: none, selective (default), or full recomputation.
'selective'









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Total saved activation storage in bytes.






Equation: M = L * (b/2) * A. At FP16, A = 34*S*B*H + 5*N_heads*S**2*B for none, 34*S*B*H for selective, and 2*S*B*H for full.
Assumptions: Equal layer shapes and the FP16 saved-tensor convention of Korthikanti et al. Selective recomputation discards attention matrices; full recomputation retains layer inputs. Other precisions scale all coefficients uniformly.
Excludes: Weights, gradients, optimizer state, kernel scratch space, allocator reserve, sequence/tensor-parallel sharding, and schedule-dependent simultaneous microbatch residency.
The attention coefficient counts softmax probabilities, a dropout mask, and dropped probabilities. The FP16 byte widths are already included in the coefficients; multiplying them by precision_bytes without dividing by two would count precision twice.



Korthikanti et al. (2023), “Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05198 (bibliography key: korthikanti2023). The linear precision rescaling is a modeling convention.



>>> full = calc_activation_memory(2, 8, 1, 16, strategy="full")
>>> selective = calc_activation_memory(2, 8, 1, 16, strategy="selective")
>>> bool(full < selective)
True




physics.memory.calc_capped_exponential_scale(mean_tokens, max_tokens)
Solve for the exponential scale of a context-capped length model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean_tokens
float
Mean resident tokens after capping, in (0, max_tokens].
required


max_tokens
float
Positive context cap in tokens.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Uncapped exponential scale in tokens; infinity when every request reaches the cap.






Equation: mean_tokens = mu * (1 - exp(-max_tokens/mu)).
Assumptions: Length is min(X, max_tokens), where X is a continuous exponential variable. Bisection solves the monotone mean relation; the shape is assumed, not fitted to a trace.
Excludes: Discrete token effects and measured request-length distributions.



Derivation: integrate the survival function P(X > s) = exp(-s/mu) from zero to max_tokens. The capped mean rises monotonically from zero to the cap.



>>> math.isinf(calc_capped_exponential_scale(16, 16))
True
>>> mu = calc_capped_exponential_scale(8, 32)
>>> math.isclose(mu * (1 - math.exp(-32 / mu)), 8)
True

Excludes: Integer segment rounding, unequal layer sizes, tensor parallelism, and recomputation runtime.

Excludes: Object headers, alignment, capacity over-allocation, and separate indexing-width choices for columns and row offsets.



Derivation: sum the three CSR arrays: nnz values, nnz column indices, and rows+1 row pointers.



>>> calc_csr_bytes(5, 3, 2, 4) == 5 * (2 + 4) + (3 + 1) * 4
True

physics.memory.calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens(
    mean_request_tokens,
    max_seq_len,
    page_size_tokens=16,
)
Estimate page allocation under a capped exponential request model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean_request_tokens
float
Positive mean resident tokens, at most max_seq_len.
required


max_seq_len
int
Positive cap on resident tokens per request.
required


page_size_tokens
int
Positive tokens per page; default 16.

Name
Type
Description





tuple
Expected allocated tokens per request and expected unused fraction of that allocation, both floats.






Equation: E[pages] = sum(exp(-j*p/mu), j=0..K-1) = (1-r**K)/(1-r), with r=exp(-p/mu), K=ceil(S_max/p). Allocation is p*E[pages], and waste is 1-mean/allocation.
Assumptions: Resident length is min(X, S_max), with an exponential X calibrated only to the supplied capped mean. At the fixed-length limit, allocate ceil(S_max/p)*p tokens.
Excludes: External fragmentation, block metadata, time-varying occupancy, prefix sharing, and departures from the assumed length distribution.



Derivation: the tail-sum identity for the integer page count gives the finite geometric series. Kwon et al. (2023), “Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180 (bibliography key: kwon2023), motivates page allocation; the exponential request model is an additional assumption.



>>> allocation, waste = calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens(16, 16, page_size_tokens=8)
>>> allocation == 16 and waste == 0
True

Excludes: Architectural validity checks, cache sizing, and distinctions between single-head MQA and other GQA configurations.



Derivation: classify whether cache storage uses a compressed latent, grouped key/value heads, or one key/value head per query head. The precedence is a local API convention.

Assumptions: Forward reads weights and writes saved activations. Backward reads both and writes gradients. The optimizer reads weights, gradients, state, then writes weights and state.

    n_layers,
    seq_len,
    batch_size,
    hidden_dim,
    n_heads=None,

    strategy='selective',
)

Type
Description
Default

int
Positive number of layers resident on the device after pipeline partitioning.
required

int
Positive tokens per sequence.
required

required

int
Positive hidden width in elements.
required

str
Saved-state policy: none, selective (default), or full recomputation.

Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Total saved activation storage in bytes.






Equation: M = L * (b/2) * A. At FP16, A = 34*S*B*H + 5*N_heads*S**2*B for none, 34*S*B*H for selective, and 2*S*B*H for full.
Assumptions: Equal layer shapes and the FP16 saved-tensor convention of Korthikanti et al. Selective recomputation discards attention matrices; full recomputation retains layer inputs. Other precisions scale all coefficients uniformly.
Excludes: Weights, gradients, optimizer state, kernel scratch space, allocator reserve, sequence/tensor-parallel sharding, and schedule-dependent simultaneous microbatch residency.
The attention coefficient counts softmax probabilities, a dropout mask, and dropped probabilities. The FP16 byte widths are already included in the coefficients; multiplying them by precision_bytes without dividing by two would count precision twice.



Korthikanti et al. (2023), “Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05198 (bibliography key: korthikanti2023). The linear precision rescaling is a modeling convention.



>>> full = calc_activation_memory(2, 8, 1, 16, strategy="full")
>>> selective = calc_activation_memory(2, 8, 1, 16, strategy="selective")
>>> bool(full < selective)
True




physics.memory.calc_capped_exponential_scale(mean_tokens, max_tokens)
Solve for the exponential scale of a context-capped length model.











Name
Type
Description
Default

float
Mean resident tokens after capping, in (0, max_tokens].
required


max_tokens
float
Positive context cap in tokens.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Uncapped exponential scale in tokens; infinity when every request reaches the cap.






Equation: mean_tokens = mu * (1 - exp(-max_tokens/mu)).
Assumptions: Length is min(X, max_tokens), where X is a continuous exponential variable. Bisection solves the monotone mean relation; the shape is assumed, not fitted to a trace.
Excludes: Discrete token effects and measured request-length distributions.



Derivation: integrate the survival function P(X > s) = exp(-s/mu) from zero to max_tokens. The capped mean rises monotonically from zero to the cap.



>>> math.isinf(calc_capped_exponential_scale(16, 16))
True
>>> mu = calc_capped_exponential_scale(8, 32)
>>> math.isclose(mu * (1 - math.exp(-32 / mu)), 8)
True

Excludes: Object headers, alignment, capacity over-allocation, and separate indexing-width choices for columns and row offsets.

>>> calc_csr_bytes(5, 3, 2, 4) == 5 * (2 + 4) + (3 + 1) * 4
True

    hidden_dim,
    vocab_size,
    mlp_ratio=4,
)

Type

Default

required

required

Counts: block weights across all layers, block_matrices across all layers, and output projection weights.






Equation: block = L*(4*d**2 + 2*r*d**2); block_matrices = 4*L; output = V*d.
Assumptions: Each block has one fused QKV matrix, one attention output matrix, and two MLP matrices. The output projection is reported separately.
Excludes: Biases, normalization scales, position embeddings, GQA/MLA geometry, and gated-MLP extra matrices.



Derivation: sum the rectangular matrix element counts d*(3*d), d*d, d*(r*d), (r*d)*d, and V*d. Fusing QKV changes matrix count, not parameter count.



>>> result = calc_decoder_matmul_weights(2, 8, 16)
>>> result["block"] == 2 * (4 + 2 * 4) * 8**2

physics.memory.calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens(
    mean_request_tokens,
    max_seq_len,
    page_size_tokens=16,
)
Estimate page allocation under a capped exponential request model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mean_request_tokens
float
Positive mean resident tokens, at most max_seq_len.
required


max_seq_len
int
Positive cap on resident tokens per request.
required


page_size_tokens
int
Positive tokens per page; default 16.
16














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Expected allocated tokens per request and expected unused fraction of that allocation, both floats.






Equation: E[pages] = sum(exp(-j*p/mu), j=0..K-1) = (1-r**K)/(1-r), with r=exp(-p/mu), K=ceil(S_max/p). Allocation is p*E[pages], and waste is 1-mean/allocation.
Assumptions: Resident length is min(X, S_max), with an exponential X calibrated only to the supplied capped mean. At the fixed-length limit, allocate ceil(S_max/p)*p tokens.
Excludes: External fragmentation, block metadata, time-varying occupancy, prefix sharing, and departures from the assumed length distribution.



Derivation: the tail-sum identity for the integer page count gives the finite geometric series. Kwon et al. (2023), “Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention,” https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180 (bibliography key: kwon2023), motivates page allocation; the exponential request model is an additional assumption.



>>> allocation, waste = calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens(16, 16, page_size_tokens=8)
>>> allocation == 16 and waste == 0
True

Assumptions: This is a routing convention based on declared geometry, not an inference from weights. Inputs describe an already valid model.
Excludes: Architectural validity checks, cache sizing, and distinctions between single-head MQA and other GQA configurations.



Derivation: classify whether cache storage uses a compressed latent, grouped key/value heads, or one key/value head per query head. The precedence is a local API convention.



>>> calc_kv_attention_design(8, kv_heads=2)

>>> calc_kv_resident_fit(10 * ureg.byte, 3 * ureg.byte) == 10 // 3

Equation: gain = 1 / (1 - f).
Assumptions: The shared prefix is stored once and becomes negligible as pool/request count grows.

required

Type

Dimensionless zero-share threshold; sparse wins above it. A negative threshold means sparse entries are already cheaper before sparsity.






Equation: z_star = 1 - b_dense/b_nonzero.
Assumptions: Only surviving nonzeros consume sparse storage; both representations cover the same logical element count.
Excludes: Per-row pointers, format headers, sparse compute overhead, and alignment.



Derivation: equate N*b_dense with N*(1-z)*b_nonzero and solve for z.

physics.memory.calc_update_step_traffic(
    weights,
    gradients,
    optimizer_state,
    activations,
)

Type
Description
Default

Quantity or float
Nonnegative weight footprint; use bytes or byte-compatible quantities consistently.
required

Quantity or float

required

required

Quantity or float
Nonnegative saved-activation footprint in the same units.
required

Type

Total step traffic and traffic from the three weight reads; both preserve the input memory units.






Equation: V = (W+A) + (A+W+G) + (W+G+S) + (W+S) = 4*W+2*A+2*G+2*S; weight_reads = 3*W.
Assumptions: Forward reads weights and writes saved activations. Backward reads both and writes gradients. The optimizer reads weights, gradients, state, then writes weights and state.
Excludes: Cache reuse, fused-kernel savings, temporary workspace, communication, and activation recomputation.



Derivation: sum each read and write at the memory boundary exactly once for the declared unfused execution sequence.

>>> total == 4*2 + 2*3 + 2*4 + 2*5 and reads == 3*2
True

title: TailEventRateScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
How often an event of probability event_probability per request occurs at request_rate.


Equation: Expected events per second=request_rate*event_probability.
Assumptions: A constant mean request rate and a probability applicable to each request.
Excludes: Event clustering, confidence intervals, and severity of an event.



Derivation: Linearity of expectation gives the mean number of qualifying requests as request count times the per-request event probability. Applying the same product to the request rate gives events per second without assuming independent event timing.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.

>>> scenario = Scenarios.RecommenderTailEvents
>>> round(scenario.events_per_second, 6)
1000.0

title: engine.solvers.storage
text:
engine.solvers.storage
Storage solvers: what a training fleet reads, saves, and pays to move.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable. Each model is a bandwidth or rate bound: it counts bytes and divides by a stated rate, and leaves queueing, contention, and protocol overheads out.





Name
Description




CheckpointStormModel
Synchronized saves when every replica writes its own copy of the state.


DataStallModel
Input wait per step when delivery and compute run in sequence or overlap.


HostIoCpuModel
Host CPU time spent issuing and completing I/O requests.


InputDemandModel
The input bandwidth a fleet draws: consumers x busy fraction x batch bytes / compute time.


ObjectStorageBillModel
The object-storage bill beyond capacity: egress per read, GET requests, archive retrieval.


PrefetchDepthModel
Ready batches a prefetch queue needs to cover a tier’s tail read latency.


StorageFootprintModel
The bytes a training run reads once and the bytes it saves again and again.


StreamVsStageModel
Streaming every epoch from remote object storage against staging once per run.


SyntheticFootprintModel
Generated training data at rest and in motion.


TieredCacheModel
Mean service of a two-tier cache: E[T] = h T_hit + (1 - h) T_miss.


TieredCheckpointModel
A checkpoint staged on each node’s local storage, then drained to a durable tier.


UtilizationLossModel
Dollars of accelerator time idled when utilization falls from one level to another.





engine.solvers.storage.CheckpointStormModel()
Synchronized saves when every replica writes its own copy of the state.
replicas copies of the full resumable state cross one shared ingest bandwidth; writing one logical copy, split across the ranks that own it, moves the state once. The ratio is the replica count.





Name
Description




solve
Compare replicated checkpoint traffic with one logical state copy.





engine.solvers.storage.CheckpointStormModel.solve(
    state_bytes,
    replicas,
    ingest_bandwidth,
)
Compare replicated checkpoint traffic with one logical state copy.











Name
Type
Description
Default




state_bytes
Quantity
Positive size of one resumable state, in bytes.
required


replicas
int
Positive number of identical copies written concurrently.
required


ingest_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive shared aggregate ingest bandwidth, in bytes/s.
required














Name
Type
Description





CheckpointStormResult
Logical and replicated bytes, transfer times in seconds, and the dimensionless replicated/single-copy slowdown.






Equation: Storm bytes = replicas * state_bytes; each transfer time is its bytes divided by the same ingest bandwidth.
Assumptions: Every replica writes a complete identical state to one shared bandwidth-limited sink.
Excludes: Deduplication, per-client bandwidth limits, queueing, and metadata operations.



Derivation: Identical complete state copies add their bytes at the shared sink. Dividing both byte totals by the same bandwidth makes the time ratio equal the copy count.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import CheckpointStormModel
>>> r = CheckpointStormModel().solve(Q_(10, "GB"), 2, Q_(1, "GB/s"))
>>> assert r.storm_time == r.single_copy_time * 2






engine.solvers.storage.DataStallModel()
Input wait per step when delivery and compute run in sequence or overlap.
In sequence a step costs delivery plus compute; overlapped, the loader fetches the next batch during compute, so a step costs the longer of the two. The stall is the share of the step not spent computing.





Name
Description




solve
Compare sequential delivery with ideally overlapped input and compute.





engine.solvers.storage.DataStallModel.solve(compute_time, io_time)
Compare sequential delivery with ideally overlapped input and compute.











Name
Type
Description
Default




compute_time
Quantity
Positive time to compute one batch.
required


io_time
Quantity
Nonnegative time to deliver one batch; compatible with compute_time.
required














Name
Type
Description





DataStallResult
Sequential and overlapped step durations, with dimensionless fractions of each step spent waiting for input.






Equation: Sequential step = compute + I/O; overlapped step = max(compute, I/O). Stall fraction = (step - compute)/step in each schedule.
Assumptions: The overlapped pipeline is in steady state and independent stages can run simultaneously.
Excludes: Pipeline startup, scheduling overhead, shared-resource contention, and variation across batches.



Derivation: Sequential stages add durations. Ideal overlap completes when the slower stage finishes. Subtracting useful compute from either step gives its input wait, which is normalized by that step duration.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import DataStallModel
>>> r = DataStallModel().solve(Q_(2, "s"), Q_(1, "s"))
>>> assert r.overlapped_step <= r.sequential_step






engine.solvers.storage.HostIoCpuModel()
Host CPU time spent issuing and completing I/O requests.
Each request costs a stated CPU service time on the host; at a request rate r the host spends r x service CPU-seconds per second, the number of cores kept busy by data movement alone.





Name
Description




solve
Convert request rates and host service times into occupied CPU cores.





engine.solvers.storage.HostIoCpuModel.solve(request_rate, service_times)
Convert request rates and host service times into occupied CPU cores.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_rate
float
Nonnegative requests per second, supplied as a scalar.
required


service_times
dict of str to Quantity
Named nonnegative CPU service times per request, convertible to seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





HostIoCpuResult
Request rate and CPU-seconds per second for each service-time scenario; the latter equals fully occupied core equivalents.






Equation: CPU-seconds per second = request_rate * service_time_in_seconds.
Assumptions: Each request consumes the stated CPU service independently; time is CPU time, not wall-clock I/O latency.
Excludes: CPU saturation, scheduling overhead, contention, and parallel execution within a request.



Derivation: Requests per second times CPU-seconds per request cancels the request unit and yields CPU-seconds per second. One such unit is one continuously occupied core.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import HostIoCpuModel
>>> r = HostIoCpuModel().solve(100, {"path": Q_(1, "ms")})
>>> assert r.cpu_seconds_per_second["path"] > 0






engine.solvers.storage.InputDemandModel()
The input bandwidth a fleet draws: consumers x busy fraction x batch bytes / compute time.
Each consumer reads a distinct batch of samples_per_step samples of bytes_per_sample every step_time of compute; busy_fraction is the share of wall-clock time spent computing.





Name
Description




solve
Compute aggregate input bandwidth demanded by active consumers.





engine.solvers.storage.InputDemandModel.solve(
    consumers,
    samples_per_step,
    bytes_per_sample,
    step_time,
    busy_fraction=1.0,
)
Compute aggregate input bandwidth demanded by active consumers.











Name
Type
Description
Default




consumers
int
Nonnegative independent consumer count.
required


samples_per_step
int
Nonnegative samples in each consumer batch.
required


bytes_per_sample
Quantity
Nonnegative stored bytes per sample.
required


step_time
Quantity
Positive compute time per batch.
required


busy_fraction
float
Dimensionless active fraction in [0, 1]; default 1 uses continuous compute.
1.0














Name
Type
Description





InputDemandResult
Per-consumer batch bytes and aggregate average bandwidth with byte/time dimensions.






Equation: Batch bytes = samples_per_step * bytes_per_sample; bandwidth = consumers * batch_bytes * busy_fraction / step_time.
Assumptions: Consumers read distinct batches at the same fixed rate; the busy fraction scales average demand rather than peak bursts.
Excludes: Caching, repeated samples, preprocessing expansion, and correlated arrival bursts.



Derivation: Samples per batch times bytes per sample gives one consumer’s transfer volume. Dividing by compute time gives its active rate; consumer count and busy fraction scale aggregate average demand.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import InputDemandModel
>>> r = InputDemandModel().solve(2, 4, Q_(1, "MB"), Q_(1, "s"))
>>> assert r.bandwidth * Q_(1, "s") == r.batch_bytes * 2






engine.solvers.storage.ObjectStorageBillModel()
The object-storage bill beyond capacity: egress per read, GET requests, archive retrieval.
Capacity is billed per byte-month; every read that leaves the region or provider pays egress per byte; each file read pays a GET fee; an archive restore pays a retrieval fee and then egress for one read.





Name
Description




solve
Price capacity, transfer, requests, and an archive restore separately.

    dataset_bytes,
    storage_rate,
    billing_period,
    egress_rate,
    reads,
    files,
    request_fee,
    requests_per_fee,
    retrieval_rate,
)
Price capacity, transfer, requests, and an archive restore separately.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Nonnegative stored dataset size, in bytes.
required


storage_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative capacity price in currency/(byte*time).
required


billing_period
Quantity
Nonnegative capacity billing duration.
required


egress_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative currency per byte transferred out.
required

int
Nonnegative complete dataset reads charged egress.
required

int
Nonnegative total GET requests to bill; not multiplied by reads.
required

Quantity
Nonnegative currency fee for requests_per_fee requests.
required


requests_per_fee
int
Positive request-count billing unit.
required


retrieval_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative archive retrieval charge in currency/byte.
required














Name
Type
Description





ObjectStorageBillResult
Separate costs as USD scalars: storage, egress, requests, archive retrieval, and archive restore including one egress read.






Equation: Storage = bytes * rate * period; egress = bytes * reads * egress_rate; requests = files * fee/requests_per_fee; restore = retrieval + one egress.
Assumptions: Prices are linear and supplied by the caller. The files input already counts the requests that should be billed.
Excludes: Provider discounts, minimum storage periods, taxes, tiered pricing, and request retries.



Derivation: Capacity charges multiply stored bytes by residence time and unit price. Transfer and retrieval charges multiply moved bytes by their prices; request charges prorate the quoted fee by its request unit.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ObjectStorageBillModel
>>> r = ObjectStorageBillModel().solve(Q_(1, "GB"), Q_(1, "USD/GB/day"),
...     Q_(1, "day"), Q_(1, "USD/GB"), 2, 10, Q_(1, "USD"),
...     10, Q_(1, "USD/GB"))
>>> assert r.egress_cost == r.egress_per_read * 2

Latency spans and ceiling depths per scenario; allocated buffer bytes per consumer and node.






Equation: Required depth for scenario k = ceil(latency[k]/compute_time). Allocated buffer = safety_depth * batch_bytes per consumer.
Assumptions: Ready batches cover deterministic compute windows; safety_depth is supplied, not automatically set to the largest required depth.
Excludes: Read throughput limits, batch-size variation, and correlated latency tails across consumers.



Derivation: A read spanning multiple compute windows needs one ready batch per window, rounded upward. Buffer capacity instead uses the separately chosen safety depth and sums identical consumer allocations.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import PrefetchDepthModel
>>> r = PrefetchDepthModel().solve(Q_(1, "s"), {"tail": Q_(2, "s")},
...     Q_(10, "MB"), 3, 2)
>>> assert r.buffer_per_node == r.buffer_per_consumer * 2






engine.solvers.storage.StorageFootprintModel()
The bytes a training run reads once and the bytes it saves again and again.
A resumable checkpoint holds bytes_per_param for every parameter and is written once per save interval, so a run of duration D saves D / interval times. Against a corpus read once, the written bytes can exceed the read bytes by orders of magnitude. The corpus is packaged into shards of shard_bytes; the archive keeps every archive_every-th checkpoint (and the final one when the count is not a multiple) plus the source and the tokenized corpus.

Equation: Checkpoint C = parameters * bytes_per_param; saves N = floor(D/I); written bytes = N*C; retained checkpoints = ceil(N/archive_every). Archive bytes add retained checkpoints, source, and corpus.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import StorageFootprintModel
>>> r = StorageFootprintModel().solve(Q_(10, "param"), Q_(2, "byte/param"),
...     Q_(100, "byte"), Q_(20, "byte"), Q_(4, "s"), Q_(1, "s"),
...     Q_(10, "byte"), 2)
>>> assert r.checkpoint_bytes_written == r.checkpoint_bytes * r.saves

Both options keep the dataset in object storage as the source of truth. Streaming pays egress for every epoch of every run; staging adds a year of local capacity and pays egress once per run. They break even where the streaming egress per run equals staging’s extra cost per run.

engine.solvers.storage.TieredCacheModel()
Mean service of a two-tier cache: E[T] = h T_hit + (1 - h) T_miss.
With service times in units of one hit, E[T] = h + (1 - h) x penalty, and the delivered rate is 1 / E[T] of the all-hit rate. Given tier bandwidths, the penalty is their ratio and the delivered rate is the hot bandwidth times that fraction (time per byte averaged over the mix).

Description

Type

None

Type
Description





TieredCacheResult
Mean service relative to a hit, delivered fraction of hot-tier rate, and delivered GB/s when bandwidths are supplied.






Equation: Mean normalized service = h + (1-h)*miss_penalty; delivered fraction = 1/mean. With bandwidths, average seconds/byte then invert.
Assumptions: The same byte volume determines hit and miss shares. Each miss uses miss-tier service alone; the hot and miss costs are alternatives.
Excludes: Queueing, additional lookup costs, concurrent independent tier service, and eviction policy.



Derivation: Average time per byte over mutually exclusive hit and miss outcomes, then invert to obtain bytes per time. Averaging bandwidths directly would not conserve the service time of the byte mixture.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TieredCacheModel
>>> r = TieredCacheModel().solve(1.0, miss_penalty=4.0)
>>> assert r.delivered_fraction == 1.0

A checkpoint staged on each node’s local storage, then drained to a durable tier.
Each node writes its shard (checkpoint / nodes) to local storage and training pauses only for that write. The durable copy proceeds in the background at the shared tier’s aggregate bandwidth, which is the same time as each node’s shard at its per-node share of that bandwidth.

)

Equation: Per-node shard = C/N; pause = C/(N*local_bandwidth); drain = C/durable_bandwidth; pause fraction = pause/save_interval.
Assumptions: All nodes write equal shards concurrently. Background drain does not reduce the stated local bandwidth.
Excludes: Backpressure when drain outlasts the save interval, replication, queueing, and durable-tier failure recovery.



Derivation: Equal sharding divides local write volume by node count. The durable tier still receives the entire checkpoint, so its drain uses aggregate bandwidth without another division by nodes.

engine.solvers.storage.DataStallModel()
Input wait per step when delivery and compute run in sequence or overlap.
In sequence a step costs delivery plus compute; overlapped, the loader fetches the next batch during compute, so a step costs the longer of the two. The stall is the share of the step not spent computing.





Name
Description

required

Type

DataStallResult
Sequential and overlapped step durations, with dimensionless fractions of each step spent waiting for input.






Equation: Sequential step = compute + I/O; overlapped step = max(compute, I/O). Stall fraction = (step - compute)/step in each schedule.
Assumptions: The overlapped pipeline is in steady state and independent stages can run simultaneously.
Excludes: Pipeline startup, scheduling overhead, shared-resource contention, and variation across batches.



Derivation: Sequential stages add durations. Ideal overlap completes when the slower stage finishes. Subtracting useful compute from either step gives its input wait, which is normalized by that step duration.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import DataStallModel
>>> r = DataStallModel().solve(Q_(2, "s"), Q_(1, "s"))
>>> assert r.overlapped_step <= r.sequential_step

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import StorageFootprintModel
>>> r = StorageFootprintModel().solve(Q_(10, "param"), Q_(2, "byte/param"),
...     Q_(100, "byte"), Q_(20, "byte"), Q_(4, "s"), Q_(1, "s"),
...     Q_(10, "byte"), 2)
>>> assert r.checkpoint_bytes_written == r.checkpoint_bytes * r.saves






engine.solvers.storage.StreamVsStageModel()
Streaming every epoch from remote object storage against staging once per run.
Both options keep the dataset in object storage as the source of truth. Streaming pays egress for every epoch of every run; staging adds a year of local capacity and pays egress once per run. They break even where the streaming egress per run equals staging’s extra cost per run.





Name
Description




solve
Compare repeated remote reads with one local staging transfer per run.





engine.solvers.storage.StreamVsStageModel.solve(
    dataset_bytes,
    epochs,
    runs_per_year,
    object_rate,
    local_rate,
    egress_rate,
    year,
)
Compare repeated remote reads with one local staging transfer per run.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive dataset size, in bytes.
required


epochs
int
Nonnegative complete dataset passes per run.
required


runs_per_year
int
Positive runs in the accounting period.
required


object_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative source storage price in currency/(byte*time).
required

Quantity
Nonnegative local storage price in currency/(byte*time).
required


egress_rate
Quantity
Positive remote transfer price in currency/byte.
required


year
Quantity
Positive accounting period duration; normally one year.
required














Name
Type
Description





StreamVsStageResult
USD cost components, stream-minus-stage savings, and the dimensionless epoch count at equal modeled cost.






Equation: Stream = source_storage + runs * epochs * bytes * egress_rate; stage = source_storage + local_storage + runs * bytes * egress_rate.
Assumptions: Both choices keep remote source storage. Local capacity is billed for the full period; each staged run transfers the dataset once.
Excludes: Local I/O costs, staging delay, cache persistence across runs, and bandwidth-dependent performance differences.



Derivation: Remote source capacity is common to both options and cancels at break-even. Staging adds local capacity and one transfer per run; streaming instead pays for a transfer on every epoch.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import StreamVsStageModel
>>> r = StreamVsStageModel().solve(Q_(1, "GB"), 2, 1,
...     Q_(1, "USD/GB/day"), Q_(1, "USD/GB/day"), Q_(1, "USD/GB"),
...     Q_(1, "day"))
>>> assert r.savings == r.stream_cost - r.stage_cost

Each sample carries provenance metadata (a fraction of its payload) at rest; the pipeline writes payload and metadata once and reads the payload once per verification pass.

Description

    payload_bytes,
    provenance_overhead,
    verification_passes,
)

Name
Type

Default

required

float

required

int

required














Name
Type
Description





SyntheticFootprintResult
Stored bytes, verification-read bytes, total pipeline bytes, and dimensionless capacity and traffic amplification.






Equation: Stored = payload*(1+overhead); verification = payload*passes; pipeline = stored + verification.
Assumptions: Payload and metadata are written once; each verification pass reads payload only.
Excludes: Intermediate generations, failed attempts, metadata rereads, compression, and replication.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SyntheticFootprintModel

engine.solvers.storage.TieredCacheModel()
Mean service of a two-tier cache: E[T] = h T_hit + (1 - h) T_miss.
With service times in units of one hit, E[T] = h + (1 - h) x penalty, and the delivered rate is 1 / E[T] of the all-hit rate. Given tier bandwidths, the penalty is their ratio and the delivered rate is the hot bandwidth times that fraction (time per byte averaged over the mix).





Name
Description




solve
Average hit and miss service time for a two-tier read mixture.





engine.solvers.storage.TieredCacheModel.solve(
    hit_rate,
    miss_penalty=None,
    hot_bandwidth=None,
    miss_bandwidth=None,
)
Average hit and miss service time for a two-tier read mixture.











Name
Type
Description
Default




hit_rate
float
Dimensionless byte-weighted hit fraction in [0, 1].
required


miss_penalty
float
Positive miss/hit service-time ratio, required unless both bandwidths are supplied.
None


hot_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive hot-tier bandwidth in bytes/s; use together with miss_bandwidth.
None


miss_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive miss-tier bandwidth in bytes/s; overrides miss_penalty when both are supplied.
None














Name
Type
Description





TieredCacheResult
Mean service relative to a hit, delivered fraction of hot-tier rate, and delivered GB/s when bandwidths are supplied.






Equation: Mean normalized service = h + (1-h)*miss_penalty; delivered fraction = 1/mean. With bandwidths, average seconds/byte then invert.
Assumptions: The same byte volume determines hit and miss shares. Each miss uses miss-tier service alone; the hot and miss costs are alternatives.
Excludes: Queueing, additional lookup costs, concurrent independent tier service, and eviction policy.



Derivation: Average time per byte over mutually exclusive hit and miss outcomes, then invert to obtain bytes per time. Averaging bandwidths directly would not conserve the service time of the byte mixture.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TieredCacheModel
>>> r = TieredCacheModel().solve(1.0, miss_penalty=4.0)
>>> assert r.delivered_fraction == 1.0






engine.solvers.storage.TieredCheckpointModel()
A checkpoint staged on each node’s local storage, then drained to a durable tier.
Each node writes its shard (checkpoint / nodes) to local storage and training pauses only for that write. The durable copy proceeds in the background at the shared tier’s aggregate bandwidth, which is the same time as each node’s shard at its per-node share of that bandwidth.





Name
Description




solve
Separate local checkpoint pause from background durable drain time.





engine.solvers.storage.TieredCheckpointModel.solve(
    checkpoint_bytes,
    nodes,
    local_bandwidth,
    durable_bandwidth,
    save_interval,
)
Separate local checkpoint pause from background durable drain time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




checkpoint_bytes
Quantity
Positive full checkpoint size, in bytes.
required


nodes
int
Positive number of equally loaded writer nodes.
required


local_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive local write bandwidth per node, in bytes/s.
required


durable_bandwidth
Quantity
Positive aggregate durable-tier bandwidth, in bytes/s.
required


save_interval
Quantity
Positive time between checkpoints.
required














Name
Type
Description





TieredCheckpointResult
Shard size, local write and durable drain times in seconds, per-node durable bandwidth, and local pause fraction.






Equation: Per-node shard = C/N; pause = C/(N*local_bandwidth); drain = C/durable_bandwidth; pause fraction = pause/save_interval.
Assumptions: All nodes write equal shards concurrently. Background drain does not reduce the stated local bandwidth.
Excludes: Backpressure when drain outlasts the save interval, replication, queueing, and durable-tier failure recovery.



Derivation: Equal sharding divides local write volume by node count. The durable tier still receives the entire checkpoint, so its drain uses aggregate bandwidth without another division by nodes.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TieredCheckpointModel
>>> r = TieredCheckpointModel().solve(Q_(100, "GB"), 2,
...     Q_(10, "GB/s"), Q_(5, "GB/s"), Q_(1, "minute"))
>>> assert r.per_node_shard * 2 == r.checkpoint_bytes






engine.solvers.storage.UtilizationLossModel()
Dollars of accelerator time idled when utilization falls from one level to another.
A fleet of n_devices billed at device_hour_rate costs its full rate every day whether it computes or waits; a drop in the busy fraction wastes that share of the daily cost.





Name
Description




solve
Price the billed accelerator time lost to a utilization decrease.





engine.solvers.storage.UtilizationLossModel.solve(
    n_devices,
    device_hour_rate,
    healthy_utilization,
    degraded_utilization,
    duration,
)
Price the billed accelerator time lost to a utilization decrease.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_devices
int
Nonnegative billed accelerator count.
required


device_hour_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative rental price per device, in currency/hour.
required


healthy_utilization
float
Dimensionless reference busy fraction in [0, 1].
required


degraded_utilization
float
Dimensionless comparison busy fraction in [0, 1]; higher values yield negative loss.
required


duration
Quantity
Nonnegative accounting duration, convertible to days.
required














Name
Type
Description





UtilizationLossResult
Full fleet cost per day, lost cost per day, and total lost cost, all as USD scalars.






Equation: Daily fleet cost = devices * hourly_rate * hours_per_day; loss = daily_cost * (healthy - degraded) * duration_in_days.
Assumptions: The fleet incurs its full rental bill whether busy or idle. Utilization differences are constant over the accounting period.
Excludes: Actual billing reductions, energy savings, and causal attribution of the utilization change.



Derivation: Multiply the full device rental rate by elapsed time to obtain billed cost. Multiplying by the lost busy fraction prices the corresponding unused capacity, without asserting that the invoice itself decreases.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import UtilizationLossModel
>>> r = UtilizationLossModel().solve(2, Q_(1, "USD/hour"), 0.8, 0.8, Q_(1, "day"))
>>> assert r.loss_total == 0.0

Grounded-intent solvers: how long a learned target stays true, and the lease that bounds it.

calc_chi_square_quantile : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: The region holding probability coverage has principal semi-axes r sigma_i, where r^2 is the chi-square quantile for one degree of freedom per axis.
Assumptions: A jointly Gaussian estimate is expressed in principal axes with the supplied standard deviations and dimension equal to their count.
Excludes: Non-Gaussian tails, uncertain covariance estimates, and obstacle geometry beyond the scalar per-axis tolerance comparison.

>>> bool(result.axes_within == 2)
True

Equation: A terminal move is admissible only if that floor fits the evidence window; otherwise the reach is staged on at least ceil(floor / window) fresh captures. The reach inside a window at the speed ceiling is v_max T.
Assumptions: The speed ceiling can be sustained and each positive evidence window can be renewed when a staged reach needs another capture.

engine.solvers.grounding.IntentCadenceModel()
A moving target’s evidence horizons against a slow proposer’s cadence.
Untracked, the target leaves its tolerance after (r_tol - e_0) / v; tracked, only residual slip remains, sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip). A proposer that renews the target from its own inference computes it from a frame captured one inference earlier and holds it one period, so the oldest evidence behind a model-only target is period + inference, and the drift it can follow is the margin over that age. A stall of T leaves the target e_0 + v T (untracked) or e_0 + a_slip T^2 / 2 (tracked) off; a stop begins one tick, one bus cycle, and one brake onset after expiry.

Equation: Untracked, the target leaves its tolerance after (r_tol - e_0) / v; tracked, only residual slip remains, sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip). A proposer that renews the target from its own inference computes it from a frame captured one inference earlier and holds it one period, so the oldest evidence behind a model-only target is period + inference, and the drift it can follow is the margin over that age. A stall of T leaves the target e_0 + v T (untracked) or e_0 + a_slip T^2 / 2 (tracked) off; a stop begins one tick, one bus cycle, and one brake onset after expiry.
Assumptions: Positive tolerance margin; untracked motion uses constant target speed and tracked residual motion uses constant slip acceleration.
Excludes: Tracking resets within the interval, time-varying slip, and physical stop-distance verification.

calc_safe_stopping_distance : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: The credible deceleration is the arm’s worst-case stop averaged over a stop from its velocity limit; at the admitted speed ceiling the stop takes v t_onset + v^2 / (2 a), and the stopping deadline is the time the remaining clearance allows at that speed. With all three countdowns started together, the lease expires at the minimum.
Assumptions: Countdowns share an origin; averaged worst-stop deceleration applies at the admitted speed. Negative deadlines remain visible.
Excludes: Stop variability beyond the supplied bound, jerk-dependent transients, and certification of the resulting lease as safe.



Derivation: Infer a=velocity_limit/worst_stop_time and compute stopping distance v*onset+v*v/(2*a). Divide remaining clearance by v, then take the earliest of that deadline and the other leases.

>>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.grounding import IntentLeaseExpiryModel
>>> result = IntentLeaseExpiryModel().solve(untracked_horizon=Q_('1 s'), tracked_horizon=Q_('2 s'), administrative_lease=Q_('0.5 s'), stop_onset=Q_('1 ms'), speed_ceiling=Q_('1 m/s'), velocity_limit=Q_('1 m/s'), worst_stop_time=Q_('1 s'), clearance=Q_('10 m'))
>>> bool(result.binding_tracked == "administrative")
True

calc_split_conformal_rank : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: Raw per-box scores are normalized over the retained candidates; the set keeps every candidate whose normalized score is at least 1 - qhat, where qhat is the calibration score at rank ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha)). A set of any size other than one is refused.
Assumptions: Nonnegative retained scores have positive total; the supplied threshold was calibrated for these scores under exchangeability.
Excludes: Calibration fitting, proof of exchangeability, and interpreting normalized detector scores as calibrated correctness probabilities.



Derivation: Normalize each score by their sum and count those at least 1-threshold_score; refuse every count except one. The rank ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) identifies the intended calibration order statistic.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.engine.solvers.grounding import ReferentSetModel
>>> result = ReferentSetModel().solve(scores=[0.9, 0.1], calibration_count=100, alpha=0.1, threshold_score=0.2)
>>> bool(not result.refuse)
True

A moving target’s evidence horizons against a slow proposer’s cadence.
Untracked, the target leaves its tolerance after (r_tol - e_0) / v; tracked, only residual slip remains, sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip). calc_safe_stopping_distance : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: The credible deceleration is the arm’s worst-case stop averaged over a stop from its velocity limit; at the admitted speed ceiling the stop takes v t_onset + v^2 / (2 a), and the stopping deadline is the time the remaining clearance allows at that speed. With all three countdowns started together, the lease expires at the minimum.
Assumptions: Countdowns share an origin; averaged worst-stop deceleration applies at the admitted speed. Negative deadlines remain visible.
Excludes: Stop variability beyond the supplied bound, jerk-dependent transients, and certification of the resulting lease as safe.

calc_split_conformal_rank : Composed numerical primitive.



Equation: Raw per-box scores are normalized over the retained candidates; the set keeps every candidate whose normalized score is at least 1 - qhat, where qhat is the calibration score at rank ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha)). A set of any size other than one is refused.

True
