Group-relative (GRPO) coefficients (r_i - mean) / (std + epsilon) of one group.
Every sampled token of rollout i carries coefficient i. The dispersion divisor (G or G - 1) and the stabilizer are part of the objective; a lone pass in a group of G binary rewards gets sqrt(G - 1) as epsilon goes to zero.





Name
Description




solve
Center and scale rewards within a rollout group.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.GroupCoefficientsModel.solve(
    rewards,
    stabilizer,
    bessel=False,
)
Center and scale rewards within a rollout group.











Name
Type
Description
Default




rewards
sequence of float
Nonempty sequence of dimensionless sampled rewards.
required


stabilizer
float
Nonnegative dimensionless denominator stabilizer.
required


bessel
bool
Use sample standard deviation when True; population deviation otherwise.
False














Name
Type
Description





GroupCoefficientsResult
Group size, reward mean and standard deviation, and dimensionless coefficients.






Equation: coefficient_i=(reward_i-mean)/(std+stabilizer).
Assumptions: One finite reward group; Bessel correction follows the supplied flag.
Excludes: Policy updates, clipping, and the effect of these coefficients on learning.



Derivation: Subtracting the group mean yields centered rewards. Dividing by the chosen standard deviation plus stabilizer defines the normalized update coefficients.



>>> result = GroupCoefficientsModel().solve([0.0, 1.0], 0.1)
>>> abs(result.coefficient_sum) < 1e-12
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.LengthNormalizationModel()
Per-token push of two rollouts with the same coefficient under per-rollout averaging.
Each rollout’s loss is divided by its own length, so the shorter rollout’s tokens each move long / short times as far. A failure is pushed down hardest when it is short, so failures drift long.





Name
Description




solve
Compare per-token weights under equal trajectory weighting.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.LengthNormalizationModel.solve(
    short_tokens,
    long_tokens,
)
Compare per-token weights under equal trajectory weighting.











Name
Type
Description
Default

int
Positive token count of the shorter rollout.
required


long_tokens
int
Positive token count of the longer rollout.
required














Name
Type
Description





LengthNormalizationResult
Dimensionless ratio of the shorter rollout’s per-token coefficient to the longer one.






Equation: per_token_ratio=long_tokens/short_tokens.
Assumptions: Equal rollout coefficients and separate per-rollout mean losses.
Excludes: Actual gradients, reward differences, and predicted sequence-length drift.



Derivation: Equal trajectory weight is divided among its tokens; the ratio of per-token weights is therefore the inverse ratio of trajectory lengths.



>>> result = LengthNormalizationModel().solve(10, 20)
>>> result.per_token_ratio == 20 / 10
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.RatioClipModel()
The probability ceiling a symmetric ratio clip 1 +/- epsilon sets on one token.
A dominant token’s ceiling can exceed 1 (the clip does not bind), while a rare token may rise only epsilon p per update.





Name
Description




solve
Translate a probability-ratio clip into absolute probability headroom.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.RatioClipModel.solve(epsilon, probability)

Name
Type

Default

float
Nonnegative dimensionless symmetric ratio-clip width.
required


probability
float
Old token probability in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





RatioClipResult
Dimensionless probability ceiling and rise, plus whether the ceiling lies below one.






Equation: ceiling=p*(1+epsilon); rise=p*epsilon; binds=(ceiling<1).
Assumptions: A symmetric probability-ratio upper clip for one token.
Excludes: Probability renormalization across tokens and optimizer dynamics.



Derivation: Multiplying the original probability by the upper ratio clip gives its clipped ceiling; subtracting the original probability gives the permitted absolute rise.



>>> result = RatioClipModel().solve(0.2, 0.5)
>>> result.binds
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.RepeatedVerificationModel()
An all-pass rule over n independent trials of one candidate.
Graded once, a group of G incorrect candidates holds at least one false pass with probability 1 - (1 - q_bad)^G. Requiring all n trials to pass accepts an incorrect candidate with q_bad^n and rejects a correct one with 1 - q_good^n. Stopping at the first failed trial runs sum_{j<n} q^j trials on average.





Name
Description




solve
Compute acceptance errors and trial cost for an all-pass rule.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.RepeatedVerificationModel.solve(
    incorrect_pass,
    correct_pass,
    trials,
    group,
)
Compute acceptance errors and trial cost for an all-pass rule.











Name
Type
Description
Default




incorrect_pass
float
Probability an incorrect candidate passes one trial, in [0, 1].
required


correct_pass
float
Probability a correct candidate passes one trial, in [0, 1].
required


trials
int
Positive count of verification trials per candidate.
required


group
int
Number of candidates per group, a positive count.
required














Name
Type
Description





RepeatedVerificationResult
Acceptance and rejection probabilities and expected counts of executed trials.






Equation: false_accept=q_bad**n; true_reject=1-q_good**n; E[trials]=sum(q**j).
Assumptions: Independent identically distributed trials and first-failure termination.
Excludes: Persistent verifier bias and correlated repeated judgments.



Derivation: Independent pass probabilities multiply across required trials. For early rejection, trial j is reached only after the preceding trials pass, so summing those survival probabilities gives expected work.



>>> result = RepeatedVerificationModel().solve(0.1, 0.9, 2, 4)
>>> result.incorrect_accepted < 0.1
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.RewardCompositionModel()
True and false accepts among one update’s rollouts under an imperfect verifier.
tasks x group rollouts pass with probability p; the verifier accepts a pass with probability valid_accept_rate and a failure with false_accept_rate. Expected counts carry no rounding. The false share is Bayes’ rule over the accepts, so it moves with the policy’s pass rate as well as with the verifier.





Name
Description




solve
Separate true and false verifier acceptances in a rollout batch.

    tasks,
    group,
    pass_rate,
    false_accept_rate,
    valid_accept_rate,
)

Name
Type
Description
Default

required


group
int
Number of candidates per group, a positive count.
required

float
Underlying binary success probability in [0, 1].
required

Probability of accepting an incorrect rollout, in [0, 1].
required


valid_accept_rate
float
Probability of accepting a correct rollout, in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





RewardCompositionResult
Expected rollout and acceptance counts, plus the dimensionless false-accept share.






Equation: n=tasks*group; true=n*p*v; false=n*(1-p)*f.
Assumptions: Stationary conditional acceptance rates and a nonempty accepted population.
Excludes: Correlated verifier errors and changes in policy quality.



Derivation: Multiply rollout counts by correctness prevalence and conditional acceptance probabilities. The false-accept share divides the false joint count by all accepts, which is Bayes conditioning on acceptance.



>>> result = RewardCompositionModel().solve(2, 4, 0.5, 0.1, 0.9)
>>> result.accepts == result.true_accepts + result.false_accepts
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.RolloutSlotCycleModel()
A sandbox slot running one episode at a time, under a cold and a snapshot reset.
Each episode is decisions x (model + tool) plus an assessment, then a reset. Capacity is slots / cycle. Faster resets raise capacity only by the reset’s share of the cycle (Amdahl’s law); the work floor remains.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate slot occupancy and throughput over rollout-reset cycles.

    slots,
    decisions,

    tool_time,

    snapshot_reset,
)

Name
Type
Description





RolloutSlotCycleResult
Work and cycle times in seconds, episodes per hour, and dimensionless capacity ratios.






Equation: work=D*(model+tool)+assessment; capacity=slots/(work+reset).
Assumptions: Serial fixed-duration stages and one episode per slot.
Excludes: Queueing, overlapping stages, startup variance, and resource contention.



Derivation: Serial model and tool stages accumulate over turns, then assessment and reset extend the cycle. Dividing available slots by cycle duration gives the capacity bound.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> result = RolloutSlotCycleModel().solve(2, 3, Q_("1 s"), Q_("2 s"), Q_("1 s"), Q_("2 s"), Q_("1 s"))
>>> result.snapshot_cycle < result.cold_cycle
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.RolloutStepBudgetModel()
One update’s generated tokens and the rollouts spent per informative group.
A group of G independent binary attempts at pass rate p carries reward contrast with probability 1 - p^G - (1 - p)^G; a group without it moves no weights, so each informative group costs G / P(contrast) rollouts (infinite at p = 0 or p = 1, where no group carries contrast).





Name
Description




solve
Count rollout tokens and groups containing both outcome classes.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.RolloutStepBudgetModel.solve(
    tasks,
    group,
    turns,
    tokens_per_turn,
    pass_rate,
)

Name
Type
Description
Default

required


group

required

int

required

required

float

required














Name
Type
Description

Rollout and token counts, contrast probability, and rollouts per informative group.






Equation: tokens=tasks*group*turns*tokens_per_turn; contrast=1-p**G-(1-p)**G.
Assumptions: Independent binary outcomes with one shared pass probability.
Excludes: Correlated outcomes, token-length variance, and update effectiveness.



Derivation: Token volume multiplies tasks, rollouts, turns, and tokens per turn. Subtracting all-pass and all-fail group probabilities from one leaves groups with both outcomes.



>>> result = RolloutStepBudgetModel().solve(2, 4, 3, 10, 0.5)
>>> result.step_tokens == result.rollouts * result.rollout_tokens
True






engine.solvers.reinforcement.VerifierPoolModel()
Verification workers for a stationary stream of completed trajectories.
By Little’s law the busy workers are the arrival rate times the service time per trajectory (every trial executes in this sizing case); the pool is that demand over the target utilization, rounded up.





Name
Description




solve
Size a verifier pool from arrival load and utilization target.





engine.solvers.reinforcement.VerifierPoolModel.solve(
    trajectories,
    interval,
    trials,
    trial_time,
    target_utilization,
)
Size a verifier pool from arrival load and utilization target.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trajectories
int
Positive completed-trajectory count in the observation interval.
required


interval
Quantity
Positive observation interval as a time quantity.
required


trials
int
Positive count of verification trials per candidate.
required


trial_time
Quantity
Positive service time quantity per verification trial.
required


target_utilization
float
Target busy fraction in (0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





VerifierPoolResult
Arrival rate in inverse seconds, mean busy-worker counts, integer slots, and utilization.






Equation: busy=arrival_rate*trials*trial_time; slots=ceil(busy/target_utilization).
Assumptions: Stationary arrivals, every trial executed, and identical workers.
Excludes: Queueing-tail guarantees, early trial termination, and burst arrivals.



Derivation: Arrival rate times trials per arrival times trial duration gives offered busy-slot demand. Divide by the utilization target and round up to obtain an integer pool size.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> result = VerifierPoolModel().solve(10, Q_("1 s"), 2, Q_("0.1 s"), 0.8)
>>> result.utilization <= 0.8
True

Quantity or str

Name
Type
Description





ComputationGraph
Work in FLOPs, resident weight bytes, parameter count, arithmetic intensity in FLOP/byte, and the available layer count.






Equation: F = inference_flops; W = size_in_bytes(precision); I = F / W.
Assumptions: inference_flops describes one image at the registered input resolution. Precision changes stored weights but does not change the declared operation count.

Derivation: multiply parameter count by storage width to obtain weight bytes, then divide the declared or approximated work by those bytes. This is a demand-accounting projection; it does not predict device time.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> model = Models.Vision.ResNet50
>>> graph = model.lower('fp16')
>>> graph.total_ops == model.inference_flops
True

title: Agents Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

AcceptedTaskCostScenario: An attempt of model tokens plus other cost, retried until accepted; optional levers on it.
AllocationAxesScenario: One output ceiling spent as one chain, candidates streams, or rounds of feedback.
AnnFootprintScenario: Resident bytes of a graph index and of product-quantization codes over one corpus.
AppendOnlyContextScenario: A trajectory that appends each turn to its prompt and resends the whole history.
ApprovalEscrowScenario: Approval escrow for a long-running workload (held resources) and an urgent one (time).
ArgmaxNoiseScenario: Argmax over equally good candidates with Gaussian score noise; a rare loophole in the pool.
AttentionDilutionScenario: One attention head with fixed logits: a target among background keys, optionally look-alikes.
BestOfNPoolScenario: Pools of independent candidates at pass_rate, and a mixed workload with the same average.
BlindRetryScenario: Mutating calls retried once after any timeout, with independent request and reply loss.
Bm25PairScenario: One query term scored by BM25 in a short and a long document of one corpus.
BoundedLiabilityAdmissionScenario: The next model call of a trajectory, tested against its dollar allowance.
CheckerPosteriorScenario: A fallible check over candidates, defect_rate of which violate the property.
CohortArmRecord: One policy’s outcomes and settled usage over a cohort of attempted tasks.
CompactionCadenceScenario: Compaction between a trigger and a target watermark over a turn budget.
ContextAdmissionScenario: A serialized request (text plus an image charge) against a window with a reserved reply.
ContextBudgetScenario: A request budgeted by role, appending each tool result against selecting a fixed share.
ContextInvalidationScenario: A superseded excerpt right after the reused prefix: remove, replace, or append a notice.
ControlledBranchScenario: Fresh continuations from one saved prefix under several branches, counted by outcome; the Wilson bound a clean branch leaves and the clean runs a target_bound needs.
CorrelatedReviewersScenario: Reviewers who each falsely approve with the same marginal rate, independent or correlated.
CounterfactualSearchScenario: Replay paths that blame for a failure must search: a whole horizon, or one checked window.
CreditWindowScenario: A producer feeding a slower model consumer, unbounded or behind a credit window.
DeadlinePolicyScenario: One candidate, breadth in parallel, or feedback, for one task under one deadline.
DeficitRoundRobinScenario: Backlogged request classes sharing model calls under weighted deficit round-robin.
DelegationCohortScenario: A single controller and a delegated design on one matched cohort, priced alike.
DelegationTokenBreakEvenScenario: Delegation at a token multiple m per attempt: cost per accepted task scales by m p_single / p_multi.
DependencyScheduleScenario: A dependency graph on interchangeable slots: aggregate work, the critical path, and both bounds.
EnvelopeAmortizationScenario: calls sequential calls of work_per_call, with envelope setup paid per call or once.
ExactScanScenario: An exact vector scan on one host: bytes, intensity, and the bandwidth floor.
FanoutDeadlineScenario: A fan-out whose workers each finish by the deadline with one probability, independently.
GraphNeighborhoodScenario: A typed traversal’s exact-tree neighborhood against a call’s retrieval allowance.
HeadSamplingMissScenario: Head sampling keeps each trial with retention_probability, decided before its outcome; a failure mode that occurs occurrences times leaves no detailed trace with miss.
HorizonCompoundingScenario: Independent, unchecked steps each right with step_success; success at each horizon.
IndexMaintenanceScenario: One edit’s synchronous re-indexing against exclusion of the stale entries.
InjectionExposureScenario: Workloads reading reads untrusted items each, a fraction payload_fraction carrying a payload, with and without a screen that misses miss_rate of payloads.
ModelCallScenario: One call of prompt_tokens (+ instruction_tokens) in and output_tokens out at floors.
ModelPollingScenario: A model that checks a pending job at a fixed interval until it completes.
ObservationCarryScenario: A raw tool output sized in windows, and its shaped view carried by later calls.
PartitionScreenScenario: A fixed partition screened over worker counts: (1 - p) + p / N + c (N - 1) of the serial time.
PolicyComparisonScenario: Two policies, each run on attacked attacked and benign separate benign episodes.
PrefixLayoutBillScenario: A trajectory of root, trunk, and leaf requests, billed volatile-first and zoned.
ProbeVsAnswerScenario: A generated explanation of answer_tokens against a prepared test of probe_time.
ProtectedFieldCheckScenario: Constraints lost independently across compaction rounds, with and without a host check.
PrunedSearchTreeScenario: A search tree of branching children per node whose step check rejects rejection_rate.
ReferencePassingScenario: Children handed a pasted repository slice, or a reference and the files they then read.
ResidualViolationScenario: A residual per-step rate of violating proposals over horizon steps, for a day’s trajectories.
RetrievalPayloadScenario: Whole serialized records staged in what a call’s window leaves for retrieval.
SamplingScenario: One fixed logit vector at a base and a sharpened temperature, then top-p at the base.
SandboxPoolReserveScenario: A warm sandbox pool under steady arrivals: active leases, a standby reserve, and memory.
ScalabilityLawScenario: Relative capacity N / (1 + sigma (N - 1) + kappa N (N - 1)) over integer worker counts.
ScopedRevisionScenario: A candidate plan of equal nodes, replaced_nodes of which a refuted premise invalidates.
SearchAccountsScenario: Flat best-of-N against beam search over the same task, kept as separate accounts.
SequentialCanaryScenario: A canary monitor: Wald’s SPRT between acceptance p_base and a specified degraded p_degraded at targets alpha (false hold) and beta (missed degradation), on fraction of eligible tasks arriving at arrival_rate, labels label_delay late.
SerialTailExposureScenario: Serial calls that each exceed their own tail latency independently.
SharedWriteScenario: Workers each writing writes_per_worker of files files, uniformly and independently.
ShortenedWindowScenario: An observation window cut to window_share of its adopted length; samples scale with it.
SpanCriticalPathScenario: One trial’s observed spans on a shared clock, the spans each waits for, and one intervention.
StorageAmplificationScenario: Auxiliary bytes and re-index time of a lexical-plus-graph and a lexical-plus-dense store.
StreamCancelScenario: A streamed reply with output_allowance tokens, rejected and canceled at reject_step.
SyscallTaxScenario: calls ordinary system calls priced by the terms each isolation envelope pays.
ToolCatalogSelectionScenario: A registered tool catalog staged whole or as a selected subset with overhead.
ToolDriftScenario: Baseline and candidate distributions of tool calls over the same tools, compared by the Jensen-Shannon divergence (natural logarithms).
ToolkitGranularityScenario: Structured tools against one shell tool, judged by cost per accepted task.
TraceRetentionScenario: One cohort period of trials in disjoint verdict classes, each with a trace_size body, retained over window by keeping everything, head sampling, or verdict-aware selection.
TrajectoryBudgetMeterScenario: An append-only trajectory metered against turns, tokens, time, and dollars.
TrajectoryResendScenario: A trajectory of turns calls that each resend the whole history (TrajectoryResendModel).
VerifiedPoolScenario: A pool of pool_size candidates, first passing one returned, under a fallible check.
WorkspaceProvisioningScenario: workspaces on one pinned base, provisioned by copy or copy-on-write, then a first write.

physics.performance.calc_amdahls_speedup(p, s)
Calculate speedup when one fraction of execution is accelerated.











Name
Type
Description
Default




p
float
Fraction of original elapsed time affected by the improvement, in [0, 1].
required


s
float
Positive speedup of the affected fraction; positive infinity removes its time entirely.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Overall dimensionless speedup; infinity when all original time is removed.






Equation: S = 1 / [(1 - p) + p/s].
Assumptions: The original work and unaffected elapsed time remain fixed.
Excludes: New overhead, workload growth, and a changing accelerated fraction.



Amdahl (1967), “Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1465482.1465560 (bibliography key: amdahl1967).
Derivation: Normalize original elapsed time to one, retain 1-p, and divide the affected p by s. This is Amdahl’s fixed-work speedup relation.



>>> calc_amdahls_speedup(0.5, float("inf"))
2.0




physics.performance.calc_bottleneck(ops, model_bytes, device_flops, device_bw)
Compare compute and memory-transfer times for a workload.











Name
Type
Description
Default




ops
Quantity
Nonnegative workload operation count in FLOPs.
required


model_bytes
Quantity
Nonnegative total traffic in bytes; this argument represents traffic, not necessarily model storage alone.
required


device_flops
Quantity
Positive available computation rate in FLOP/s.
required


device_bw
Quantity
Positive available memory bandwidth in byte/s.
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
Compute_ms and memory_ms are time magnitudes; bottleneck is Compute or Memory; ratio compares larger to smaller time; intensity is FLOP/byte.






Equation: T_compute = C/F; T_memory = M/BW; intensity = C/M.
Assumptions: Compute and memory are independent ceilings; ties are labeled Compute. Times below the implementation zero threshold use explicit degenerate-work cases.
Excludes: Dispatch overhead, communication, nonideal overlap, and any traffic omitted from model_bytes.



Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009).



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> result = calc_bottleneck(Q_(2, "flop"), Q_(4, "byte"), Q_(2, "flop/s"), Q_(2, "byte/s"))
>>> result["bottleneck"]
'Memory'




physics.performance.calc_effective_flops(
    peak_flops,
    mfu,
    scaling_eff,
    goodput_ratio,
)
Apply utilization, scaling, and goodput factors to peak rate.











Name
Type
Description
Default




peak_flops
Quantity or float
Positive computation rate; bare values are interpreted as FLOP/s.
required


mfu
float
Model FLOP utilization factor in [0, 1].
required


scaling_eff
float
Additional distributed scaling factor in [0, 1].
required


goodput_ratio
float
Fraction of elapsed time contributing useful progress, in [0, 1].
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Effective useful computation rate in FLOP/s.






Equation: F_effective = F_peak * mfu * scaling_eff * goodput_ratio.
Assumptions: Factors describe distinct losses; the caller must avoid charging a loss twice.
Excludes: Estimating the factors, phase-dependent utilization, and changing workload intensity.



Derivation: Apply successive dimensionless useful-work fractions to the same baseline rate; the product is valid only when the factors do not duplicate losses.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> calc_effective_flops(Q_(8, "flop/s"), 0.5, 0.5, 1.0) == Q_(2, "flop/s")
True




physics.performance.calc_pareto_frontier(points)
Return indices of points undominated in cost and value.











Name
Type
Description
Default




points
sequence of tuple of float
Pairs (cost, value), with lower cost and higher value preferred. Each axis must use a consistent unit.
required














Name
Type
Description





list of int
Original indices of nondominated points; equal duplicates are retained.






Equation: Point i is excluded if some j has cost_j <= cost_i and value_j >= value_i, with at least one strict inequality.
Assumptions: Both objectives are deterministic and directly comparable within their axes.
Excludes: Uncertainty, scalar preference weights, and constraints beyond the two axes.



Derivation: Apply the definition of Pareto dominance pairwise to every input point.



>>> calc_pareto_frontier([(1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3)])
[0, 2]




physics.performance.calc_partial_slowdown_stretch(stall_fraction, slowdown)
Calculate elapsed-time growth when one task fraction slows.











Name
Type
Description
Default




stall_fraction
float
Fraction of unloaded elapsed time exposed to the slowdown, in [0, 1].
required


slowdown
float
Multiplicative duration increase for that fraction, at least one.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Loaded duration divided by unloaded duration.






Equation: stretch = (1 - f) + f S.
Assumptions: The affected fraction f is measured in the unloaded task and remains fixed.
Excludes: Changes in work, additional interference paths, and queueing beyond the supplied slowdown.



Amdahl (1967), “Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1465482.1465560 (bibliography key: amdahl1967).
Derivation: Apply the fixed-fraction time decomposition of Amdahl’s law, with a slowdown rather than a speedup.



>>> calc_partial_slowdown_stretch(0.5, 3) == (1 - 0.5) + 0.5 * 3
True




physics.performance.calc_pipeline_bubble(n_stages, n_microbatches, v_stages=1)
Estimate the fill-and-drain fraction of a balanced pipeline.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_stages
int
Positive physical pipeline-stage count.
required


n_microbatches
int
Positive microbatch count per training step.
required


v_stages
int
Positive virtual-stage factor; default one represents no interleaving.
1









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless idle fraction in [0, 1).






Equation: bubble = (p - 1) / (v m + p - 1).
Assumptions: Stages have equal duration; virtual stages reduce the fill/drain penalty according to the stated schedule approximation.
Excludes: Stage imbalance, communication stalls, runtime scheduling details, and activation feasibility.



Derivation: Count p-1 fill/drain slots against v*m useful slots in the balanced pipeline approximation. The virtual-stage substitution summarizes interleaving; it is not an event-level schedule simulation.



>>> calc_pipeline_bubble(1, 4)
0.0
>>> calc_pipeline_bubble(4, 8, 2) < calc_pipeline_bubble(4, 8)
True




physics.performance.calc_stall_share_breakeven(allowed_stretch, slowdown)
Find the largest slowed task fraction within a duration budget.











Name
Type
Description
Default




allowed_stretch
float
Maximum total duration divided by unloaded duration, at least one.
required


slowdown
float
Duration multiplier for the affected portion, at least one.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Largest admissible affected fraction, capped at one.






Equation: f_max = min(1, (allowed_stretch - 1) / (slowdown - 1)); f_max = 1 when slowdown = 1.
Assumptions: The allowed duration is no smaller than the unloaded duration.
Excludes: Time-varying interference and uncertainty in the baseline duration.



Derivation: Solve 1 + f(S - 1) <= allowed_stretch for f and cap the physical fraction at one.



>>> calc_stall_share_breakeven(2, 3) == (2 - 1) / (3 - 1)
True




physics.performance.calc_strong_scaling_speedup(
    num_devices,
    communication_fraction,
)
Estimate fixed-work scaling with a nonparallel time fraction.











Name
Type
Description
Default




num_devices
int
Participating device count, at least one.
required


communication_fraction
float
Fraction of baseline time modeled as nonparallel communication, in [0, 1].
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless speedup relative to one device.






Equation: S(N) = N / [1 + (N - 1) f].
Assumptions: Communication fraction f is constant and the remaining work scales perfectly.
Excludes: Topology-dependent communication growth, overlap changes, and load imbalance.



Derivation: Rewrite Amdahl’s 1 / [f + (1-f)/N] by multiplying numerator and denominator by N.



>>> calc_strong_scaling_speedup(4, 0.0)
4.0




physics.performance.calc_universal_scalability_law(n, sigma, kappa)
Evaluate capacity under serialization and pairwise coordination costs.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n
int or float
Dimensionless concurrency, at least one.
required


sigma
float
Serialization/contention parameter in [0, 1].
required


kappa
float
Nonnegative pairwise-coordination coefficient.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Relative capacity C(n), normalized to one at n = 1.






Equation: C(n) = n / [1 + sigma(n - 1) + kappa n(n - 1)].
Assumptions: sigma and kappa are supplied workload parameters, not hardware constants.
Excludes: A fit or independent validation of the parameters and explicit queueing dynamics.



Gunther (2008), “A General Theory of Computational Scalability Based on Rational Functions.” https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431 (bibliography key: gunther2008general).
Derivation: The Universal Scalability Law models normalized overhead as a serialization term proportional to n-1 and a coordination term proportional to n(n-1); capacity divides concurrency by this overhead. These terms define the model rather than a physical identity.



>>> calc_universal_scalability_law(4, 0.0, 0.0)
4.0




physics.performance.calc_usl_optimal_concurrency(sigma, kappa)
Find the stationary concurrency of the scalability model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




sigma
float
Serialization parameter in [0, 1].
required


kappa
float
Nonnegative pairwise-coordination coefficient.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Continuous stationary concurrency, not rounded or clamped to a realizable device count; infinity for kappa = 0 and one for sigma = 1 with positive kappa.






Equation: N_star = sqrt((1 - sigma) / kappa) for kappa > 0 and sigma < 1.
Assumptions: The continuous USL model applies with fixed coefficients. Values below one require boundary handling by the caller.
Excludes: Integer search, capacity constraints, and an empirical fit of USL coefficients.



Gunther (2008), “A General Theory of Computational Scalability Based on Rational Functions.” https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431 (bibliography key: gunther2008general).
Derivation: Set the derivative of n/[1+sigma(n-1)+kappa*n*(n-1)] to zero. Its numerator is 1-sigma-kappa*n**2.



>>> calc_usl_optimal_concurrency(0.0, 0.25)
2.0




physics.performance.dTime(
    total_ops,
    num_devices,
    peak_flops_per_device,
    efficiency_eta,
)
Estimate execution time from total work and effective fleet throughput.











Name
Type
Description
Default




total_ops
Quantity
Nonnegative total floating-point operation count.
required


num_devices
int
Number of identical accelerators, at least one.
required


peak_flops_per_device
Quantity
Positive peak computation rate per device in FLOP/s-compatible units.
required


efficiency_eta
float
Achieved fraction of aggregate peak throughput, in (0, 1].
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled execution duration in seconds.






Equation: T = C / (N F_peak eta).
Assumptions: The workload is divisible across identical devices; eta already includes the utilization losses the caller intends to model.
Excludes: Separate memory, communication, and recovery terms; add these explicitly or incorporate them consistently into eta.



Derivation: Aggregate useful computation rate is N F_peak eta; divide the required work C by that rate.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> dTime(Q_(8, "flop"), 2, Q_(4, "flop/s"), 0.5) == Q_(2, "s")
True

Loaded duration divided by unloaded duration.






Equation: stretch = (1 - f) + f S.
Assumptions: The affected fraction f is measured in the unloaded task and remains fixed.
Excludes: Changes in work, additional interference paths, and queueing beyond the supplied slowdown.



Amdahl (1967), “Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1465482.1465560 (bibliography key: amdahl1967).
Derivation: Apply the fixed-fraction time decomposition of Amdahl’s law, with a slowdown rather than a speedup.



>>> calc_partial_slowdown_stretch(0.5, 3) == (1 - 0.5) + 0.5 * 3
True

required

required

1

Type
Description

Dimensionless idle fraction in [0, 1).






Equation: bubble = (p - 1) / (v m + p - 1).
Assumptions: Stages have equal duration; virtual stages reduce the fill/drain penalty according to the stated schedule approximation.
Excludes: Stage imbalance, communication stalls, runtime scheduling details, and activation feasibility.



Derivation: Count p-1 fill/drain slots against v*m useful slots in the balanced pipeline approximation. The virtual-stage substitution summarizes interleaving; it is not an event-level schedule simulation.



>>> calc_pipeline_bubble(1, 4)

>>> calc_pipeline_bubble(4, 8, 2) < calc_pipeline_bubble(4, 8)
True

Find the largest slowed task fraction within a duration budget.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Maximum total duration divided by unloaded duration, at least one.
required

Duration multiplier for the affected portion, at least one.
required














Name
Type
Description

Largest admissible affected fraction, capped at one.






Equation: f_max = min(1, (allowed_stretch - 1) / (slowdown - 1)); f_max = 1 when slowdown = 1.
Assumptions: The allowed duration is no smaller than the unloaded duration.
Excludes: Time-varying interference and uncertainty in the baseline duration.



Derivation: Solve 1 + f(S - 1) <= allowed_stretch for f and cap the physical fraction at one.



>>> calc_stall_share_breakeven(2, 3) == (2 - 1) / (3 - 1)

Equation: S(N) = N / [1 + (N - 1) f].
Assumptions: Communication fraction f is constant and the remaining work scales perfectly.
Excludes: Topology-dependent communication growth, overlap changes, and load imbalance.

>>> calc_strong_scaling_speedup(4, 0.0)

physics.performance.calc_universal_scalability_law(n, sigma, kappa)
Evaluate capacity under serialization and pairwise coordination costs.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n
int or float
Dimensionless concurrency, at least one.
required


sigma
float
Serialization/contention parameter in [0, 1].
required


kappa
float
Nonnegative pairwise-coordination coefficient.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Relative capacity C(n), normalized to one at n = 1.






Equation: C(n) = n / [1 + sigma(n - 1) + kappa n(n - 1)].
Assumptions: sigma and kappa are supplied workload parameters, not hardware constants.
Excludes: A fit or independent validation of the parameters and explicit queueing dynamics.



Gunther (2008), “A General Theory of Computational Scalability Based on Rational Functions.” https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431 (bibliography key: gunther2008general).
Derivation: The Universal Scalability Law models normalized overhead as a serialization term proportional to n-1 and a coordination term proportional to n(n-1); capacity divides concurrency by this overhead. These terms define the model rather than a physical identity.



>>> calc_universal_scalability_law(4, 0.0, 0.0)
4.0




physics.performance.calc_usl_optimal_concurrency(sigma, kappa)
Find the stationary concurrency of the scalability model.











Name
Type
Description
Default




sigma
float
Serialization parameter in [0, 1].
required


kappa
float
Nonnegative pairwise-coordination coefficient.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Continuous stationary concurrency, not rounded or clamped to a realizable device count; infinity for kappa = 0 and one for sigma = 1 with positive kappa.






Equation: N_star = sqrt((1 - sigma) / kappa) for kappa > 0 and sigma < 1.
Assumptions: The continuous USL model applies with fixed coefficients. Values below one require boundary handling by the caller.
Excludes: Integer search, capacity constraints, and an empirical fit of USL coefficients.



Gunther (2008), “A General Theory of Computational Scalability Based on Rational Functions.” https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431 (bibliography key: gunther2008general).
Derivation: Set the derivative of n/[1+sigma(n-1)+kappa*n*(n-1)] to zero. Its numerator is 1-sigma-kappa*n**2.



>>> calc_usl_optimal_concurrency(0.0, 0.25)
2.0

Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
C = A B with A m x k and B k x n, computed one tile_m x tile_n output tile at a time, stepping through the reduction tile_k elements per step.
Operands are operand_bytes each and the accumulator accumulator_bytes. The on-chip store holds one A tile and one B tile (two of each when double buffered) and the accumulator tile. Traffic counts element moves between memory and the on-chip store: A is loaded once per output-tile column, B once per output-tile row, and C written once. The single-cell loop orders (no tile) count one held value per cell: the other operands stream once per MAC, and a partial sum that is not held is read and written once per MAC.

title: physics.layers
text:
physics.layers
Layer-level counting laws for neural network architectures (added 2026-10-20).
Weight, multiply-add, and byte counts for one layer are products of its dimensions and live on the calculation scenarios (engine/scenario_types.py: DenseLayerScenario, ConvLayerScenario, RecurrentStepScenario). This module holds the few laws those counts compose with: how a stack of convolutions widens its view, how a depthwise separable factoring shrinks a convolution, and how a product of per-layer gradient gains decays with depth.





Name
Description




calc_gradient_product
Multiply equal gradient gains through a plain layer stack.


calc_layers_for_receptive_field
Find the layer count needed to reach a receptive-field width.


calc_receptive_field
Calculate receptive-field width for stride-one convolutions.


calc_resnet_bottleneck_macs
Count convolution and classifier MACs in a bottleneck ResNet.


calc_separable_cost_fraction
Compare depthwise-separable and dense convolution work.





physics.layers.calc_gradient_product(gain, depth)
Multiply equal gradient gains through a plain layer stack.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gain
float
Dimensionless per-layer scalar derivative factor.
required


depth
int
Nonnegative number of multiplied factors.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless product of local derivative factors.






Equation: g_total = gain**depth.
Assumptions: All scalar gains are identical and the computation follows one serial path.
Excludes: Residual paths, Jacobian spectra, and variation among layers.



Derivation: Apply the scalar chain rule repeatedly across depth layers.



>>> calc_gradient_product(0.5, 3) == 0.5**3
True




physics.layers.calc_layers_for_receptive_field(field, kernel)
Find the layer count needed to reach a receptive-field width.











Name
Type
Description
Default




field
int
Target width in input pixels, at least one.
required


kernel
int
Kernel width in pixels, greater than one.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Minimum nonnegative count of stride-one convolution layers.






Equation: L = ceil((R - 1) / (K - 1)).
Assumptions: Each layer increases receptive-field width by K - 1.
Excludes: Strides, dilation, and a kernel of width one, which cannot enlarge the field.



Derivation: Solve R = 1 + L(K - 1) for L and round upward to a whole layer.



>>> calc_layers_for_receptive_field(7, 3) == 3
True




physics.layers.calc_receptive_field(layers, kernel)
Calculate receptive-field width for stride-one convolutions.





Name
Type
Description
Default




layers
int
Nonnegative convolution layer count.
required


kernel
int
Positive kernel width in pixels.
required









Name
Type
Description





int
Receptive-field width in input pixels.






Equation: R = 1 + L (K - 1).
Assumptions: Every convolution has the same kernel width, unit stride, and unit dilation.
Excludes: Pooling, strided layers, dilation, and boundary clipping.



Derivation: R = 1 + L (K - 1).



>>> calc_receptive_field(3, 3) == 1 + 3 * (3 - 1)
True




physics.layers.calc_resnet_bottleneck_macs(
    stages=((64, 3), (128, 4), (256, 6), (512, 3)),
    input_size=224,
    num_classes=1000,
    stride_on_3x3=False,
)
Count convolution and classifier MACs in a bottleneck ResNet.











Name
Type
Description
Default




stages
sequence of tuple of int
Positive (bottleneck width, block count) pairs; default describes ResNet-50.
((64, 3), (128, 4), (256, 6), (512, 3))


input_size
int
Square image side in pixels; default 224. Spatial downsampling uses integer division.
224


num_classes
int
Positive classifier output width; default 1000.
1000


stride_on_3x3
bool
Put downsampling stride on the 3-by-3 convolution for v1.5; default False puts it on the first 1-by-1.
False














Name
Type
Description





dict
MAC counts under keys 7x7, 3x3, 1x1, fc, and total, per image.






Equation: MAC_conv = H_out**2 C_in C_out K**2; MAC_fc = C_in C_out; total sums all counted layers.
Assumptions: A 7-by-7 stride-two stem, stride-two pooling, bottleneck expansion by four, and projection at each stage’s first block.
Excludes: Bias, batch normalization, pooling, nonlinearities, and residual-add operations.
The original bottleneck places a downsampling stride in its first 1-by-1 convolution. Moving that stride to the 3-by-3 convolution retains more first-projection work, so the two variants need not have identical MAC counts.



Derivation: Enumerate the stem, three convolutions per bottleneck, stage-entry projection, and classifier; multiply each output element by its convolution reduction length. The architecture follows He et al. (2016), “Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition,” Table 1. https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385



>>> work = calc_resnet_bottleneck_macs(stages=((4, 1),), input_size=32, num_classes=2)
>>> work["total"] == sum(work[k] for k in ("7x7", "3x3", "1x1", "fc"))
True




physics.layers.calc_separable_cost_fraction(kernel, out_channels)
Compare depthwise-separable and dense convolution work.





Name
Type
Description
Default




kernel
int
Positive square kernel width.
required


out_channels
int
Positive output channel count.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Separable-to-dense MAC or weight-count ratio.






Equation: rho = 1 / C_out + 1 / K**2.
Assumptions: A depthwise K-by-K convolution is followed by a dense pointwise convolution; spatial shape is identical.
Excludes: Biases, nonlinearities, memory movement, and achieved kernel speed.



Derivation: Divide K**2 C_in + C_in C_out by the dense cost K**2 C_in C_out. This is the counting argument used for depthwise-separable convolutions.



>>> calc_separable_cost_fraction(3, 8) == 1 / 8 + 1 / 3**2
True

title: QuantizationGridScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Values stored on a bits-bit integer grid over a clipping range.
Affine (symmetric=False): s = (beta - alpha) / (2^b - 1) and a zero-point z = qmin + round(-alpha / s); codes run 0 to 2^b - 1, or -2^(b-1) to 2^(b-1) - 1 when signed. Symmetric: s = max(|alpha|, |beta|) / (2^(b-1) - 1), z = 0, codes +-(2^(b-1) - 1). alpha and beta default to the values’ minimum and maximum (min-max calibration). Rounding is to nearest, ties to even.


Equation: The calculation members below define lo, hi, steps, qmin, qmax, scale, zero_point_exact, zero_point, codes, readback, errors, max_rounding_error.
Assumptions: All input values share a finite clipping range and one integer grid; the scale is positive.
Excludes: Learned per-channel scales and accuracy effects beyond reconstruction error.



Derivation: Values stored on a bits-bit integer grid over a clipping range. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.Uint8RangeMinusOneToThree
>>> value = case.max_rounding_error
>>> print(f"{value:.3g}")
0.00784

Description




alpha



beta



bits



codes

errors
Absolute reconstruction error per input, in the same units as the input values.


hi
Upper clipping endpoint, explicit beta or the maximum input value.

Lower clipping endpoint, explicit alpha or the minimum input value.

Half a grid step in input units; excludes clipping error outside the supported range.

Reconstructed input-unit values from codes via calc_dequantize.

symmetric



values

Integer code offset used to represent zero, via calc_zero_point.

Unrounded zero-point displacement, or zero for a symmetric grid.

title: BatchVersusStreamingIngestScenario
text:
Data scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/data.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One event stream ingested by always-on streaming cores or by a batch job each hour.
Streaming runs stream_cores (redundancy_factor cores per primary) for stream_hours_per_day; batch runs batch_cores for batch_window of each clock hour. Both pay core_hour_price.


Equation: daily bill = occupied core-hours * price; per-core throughput = required aggregate bandwidth / productive cores.
Assumptions: A batch drains one hour of arrivals inside each batch window; streaming redundancy is already included in reserved core count.
Excludes: Traffic bursts, queue latency, storage I/O bottlenecks, and scheduling overhead.



Derivation: daily bill = occupied core-hours * price; per-core throughput = required aggregate bandwidth / productive cores. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.

>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.MillionEventBatchVersusStreaming
>>> round(float(case.throughput.to('GB/s').magnitude), 3)
1.0

A canary monitor: Wald’s SPRT between acceptance p_base and a specified degraded p_degraded at targets alpha (false hold) and beta (missed degradation), on fraction of eligible tasks arriving at arrival_rate, labels label_delay late.

Per-group metric monitoring of a decision service at request_rate.
sample_share of decisions are logged at record_size each; groups subgroups x metrics_per_group metrics are each tested at false_alarm_rate per evaluation interval on a stable process.

text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
workload’s decoder blocks at a context of context_tokens: the classic block’s weights (4 d^2 attention projections, 2 x ffn_multiple d^2 MLP), its dense and attention multiply-adds, and, with hardware, the attention arithmetic of one prompt at peak.


Equation: Shared transformer helpers count dense block parameters and full attention products; two FLOPs are counted per MAC.
Assumptions: Classic dense blocks at the declared FFN multiplier; exact_parameters specifically describes the GPT-2 bias-enabled layout.
Excludes: Gated FFNs, grouped-query geometry, kernel fusion, and vocabulary-output work from prompt_flops.

The exact_parameters property adds GPT-2-specific biases, normalization parameters, and position embeddings rather than treating the coarse block rule as exact.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.Gpt2XlBlockFullWindow
>>> s.block_macs == s.dense_macs+s.attention_macs
True

engine.scenario_types.TransformerBlockScenario.attention_to_dense

The crossover in units of the width (six for the classic block).
Equation: crossover / width.

Every block’s attention products over the prompt, two FLOPs per multiply-add.

Prompt FLOPs combining dense block work and attention products, excluding vocabulary output work.

A training step in forward passes: 6P over 2P per token.
Equation: p = workload.parameters; (calc_transformer_training_flops(p, 1) / calc_transformer_decode_flops(p, 1)).to('').magnitude.



engine.scenario_types.TransformerBlockScenario.layer_forward_flops
One block’s forward FLOPs for the whole batch: dense and attention products, two FLOPs each.
Equation: Q_(2 * block_macs * batch_size, 'flop').to('GFLOP').



engine.scenario_types.TransformerBlockScenario.training_step_flops
One training step counted layer by layer, attention products included.

The same step by the 6P-per-token rule, which omits the attention products.

models.types.TransformerWorkload()
Workload representation of an autoregressive Transformer (e.g., LLMs).





Name
Description




head_width
Return the number of components in one attention head.


kv_width
Return the expanded key or value feature width per layer.


queries_per_kv_head
Return the query-head sharing ratio for grouped attention.









Name
Description

Count cached attention state for a batch of sequences.

Lower one Transformer forward work unit and its resident weights.


training_memory
Estimate per-device weights, gradients, optimizer state, and activations.





models.types.TransformerWorkload.get_kv_cache_size(
    seq_len,
    batch_size,
    precision=BYTES_FP16,
)
Count cached attention state for a batch of sequences.











Name
Type
Description
Default




seq_len
int
Nonnegative cached tokens per sequence, including any shared prefix separately in every request; this method does not deduplicate pages.
required


batch_size
int
Nonnegative number of resident sequences.
required


precision
Quantity or str
Bytes per stored element, or a registered format such as ‘fp16’. A byte quantity specifies the width directly; it must be positive.
BYTES_FP16














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Cache storage in bytes for all layers and sequences.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : Standard KV tensor accounting. mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_mla_cache_size : Compressed latent accounting.



Equation: M_KV = 2 * L * H_KV * d_head * S * B * b for standard multi-head or grouped-query attention. When both MLA ranks are present, M_MLA = L * (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) * S * B * b.
Assumptions: all layers share the same attention geometry. Missing hidden_dim and heads fall back to 4096 and 32 here; an explicit head_dim overrides hidden_dim // heads. Missing kv_heads means full multi-head attention. Both MLA dimensions must be present to select the latent path.
Excludes: query activations, weight storage, page rounding, cache sharing, allocator metadata, and inference-engine workspaces.



Derivation: standard attention stores one key and one value vector per KV head, layer, token, and sequence. MLA stores a shared latent vector and the rotary-position key components instead of expanded head tensors. The arithmetic is delegated to the two named cache-accounting functions.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> model = Models.Language.Llama3_8B
>>> model.get_kv_cache_size(128, 2) == 2 * model.get_kv_cache_size(128, 1)
True




models.types.TransformerWorkload.lower(precision=BYTES_FP16)
Lower one Transformer forward work unit and its resident weights.











Name
Type
Description
Default




precision
Quantity or str
Bytes per stored element, or a registered format such as ‘fp16’. A byte quantity specifies the width directly; it must be positive.
BYTES_FP16














Name
Type
Description





ComputationGraph
Work in FLOPs, resident weight bytes, parameter count, arithmetic intensity in FLOP/byte, and the available layer count.






Equation: F = inference_flops if specified, otherwise 2 * P; W = size_in_bytes(precision); I = F / W.
Assumptions: the registered FLOP count defines the work unit when supplied; the fallback represents parameter-dominated dense work for one token. Layer count is copied into the graph for later overhead modeling.
Excludes: attention over cached context, KV storage, backward work, activation traffic, and device timing. Do not interpret this graph alone as a complete decode model.



Derivation: multiply parameter count by storage width to obtain weight bytes, then divide the declared or approximated work by those bytes. This is a demand-accounting projection; it does not predict device time.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> model = Models.Language.Llama3_8B
>>> graph = model.lower('fp16')
>>> graph.weight_bytes == model.size_in_bytes('fp16')
True




models.types.TransformerWorkload.training_memory(
    batch_size,
    seq_len,
    precision='fp16',
    optimizer='adam',
    strategy='selective',
    zero_stage=0,
    dp_size=1,
    is_lora=False,
    lora_rank=16,
)
Estimate per-device weights, gradients, optimizer state, and activations.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_size
int
Positive sequences resident on this device for activation accounting.
required


seq_len
int
Positive tokens per sequence.
required


precision
str
Registered weight and gradient format; optimizer storage uses its own mixed-precision convention in optimizer_state_bytes.
'fp16'


optimizer
str
Optimizer convention: ‘adam’, ‘adamw’, ‘sgd’, or ‘none’.
'adam'


strategy
str
Activation recomputation mode: ‘none’, ‘selective’, or ‘full’, delegated to calc_activation_memory.
'selective'


zero_stage
int
ZeRO stage: 0 leaves state local; 1 shards optimizer state; 2 also shards gradients; 3 also shards weights.
0


dp_size
int
Positive number of data-parallel ranks sharing the sharded state.
1


is_lora
bool
Restrict trainable gradient and optimizer state to an approximate adapter parameter fraction. Full frozen weights remain resident.
False


lora_rank
int
Positive adapter rank when is_lora is true. The model assumes adapters on Q, K, V, and O projections in every layer.
16














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled resident memory per device in GiB. This method does not compare the result with a device capacity or declare feasibility.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_activation_memory : Activation assumptions. mlsysim.physics.memory.optimizer_state_bytes : Optimizer storage convention.



Equation: M = M_weights + M_gradients + M_optimizer + M_activations. Weights and gradients initially cost P * b each; optimizer state costs P * optimizer_state_bytes(optimizer). LoRA multiplies gradient and optimizer storage by min(8 * rank * hidden_dim * layers / P, 1). ZeRO divides each selected state category by dp_size.
Assumptions: homogeneous data-parallel shards and the selected activation formula. Missing hidden_dim uses 4096. The adapter estimate covers four square attention projections, not every linear layer or architecture. Optimizer state follows the shared mixed-precision byte convention.
Excludes: communication buffers, allocator reserve, runtime workspaces, fragmentation, tensor-parallel activation partitioning, and peak transient all-gather state. ZeRO sharding is a storage estimate, not a latency model.



Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models.” https://doi.org/10.1109/sc41405.2020.00024 (bibliography key: rajbhandari2020). The LoRA projection count and frozen-weight accounting are explicit implementation assumptions; the ZeRO citation supports state partitioning.



>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> model = Models.Language.Llama3_8B
>>> local = model.training_memory(1, 128, zero_stage=0)
>>> sharded = model.training_memory(1, 128, zero_stage=3, dp_size=2)
>>> sharded < local
True

mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : Standard KV tensor accounting. mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_mla_cache_size : Compressed latent accounting.



Equation: M_KV = 2 * L * H_KV * d_head * S * B * b for standard multi-head or grouped-query attention. When both MLA ranks are present, M_MLA = L * (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) * S * B * b.
Assumptions: all layers share the same attention geometry. Missing hidden_dim and heads fall back to 4096 and 32 here; an explicit head_dim overrides hidden_dim // heads. Missing kv_heads means full multi-head attention. Both MLA dimensions must be present to select the latent path.
Excludes: query activations, weight storage, page rounding, cache sharing, allocator metadata, and inference-engine workspaces.



Derivation: standard attention stores one key and one value vector per KV head, layer, token, and sequence. MLA stores a shared latent vector and the rotary-position key components instead of expanded head tensors. The arithmetic is delegated to the two named cache-accounting functions.

ComputationGraph
Work in FLOPs, resident weight bytes, parameter count, arithmetic intensity in FLOP/byte, and the available layer count.






Equation: F = inference_flops if specified, otherwise 2 * P; W = size_in_bytes(precision); I = F / W.
Assumptions: the registered FLOP count defines the work unit when supplied; the fallback represents parameter-dominated dense work for one token. Layer count is copied into the graph for later overhead modeling.
Excludes: attention over cached context, KV storage, backward work, activation traffic, and device timing. Do not interpret this graph alone as a complete decode model.



Derivation: multiply parameter count by storage width to obtain weight bytes, then divide the declared or approximated work by those bytes. This is a demand-accounting projection; it does not predict device time.

workload trained for epochs over dataset on one hardware at utilization, against a keep_fraction coreset scored by one forward pass of workload or proxy.
The selection inequality compares scoring plus subset training with full training; rescoring repeats the scoring pass before every epoch. Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Utility per applicant of raising group’s TPR to reference_group’s by moving its threshold, when that move raises its FPR by fpr_increase: a repaid loan earns repay_margin, a default loses default_loss (both USD).


Equation: Utility is TPR*base_rate*repay_margin-FPR*(1-base_rate)*default_loss; threshold changes add their corresponding expected-value differences.
Assumptions: The TPR target and added FPR are supplied jointly, with fixed base rates and monetary outcomes.
Excludes: Estimating an ROC frontier, downstream behavioral changes, and a policy judgment about the acceptability of the tradeoff.



Derivation: Utility is TPR*base_rate*repay_margin-FPR*(1-base_rate)*default_loss; threshold changes add their corresponding expected-value differences. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.

The mean of a public roster of group_size values in [0, value_range] released under epsilon-DP by one Laplace draw on the sum (replace-one adjacency).


Equation: Laplace scale equals sensitivity divided by epsilon; dividing that scale by roster size gives mean error.
Assumptions: A public fixed-size roster, bounded values, replace-one adjacency, and positive epsilon.
Excludes: Membership privacy of the roster and composition across repeated releases.

Individual property contracts identify the exact accounting expression or reusable calculation. Registry entries supply the scenario inputs; this class does not turn them into measured outcomes.

Cross-entropy losses for named predicted probabilities of the correct class, among classes.
misread gives the probabilities of a confident mistake, keyed "true" (the correct class) and "wrong" (the class predicted); the gradient on each score is its probability minus its target.


Equation: Correct-class loss is -ln(p); softmax-logit gradients are predicted probability minus one-hot target.

Equation: mass_flow = heat_load/(specific_heat * temperature_rise). Assumptions: steady single-phase flow, constant specific heat, and complete transfer of the stated heat load to the coolant. text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Three memories of workload as context grows on hardware: fixed weights, a KV cache linear in tokens, and one layer’s stored scores (all heads) quadratic in tokens.


Equation: Weights are fixed, full-request KV is linear in context, and one layer of scores grows quadratically.
Assumptions: All query heads materialize scores and the workload supplies its KV geometry.
Excludes: Other layers of scores in score_crossing, workspaces, and a combined residency feasibility test.



Derivation: Equate the constant weight footprint with linear KV storage to find their crossing. Equate device capacity with the quadratic score footprint for a score-only capacity crossing. Equating linear KV with quadratic scores and canceling one positive context factor gives the KV-score crossing.

Jobs of job_gpus GPUs packed on nodes nodes of gpus_per_node.

text:
Agents scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/agents.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A producer feeding a slower model consumer, unbounded or behind a credit window.
The consumer serves one item per tokens_per_item at its decode rate. With no bound the queue grows at the rate difference; a saturated window of W credits holds each item about W / mu by Little’s law.


Equation: Service rate is decode_rate/tokens_per_item; fluid backlog is (producer_rate-service_rate)*horizon; saturated window residence is credits/service_rate.
Assumptions: Rates and per-item work remain constant, the initial backlog is zero, and the growth calculation describes overload.
Excludes: Bursts, integer event scheduling, and a nonnegative queue clamp; underload produces a negative fluid backlog.



Derivation: Service rate is decode_rate/tokens_per_item; fluid backlog is (producer_rate-service_rate)*horizon; saturated window residence is credits/service_rate. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.

text:
Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/demonstrations.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
An observation paired with an action lag later, against a clearance, at a transit speed and at site’s guarded and fast latch approaches.


Equation: Alignment displacement=speed*lag; permissible lag=clearance/speed.
Assumptions: Constant speed during pairing or shutter delay and a scalar clearance budget.
Excludes: Acceleration, rotation, deformable contact, and a safety certificate.

title: GradientChainScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
The activation-slope factor a gradient keeps after depth layers, at each slope’s peak.


Equation: The activation-only gradient factor is max_sigmoid_slope**depth.
Assumptions: Every layer is evaluated at the sigmoid derivative maximum; weight Jacobians are treated separately.
Excludes: Weight-matrix amplification, residual paths, and actual training-gradient distributions.



Derivation: The chain rule multiplies activation derivatives across layers. The maximum sigmoid derivative is supplied by mlsysim.physics.neural.calc_sigmoid_slope at zero; raising it to depth isolates the activation-only factor without assigning values to the weight Jacobians.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.TwentySigmoidLayers
>>> s.variant(depth=s.depth+1).surviving_fraction <= s.surviving_fraction
True

depth

title: UtilizationGainScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A fleet of fleet_gpus raised from utilization_before to utilization_after.
The gain in fully active GPU-equivalents is N (u_after - u_before). Buying that capacity under the old policy would take gain / u_before raw GPUs, which is what the gain is worth. pools and pool_metrics optionally record the GPU pools and each pool’s measured shares.


Equation: productive gain = fleet size * utilization change; raw equivalent = productive gain / old utilization.
Assumptions: Utilization fractions refer to the same useful-work definition, and old utilization is positive.
Excludes: A measured causal effect of a policy, workload-mix changes, and procurement overhead.

engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.sequence
Context length used by the activation model. Equation: explicit seq_len when present, otherwise workload.context_length. Units: tokens per sequence.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.per_token_bytes_coefficient
Linear activation coefficient scaled to the requested element width. Equation: KORTHIKANTI_PER_TOKEN_BYTES * precision_bytes / 2. Units: bytes per hidden element; the reference coefficient is normalized to two-byte storage.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.score_bytes_coefficient
Attention-score coefficient expressed relative to the linear hidden-state term. Equation: KORTHIKANTI_SCORE_BYTES * heads * sequence / hidden_dim * precision_bytes / 2. Units: bytes per hidden element under the same activation accounting convention.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.score_share
Attention-score fraction of the unrecomputed activation estimate. Equation: score coefficient divided by the sum of linear and score coefficients. Units: dimensionless; all shared shape factors cancel.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.per_sequence_activations
Selective-recomputation activation footprint per sequence. Equation: per_token_activations / micro_batch. Units: GB; the property name refers to sequence allocation, not a single token.
Per-token activations of one sequence (scores not stored): the slope against batch size.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.segment_layers
Integer number of layers within each checkpoint segment. Equation: workload.layers // checkpoint_segments. Units: layers; leftover layers are not represented by this floor- division estimate.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.segment_input
One segment boundary’s retained hidden-state tensor. Equation: batch times sequence times hidden width times element bytes via _elements. Units: MB; other boundary state is excluded.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.segment_inputs
Retained inputs across all checkpoint segments. Equation: checkpoint_segments * segment_input. Units: GB; the same tensor shape is assumed at each boundary.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.live_segment
Linear activation footprint of the currently live segment. Equation: full linear footprint divided by model layers times segment layers. Units: GB; segments are treated as equal-sized.
One segment’s per-token activations, rebuilt in the backward pass (scores not stored).



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.checkpointed_activations
Boundary storage plus live-segment activations. Equation: segment_inputs + live_segment. Units: GB; runtime workspaces and uneven segment effects are excluded.
Segment inputs plus one live rebuilt segment (its input counted twice: conservative).



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.per_token_activations
Linear-in-sequence activation footprint with attention-score recomputation. Equation: activations('selective'). Units: GB; despite the name this is the whole microbatch, not per-token storage.
Activations that grow in proportion to sequence length (everything but the attention scores).



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.score_activations
Stored attention-score contribution removed by selective recomputation. Equation: activations('none') - activations('selective'). Units: GB; both branches use identical workload geometry.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.projection_activations_per_layer
Illustrative saved state for four hidden-width projection tensors. Equation: 4 * _elements(hidden_dim) * precision_bytes. Units: MB per layer; this line-item view is distinct from the aggregate coefficient model.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.ffn_activations_per_layer
Illustrative expanded feed-forward activation tensor. Equation: _elements(ffn_multiple * hidden_dim) * precision_bytes. Units: MB per layer; the supplied expansion factor sets the intermediate width.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.score_activations_per_layer
Average stored attention-score footprint per layer. Equation: score_activations / workload.layers. Units: MB; layers share the same geometry.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.line_items_per_layer
Sum of the explicit projection, feed-forward, score, and optional normalization tensors. Equation: add these line items, using zero for unspecified normalization. Units: MB per layer; this is not forced to equal the separate aggregate coefficient estimate.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.line_items_total
Explicit line-item footprint across the model. Equation: line_items_per_layer * workload.layers. Units: GB; identical layer shapes are assumed.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.forward_equivalents
Training arithmetic expressed in forward-pass work units. Equation: calc_transformer_training_flops(P, 1) / calc_transformer_decode_flops(P, 1). Units: dimensionless; parameter-dominated accounting omits context attention.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.recompute_forward_equivalents
Full-recomputation training arithmetic in forward-pass work units. Equation: forward_equivalents * (1 + recompute_overhead). Units: dimensionless; the extra work is a recomputed forward pass.



engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.recompute_overhead
Relative arithmetic increase from full activation recomputation. Equation: checkpointed training FLOPs divided by baseline training FLOPs, minus one. Units: dimensionless; this is a work ratio, not measured runtime overhead.

title: ActivationMemoryScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.forward_equivalents
Training arithmetic expressed in forward-pass work units. Equation: calc_transformer_training_flops(P, 1) / calc_transformer_decode_flops(P, 1). Units: dimensionless; parameter-dominated accounting omits context attention.

title: ActivationMemoryScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.recompute_forward_equivalents
Full-recomputation training arithmetic in forward-pass work units. Equation: forward_equivalents * (1 + recompute_overhead). Units: dimensionless; the extra work is a recomputed forward pass.

title: ActivationMemoryScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.ActivationMemoryScenario.recompute_overhead
Relative arithmetic increase from full activation recomputation. Equation: checkpointed training FLOPs divided by baseline training FLOPs, minus one. Units: dimensionless; this is a work ratio, not measured runtime overhead.

title: solvers.TransformationModel
text:
solvers.TransformationModel()
Quantifies the CPU preprocessing bottleneck (Wall 9: Transformation).
This model simulates the ‘Transformation Wall’ — the gap between CPU-bound data preprocessing (JPEG decode, tokenization, augmentation) and accelerator step time. When preprocessing cannot keep up, the accelerator starves and utilization drops.
Literature Source: 1. Mohan et al. (2022), “Analyzing and Mitigating Data Bottlenecks in Deep Learning Training.” 2. Murray et al. (2021), “tf.data: A Machine Learning Data Processing Framework.” (Pipeline stall analysis.) 3. NVIDIA DALI Documentation (2024). (GPU-accelerated preprocessing.)





Name
Description




solve
Compare batch preprocessing time with accelerator step time.





solvers.TransformationModel.solve(
    batch_size,
    sample_size_bytes,
    cpu_throughput,
    accelerator_step_time,
)
Compare batch preprocessing time with accelerator step time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_size
int
Positive number of samples in one batch.
required


sample_size_bytes
Quantity
Nonnegative encoded or transformed byte size per sample, as appropriate for the supplied CPU throughput measurement.
required


cpu_throughput
Quantity
Positive aggregate preprocessing throughput, convertible to byte/s.
required


accelerator_step_time
Quantity
Positive time for the accelerator to process that same batch.
required














Name
Type
Description





TransformationResult
Preprocessing and accelerator times in ms, bottleneck flag, dimensionless utilization, and slowdown relative to the accelerator alone.






Equation: T_cpu = batch_size * sample_size_bytes / cpu_throughput; T_step = max(T_cpu, T_accelerator), utilization = T_accelerator/T_step.
Assumptions: steady-state prefetch perfectly overlaps the CPU and accelerator stages; CPU throughput is already aggregate across its workers.
Excludes: pipeline fill/drain, transfer latency, storage stalls, and contention. The maximum describes overlap, not serial execution.



Derivation: byte volume divided by byte rate gives stage service time; the slower of two fully overlapped stages determines steady-state cadence.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = TransformationModel().solve(2, Q_("1 MB"), Q_("1 MB/s"), Q_("1 s"))
>>> result.accelerator_utilization == 0.5
True

Derivation: byte volume divided by byte rate gives stage service time; the slower of two fully overlapped stages determines steady-state cadence.

>>> result = TransformationModel().solve(2, Q_("1 MB"), Q_("1 MB/s"), Q_("1 s"))
>>> result.accelerator_utilization == 0.5
True
