title: engine.solvers.goodput
text:
engine.solvers.goodput
Fleet goodput solvers: ML productivity goodput and runtime goodput.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). Added 2026-10-20.





Name
Description




GoodputModel
ML productivity goodput: the share of offered capacity-time that becomes


RuntimeGoodputModel
Runtime goodput of one job: the share of its held time spent on retained steps.





engine.solvers.goodput.GoodputModel()
ML productivity goodput: the share of offered capacity-time that becomes ideal-rate work, MPG = S x R x P.
Scheduling goodput S is held over offered capacity-time, runtime goodput R retained over held time, and program goodput P ideal over retained time. Each factor divides by what the previous one passed, so the factors multiply and every lost interval is charged once, at the first boundary it fails: 1 = (1 - S) + S(1 - R) + SR(1 - P) + SRP. One point of a factor is worth the product of the other two, and a lever that lifts a factor to its ceiling multiplies MPG by the ceiling’s ratio. A useful accelerator-hour costs the offered rate divided by MPG.
Literature Source: 1. Wongpanich et al. (2025), “Machine Learning Fleet Efficiency: Analyzing and Optimizing Large-Scale Google TPU Systems with ML Productivity Goodput.”





Name
Description




solve
Partition offered capacity-time into retained work and stage losses.





engine.solvers.goodput.GoodputModel.solve(
    scheduling,
    runtime,
    program,
    ceilings=None,
    device_hour_rate=None,
)
Partition offered capacity-time into retained work and stage losses.











Name
Type
Description
Default




scheduling
float
Scheduling fraction S in (0, 1], measured over offered capacity-time.
required


runtime
float
Runtime fraction R in (0, 1], measured over scheduled capacity-time.
required


program
float
Program fraction P in (0, 1], measured over retained runtime.
required


ceilings
dict of str to float
Proposed fractions in (0, 1] keyed by S, R, or P; each change is evaluated alone with the other factors held fixed.
None


device_hour_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative price per offered device-hour, convertible to USD/hour.
None














Name
Type
Description





GoodputResult
Dimensionless goodput, disjoint loss shares, factor sensitivities, and one-factor ceiling gains. useful_rate is USD/hour of useful work, or None when no price is supplied.






Equation: MPG = S*R*P; losses are 1-S, S*(1-R), and S*R*(1-P). A factor’s marginal point value is the product of the other two factors; useful_rate = device_hour_rate / MPG.
Assumptions: factors have consecutive nested denominators. Positive factors are required because costs and relative gains divide by them.
Excludes: correlated responses to simultaneous interventions, capital costs, and forecasts of attainable ceilings. Inputs are supplied fractions.



Derivation: expand 1 = (1-S) + S*(1-R) + S*R*(1-P) + S*R*P; the partition charges each lost interval only at its first failed boundary.



>>> result = GoodputModel().solve(0.5, 0.5, 1.0)
>>> result.mpg == 0.25
True
>>> result.scheduling_share + result.runtime_share + result.program_share + result.mpg == 1
True






engine.solvers.goodput.RuntimeGoodputModel()
Runtime goodput of one job: the share of its held time spent on retained steps.
The loss is the sum of five owners’ terms on one denominator, held time (first order; each term is small):

startup: restart, checkpoint load, and warmup once per held window;
input waits: complete allocations stalled on the input pipeline;
checkpoint waste at the Young-Daly interval, write share plus rework;
recovery: the four-term cold-restart budget over the failure interval (rework is already counted in the checkpoint term);
forced preemption: rate times (work since the last save + startup).

Reuses CheckpointIntervalModel for the checkpoint term and the recovery profile’s cold_restart_time for recovery, startup, and the preemption relaunch (the same source as RecoveryBudgetModel and PreemptionTaxModel).
Literature Source: 1. Young (1974); Daly (2006), optimal checkpoint interval. 2. Wongpanich et al. (2025), runtime goodput.





Name
Description




solve
Account for first-order runtime losses on one held-time denominator.





engine.solvers.goodput.RuntimeGoodputModel.solve(
    mtbf,
    checkpoint_bytes,
    recovery,
    input_wait,
    window,
    lost_work,
    preemption_rate,
)
Account for first-order runtime losses on one held-time denominator.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mtbf
Quantity
Positive mean time between job failures, convertible to hours.
required


checkpoint_bytes
Quantity
Nonnegative bytes written and reloaded per checkpoint.
required


recovery
object
Recovery profile with positive checkpoint_write_bw_gbs and a cold_restart_time method returning time, including optional detection.
required


input_wait
float
Fraction of held time lost to input stalls, between zero and one.
required


window
Quantity
Positive held-time window over which one startup is amortized.
required


lost_work
Quantity
Nonnegative work duration discarded by each forced preemption.
required


preemption_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative forced-preemption frequency, convertible to inverse hours.
required














Name
Type
Description





RuntimeGoodputResult
Checkpoint and recovery time budgets, dimensionless loss shares, and runtime_goodput = 1 - summed losses. The value is not clipped; a negative result signals that the small-loss approximation is outside its regime.






mlsysim.engine.solvers.reliability.CheckpointIntervalModel.solve : Checkpoint waste accounting.



Equation: loss = startup/window + input_wait + checkpoint_waste + recovery_time/mtbf + preemption_rate*(lost_work + startup). The effective interruption interval is 1/(1/mtbf + preemption_rate).
Assumptions: terms are small, disjoint first-order charges. The checkpoint term includes failure rework; the recovery term excludes that rework. Startup excludes failure detection for a scheduler-initiated restart.
Excludes: overlapping outages, correlated preemptions, recovery queueing, and dynamic checkpoint adaptation. The interruption checkpoint interval is reported separately rather than substituted into the primary loss budget.



Derivation: amortize each event duration over its observation window or multiply it by its event frequency, then sum losses on held time. The checkpoint submodel supplies its separately documented interval rule.



>>> from mlsysim import Systems, Q_
>>> result = RuntimeGoodputModel().solve(Q_("100 hour"), Q_("1 GB"),
...     Systems.Reliability.Recovery, 0.0, Q_("24 hour"), Q_("0 s"), Q_("0 / hour"))
>>> result.preemption_share == 0
True
>>> result.runtime_goodput == 1 - result.runtime_loss
True

title: engine.solvers.curation
text:
engine.solvers.curation
Trajectory curation solvers: what a recorded corpus may teach, and what collecting it costs.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on stated counts, rates, and service times: failures that counterfactual probes attribute to the system, and the price of training on all of them anyway; how often a random split of runs places one task on both sides; the expected checking time of an admission route run in different orders; one record class’s share of a pool under three denominators; and how fast a verifier timeout burst fills reserved staging.





Name
Description




AdmissionOrderModel
One admission route’s independent checks run in different orders, each stopping at its first failure.


CorpusDenominatorsModel
One record class’s share of a retained pool counted three ways: records, stored tokens, selected targets.


FailureTriageModel
Failures that counterfactual probes remove below the weights, and the price of training on all of them.


RunSplitLeakageModel
Tasks whose runs a random split of runs places on both sides of the partition.


StagingBurstModel
Reserved staging under a verifier timeout burst, with every record charged at its ceiling.





engine.solvers.curation.AdmissionOrderModel()
One admission route’s independent checks run in different orders, each stopping at its first failure.
Every order admits the same records (the route yield is the product of the pass rates); the expected slot time per attempted record differs. Time per admitted record divides by the yield. The saving compares the cheapest order with the dearest.





Name
Description




solve
Compare expected checking time for short-circuit admission orders.

    checks,
    orders,
    candidates=None,
)

required

required

int

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Wald’s SPRT between an unacceptable failure rate p_unacceptable and an acceptable one p_acceptable at error rates alpha and beta; the score after trace_clean_runs clean runs and one failure; and the fixed zero-failure test for success 1 - p_unacceptable at the same alpha.


Equation: Success and failure log-likelihood increments accumulate until a Wald boundary is crossed.
Assumptions: Independent Bernoulli outcomes under the two fixed hypotheses and the specified SPRT error budgets.
Excludes: Changing hypotheses, dependent outcomes, and a guaranteed stopping-time distribution.



Derivation: Success and failure log-likelihood increments accumulate until a Wald boundary is crossed. Individual property contracts identify the exact accounting expression or reusable calculation. Registry entries supply the scenario inputs; this class does not turn them into measured outcomes.



Evaluate a named scenario using its declared inputs.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.LatchSequentialTest
>>> round(float(scenario.success_increment), 4)
0.0953






Name
Description




accept
Upper log-likelihood boundary for accepting the lower-failure hypothesis.


alpha



beta



failure_increment
Log-likelihood increment after a failed trial under the same two Bernoulli hypotheses.


false_accept_bound
Nominal exponential false-accept bound implied by the upper boundary.


false_reject_bound
Nominal exponential false-reject bound implied by the lower boundary.


fixed_rejects_acceptable
Probability the fixed zero-failure rule sees at least one failure under the acceptable

Zero-failure fixed-sample trial count for the unacceptable-rate ceiling at confidence


p_acceptable



p_unacceptable

Lower log-likelihood boundary for rejecting the lower-failure hypothesis.


runs_to_accept
Ceiling number of consecutive successful trials needed to reach the acceptance boundary

Log-likelihood increment after a successful trial, from calc_sprt_increments.


trace_clean_runs

Log-likelihood score of the illustrative trace: declared successful trials plus one

engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.success_increment
Log-likelihood increment after a successful trial, from calc_sprt_increments.
Equation: calc_sprt_increments(p_unacceptable, p_acceptable)[0].



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.failure_increment
Log-likelihood increment after a failed trial under the same two Bernoulli hypotheses.
Equation: calc_sprt_increments(p_unacceptable, p_acceptable)[1].



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.accept
Upper log-likelihood boundary for accepting the lower-failure hypothesis.
Equation: calc_sprt_boundaries(alpha, beta)[0].



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.reject
Lower log-likelihood boundary for rejecting the lower-failure hypothesis.
Equation: calc_sprt_boundaries(alpha, beta)[1].



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.runs_to_accept
Ceiling number of consecutive successful trials needed to reach the acceptance boundary from zero.
Equation: _math.ceil(accept / success_increment).



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.false_accept_bound
Nominal exponential false-accept bound implied by the upper boundary.
Ville’s inequality: e^-A = alpha / (1 - beta).
Equation: _math.exp(-accept).



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.false_reject_bound
Nominal exponential false-reject bound implied by the lower boundary.
Equation: _math.exp(reject).



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.trace_score
Log-likelihood score of the illustrative trace: declared successful trials plus one failure.
Equation: trace_clean_runs * success_increment + failure_increment.



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.fixed_runs
Zero-failure fixed-sample trial count for the unacceptable-rate ceiling at confidence one minus alpha.
Equation: calc_zero_failure_sample_size(1.0 - p_unacceptable, 1.0 - alpha).



engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.fixed_rejects_acceptable
Probability the fixed zero-failure rule sees at least one failure under the acceptable rate.
Chance that a policy at the acceptable rate fails the fixed zero-failure test.
Equation: 1.0 - (1.0 - p_acceptable) ** fixed_runs.

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.runs_to_accept
Ceiling number of consecutive successful trials needed to reach the acceptance boundary from zero.
Equation: _math.ceil(accept / success_increment).

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.false_accept_bound
Nominal exponential false-accept bound implied by the upper boundary.
Ville’s inequality: e^-A = alpha / (1 - beta).
Equation: _math.exp(-accept).

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.false_reject_bound
Nominal exponential false-reject bound implied by the lower boundary.
Equation: _math.exp(reject).

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.trace_score
Log-likelihood score of the illustrative trace: declared successful trials plus one failure.

title: SequentialTestScenario
text:
engine.scenario_types.SequentialTestScenario.fixed_runs
Zero-failure fixed-sample trial count for the unacceptable-rate ceiling at confidence one minus alpha.
Equation: calc_zero_failure_sample_size(1.0 - p_unacceptable, 1.0 - alpha).

title: SequentialTestScenario

Probability the fixed zero-failure rule sees at least one failure under the acceptable rate.
Chance that a policy at the acceptable rate fails the fixed zero-failure test.
Equation: 1.0 - (1.0 - p_acceptable) ** fixed_runs.

title: engine.solvers.collective
text:
engine.solvers.collective
Collective-communication solvers: AllReduce schedules, hierarchy, AllToAll dispatch, gradient compression, and overlap with the backward pass.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable. Every model is an alpha-beta bound: a startup alpha per round or message plus bytes over a stated bandwidth beta, with contention, protocol overhead, and the reduction arithmetic left out.





Name
Description




AllReduceAlgorithmModel
Ring, simple-tree, and parameter-server (star) AllReduce of one buffer at several group sizes.


AllToAllDispatchModel
One mixture-of-experts dispatch AllToAll under uniform routing, and one hot receiver.


CompressionRunModel
Time to a quality target with and without gradient compression, per network.


ErrorFeedbackModel
A compressor that sends each value rounded to a whole unit, with error feedback.


HierarchicalAllReduceModel
Three-phase hierarchical AllReduce against one flat ring across every GPU.


OverlapBudgetModel
Layer-by-layer gradient AllReduce, run after the backward pass or overlapped with it.


RingTraceModel
Every step of a ring AllReduce on one small vector per GPU, the vectors split into N chunks.





engine.solvers.collective.AllReduceAlgorithmModel()
Ring, simple-tree, and parameter-server (star) AllReduce of one buffer at several group sizes.
A ring takes 2(N-1) rounds, each paying one startup alpha and moving one chunk of M/N bytes, so each rank sends 2(N-1)/N times the buffer. The simple tree reduces up and broadcasts down in 2 log2 N rounds, forwarding the whole buffer each round. A single parameter server receives and sends N buffers through one port. The crossover is the buffer at which ring and tree cost the same: the log-aware estimate N alpha beta / log2 N and the exact intersection of the two models.
Literature Source: 1. Patarasuk and Yuan (2009), bandwidth-optimal ring AllReduce. 2. Thakur, Rabenseifner, and Gropp (2005), tree and ring collectives.





Name
Description




solve
Compare ring, tree, and star transfer bounds.





engine.solvers.collective.AllReduceAlgorithmModel.solve(
    message,
    group_sizes,
    alpha,
    bandwidth,
)
Compare ring, tree, and star transfer bounds.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Nonnegative buffer size as a byte-compatible quantity.
required


group_sizes
Sequence[int]
Integer rank counts, each at least two.
required


alpha
Quantity
Nonnegative startup latency per round as a time quantity.
required


bandwidth
Quantity
Positive per-port transfer rate in bytes per second.
required














Name
Type
Description





AllReduceAlgorithmResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: T_ring = 2(N-1) alpha + 2(N-1)M/(N bandwidth); tree uses twice the ceiling of log2(N) rounds.
Assumptions: Equal chunks and serialized startup-plus-transfer costs.
Excludes: Contention, reduction arithmetic, and protocol overhead.



Derivation: T_ring = 2(N-1) alpha + 2(N-1)M/(N bandwidth); tree uses twice the ceiling of log2(N) rounds. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = AllReduceAlgorithmModel().solve(Q_('1 MB'), [2, 4], Q_('1 us'), Q_('1 GB/s'))
>>> r.ring_time[4] > r.ring_startup_time[4]
True






engine.solvers.collective.AllToAllDispatchModel()
One mixture-of-experts dispatch AllToAll under uniform routing, and one hot receiver.
Each device holds tokens / N tokens and sends an equal share to every device, keeping its own; a token is hidden_dim values. The concurrent peer streams share one injection port, so dispatch takes at least alpha + sent / beta. On the receive side the bound is the receiving port: a device whose experts draw skew times the uniform remote load takes skew times longer, and every device waiting on its outputs waits with it.

engine.solvers.collective.ErrorFeedbackModel()
A compressor that sends each value rounded to a whole unit, with error feedback.
Without a residual, every value below half a unit is lost. With error feedback the worker adds the carried residual e_t to the gradient, sends the rounded v_t, and keeps e_{t+1} = g_t + e_t - v_t; what is sent plus the last residual equals the true sum at every step.
Literature Source: Karimireddy et al. (2019), “Error Feedback Fixes SignSGD”.





Name
Description




solve
Track rounding residuals across gradient transmissions.





engine.solvers.collective.ErrorFeedbackModel.solve(gradients)
Track rounding residuals across gradient transmissions.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gradients
Sequence[float]
Scalar gradient sequence in consistent arbitrary units.
required














Name
Type
Description





ErrorFeedbackResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: v_t = round(g_t + e_t); e_(t+1) = g_t + e_t - v_t.
Assumptions: Scalar whole-unit compressor with ties rounded away from zero.
Excludes: Optimizer convergence and vector compression costs.



Derivation: v_t = round(g_t + e_t); e_(t+1) = g_t + e_t - v_t. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = ErrorFeedbackModel().solve([0.25, 0.25])
>>> r.total_sent + r.final_error == r.true_total
True






engine.solvers.collective.HierarchicalAllReduceModel()
Three-phase hierarchical AllReduce against one flat ring across every GPU.
Inside each node of G GPUs a ReduceScatter over the fast link leaves each GPU 1/G of the node’s partial sum, sending (G-1)/G of the buffer. GPUs in the same position on every node then ring-AllReduce their M/G shard across nodes, one ring per GPU position, each on its own port; an AllGather inside the node rebuilds the sum. The in-node phases carry no startup term here. The flat ring runs at the slowest edge, the inter-node port; flat_bound_time is its large-N byte bound 2M/beta.
Literature Source: Sergeev and Del Balso (2018); NCCL hierarchical rings.





Name
Description




solve
Compare hierarchical and flat AllReduce bounds.

)

HierarchicalAllReduceResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: T = 2 M(G-1)/(G intra_bandwidth) + T_ring(M/G, nodes, inter_bandwidth, inter_alpha).
Assumptions: Independent inter-node ports per GPU position and no intra-node startup.
Excludes: Shared-port contention and reduction arithmetic.



Derivation: T = 2 M(G-1)/(G intra_bandwidth) + T_ring(M/G, nodes, inter_bandwidth, inter_alpha). The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = HierarchicalAllReduceModel().solve(Q_('1 MB'), 2, 2, Q_('10 GB/s'), Q_('1 GB/s'), Q_('1 us'))
>>> r.total_time > r.inter_time
True






engine.solvers.collective.OverlapBudgetModel()
Layer-by-layer gradient AllReduce, run after the backward pass or overlapped with it.
Each of L equal layers yields its gradient, reduced in fixed-size buckets that each take time_per_bucket. Sequentially, the step pays the whole backward pass and then every reduction. Overlapped, a layer’s reduction starts when its backward finishes; when a reduction outlasts the next layer’s backward, the excess accumulates, and the last reduction has no compute left to hide under.





Name
Description




solve
Account for layerwise reduction overlap.





engine.solvers.collective.OverlapBudgetModel.solve(
    workload,
    bytes_per_value,
    backward_per_layer,
    bucket_size,
    time_per_bucket,
)
Account for layerwise reduction overlap.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workload
Workload
Layered workload with positive layer count and weight-size conversion.
required


bytes_per_value
Quantity
Gradient storage per element as a byte quantity.
required


backward_per_layer
Quantity
Nonnegative backward duration of each equal layer.
required


bucket_size
Quantity
Positive gradient bucket size as a byte quantity.
required


time_per_bucket
Quantity
Nonnegative reduction duration per bucket.
required














Name
Type
Description





OverlapBudgetResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: T_overlap = L b + c + (L-1) max(0,c-b), where c is rounded-up bucket count times bucket duration.
Assumptions: Equal layers and serialized communication with backward/reduction overlap.
Excludes: Variable layer sizes and transport contention.



Derivation: T_overlap = L b + c + (L-1) max(0,c-b), where c is rounded-up bucket count times bucket duration. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> r = OverlapBudgetModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Q_('2 byte'), Q_('1 ms'), Q_('1 GB'), Q_('1 ms'))
>>> r.overlapped_time <= r.sequential_time
True






engine.solvers.collective.RingTraceModel()
Every step of a ring AllReduce on one small vector per GPU, the vectors split into N chunks.
In ReduceScatter step s, GPU i sends chunk (i - s) mod N to GPU i + 1, which adds it into its own copy; after N - 1 steps GPU i owns the fully reduced chunk (i + 1) mod N. In AllGather step s (from 1), GPU i forwards chunk (i - s + 2) mod N, the one it completed or received most recently, so after N - 1 more steps every GPU holds every chunk.





Name
Description




solve
Trace integer reduction and gathering around a ring.





engine.solvers.collective.RingTraceModel.solve(vectors)
Trace integer reduction and gathering around a ring.











Name
Type
Description
Default




vectors
Sequence[Sequence[int]]
Square sequence of integer vectors, one vector and one chunk per rank.
required














Name
Type
Description





RingTraceResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: Each of N-1 scatter steps adds the received chunk; N-1 gather steps disseminate completed sums.
Assumptions: Square input vectors with one scalar chunk per rank.
Excludes: Transfer time, floating-point reduction order, and failures.



Derivation: Each of N-1 scatter steps adds the received chunk; N-1 gather steps disseminate completed sums. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RingTraceModel().solve([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
>>> r.totals == [sum(x) for x in zip([1, 2], [3, 4])]
True

Each of L equal layers yields its gradient, reduced in fixed-size buckets that each take time_per_bucket. Sequentially, the step pays the whole backward pass and then every reduction. Overlapped, a layer’s reduction starts when its backward finishes; when a reduction outlasts the next layer’s backward, the excess accumulates, and the last reduction has no compute left to hide under.





Name
Description




solve
Account for layerwise reduction overlap.





engine.solvers.collective.OverlapBudgetModel.solve(
    workload,
    bytes_per_value,
    backward_per_layer,
    bucket_size,
    time_per_bucket,
)
Account for layerwise reduction overlap.











Name
Type
Description
Default




workload
Workload
Layered workload with positive layer count and weight-size conversion.
required


bytes_per_value
Quantity
Gradient storage per element as a byte quantity.
required


backward_per_layer
Quantity
Nonnegative backward duration of each equal layer.
required


bucket_size
Quantity
Positive gradient bucket size as a byte quantity.
required


time_per_bucket
Quantity
Nonnegative reduction duration per bucket.
required














Name
Type
Description





OverlapBudgetResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: T_overlap = L b + c + (L-1) max(0,c-b), where c is rounded-up bucket count times bucket duration.
Assumptions: Equal layers and serialized communication with backward/reduction overlap.
Excludes: Variable layer sizes and transport contention.



Derivation: T_overlap = L b + c + (L-1) max(0,c-b), where c is rounded-up bucket count times bucket duration. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> from mlsysim import Models
>>> r = OverlapBudgetModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Q_('2 byte'), Q_('1 ms'), Q_('1 GB'), Q_('1 ms'))
>>> r.overlapped_time <= r.sequential_time
True






engine.solvers.collective.RingTraceModel()
Every step of a ring AllReduce on one small vector per GPU, the vectors split into N chunks.
In ReduceScatter step s, GPU i sends chunk (i - s) mod N to GPU i + 1, which adds it into its own copy; after N - 1 steps GPU i owns the fully reduced chunk (i + 1) mod N. In AllGather step s (from 1), GPU i forwards chunk (i - s + 2) mod N, the one it completed or received most recently, so after N - 1 more steps every GPU holds every chunk.





Name
Description




solve
Trace integer reduction and gathering around a ring.





engine.solvers.collective.RingTraceModel.solve(vectors)
Trace integer reduction and gathering around a ring.











Name
Type
Description
Default




vectors
Sequence[Sequence[int]]
Square sequence of integer vectors, one vector and one chunk per rank.
required














Name
Type
Description





RingTraceResult
Modeled accounting components with unit-bearing sizes and times; ratios are dimensionless. These components do not certify deployment feasibility.






Equation: Each of N-1 scatter steps adds the received chunk; N-1 gather steps disseminate completed sums.
Assumptions: Square input vectors with one scalar chunk per rank.
Excludes: Transfer time, floating-point reduction order, and failures.



Derivation: Each of N-1 scatter steps adds the received chunk; N-1 gather steps disseminate completed sums. The class documentation describes the accounting sequence and its modeling context.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = RingTraceModel().solve([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
>>> r.totals == [sum(x) for x in zip([1, 2], [3, 4])]
True

title: engine.solvers.fine_tuning
text:
engine.solvers.fine_tuning
Fine-tuning solvers: what a serialized trajectory teaches, and what the update costs.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on stated counts: one serialized example’s positions under a target mask, one example per model call against one transcript, recorded transcripts split by role, a long trajectory’s weight under token and example averaging, padding against packing, one preference pair under the DPO loss, a distilled per-turn prefix against its bill, and a candidate policy’s release comparison. None models a trained network’s learning dynamics.





Name
Description




LossNormalizationModel
One long trajectory’s weight in a batch under token and example averaging.


PerInvocationSerializationModel
One training example per model call against one stored transcript.


PreferencePairModel
One preference pair under the DPO loss, against its value at a zero margin.


SequencePackingModel
Variable-length examples padded to the longest against packed into fixed buffers.


TargetMaskModel
One serialized example’s positions under two target masks.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.LossNormalizationModel()
One long trajectory’s weight in a batch under token and example averaging.
The batch holds the trajectory, split into focus_pieces records that each select every turn’s response once, and other_examples examples of other_targets selected targets each. Token averaging weights each example by its target count, so splitting changes nothing; example averaging weights each record once, so the trajectory’s share rises from 1/B to k/(B - 1 + k).





Name
Description




solve
Compare target-token weighting with equal-record weighting.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.LossNormalizationModel.solve(
    focus_targets,
    other_examples,
    other_targets,
    focus_pieces=1,
)
Compare target-token weighting with equal-record weighting.











Name
Type
Description
Default




focus_targets
int
Positive selected-target count of the focus trajectory.
required


other_examples
int
Positive count of other records.
required


other_targets
int
Positive target count in each other record.
required


focus_pieces
int
Positive number of focus records after splitting; default one.
1














Name
Type
Description





LossNormalizationResult
Counts and dimensionless weighting shares.






Equation: focus_token_share = focus_targets / (focus_targets + other_examples * other_targets); focus_example_share = focus_pieces / (focus_pieces + other_examples).
Assumptions: Splitting preserves all focus targets; other records have equal target counts.
Excludes: Gradient magnitudes, optimization dynamics, and changes in training quality.



Derivation: Token averaging normalizes by target counts; equal-record averaging normalizes by the count of records.



>>> LossNormalizationModel().solve(20, 2, 10).focus_token_share
0.5






engine.solvers.fine_tuning.PerInvocationSerializationModel()
One training example per model call against one stored transcript.
When each of H turns adds about a tokens, call t carries t a tokens, so separate examples store a H (H + 1) / 2 tokens against a H for one transcript: the append-only resend triangle (calc_append_only_context with s0 = delta = a), an expansion of (H + 1) / 2.





Name
Description




solve
Compare repeated call prefixes with one stored transcript.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.PerInvocationSerializationModel.solve(
    turns,
    tokens_per_turn,
)
Compare repeated call prefixes with one stored transcript.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Positive number of turns.
required


tokens_per_turn
int
Positive number of tokens appended per turn.
required














Name
Type
Description





PerInvocationSerializationResult
Token counts and a dimensionless storage expansion.






Equation: transcript = a H; per_invocation = a H (H + 1) / 2.
Assumptions: Every turn appends the same a tokens and stores its full prefix.
Excludes: Compression, deduplication, tokenization, and model execution.



Derivation: Summing prefix lengths a, 2a, …, Ha yields the arithmetic-series total.



>>> PerInvocationSerializationModel().solve(3, 10).expansion
2.0






engine.solvers.fine_tuning.PreferencePairModel()
One preference pair under the DPO loss, against its value at a zero margin.
At initialization the policy equals the reference, so both scores are zero, the loss is ln 2, the saturation factor is 1/2, and the coefficient is beta / 2. The logistic score depends on beta, so it measures fit to this comparison, not a success probability.





Name
Description




solve
Evaluate one DPO preference margin and logistic loss.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.PreferencePairModel.solve(
    policy_preferred,
    reference_preferred,
    policy_dispreferred,
    reference_dispreferred,
    beta,
)
Evaluate one DPO preference margin and logistic loss.











Name
Type
Description
Default




policy_preferred
float
Log probability of the preferred response under the policy, dimensionless.
required


reference_preferred
float
Log probability of the preferred response under the reference, dimensionless.
required


policy_dispreferred
float
Log probability of the dispreferred response under the policy, dimensionless.
required


reference_dispreferred
float
Log probability of the dispreferred response under the reference, dimensionless.
required


beta
float
Positive dimensionless scale of the policy/reference log-ratio margin.
required














Name
Type
Description





PreferencePairResult
Dimensionless margin, logistic score, loss, saturation, and gradient coefficient.






Equation: margin = beta * ((policy_preferred - reference_preferred) - (policy_dispreferred - reference_dispreferred)); loss = -log(sigmoid(margin)).
Assumptions: The supplied log probabilities describe one preferred/dispreferred pair; initialization has zero log-ratio margin.
Excludes: Sequence generation, empirical success probability, and training dynamics.



Derivation: The negative log-sigmoid gives pairwise logistic loss; differentiating the margin yields the saturation factor and beta-scaled coefficient. This wrapper delegates the calculation to calc_preference_pair.



>>> PreferencePairModel().solve(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.2).preference_score
0.5






engine.solvers.fine_tuning.SequencePackingModel()
Variable-length examples padded to the longest against packed into fixed buffers.
Padding allocates N rows of the longest length, so occupancy is the mean length over the maximum. Packing places examples longest first into the first capacity-token buffer with room (first-fit decreasing). Occupancy counts context and targets alike; it is not measured throughput.





Name
Description




solve
Compare padding with first-fit-decreasing sequence packing.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.SequencePackingModel.solve(lengths, capacity)
Compare padding with first-fit-decreasing sequence packing.











Name
Type
Description
Default




lengths
sequence of int
Nonempty sequence of positive token counts, each no larger than capacity.
required


capacity
int
Positive token capacity of each packing buffer.
required














Name
Type
Description





SequencePackingResult
Token-position counts, buffer loads, and dimensionless occupancies.






Equation: padded = N * max(lengths); packed = number_of_buffers * capacity; occupancy = sum(lengths) / allocated_positions.
Assumptions: Examples remain whole; first-fit decreasing determines the buffer placement.
Excludes: Attention masking costs, runtime throughput, and optimal bin packing.



Derivation: Allocated positions count rectangular padding or fixed buffers; occupancy is occupied divided by allocated positions.



>>> SequencePackingModel().solve([2, 2], 4).packed_occupancy
1.0






engine.solvers.fine_tuning.TargetMaskModel()
One serialized example’s positions under two target masks.
The example stores a prompt, a task, an optional rationale, the policy’s responses, and the observations. Targets are the responses minus the unselected ones (kept as context), with or without the rationale. The first stored position has no preceding position, so an unmasked token average divides by stored - 1 prediction terms; each target’s weight shrinks by (stored - 1) / targets.





Name
Description




solve
Count stored context and selected prediction targets.





engine.solvers.fine_tuning.TargetMaskModel.solve(
    prompt,
    task,
    rationale,
    response,
    observation,
    unselected_response,
)
Count stored context and selected prediction targets.











Name
Type
Description
Default




prompt
int
Prompt token count, nonnegative.
required


task
int
Task-description token count, nonnegative.
required


rationale
int
Rationale token count, nonnegative.
required


response
int
Response token count, positive.
required


observation
int
Observation token count, nonnegative.
required


unselected_response
int
Response tokens retained as context; from zero to response minus one.
required














Name
Type
Description





TargetMaskResult
Token counts and dimensionless target shares and dilution ratios.






Equation: stored = prompt + task + rationale + response + observation; selected = response - unselected_response; predicted = stored - 1.
Assumptions: Counts refer to a single serialized sequence; the first position has no preceding predictor.
Excludes: Tokenizer behavior, model quality, and loss values.



Derivation: Subtracting excluded responses counts targets; dividing by stored positions or prediction terms gives the reported shares and dilution.



>>> TargetMaskModel().solve(2, 1, 1, 4, 2, 1).selected_response
3

text:
engine.scenarios.Scenario()
Concrete executable case: a workload on a system with constraints.
application names the product/domain context, while the scenario itself is what the simulator can evaluate. Model facts stay in Models.*; hardware and fleet facts stay in Hardware.* / Systems.*.





Name
Description




is_distributed
Identify whether the scenario supplies a fleet object.









Name
Description




evaluate
Compose feasibility, performance, and annual accounting summaries.


validate
Raise when the scenario’s implemented feasibility or latency check fails.





engine.scenarios.Scenario.evaluate(batch_size=1, precision='fp16')
Compose feasibility, performance, and annual accounting summaries.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_size
int
Positive batch count forwarded to the selected performance solver. Its work unit follows that solver: samples for generic single-node inference and the distributed solver’s default training convention.
1


precision
str
Registered weight format used for weight size and performance.
'fp16'














Name
Type
Description





SystemEvaluation
Three levels containing status, explanation, and metrics: weight/data feasibility, latency/SLA performance, and annual carbon/TCO estimates. Results include quantities with units; carbon_kg and tco_usd are scalars in kilograms and USD. A FAIL level does not stop later calculations.






Equation: feasible = (weight_bytes <= one_accelerator_capacity) and not data_stalled. Performance passes when no latency SLA is supplied or modeled_latency <= sla_latency. Macro metrics come from EconomicsModel with duration_days=365 and its other default assumptions.
Assumptions: a Fleet uses DistributedModel; a HardwareNode uses SingleNodeModel. The initial memory check is weights on one accelerator, even for a Fleet. The single-node accounting branch constructs a one-node fleet with an Ethernet_10G fabric. Declared data_rate is checked through DataModel. Macro status is always PASS because it has no threshold here.
Excludes: validation of target_accuracy or power_budget (stored fields not evaluated by this method), KV-aware serving capacity, allocator reserve, an explicit training-memory feasibility test at the first level, and matching macro utilization to the performance result. Solver defaults must be reviewed before treating the combined scorecard as a deployment.



Derivation: this orchestration method composes existing solver results and applies explicit comparisons to weight capacity, data supply, and latency. It does not introduce a new performance law; annual economics is a separate default scenario rather than measured operating cost.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenario, Models, Hardware
>>> scenario = Scenario(name='Example', description='Single device', workload=Models.Vision.ResNet50, system=Hardware.Cloud.H100)
>>> result = scenario.evaluate()
>>> result.feasibility.metrics['weight_size'] == scenario.workload.size_in_bytes('fp16')
True
>>> result.macro.status
'PASS'

The first evaluation level fails, including a data-pipeline failure as well as insufficient single-accelerator weight capacity.



SLAViolation
The modeled latency exceeds the supplied SLA after feasibility passes.






Equation: validate returns True iff evaluate’s feasibility and performance statuses are not FAIL; feasibility failures are raised first.
Assumptions: evaluate defines the entire check scope. This method reruns that evaluation, including annual accounting, rather than using a cache.
Excludes: checks for target_accuracy, power_budget, macro thresholds, KV residency, physical deployment safety, and validity of every modeling assumption. A passing result covers only the implemented comparisons.



Derivation: translate the two evaluation statuses into exceptions in feasibility-first order. No new numerical calculation is performed beyond the delegated scenario evaluation.

>>> scenario = Scenario(name='Example', description='Single device', workload=Models.Vision.ResNet50, system=Hardware.Cloud.H100)
>>> scenario.validate()
True

title: solvers.PlacementOptimizer
text:
solvers.PlacementOptimizer()
Finds the datacenter region that minimizes TCO plus a carbon tax.
Sweeps a list of grid regions, runs EconomicsModel for each, and ranks them by the combined objective TCO_usd + carbon_tons * carbon_tax_per_ton. This makes the carbon/cost trade-off explicit: a cheap-but-dirty grid can lose to a pricier low-carbon one once carbon is priced in.





Name
Description




solve
Determine the datacenter region minimizing TCO plus carbon tax.





solvers.PlacementOptimizer.solve(
    fleet,
    duration_days,
    regions=None,
    carbon_tax_per_ton=100.0,
    mfu=1.0,
)
Determine the datacenter region minimizing TCO plus carbon tax.











Name
Type
Description
Default




fleet
Fleet
The cluster to place.
required


duration_days
float
Operation duration in days.
required


regions
List[str]
Candidate grid names looked up on Infrastructure.Grids; unknown names are skipped silently.
None


carbon_tax_per_ton
float
Carbon price in USD per metric ton CO2e (default 100, a common mid-range social-cost-of-carbon teaching value).
100.0


mfu
float
Model FLOPs Utilization in [0, 1]; passed through to the energy model.
1.0














Name
Type
Description





PlacementOptimizerResult
Best region with its TCO (USD), carbon footprint (metric tons), PUE, and the full ranked candidate list.






Equation: objective = TCO_USD + carbon_kg / 1000 * carbon_tax_per_ton. Evaluate EconomicsModel independently for each recognized candidate and return the minimum.
Assumptions: Identical fleet, duration, and MFU across candidates; at least one region must resolve. The candidate list defines the search space. Excludes: Network latency, data sovereignty, capacity availability, and provisioning constraints.



Derivation: Enumerate the supplied regions and minimize the sum of their modeled financial cost and carbon mass priced in USD per metric ton. This is finite candidate search, not a continuous geographic optimum.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_, Systems
>>> result = PlacementOptimizer().solve(Systems.Clusters.Research_256, duration_days=1, regions=["Quebec"])
>>> result.best_region == "Quebec"
True

title: PrefixSharingScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
KV cache for users who share one prompt prefix, stored per user or once.


Equation: Independent storage=users*(prefix+unique)*KV_bytes_per_token; shared storage=(prefix+users*unique)*KV_bytes_per_token.
Assumptions: Uniform KV width and token storage, one physically shared prefix, positive user count.
Excludes: Allocator fragmentation, copy-on-write suffix blocks, and prefix cache misses.



Implementation references: mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size. These helper contracts state the source assumptions; the scenario binds their inputs and derives the displayed ratios and budgets.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.ChatbotSharedSystemPrompt
>>> round(scenario.capacity_ratio, 6)
4.98008

title: solvers.SynthesisSolver
text:
solvers.SynthesisSolver()
Given an SLA, synthesizes the required hardware specs (Wall 22: Inverse Solve).
This solver inverts the Roofline model to derive minimum hardware specifications required to meet a target latency SLA.
Literature Source: 1. Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline Model.” 2. Jouppi et al. (2017), “In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a TPU.”





Name
Description




solve
Synthesize minimum hardware requirements from a latency SLA.





solvers.SynthesisSolver.solve(
    model,
    target_latency,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
)
Synthesize minimum hardware requirements from a latency SLA.
Inverts the Roofline model: instead of asking “how fast does this hardware run the model?”, asks “what hardware would run the model in target_latency?”. Assumes a single full pass that streams every weight once (batch size 1, no weight reuse), so:

required_bw = weight_bytes / T_target [GB/s] — the bandwidth needed if the workload is memory-bound;
required_flops = total_ops / (T_target * efficiency) [TFLOP/s] — the compute rate needed if it is compute-bound;
compute_memory_ratio = required_flops / required_bw [FLOP/byte] — the hardware balance point a matching part should sit near.












Name
Type
Description
Default




model
Workload
The workload to serve; sets weight bytes and operation count.
required


target_latency
Quantity
The SLA latency target (any time unit; converted to seconds).
required


precision
str
Numerical precision; sets bytes per parameter.
'fp16'


efficiency
float
Expected software efficiency in (0, 1]; lower values inflate the required FLOPS to compensate.
0.5














Name
Type
Description





SynthesisResult
Required bandwidth, FLOPS, memory capacity, and the compute:memory balance ratio.






Equation: BW_required = weight_bytes / T; peak_required = F / (T*eta). Required capacity is weight storage alone and the reported balance is peak_required / BW_required.
Assumptions: positive target time and efficiency in (0, 1], batch one, one full weight read, and the workload’s lowered forward operation count. Excludes: activations, KV cache, dispatch overhead, and communication. These are screening requirements, not a sufficient deployment specification.



Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). Derivation: solve each resource-time inequality for its required rate.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SynthesisSolver
>>> r = SynthesisSolver().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Q_("50 ms"))
>>> bool(r.required_bw.m_as("GB/s") > 0 and r.required_memory.m_as("GB") > 0)
True

title: physics.networking
text:
physics.networking
Network latency and distance physics.





Name
Description




calc_great_circle_distance
Calculate spherical great-circle distance between geographic coordinates.


calc_network_latency_ms
Calculate the round-trip propagation floor for an optical-fiber path.





physics.networking.calc_great_circle_distance(
    lat1_deg,
    lon1_deg,
    lat2_deg,
    lon2_deg,
)
Calculate spherical great-circle distance between geographic coordinates.











Name
Type
Description
Default




lat1_deg
float
First latitude in degrees, conventionally in [-90, 90].
required


lon1_deg
float
First longitude in degrees, conventionally in [-180, 180].
required


lat2_deg
float
Second latitude in degrees, conventionally in [-90, 90].
required


lon2_deg
float
Second longitude in degrees, conventionally in [-180, 180].
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Shortest spherical surface distance in kilometers.






Equation: d = 2 R asin(sqrt(sin(dphi/2)**2 + cos(phi1) cos(phi2) sin(dlambda/2)**2)), with angles in radians and the registry mean Earth radius R.
Assumptions: Earth is a sphere; input coordinates refer to points on its surface.
Excludes: Ellipsoidal geodesy, terrain, cable-route detours, and network delay.



Derivation: the haversine identity converts the central angle between spherical coordinates to an arc length R times angle. EARTH_MEAN_RADIUS is sourced in mlsysim.physics.constants.



>>> calc_great_circle_distance(0, 0, 0, 0).magnitude == 0
True
>>> calc_great_circle_distance(0, 0, 0, 90) == calc_great_circle_distance(0, 90, 0, 0)
True




physics.networking.calc_network_latency_ms(distance_km)
Calculate the round-trip propagation floor for an optical-fiber path.











Name
Type
Description
Default




distance_km
Quantity or float
Nonnegative one-way fiber-route length; bare numbers mean kilometers.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Round-trip propagation duration in milliseconds.






Equation: RTT = 2 d/vfiber, using SPEED_OF_LIGHT_FIBER_KM_S.
Assumptions: Both directions have the supplied route length and the registry’s constant propagation speed.
Excludes: Switching, queueing, serialization, transceiver processing, and route stretch if supplied distance is geographic.



Derivation: distance divided by speed gives one-way travel time; the return path doubles it. The propagation-speed convention is sourced with SPEED_OF_LIGHT_FIBER_KM_S in mlsysim.physics.constants.



>>> calc_network_latency_ms(200) == 2 * calc_network_latency_ms(100)
True

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Selection that takes selection_time and leaves a subset that trains in subset_time, against full training in full_time (the selection inequality in hours).


Equation: total_time is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: Selection and subset training run sequentially, with all compared durations supplied.
Excludes: Accuracy equivalence, overlapping stages, and any price per unit time.

Execute the registered worked inputs; this is a modeled calculation.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios

title: SameTestSetAccuracyComparisonScenario
text:
Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Two models scored on the same n_samples test items: independent-set interval and McNemar’s limit.
The scores fix the net gap b - c (items only the baseline gets right minus items only the candidate gets right) but not the disagreements b + c; McNemar’s statistic (no continuity correction) exceeds the chi-square critical value z^2 only when b + c <= floor(gap^2 / z^2).


Equation: The calculation members below define z, baseline_errors, candidate_errors, baseline_error_sd, accuracy_difference, independent_interval, net_gap, chi2_critical, max_discordant, max_discordant_share.
Assumptions: Scores use the same item count; the displayed independent interval is a counterfactual comparison, while the McNemar threshold constrains discordant pairs.
Excludes: Recovering actual discordant counts from aggregate accuracies alone.



Derivation: Two models scored on the same n_samples test items: independent-set interval and McNemar’s limit. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.NinetyFiveAgainstNinetyFourOnSameImages
>>> value = case.max_discordant
>>> print(value)
26

text:
physics.transformer
Transformer FLOP accounting identities.





Name
Description




calc_attention_crossover
Find where full attention and dense block multiply-add counts match.


calc_attention_matmul_flops
Count work in both rectangular attention matrix products.


calc_attention_score_macs
Count multiply-adds in both full attention matrix products.


calc_online_softmax
Accumulate softmax normalization and weighted values in score blocks.


calc_score_matrix_intensity
Compute arithmetic intensity for materialized attention scores.


calc_transformer_block_weights
Count attention and feed-forward weights in a dense decoder block.

Estimate parameter-dominated forward work for generated tokens.


calc_transformer_prefill_flops
Estimate projection and attention work for one prompt.


calc_transformer_training_flops
Estimate parameter-dominated Transformer training work.


calc_vla_inference_latency
Bound one vision-language-action evaluation by compute and weight traffic.


calc_weight_only_step_time
Bound forward-pass time using weight traffic and linear computation.





physics.transformer.calc_attention_crossover(
    width,
    ffn_multiple=4,
    attention_projections=4,
)
Find where full attention and dense block multiply-add counts match.











Name
Type
Description
Default




width
int
Positive hidden width H in scalar features.
required


ffn_multiple
float
Positive feed-forward width expansion ratio; default four.
4


attention_projections
int
Nonnegative number of square attention projections; default four.
4














Name
Type
Description





float
Sequence length in tokens at the algebraic crossover; not rounded to an integer token boundary.






Equation: S_cross = W_block / (2 H), obtained from W_block*S = 2 S**2 H. Assumptions: the dense block shape in calc_transformer_block_weights and full square attention. This compares operation counts, not execution time. Excludes: different kernel efficiencies, memory bandwidth, causal masking, biases, embeddings, and grouped-query or sparse-expert architectures.



Derivation: divide the equality of dense and attention MAC counts by the positive sequence length and solve for S. Both sides use MACs, so no FLOP conversion factor is needed.



>>> width = 8
>>> context = calc_attention_crossover(width)
>>> weights = calc_transformer_block_weights(width)[2]
>>> weights * context == calc_attention_score_macs(context, width)
True




physics.transformer.calc_attention_matmul_flops(
    n_layers,
    hidden_dim,
    query_tokens,
    key_tokens,
    batch_size=1,
)
Count work in both rectangular attention matrix products.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_layers
int
Number of transformer layers evaluated.
required


hidden_dim
int
Query-head count times head width, in elements.
required


query_tokens
int or float
Query positions evaluated per request.
required


key_tokens
int or float
Key/value positions visited by each query; may be an expected context.
required


batch_size
int
Independent requests, default one.
1














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Work in flop for QK-transpose and attention-weighted V.






Equation: F = 4 L H Q S B. Each matrix product costs two FLOPs per multiply-accumulate; the two products have the same operation count. Assumptions: every query visits every supplied key position. H is the query width, including grouped-query attention’s query heads. Key and value head widths are equal. Excludes: projections, softmax, masking, data movement, and overhead. A causal prefill that skips the masked triangle applies its own reduction; this helper does not silently choose that execution convention.



Vaswani et al. (2017), “Attention Is All You Need,” Section 3.2.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 (bibliography key: vaswani2017attention). The FLOP count follows the two matrix products in the attention equation.



Partitioning queries into chunks preserves total matrix-product work.
>>> whole = calc_attention_matmul_flops(2, 16, 8, 32)
>>> chunk = calc_attention_matmul_flops(2, 16, 4, 32)
>>> bool(whole == 2 * chunk)
True




physics.transformer.calc_attention_score_macs(seq_len, width)
Count multiply-adds in both full attention matrix products.











Name
Type
Description
Default




seq_len
int
Nonnegative sequence length S in token positions.
required


width
int
Nonnegative hidden width H, summed across attention heads.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Multiply-add count for QK-transpose and attention-times-V in one layer.






Equation: MACs = 2 S**2 H. Assumptions: full square attention, equal query/key/value sequence lengths, and head widths summing to H. A multiply-add counts as one MAC here. Excludes: projection matrices, softmax, causal triangular savings, normalization, and conversion from MACs to FLOPs.



Derivation: QK-transpose computes S**2 dot products of width H across all heads. Multiplying the resulting attention matrix by V requires the same number of multiply-adds, giving two equal terms.



>>> work = calc_attention_score_macs(8, 4)
>>> calc_attention_score_macs(16, 4) == 4 * work
True




physics.transformer.calc_online_softmax(scores, values, block_size)
Accumulate softmax normalization and weighted values in score blocks.











Name
Type
Description
Default




scores
sequence of float
Finite, dimensionless logits; empty input returns an empty trace.
required


values
sequence of float
Scalar values paired with scores, of the same length and shared units.
required


block_size
int
Positive number of score/value pairs processed per block.
required














Name
Type
Description





list of dict
One record per block with running max, rescale factor, exponential sum, and unnormalized weighted output. Divide output by sum to obtain the normalized weighted mean. The output retains the values’ numeric scale.






Equation: for new maximum m, rescale old sums by exp(m_old-m), then add sum(exp(x-m)) and sum(exp(x-m)*v) for the current block. Assumptions: finite scalar logits and scalar values; each block uses its maximum to avoid overflow from exponentiating large positive logits. Excludes: vector values, attention masking, normalization of the returned output, GPU execution, and memory-traffic timing. In exact arithmetic, output/sum agrees with full-row softmax; floating-point rounding can differ.



Milakov and Gimelshein (2018), “Online Normalizer Calculation for Softmax.” https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02867. The running weighted numerator follows the same exponential rescaling as the normalizer.



>>> trace = calc_online_softmax([0.0, 0.0], [2.0, 4.0], 1)
>>> last = trace[-1]
>>> last["output"] / last["sum"] == sum([2.0, 4.0]) / len([2.0, 4.0])
True




physics.transformer.calc_score_matrix_intensity(head_dim, bytes_per_value)
Compute arithmetic intensity for materialized attention scores.











Name
Type
Description
Default




head_dim
int
Positive dot-product width H of one attention head.
required


bytes_per_value
Quantity or float
Positive storage size b of one score in bytes; bare values mean bytes.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
FLOPs per byte for score formation with one write and one subsequent read.






Equation: intensity = (2 H) / (2 b) = H / b FLOP/byte. Assumptions: two FLOPs per dot-product element and each score is written once to memory and later read once. Excludes: Q/K input traffic, softmax, value products, cache reuse, and fused attention kernels that avoid materializing the score matrix. This local intensity is not the whole layer’s arithmetic intensity.



Derivation: each score is one length-H dot product, costing 2 H FLOPs. Writing and reading its b-byte representation costs 2 b bytes; divide work by traffic to obtain the score-materialization intensity.



>>> intensity = calc_score_matrix_intensity(8, 2)
>>> calc_score_matrix_intensity(16, 2) == 2 * intensity
True




physics.transformer.calc_transformer_block_weights(
    width,
    ffn_multiple=4,
    attention_projections=4,
)
Count attention and feed-forward weights in a dense decoder block.











Name
Type
Description
Default




width
int
Positive hidden width H in scalar features.
required


ffn_multiple
float
Positive expansion ratio R of the feed-forward hidden width; default four.
4


attention_projections
int
Nonnegative number A of square H-by-H projections; default four represents query, key, value, and output projections.
4














Name
Type
Description





tuple
Attention, feed-forward, and total scalar weight counts, respectively.






Equation: W_attention = A H**2; W_ffn = 2 R H**2; W_total = W_attention + W_ffn. Assumptions: square attention projections and two dense feed-forward matrices with widths H to R*H to H. Excludes: biases, normalization parameters, embeddings, gated feed-forward branches, grouped-query dimensions, and sparse experts.



Derivation: a dense matrix contributes its row count times its column count. The attention matrices each have H**2 entries; each of the two feed-forward matrices has R H**2 entries. Different architectures need different shapes.



>>> attention, feed_forward, total = calc_transformer_block_weights(8)
>>> total == attention + feed_forward
True
>>> calc_transformer_block_weights(16)[2] == 4 * total
True




physics.transformer.calc_transformer_decode_flops(n_params, n_tokens=1)
Estimate parameter-dominated forward work for generated tokens.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity or int
Nonnegative model parameter count P, in param or as a count.
required


n_tokens
Quantity or int
Nonnegative number N of token positions; default one token.
1









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Linear projection and feed-forward work in flop.






Equation: F = 2 P N, using the registered Chinchilla decode coefficient. Assumptions: dense parameter-dominated execution; each parameter contributes one multiply and one addition per token position. Excludes: attention products over the KV cache, softmax, normalization, communication, and runtime overhead. At long contexts, callers must add attention work separately; this is not a complete decode FLOP count.



Kaplan et al. (2020), “Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361 (bibliography key: kaplan2020scaling).



>>> single = calc_transformer_decode_flops(1000)
>>> calc_transformer_decode_flops(1000, 2) == 2 * single
True

Equation: F = 2 P S + a L H S**2, where a is 2 for causal attention and 4 for bidirectional attention. If either attention dimension is omitted, only 2 P S is returned. Causal attention uses half of the square matrix rather than the exact triangular S(S+1)/2 count. Excludes: softmax, normalization, embedding lookup, vision encoders, communication, and kernel overhead. A batch of prompts requires summing or multiplying this per-prompt work.



Derivation: QK-transpose and attention-times-V each require S**2 H multiply-adds per layer. Counting two FLOPs per multiply-add yields 4 L H S**2; the causal approximation halves that term. Parameter products contribute 2 P S independently.

>>> causal = calc_transformer_prefill_flops(1000, 8, 2, 4)
>>> full = calc_transformer_prefill_flops(1000, 8, 2, 4, causal=False)
>>> full - dense == 2 * (causal - dense)

Type

required

False

int

None

int

None














Name
Type
Description





dict
FLOPs in prefill_flops; millisecond quantities t_prefill_compute, t_weight_sweep, t_prefill, t_decode_step, t_decode, and t_total; frequency f_max in hertz; integer prefill_tokens and decode_steps; and prefill_bound identifying the larger prefill resource time.






Equation: T_prefill = max(F_prefill / (peak_flops * compute_utilization), weight_memory / (memory_bandwidth * bus_efficiency)). Serial decoding adds (D-1) * max(2 P / effective_compute, weight_memory / effective_bandwidth). Parallel decoding instead evaluates S+D prompt positions with bidirectional attention and no serial decode phase. Assumptions: ideal compute/memory overlap within each pass, serial passes, and one full weight sweep per pass. Efficiency factors are caller inputs, not predictions. Weight-only quantization changes weight_memory; callers must still supply compute capacity at the activation execution precision. Excludes: a separately timed vision encoder, KV-cache traffic and decode attention products, launch/framework overhead, and other bus clients. A weight-dominated pass often binds on bandwidth, but the maximum also permits compute to bind; this is not a measured robot-control latency.



Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). The pass composition is a modeling choice. Parallel action decoding motivates the parallel_decode scenario; this function does not reproduce that paper’s measured speedup. Autoregressive action-token generation motivates the serial scenario.

>>> result = calc_vla_inference_latency(
...     1000, Q_(2000, "byte"), 8, 1,
...     Q_(1, "TFLOP/s"), Q_(1, "GB/s"))
>>> result["decode_steps"] == 0
True
>>> result["t_total"] == result["t_prefill"]
True

One record per block with running max, rescale factor, exponential sum, and unnormalized weighted output. Divide output by sum to obtain the normalized weighted mean. The output retains the values’ numeric scale.






Equation: for new maximum m, rescale old sums by exp(m_old-m), then add sum(exp(x-m)) and sum(exp(x-m)*v) for the current block. title: ReviewStaffingScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Substantive human review: appeal_rate of decisions_per_day at time_per_case each, staffed in shift-long shifts; optionally against a reported compare_cases handled at compare_time_per_case.


Equation: Review labor is decisions_per_day*appeal_rate*time_per_case; fractional shift equivalents divide by shift duration.
Assumptions: Review duration is constant and every appealed case requires one review.
Excludes: Integer staffing, breaks, peak demand, supervision overhead, and evidence that the declared time permits substantive review.



Derivation: Review labor is decisions_per_day*appeal_rate*time_per_case; fractional shift equivalents divide by shift duration. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.CreditAppealReview
>>> value = scenario.appeals_per_day
>>> round(float(value), 3)
1000.0






Name
Description




appeal_rate



appeals_per_day
Expected daily appealed decisions from decision count times appeal fraction.


cases_per_hour
Cases one reviewer processes in an hour at constant review duration.


compare_cases



compare_cases_per_hour
Comparison-cohort cases per reviewer-hour at its supplied duration.


compare_hours

title: ServingConsolidationScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Small and large serving models on whole devices, exclusive against shared in pairs.
Each small model occupies small_footprint (weights, KV cache, and activations) of a device_memory budget; tenants small models share one device when load tests allow. Each large model takes gpus_per_large devices for tensor parallelism either way.


Equation: shared devices = floor(small models / tenants) + large-model devices; savings = exclusive minus shared devices.
Assumptions: Small-model count is divisible by tenants for complete accounting; tenant throughput and memory isolation are supplied assumptions.
Excludes: Partial tenant groups, interference, latency-tail guarantees, and workspace in the large-model weight-only floor.



Derivation: shared devices = floor(small models / tenants) + large-model devices; savings = exclusive minus shared devices. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.

title: engine.solvers.realtime
text:
engine.solvers.realtime
Real-time solvers: the timed path between a learned proposer and the drives.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.robotics.control (phase lag of a delay, response-time bound, CAN FD and EtherCAT serialization, the lease ceiling) and physics.robotics.stopping; these models compose them for one stated situation (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




CanFdBusModel
Serialization occupancy of a cyclic CAN FD exchange: frames x t_frame against the cycle.


CommandAuthenticationModel
Authentication of a remote command as one more pre-brake delay, and a flood of forgeries.


EtherCatCycleModel
One EtherCAT summation frame through a chain of drives (calc_ethercat_cycle_time).


LeaseBudgetModel
A chunk lease as a term of the stopping budget, bounded by the lease rule.


PhaseLagBudgetModel
Phase a sampled loop spends on delay at its crossover frequency.


ResponseTimeModel
Response-time bound of one periodic task, R = C + B + I, against its deadline.


SharedDramReadModel
A permission tick’s snapshot read behind FIFO backlogs on a shared DRAM controller.


ThermalThrottleModel
A tick on a governed clock: a thermal trip reduces the clock until the junction clears.





engine.solvers.realtime.CanFdBusModel()
Serialization occupancy of a cyclic CAN FD exchange: frames x t_frame against the cycle.
Frame time and bits come from calc_canfd_bus_utilization (ISO 11898-1:2015 frame format, worst-case stuffing by default). Occupancy is a necessary check only; blocking and retransmission need a response-time analysis. axes_capacity is the most axes whose frames fit one cycle.





Name
Description




solve
Count CAN FD serialization occupancy within one control cycle.





engine.solvers.realtime.CanFdBusModel.solve(
    num_axes,
    payload_bytes,
    frames_per_axis,
    baud_arbitration,
    baud_data,
    cycle,
)
Count CAN FD serialization occupancy within one control cycle.











Name
Type
Description
Default




num_axes
int
Positive number of axes sharing this bus.
required


payload_bytes
int
Application bytes per frame, from zero through 64; padded to a legal CAN FD data-field size.
required


frames_per_axis
int
Positive number of command/feedback frames per axis per cycle.
required


baud_arbitration
Quantity
Positive nominal-phase bit rate, convertible to bit/s.
required


baud_data
Quantity
Positive data-phase bit rate, convertible to bit/s.
required


cycle
Quantity
Positive cycle duration in time units.
required














Name
Type
Description





CanFdBusResult
Frame bit counts, times in microseconds, utilization fraction, and axes_capacity. fits is a serialization-only occupancy check.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.control.calc_canfd_bus_utilization : CAN FD frame accounting and serialization.



Equation: t_frame = bits_nominal/baud_arbitration + bits_data/baud_data; occupancy = num_axes*frames_per_axis*t_frame; axes_capacity = floor(cycle/(frames_per_axis*t_frame)).
Assumptions: Standard identifiers, worst-case dynamic stuffing, and the frame-format accounting of calc_canfd_bus_utilization; all frames have the supplied payload.
Excludes: Competing traffic, nonpreemptive blocking, retransmissions, and a schedulability guarantee.



Derivation: serialization time is bit count divided by bit rate, summed across the nominal and data phases. Frame-format assumptions are documented in the linked physics function.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import CanFdBusModel
>>> result = CanFdBusModel().solve(1, 8, 2, Q_(1, "Mbit/s"),
...     Q_(5, "Mbit/s"), Q_(1, "ms"))
>>> bool(result.fits and result.axes_capacity >= 1)
True






engine.solvers.realtime.CommandAuthenticationModel()
Authentication of a remote command as one more pre-brake delay, and a flood of forgeries.
A supplied cycle count divided by the permission processor’s clock gives the time of one signature verification and of a MAC over a frame of mac_blocks cipher blocks. Verification adds to the delay before a remote stop can act, so each millisecond is travel at speed against the finished budget’s spare; a replay at the edge of the freshness window carries the machine v x tau_fresh. Verified serially, n forged signed packets queued ahead of a genuine veto finish it at (n + 1) t_verify; the fewest that push it past the deadline is n = floor(T_latest / t_verify), sustained at n / ((n + 1) t_verify) packets per second (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Charge serial authentication work against a remote-command deadline.





engine.solvers.realtime.CommandAuthenticationModel.solve(
    clock,
    verify_cycles,
    mac_block_cycles,
    mac_blocks,
    speed,
    spare,
    deadline,
    deadline_after_admission,
    freshness_window,
)
Charge serial authentication work against a remote-command deadline.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive verification-processor clock frequency in Hz.
required


verify_cycles
float
Positive assumed cycle count for one signature verification.
required


mac_block_cycles
float
Positive assumed cycle count for authenticating one cipher block.
required


mac_blocks
int
Positive cipher-block count per authenticated command.
required


speed
Quantity
Nonnegative machine speed held during verification and freshness delays.
required


spare
Quantity
Remaining distance allowance before adding authentication delay.
required


deadline
Quantity
Positive total command-verification deadline.
required


deadline_after_admission
Quantity
Positive verification allowance for a command already admitted.
required

Quantity
Nonnegative maximum age accepted by the command freshness check.
required














Name
Type
Description





CommandAuthenticationResult
Signature time in ms, MAC time in microseconds, travel in mm, and forged-packet counts/rate. Negative remaining spare denotes budget exhaustion.






mlsysim.physics.quantities.compute_time : Work divided by service rate.



Equation: t_sig = verify_cycles/clock; t_mac = mac_blocks*mac_block_cycles/clock; travel = speed*time; n = floor(deadline/t_sig) forged commands delay the following veto until (n+1)*t_sig.
Assumptions: Cycle counts are supplied, verification is serial, and each forged signed packet consumes a full verification before rejection.
Excludes: Cryptographic security strength, early rejection, parallel verification, network admission controls, and a deployed-system timing guarantee.



Derivation: convert cycles to time at a fixed clock and count serial service slots before the deadline; integrate constant speed over that delay.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import CommandAuthenticationModel
>>> result = CommandAuthenticationModel().solve(Q_(1, "MHz"), 1000, 10, 1,
...     Q_(1, "m/s"), Q_(1, "m"), Q_(10, "ms"), Q_(5, "ms"), Q_(1, "ms"))
>>> bool(result.veto_verified_at > result.deadline)
True






engine.solvers.realtime.EtherCatCycleModel()
One EtherCAT summation frame through a chain of drives (calc_ethercat_cycle_time).
The frame carries every axis’s process data; each node forwards it with a fixed hop delay, so occupancy is serialization plus forwarding.





Name
Description




solve
Budget one summation frame through an EtherCAT drive chain.

    num_axes,
    bytes_per_axis,
    baud_rate,
    header_bytes,
    hop_delay,
    cycle,
)
Budget one summation frame through an EtherCAT drive chain.











Name
Type
Description
Default




num_axes
int
Positive number of nodes traversed by the frame.
required


bytes_per_axis
int
Positive process-data payload bytes contributed by each node.
required


baud_rate
Quantity
Positive link bit rate, convertible to bit/s.
required

int
Nonnegative total framing overhead in bytes, supplied by the caller.
required

Quantity
Nonnegative forwarding time per node.
required

Name
Type

EtherCatCycleResult
Serialization, forwarding, occupancy, and margin times; dimensionless utilization and fits comparing total occupancy with cycle.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.control.calc_ethercat_cycle_time : Summation-frame occupancy.



Equation: occupancy = 8*(header_bytes + num_axes*bytes_per_axis)/baud_rate + num_axes*hop_delay; utilization = occupancy/cycle.
Assumptions: One frame carries all process data and each node adds a fixed forwarding delay.
Excludes: Cable propagation unless included in hop_delay, multi-frame fragmentation, host jitter, and protocol error recovery.



Derivation: transmit all frame bits at the declared line rate, then add the per-node forwarding budgets along the chain.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import EtherCatCycleModel
>>> result = EtherCatCycleModel().solve(2, 32, Q_(100, "Mbit/s"),
...     64, Q_(1, "us"), Q_(1, "ms"))
>>> bool(result.fits and result.unallocated > Q_(0, "us"))
True






engine.solvers.realtime.LeaseBudgetModel()
A chunk lease as a term of the stopping budget, bounded by the lease rule.
After the last admission a stalled proposer’s chunk drives on for the lease; the tick that notices expiry and the bus cycle that carries the stop follow, then the brake onset. That interval is travel at speed, added to the braking travel, the localization and margin overhead, and the onset travel (StoppingBudgetModel). The lease rule bounds the lease from both sides:
T_renew + T_jitter  <  T_lease  <=  tau_max - T_tick - T_bus - T_onset - age
where tau_max is the longest pre-brake delay whose stop fits and age is the evidence’s age when the chunk is admitted. The stall timeline puts the stall after the second renewal completes.





Name
Description
