engine.solvers.performance.SynthesisSolver()
Given an SLA, synthesizes the required hardware specs (Wall 22: Inverse Solve).
This solver inverts the Roofline model to derive minimum hardware specifications required to meet a target latency SLA.
Literature Source: 1. Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline Model.” 2. Jouppi et al. (2017), “In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a TPU.”





Name
Description




solve
Synthesize minimum hardware requirements from a latency SLA.





engine.solvers.performance.SynthesisSolver.solve(
    model,
    target_latency,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
)
Synthesize minimum hardware requirements from a latency SLA.
Inverts the Roofline model: instead of asking “how fast does this hardware run the model?”, asks “what hardware would run the model in target_latency?”. Assumes a single full pass that streams every weight once (batch size 1, no weight reuse), so:

required_bw = weight_bytes / T_target [GB/s] — the bandwidth needed if the workload is memory-bound;
required_flops = total_ops / (T_target * efficiency) [TFLOP/s] — the compute rate needed if it is compute-bound;
compute_memory_ratio = required_flops / required_bw [FLOP/byte] — the hardware balance point a matching part should sit near.












Name
Type
Description
Default

Workload

required

Quantity
The SLA latency target (any time unit; converted to seconds).
required


precision
str
Numerical precision; sets bytes per parameter.
'fp16'


efficiency
float
Expected software efficiency in (0, 1]; lower values inflate the required FLOPS to compensate.
0.5














Name
Type
Description





SynthesisResult
Required bandwidth, FLOPS, memory capacity, and the compute:memory balance ratio.






Equation: BW_required = weight_bytes / T; peak_required = F / (T*eta). Required capacity is weight storage alone and the reported balance is peak_required / BW_required.
Assumptions: positive target time and efficiency in (0, 1], batch one, one full weight read, and the workload’s lowered forward operation count. Excludes: activations, KV cache, dispatch overhead, and communication. These are screening requirements, not a sufficient deployment specification.



Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). Derivation: solve each resource-time inequality for its required rate.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import SynthesisSolver
>>> r = SynthesisSolver().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Q_("50 ms"))
>>> bool(r.required_bw.m_as("GB/s") > 0 and r.required_memory.m_as("GB") > 0)
True

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Scheduled sessions of attempt-and-reset cycles: demonstrations kept per session, the campaign that keeps target_kept of them, and the wear it puts on a gear and a cable.


Equation: Cycles=floor(active_time/(attempt+reset)); retention=(1-failure_rate)*(1-qa_rate); campaign_attempts=ceil(target/retention).
Assumptions: QA rejects only nonfailed attempts; fixed cycle costs and constant expected rejection rates.
Excludes: A confidence guarantee for retained count, fatigue-dependent rates, and stochastic wear.



Derivation: Whole attempt/reset cycles are packed into available session time. Sequential filtering retains the nonfailed share times the QA-surviving share; the expected retained count and nominal cycle consumption then determine the campaign budget.

title: SoftContactExploitScenario
text:
Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/learning.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
machine’s arm coasting into site’s latch plate at the fast approach: the peak force a penalty spring that lets the gripper sink penalty_penetration reports, the peak the real plate imposes on a rigid arm, and the arm stiffness at which the series chain reaches the limit. The moving mass is the arm’s effective contact mass without its payload capacity (the gripper holds no object at the door).


Equation: Impact energy m*v**2/2 becomes spring energy k*x**2/2; series compliance sets the effective k.
Assumptions: Linear undamped springs, empty gripper, and the declared effective contact mass.
Excludes: Damping, controller intervention, nonlinear contact, and any safety certification.



Derivation: Conservation of kinetic energy against a linear spring gives F_peak = v*sqrt(m*k). Springs in series add their compliances. The implementation composes mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation.calc_transient_impact_force with mlsysim.physics.robotics.learning.calc_series_stiffness and calc_complementary_series_stiffness.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.LatchSoftSpringExploit
>>> s.penalty_timescale.to("second").magnitude > 0
True

title: engine.solvers.deliberation
text:
engine.solvers.deliberation
Test-time deliberation solvers: spending more work on one decision with the weights fixed.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on stated token counts, pass rates, check error rates, and the per-token decode floor of a DecodeScenario: how one output ceiling turns into different latencies and bills as depth, breadth, or feedback; what a pool of independent candidates holds and what a fallible check lets through; how argmax selection concentrates scoring error; how a step check bounds a search tree; and what flat sampling, beam search, and feedback policies spend under one deadline. None models queueing, batching, prefill, or serving overhead unless a scenario states it.





Name
Description




AllocationAxesModel
One output ceiling spent three ways: depth, breadth, and feedback.


ArgmaxNoiseModel
Argmax over N equally good candidates whose scores carry independent noise.


BestOfNPoolModel
A parallel pool of N independent candidates against sequential retry.


DeadlinePolicyModel
Three deliberation policies for one task under one deadline.


ProbeVsAnswerModel
A generated explanation of K tokens against a prepared test of T_probe.


PrunedSearchTreeModel
Size of a search tree whose step check rejects each child with probability r.


ScopedRevisionModel
Output of regenerating a whole candidate plan against only its affected nodes.


SearchAccountsModel
Flat best-of-N against beam search, kept as separate accounts.


VerifiedPoolModel
First-passing selection from a fixed pool of n under a fallible check.





engine.solvers.deliberation.AllocationAxesModel()
One output ceiling spent three ways: depth, breadth, and feedback.
Depth generates the whole ceiling in one chain. Breadth runs N concurrent candidates, each billed its own copy of the S-token prompt, so it re-reads (N - 1) S tokens. Feedback runs H rounds of a candidate plus a check; each later request appends the earlier candidates and reports, so input is H S + (K + R) H (H - 1) / 2. Times are generation at the decode floor plus checks; bills count model tokens only.





Name
Description




solve
One output ceiling spent three ways: depth, breadth, and feedback.





engine.solvers.deliberation.AllocationAxesModel.solve(
    decode_per_token,
    prompt,
    ceiling,
    candidates,
    candidate_tokens,
    rounds,
    report_tokens,
    check_time,
    input_price,
    output_price,
    context_growth=None,
)

Name
Type
Description





AllocationAxesResult
Per-policy input/output token counts, duration in seconds, USD bills, and dimensionless latency/cost ratios.






Equation: Depth output = ceiling; breadth output = N K; feedback input = H S + (K + R) H (H - 1) / 2.
Assumptions: Breadth executes concurrently; feedback executes serially; each request pays its full prompt.
Excludes: Prefill, queueing, resource contention, and effectiveness of reasoning.



Derivation: Parallel candidates each pay for a separate prompt. Feedback round j resends j earlier increments, so repeated context is an arithmetic series. Adding the generated tokens and check durations gives the serial feedback time; breadth instead charges concurrent candidates separately.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> AllocationAxesModel().solve(Q_("1 ms"), 10, 20, 2, 10, 2, 2, Q_("1 ms"), Q_("1 USD/token"), Q_("1 USD/token")).breadth_output == 20
True






engine.solvers.deliberation.ArgmaxNoiseModel()
Argmax over N equally good candidates whose scores carry independent noise.
The winner’s expected scoring error is the expected maximum of N standard normals (in units of the noise’s spread), below the large-N asymptote sqrt(2 ln N). A loophole present in a fraction g of single samples appears in a pool of N with 1 - (1 - g)^N.





Name
Description




solve
Argmax over N equally good candidates whose scores carry independent noise.





engine.solvers.deliberation.ArgmaxNoiseModel.solve(
    pool_sizes,
    large_pool,
    exploit_rate,
)

Name
Type
Description
Default

Sequence[int]
Nonempty positive candidate counts; the final entry is the comparison pool.
required


large_pool
int
Positive candidate count for the exploit-presence calculation.
required


exploit_rate
float
Independent per-candidate exploit probability, in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





ArgmaxNoiseResult
Expected winner noise in standard-deviation units and dimensionless exploit-presence probabilities.






Equation: Expected winner noise = E[max(Z_1,…,Z_n)]; exploit presence = 1 - (1 - g)^N.
Assumptions: Candidates have equal underlying quality and independent standard-normal score noise.

engine.solvers.deliberation.VerifiedPoolModel()
First-passing selection from a fixed pool of n under a fallible check.
Each candidate is valid with rate v; the check rejects valid ones with eps_FR and passes invalid ones with eps_FA, so a candidate passes with q = v (1 - eps_FR) + (1 - v) eps_FA. Passing-set precision is v (1 - eps_FR) / q, one minus the Bayes posterior of a defect given a pass (CheckerPosteriorModel with defect_rate = 1 - v). The pool selects with 1 - (1 - q)^n and otherwise abstains; a selection is defective with 1 - precision. An incident loss prices each defective selection; the output bill prices the whole pool.

engine.solvers.deliberation.VerifiedPoolModel()
First-passing selection from a fixed pool of n under a fallible check.
Each candidate is valid with rate v; the check rejects valid ones with eps_FR and passes invalid ones with eps_FA, so a candidate passes with q = v (1 - eps_FR) + (1 - v) eps_FA. Passing-set precision is v (1 - eps_FR) / q, one minus the Bayes posterior of a defect given a pass (CheckerPosteriorModel with defect_rate = 1 - v). The pool selects with 1 - (1 - q)^n and otherwise abstains; a selection is defective with 1 - precision. An incident loss prices each defective selection; the output bill prices the whole pool.

Equation: q = v (1 - false_reject_rate) + (1 - v) false_accept_rate; precision = v (1 - false_reject_rate) / q.
Assumptions: Independent candidates, constant checker error rates, and q > 0; the entire pool is billed.

>>> VerifiedPoolModel().solve(2, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0, Q_("10 token"), Q_("1 USD/token"), Q_("10 USD")).precision == 1.0
True

Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Two teams in one development window: a slow cycle against a fast one, with assumed gains per run.
Accuracies are in percent and gains in points per run. The slow team learns from every run; the fast team can run far more than it can learn from, so fast_effective_runs caps the runs that count. Both stop at ceiling.


Equation: final accuracy = min(start + useful runs * gain per run, ceiling).
Assumptions: Accuracy values are percentages and gains are percentage points. Run gains and effective fast runs are illustrative inputs, not learned response curves.
Excludes: A statistical learning-curve model and a causal claim that faster experiments improve accuracy by this amount.



Derivation: final accuracy = min(start + useful runs * gain per run, ceiling). The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.

>>> round(float(case.slow_runs), 3)
26.0

title: KvDecodeBatchScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Batched decode on one accelerator when every sequence also reads its own KV cache.
Each step reads the weights once and each sequence’s cache of context_tokens: bytes W + B m_seq, time (W + B m_seq) / B_mem (a bandwidth floor), aggregate rate B / step. The rate approaches B_mem / m_seq as caches dominate. A TPOT target caps the batch at floor((t B_mem - W) / m_seq); memory caps it at floor((M - W) / m_seq). Prefill of prompt_tokens runs at prefill_efficiency of the peak_precision peak.


Equation: Each memory step reads W+B*KV_sequence bytes; rate is B/step_time; capacity and latency ceilings solve those inequalities for B.
Assumptions: Every sequence reads a fixed full-length cache, weights are read once per batch, and memory transfers use peak bandwidth.
Excludes: Decode compute, collectives, launch overhead, workspaces, and evolving sequence lengths; prefill uses only the registered per-token forward count.



Derivation: the scenario composes mlsysim.physics.transfer_time. Their contracts supply the underlying equations; property equations show the remaining unit conversions and accounting.

title: solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel
text:
solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel()
Models the computational cost of responsible AI practices (Wall 20: Safety).
This model quantifies the ‘Safety Tax’ — the additional compute and data required for differential privacy or fairness guarantees.
Literature Source: 1. Abadi et al. (2016), “Deep Learning with Differential Privacy.” 2. Anil et al. (2022), “Large-Scale Differentially Private BERT.”





Name
Description




solve
Calculate the compute and data overhead of responsible-AI guarantees.





solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel.solve(
    base_training_time,
    epsilon=1.0,
    delta=1e-05,
    min_subgroup_prevalence=0.01,
)
Calculate the compute and data overhead of responsible-AI guarantees.
Two first-order cost models:

Privacy (DP-SGD slowdown): slowdown = 1 + coefficient / epsilon — tighter privacy budgets (smaller epsilon) require more noise and per-sample clipping work, so training time grows hyperbolically as epsilon -> 0. The coefficient is a pedagogical calibration constant (DP_SGD_SLOWDOWN_COEFFICIENT in engine/calibration.py).
Fairness (data requirement): additional_data = 1 / min_subgroup_prevalence — to collect N samples of a subgroup seen at prevalence p, you must collect ~N/p samples overall.












Name
Type
Description
Default




base_training_time
Quantity
Training time without privacy guarantees (any time unit; the result keeps the same unit).
required


epsilon
float
Differential-privacy budget (> 0); smaller is stricter. Clamped below at 0.01 to avoid a singular slowdown.
1.0


delta
float
DP failure probability (reported, not used in the slowdown model).
1e-05


min_subgroup_prevalence
float
Prevalence in (0, 1] of the rarest subgroup that must be adequately represented.
0.01














Name
Type
Description





ResponsibleEngineeringResult
DP slowdown factor (dimensionless), effective training time, and the data-collection multiplier.






Equation: slowdown = 1 + c / max(epsilon, 0.01); effective_time = base_time * slowdown; data_factor = 1 / max(prevalence, 1e-6). The coefficient c is the declared pedagogical default in calibration.py, not a measured DP-SGD law.
Assumptions: Fixed illustrative coefficient and inverse-prevalence sampling account. Delta is reported but does not affect the slowdown. Excludes: Privacy accounting, proof of differential privacy, actual clipping/noise implementation, and fairness certification.



Derivation: The inverse-epsilon slowdown is a pedagogical assumption. Inverse prevalence follows the expected sample count needed to observe a subgroup; neither expression proves privacy or fairness.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_, Systems
>>> result = ResponsibleEngineeringModel().solve(Q_("1 hour"), epsilon=1)
>>> result.effective_training_time > Q_("1 hour")
True

A GPU-parallel on-policy run: robots environments each stepping steps_per_update times per update for updates updates within training_time, at policy_rate.


Equation: Transitions=robots*steps_per_update*updates; throughput=transitions/training_time.
Assumptions: Uniform update sizes and a throughput representative of the requested extrapolation.

physics.privacy
Differential privacy and information-leakage formulas (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




calc_basic_composition
Sum pure-DP budgets for sequential releases on the same data.


calc_laplace_scale
Calculate the noise scale for a scalar Laplace mechanism.


calc_level_bits
Calculate the information in an equiprobable finite choice.


calc_membership_tpr_ceiling
Bound membership-test sensitivity under pure differential privacy.





physics.privacy.calc_basic_composition(epsilons)
Sum pure-DP budgets for sequential releases on the same data.











Name
Type
Description
Default




epsilons
iterable of float
Nonnegative dimensionless privacy budgets for individual releases.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless basic sequential-composition budget; an empty iterable returns the additive identity zero.






Equation: epsilon_total = sum(epsilons).
Assumptions: Each release satisfies its stated pure-DP guarantee under the same neighboring-dataset definition; releases may be adaptive.
Excludes: Advanced composition, disjoint-data parallel composition, and delta terms.



Derivation: conditional density-ratio bounds multiply across releases; their logarithmic epsilon bounds therefore add.



>>> round(calc_basic_composition([0.1, 0.2]), 2)
0.3




physics.privacy.calc_laplace_scale(sensitivity, epsilon)
Calculate the noise scale for a scalar Laplace mechanism.











Name
Type
Description
Default




sensitivity
float or Quantity
Nonnegative global L1 sensitivity of the query, in its output units.
required


epsilon
float
Positive dimensionless pure-differential-privacy budget.
required














Name
Type
Description





float or Quantity
Laplace scale b in the same units as sensitivity; also the expected absolute error of one Laplace(0, b) draw.






Equation: b = sensitivity / epsilon.
Assumptions: Sensitivity bounds every allowed neighboring-dataset change and the mechanism uses independent Laplace noise with this scale.
Excludes: Sensitivity estimation, noise sampling, and approximate-DP accounting.



Derivation: the Laplace density ratio is bounded by exp(sensitivity/b); choosing b=sensitivity/epsilon bounds that ratio by exp(epsilon).



>>> calc_laplace_scale(2, 1)
2.0




physics.privacy.calc_level_bits(levels)
Calculate the information in an equiprobable finite choice.











Name
Type
Description
Default




levels
int
Positive number of equally likely distinguishable values.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Shannon information in bits.






Equation: bits = log2(levels).
Assumptions: Each level is equally probable and observable without ambiguity.
Excludes: Nonuniform distributions, side information, and measurement noise.



Derivation: entropy of L equiprobable values is -sum((1/L)*log2(1/L)) = log2(L).



>>> calc_level_bits(8)
3.0




physics.privacy.calc_membership_tpr_ceiling(fpr, epsilon)
Bound membership-test sensitivity under pure differential privacy.











Name
Type
Description
Default




fpr
float
Membership-test false-positive rate, dimensionless, in [0, 1].
required


epsilon
float
Nonnegative dimensionless pure-DP budget, with delta equal to zero.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Upper bound on the membership-test true-positive rate, as a fraction.






Equation: TPR <= min(exp(epsilon)*FPR, 1-exp(-epsilon)*(1-FPR)).
Assumptions: The member/nonmember hypotheses are neighboring datasets under the release’s pure-DP definition.
Excludes: Approximate-DP delta, prior membership probability, and construction of an attack achieving the ceiling.



Derivation: apply the DP inequality to the event that a test flags a member, then apply the reverse inequality to its complement.



>>> round(calc_membership_tpr_ceiling(0.1, 0), 2)
0.1

title: engine.solvers.serving_scale
text:
engine.solvers.serving_scale
Serving-at-scale solvers: request traces, measured frontiers, KV admission, routing.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.serving (Little’s law, the batching knee, padding waste, speculative rounds) and physics.memory (KV-cache size); these models apply them to a published trace, a benchmark table, or one stated replica (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




KvAdmissionModel
How many requests of one context length a replica’s KV budget admits.


PrecisionDividendModel
The maximum batch before and after lower-precision weights and KV cache.





engine.solvers.serving_scale.KvAdmissionModel()
How many requests of one context length a replica’s KV budget admits.
The budget is the replica’s HBM minus its weights and a runtime reserve; each request holds 2 L H_kv d_head b bytes per token for its whole context (calc_kv_cache_size). Paging changes none of these bytes, only the waste around them.





Name
Description




solve
Divide a replica’s available KV memory by one request’s KV footprint.





engine.solvers.serving_scale.KvAdmissionModel.solve(
    model,
    accelerators,
    hbm_per_accelerator,
    weight_bytes_per_param,
    reserve,
    context_tokens,
    kv_bytes_per_elem,
)
Divide a replica’s available KV memory by one request’s KV footprint.











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
TransformerWorkload
Transformer dimensions and parameter count; hidden width must be divisible by attention heads for the integer head width used here.
required


accelerators
int
Positive number of devices whose HBM is pooled into the replica.
required


hbm_per_accelerator
Quantity
Positive memory capacity per accelerator, convertible to bytes.
required


weight_bytes_per_param
Quantity
Positive bytes stored per weight element, expressed as a byte quantity.
required


reserve
Quantity
Nonnegative total replica memory reserved for other runtime state.
required


context_tokens
int
Positive resident context tokens per request.
required


kv_bytes_per_elem
Quantity
Positive bytes stored per key or value element.
required














Name
Type
Description





KvAdmissionResult
Weights and KV budget in GB, per-token/per-request cache storage, and integer request capacity. Negative budgets are not clamped; they indicate an infeasible allocation rather than a valid admission count.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : Key/value tensor footprint.



Equation: KV_request = 2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*context_tokens*element_bytes; budget = accelerators*HBM - weights - reserve; max_requests = int(budget/KV_request).
Assumptions: uniform request lengths and a perfectly pooled replica budget. For a nonnegative budget, integer truncation implements floor division. Missing kv_heads falls back to the query-head count.
Excludes: per-device imbalance, communication, block fragmentation, and workspace beyond the explicitly supplied reserve.



Derivation: count both key and value tensors for every layer and resident token, subtract static allocation, and divide remaining bytes by request bytes.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Q_
>>> result = KvAdmissionModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 1,
...     Q_("80 GB"), Q_("2 byte"), Q_("4 GB"), 1024, Q_("2 byte"))
>>> result.max_requests > 0
True






engine.solvers.serving_scale.PrecisionDividendModel()
The maximum batch before and after lower-precision weights and KV cache.
Weights and each request’s KV cache split evenly across tp_size devices. Lower-precision weights raise each device’s KV budget once; lower-precision KV shrinks every request’s share. The dividend is the ratio of the two maximum batches.





Name
Description




solve
Compare KV admission limits before and after reducing storage precision.

    model,
    tp_size,
    hbm_per_accelerator,
    context_tokens,
    kv_heads,
    weight_bytes,
    weight_bytes_low,
    kv_bytes,
    kv_bytes_low,
)

Name
Type
Description
Default

required


tp_size
int
Positive tensor-parallel degree for even weight and KV sharding.
required


hbm_per_accelerator
Quantity
Positive device capacity, convertible to bytes.
required

Positive resident tokens per request.
required


kv_heads
int
Positive key/value-head count in the modeled attention layout.
required


weight_bytes
Quantity

required

required

required

Quantity

required














Name
Type
Description





PrecisionDividendResult
Weight and KV byte budgets per device, whole-request capacities, and dimensionless capacity dividend. Baseline capacity must be positive because the dividend divides by it; no feasibility flag is returned.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : KV tensor footprint.



Equation: budget = HBM - weights/tp_size; batch = int(budget / (KV_request/tp_size)); dividend = batch_low/batch. Both branches use the same context and head count, varying only element sizes.
Assumptions: even sharding and identical devices; usable HBM is devoted only to weights and KV. Integer truncation is a floor only for nonnegative budgets.
Excludes: quantization accuracy, dequantization cost, workspace, allocator reserve, and communication. A memory dividend is not a throughput prediction.



Derivation: divide per-device free bytes by the per-device request footprint for each representation, then compare the integer capacities.

>>> result = PrecisionDividendModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 1,

engine.solvers.serving_scale.KvAdmissionModel()
How many requests of one context length a replica’s KV budget admits.
The budget is the replica’s HBM minus its weights and a runtime reserve; each request holds 2 L H_kv d_head b bytes per token for its whole context (calc_kv_cache_size). Paging changes none of these bytes, only the waste around them.





Name
Description




solve
Divide a replica’s available KV memory by one request’s KV footprint.





engine.solvers.serving_scale.KvAdmissionModel.solve(
    model,
    accelerators,
    hbm_per_accelerator,
    weight_bytes_per_param,
    reserve,
    context_tokens,
    kv_bytes_per_elem,
)
Divide a replica’s available KV memory by one request’s KV footprint.











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
TransformerWorkload
Transformer dimensions and parameter count; hidden width must be divisible by attention heads for the integer head width used here.
required


accelerators
int
Positive number of devices whose HBM is pooled into the replica.
required


hbm_per_accelerator
Quantity
Positive memory capacity per accelerator, convertible to bytes.
required


weight_bytes_per_param
Quantity
Positive bytes stored per weight element, expressed as a byte quantity.
required


reserve
Quantity
Nonnegative total replica memory reserved for other runtime state.
required


context_tokens
int
Positive resident context tokens per request.
required


kv_bytes_per_elem
Quantity
Positive bytes stored per key or value element.
required














Name
Type
Description





KvAdmissionResult
Weights and KV budget in GB, per-token/per-request cache storage, and integer request capacity. Negative budgets are not clamped; they indicate an infeasible allocation rather than a valid admission count.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : Key/value tensor footprint.



Equation: KV_request = 2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*context_tokens*element_bytes; budget = accelerators*HBM - weights - reserve; max_requests = int(budget/KV_request).
Assumptions: uniform request lengths and a perfectly pooled replica budget. For a nonnegative budget, integer truncation implements floor division. Missing kv_heads falls back to the query-head count.
Excludes: per-device imbalance, communication, block fragmentation, and workspace beyond the explicitly supplied reserve.



Derivation: count both key and value tensors for every layer and resident token, subtract static allocation, and divide remaining bytes by request bytes.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Q_
>>> result = KvAdmissionModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 1,
...     Q_("80 GB"), Q_("2 byte"), Q_("4 GB"), 1024, Q_("2 byte"))
>>> result.max_requests > 0
True






engine.solvers.serving_scale.PrecisionDividendModel()
The maximum batch before and after lower-precision weights and KV cache.
Weights and each request’s KV cache split evenly across tp_size devices. Lower-precision weights raise each device’s KV budget once; lower-precision KV shrinks every request’s share. The dividend is the ratio of the two maximum batches.





Name
Description




solve
Compare KV admission limits before and after reducing storage precision.





engine.solvers.serving_scale.PrecisionDividendModel.solve(
    model,
    tp_size,
    hbm_per_accelerator,
    context_tokens,
    kv_heads,
    weight_bytes,
    weight_bytes_low,
    kv_bytes,
    kv_bytes_low,
)
Compare KV admission limits before and after reducing storage precision.











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
TransformerWorkload
Transformer dimensions and weight count; hidden width must divide by heads.
required


tp_size
int
Positive tensor-parallel degree for even weight and KV sharding.
required


hbm_per_accelerator
Quantity
Positive device capacity, convertible to bytes.
required


context_tokens
int
Positive resident tokens per request.
required


kv_heads
int
Positive key/value-head count in the modeled attention layout.
required


weight_bytes
Quantity
Positive baseline bytes per weight element.
required


weight_bytes_low
Quantity
Positive alternative bytes per weight element.
required


kv_bytes
Quantity
Positive baseline bytes per key/value element.
required


kv_bytes_low
Quantity
Positive alternative bytes per key/value element.
required














Name
Type
Description





PrecisionDividendResult
Weight and KV byte budgets per device, whole-request capacities, and dimensionless capacity dividend. Baseline capacity must be positive because the dividend divides by it; no feasibility flag is returned.






mlsysim.physics.memory.calc_kv_cache_size : KV tensor footprint.



Equation: budget = HBM - weights/tp_size; batch = int(budget / (KV_request/tp_size)); dividend = batch_low/batch. Both branches use the same context and head count, varying only element sizes.
Assumptions: even sharding and identical devices; usable HBM is devoted only to weights and KV. Integer truncation is a floor only for nonnegative budgets.
Excludes: quantization accuracy, dequantization cost, workspace, allocator reserve, and communication. A memory dividend is not a throughput prediction.



Derivation: divide per-device free bytes by the per-device request footprint for each representation, then compare the integer capacities.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Q_
>>> result = PrecisionDividendModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, 1,
...     Q_("80 GB"), 1024, 8, Q_("2 byte"), Q_("1 byte"), Q_("2 byte"), Q_("1 byte"))
>>> result.max_batch_low >= result.max_batch
True

title: engine.solvers.context
text:
engine.solvers.context
Context-engineering solvers: what one agent request carries, and what it costs.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on serialized token counts: a budget by role against the window, one attention head’s softmax over fixed logits, a measured comprehension sweep, the input bill of a zoned layout under prefix reuse, compaction between two watermarks, the edits that retire a stale observation, and the cost per accepted task of a protected-field check. None models tokenization across joins, cache eviction, or a trained model’s attention.





Name
Description




AttentionDilutionModel
One head’s weight on a target key among keys whose logits stay fixed.


CompactionCadenceModel
Compaction between a trigger and a target watermark (hysteresis).


ContextBudgetModel
A request budgeted by role: S_sys + S_tools + S_state + S_obs <= S_max - K_max.


ContextInvalidationModel
Three edits that retire a superseded excerpt at the start of the trunk.


PrefixLayoutBillModel
Input bill of turns calls whose requests are ordered root, trunk, leaf.


ProtectedFieldCheckModel
Cost per accepted task with and without a protected-field check at each compaction.





engine.solvers.context.AttentionDilutionModel()
One head’s weight on a target key among keys whose logits stay fixed.
short_keys and long_keys count every key, the target included, at background_logit. The look-alike case counts competitors only: unrelated_keys at the background logit plus lookalike_keys at the higher lookalike_logit of text that shares the evidence’s identifiers. A sufficient condition for dilution, not a forecast of a trained model.





Name
Description




solve
Compare target attention mass under fixed-logit key populations.





engine.solvers.context.AttentionDilutionModel.solve(
    target_logit,
    background_logit,
    short_keys,
    long_keys,
    unrelated_keys=None,
    lookalike_keys=None,
    lookalike_logit=None,
)
Compare target attention mass under fixed-logit key populations.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_logit
float
Finite dimensionless logit of the target key.
required


background_logit
float
Finite dimensionless logit shared by ordinary competing keys.
required


short_keys
int
Positive total key count in the short case, including the target.
required


long_keys
int
Positive total key count in the long case, including the target.
required


unrelated_keys
int
Nonnegative competitor count, excluding the target, for the look-alike case.
None


lookalike_keys
int
Nonnegative look-alike competitor count; provide with unrelated_keys.
None


lookalike_logit
float
Finite logit of each look-alike; required when both competitor counts are supplied.
None














Name
Type
Description





AttentionDilutionResult
Dimensionless target weights and optional equivalent-key counts under the supplied logit populations.






Equation: Target mass is exp(z_target) / (exp(z_target) + sum_j n_j*exp(z_j)). Equivalent background keys equal n_look*exp(z_look-z_background).
Assumptions: The logits stay fixed when competitors are added. Each member of a population has the same logit; counts are not learned.
Excludes: Queries changing with context, positional effects, multiple heads, value aggregation, and any prediction of answer accuracy.



Derivation: The softmax denominator sums one exponential per key. Grouping identical logits gives n_j*exp(z_j); equating denominator contributions yields equivalent-key count. Helpers live in physics.context.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import AttentionDilutionModel
>>> result = AttentionDilutionModel().solve(1.0, 0.0, 2, 8)
>>> result.long_weight < result.short_weight
True






engine.solvers.context.CompactionCadenceModel()
Compaction between a trigger and a target watermark (hysteresis).
Each turn appends delta tokens; a pass fires on the first turn that reaches the trigger and resets the request to the target, so passes come every ceil((trigger - target) / delta) turns. The trigger is soft: the request can overshoot it by less than one append, and the output reserve must still fit. An optional alternate target prices a narrower gap.





Name
Description




solve
Trace fixed-growth context between compaction watermarks.





engine.solvers.context.CompactionCadenceModel.solve(
    window,
    output_reserve,
    target,
    trigger,
    tokens_per_turn,
    turns,
    alternate_target=None,
)
Trace fixed-growth context between compaction watermarks.











Name
Type
Description
Default




window
int
Positive context-window capacity, in tokens.
required


output_reserve
int
Nonnegative output-token reservation.
required


target
int
Nonnegative token count immediately after each compaction.
required


trigger
int
Token watermark above target that triggers a compaction.
required


tokens_per_turn
int
Positive token increment appended on every turn.
required


turns
int
Nonnegative number of appended turns to trace.
required


alternate_target
int
Alternative nonnegative reset length below trigger; None omits its trace.
None














Name
Type
Description





CompactionCadenceResult
Integer cycle length and token traces, pass counts, overshoot, and whether the peak request plus reservation fits the window.






Equation: Cycle length is ceil((trigger - target)/tokens_per_turn). Peak length is target + cycle*tokens_per_turn; passes equal turns//cycle.
Assumptions: Compaction instantly resets length to target after the turn that reaches the trigger. The trigger is soft and can be overshot.
Excludes: Summarizer runtime, fidelity loss, variable observation sizes, and interruptions while compaction runs.



Derivation: The first integer increment count reaching the trigger is the ceiling of its distance from target divided by tokens_per_turn. Repeating that reset yields the trace in _trace and the cycle helper in physics.context.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import CompactionCadenceModel
>>> result = CompactionCadenceModel().solve(100, 10, 20, 60, 10, 8)
>>> result.fits_window and result.passes > 0
True






engine.solvers.context.ContextBudgetModel()
A request budgeted by role: S_sys + S_tools + S_state + S_obs <= S_max - K_max.
Appending every tool result grows S_obs by delta per turn until the observation budget overflows, and resends the history, so the input bill grows quadratically. Selecting a fixed observation share keeps every request the same size and the bill linear. Bills assume no prefix reuse and, for the appending policy, a window large enough to admit every request.





Name
Description




solve
Compare appending and selecting observations within a token budget.





engine.solvers.context.ContextBudgetModel.solve(
    window,
    output_reserve,
    system_tokens,
    tool_tokens,
    state_tokens,
    observation_per_turn,
    selected_observation,
    turns,
    digest_tokens,
)
Compare appending and selecting observations within a token budget.











Name
Type
Description
Default




window
int
Positive total context-window capacity, in tokens.
required


output_reserve
int
Nonnegative reply reservation, in tokens, no larger than window.
required


system_tokens
int
Nonnegative serialized system-instruction count, in tokens.
required


tool_tokens
int
Nonnegative serialized tool-descriptor count, in tokens.
required


state_tokens
int
Nonnegative retained-state count, in tokens.
required


observation_per_turn
int
Positive count of observation tokens appended each turn.
required


selected_observation
int
Nonnegative observation tokens selected for each fixed-size request.
required


turns
int
Positive number of requests to account for.
required


digest_tokens
int
Positive tokens per digest, used for an alternative capacity calculation.
required














Name
Type
Description





ContextBudgetResult
Token budgets and per-turn request traces, integer overflow turns, cumulative token bills, and dimensionless ratios.






Equation: Observation budget is window - output_reserve - system_tokens - tool_tokens - state_tokens. Appending sums fixed + t*observation_per_turn for t=1..turns; selection sends turns*(fixed + selected_observation).
Assumptions: Counts are already serialized tokens. Fixed roles fit inside the input budget; selected requests are nonempty. The append bill counts all requested turns even when their sizes exceed the supplied window.
Excludes: Cache reuse, tokenization across joins, retrieval quality, compaction cost, and automatic rejection or truncation of oversized requests.



Derivation: Subtract reserved roles from a finite capacity, then sum an arithmetic progression for appending and a constant sequence for selection. The helpers in physics.context compute remaining capacity and integer fit.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ContextBudgetModel
>>> result = ContextBudgetModel().solve(100, 10, 5, 5, 10, 10, 10, 3, 5)
>>> result.append_bill > result.select_bill
True






engine.solvers.context.ContextInvalidationModel()
Three edits that retire a superseded excerpt at the start of the trunk.
Removing it or replacing it in place with a short marker changes the request right after the reused root, so every later token is prefilled again; appending a notice keeps the prefix and prefills only the notice, but leaves the stale tokens resident on every later call.





Name
Description




solve
Count cache suffixes for three ways to retire stale text.





engine.solvers.context.ContextInvalidationModel.solve(
    request_tokens,
    prefix_tokens,
    superseded_tokens,
    marker_tokens,
    notice_tokens,
)
Count cache suffixes for three ways to retire stale text.











Name
Type
Description
Default




request_tokens
int
Positive original request length, in tokens.
required


prefix_tokens
int
Nonnegative reusable prefix ending before the superseded passage.
required


superseded_tokens
int
Nonnegative passage length; prefix plus passage must fit the request.
required


marker_tokens
int
Nonnegative replacement-marker length.
required


notice_tokens
int
Positive length of a notice appended after the original request.
required














Name
Type
Description





ContextInvalidationResult
Total and newly prefilling suffix lengths in tokens for deletion, replacement, and append, plus a dimensionless suffix ratio.






Equation: Deletion leaves request_tokens - superseded_tokens; replacement adds marker_tokens. Their fresh suffix starts at prefix_tokens. Appending adds notice_tokens, all of which are new.
Assumptions: Cached prefix validity ends exactly at the first edited token. The appended notice leaves every original token resident.
Excludes: Semantic compliance with the notice, cache eviction, tokenization changes at edit boundaries, and the cost of editing.



Derivation: Subtract removed spans and add inserted spans to obtain total length. Subtract the unchanged prefix to obtain work requiring fresh prefill.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ContextInvalidationModel
>>> result = ContextInvalidationModel().solve(100, 20, 30, 5, 5)
>>> result.removed_total < result.replaced_total < result.appended_total
True






engine.solvers.context.PrefixLayoutBillModel()
Input bill of turns calls whose requests are ordered root, trunk, leaf.
With a volatile field first, no prefix is reused and every input token is billed at full price. Ordered by change rate, the first call is cold, each trunk rewrite prefills trunk and leaf, and every other call prefills only the leaf; reused tokens are billed at cached_fraction of the price. Assumes compatible cached state is retained; prices only input tokens.





Name
Description




solve
Price repeated requests with root, trunk, and leaf cache zones.





engine.solvers.context.PrefixLayoutBillModel.solve(
    turns,
    root_tokens,
    trunk_tokens,
    leaf_tokens,
    trunk_rewrites,
    input_price,
    cached_fraction,
)
Price repeated requests with root, trunk, and leaf cache zones.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Positive number of calls.
required


root_tokens
int
Nonnegative tokens in the unchanged root prefix.
required


trunk_tokens
int
Nonnegative tokens in the occasionally rewritten trunk.
required


leaf_tokens
int
Positive tokens in the per-call leaf.
required


trunk_rewrites
int
Number of trunk changes after the cold call, from zero through turns - 1.
required


input_price
Quantity
Nonnegative uncached price, convertible to USD/token; positive for cost ratios.
required


cached_fraction
float
Cached-input price as a fraction of uncached price, in [0, 1].
required














Name
Type
Description





PrefixLayoutBillResult
Token counts, dimensionless reuse and cost ratios, and USD-valued total and per-call bills for the two layouts.






Equation: Total input is turns*(root + trunk + leaf). Fresh prefill is root + trunk + leaf + trunk_rewrites*(trunk + leaf) + (turns - 1 - trunk_rewrites)*leaf; cached input is the remainder.
Assumptions: The first call is cold. Compatible cached state remains available, and each trunk rewrite invalidates all following tokens.
Excludes: Cache eviction, output-token bills, latency, and differences in answer quality between layouts.



Derivation: Partition calls into cold, trunk-rewrite, and leaf-only cases. Sum their newly computed tokens, then charge cached tokens at the stated price fraction. physics.context.calc_zoned_prefill_tokens owns the count.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import PrefixLayoutBillModel
>>> result = PrefixLayoutBillModel().solve(3, 20, 10, 5, 0, Q_(1, "USD/token"), 0.5)
>>> result.stable_cost < result.unstable_cost
True






engine.solvers.context.ProtectedFieldCheckModel()
Cost per accepted task with and without a protected-field check at each compaction.
Each of constraints is lost independently with loss_per_round in each of rounds; a lost constraint makes the task unacceptable, so acceptance is p_intact (1 - eps)^(n R). A check that detects detection of losses and repairs them leaves eps (1 - detection) per round and adds check_cost per round to the attempt.





Name
Description




solve
Compare acceptance cost with checks at context compactions.





engine.solvers.context.ProtectedFieldCheckModel.solve(
    constraints,
    loss_per_round,
    rounds,
    acceptance_if_intact,
    attempt_cost,
    detection,
    check_cost_per_round,
    survival_floor,
    target_survival=None,
)
Compare acceptance cost with checks at context compactions.











Name
Type
Description
Default




constraints
int
Positive number of protected constraints exposed at each compaction.
required


loss_per_round
float
Independent loss probability per constraint per round, in (0, 1).
required


rounds
int
Positive number of compaction rounds.
required


acceptance_if_intact
float
Task acceptance probability conditional on intact constraints, in (0, 1].
required


attempt_cost
Quantity
Positive unchecked attempt cost, convertible to USD.
required


detection
float
Fraction of losses detected and repaired, in [0, 1); exact one is outside the horizon-ratio calculation.
required


check_cost_per_round
Quantity
Nonnegative cost of each check in USD.
required


survival_floor
float
Probability in (0, 1) used to locate the first unacceptable round count.
required


target_survival
float
Desired intact probability in (0, 1); None omits the inverse loss budget.
None














Name
Type
Description





ProtectedFieldCheckResult
Dimensionless survival and acceptance probabilities, USD-valued scalar costs, exposure counts, and optional maximum loss probability.






Equation: With N=constraints*rounds and loss e, survival is (1-e)**N. Checking changes e to e*(1-detection) and adds rounds*check_cost_per_round to attempt cost. Effective cost divides attempt cost by acceptance.
Assumptions: Losses are independent; all detected losses are repaired. Every constraint must remain intact, and checking has no other side effects.
Excludes: Correlated loss, imperfect repairs, false alarms, and measured quality improvements; detection and conditional acceptance are inputs.



Derivation: Multiply survival probabilities across constraint-round exposures, then multiply by conditional acceptance. Expected repeated-attempt cost follows the geometric identity implemented in physics.agents.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ProtectedFieldCheckModel
>>> result = ProtectedFieldCheckModel().solve(2, 0.1, 3, 0.9, Q_(1, "USD"), 0.5, Q_(0.1, "USD"), 0.8)
>>> result.survival_checked > result.survival_unchecked
True

ContextBudgetResult
Token budgets and per-turn request traces, integer overflow turns, cumulative token bills, and dimensionless ratios.






Equation: Observation budget is window - output_reserve - system_tokens - tool_tokens - state_tokens. Appending sums fixed + t*observation_per_turn for t=1..turns; selection sends turns*(fixed + selected_observation).
Assumptions: Counts are already serialized tokens. Fixed roles fit inside the input budget; selected requests are nonempty. The append bill counts all requested turns even when their sizes exceed the supplied window.
Excludes: Cache reuse, tokenization across joins, retrieval quality, compaction cost, and automatic rejection or truncation of oversized requests.



Derivation: Subtract reserved roles from a finite capacity, then sum an arithmetic progression for appending and a constant sequence for selection. The helpers in physics.context compute remaining capacity and integer fit.

>>> result = ContextBudgetModel().solve(100, 10, 5, 5, 10, 10, 10, 3, 5)
>>> result.append_bill > result.select_bill
True






engine.solvers.context.ContextInvalidationModel()
Three edits that retire a superseded excerpt at the start of the trunk.
Removing it or replacing it in place with a short marker changes the request right after the reused root, so every later token is prefilled again; appending a notice keeps the prefix and prefills only the notice, but leaves the stale tokens resident on every later call.

ContextInvalidationResult
Total and newly prefilling suffix lengths in tokens for deletion, replacement, and append, plus a dimensionless suffix ratio.






Equation: Deletion leaves request_tokens - superseded_tokens; replacement adds marker_tokens. Their fresh suffix starts at prefix_tokens. Appending adds notice_tokens, all of which are new.
Assumptions: Cached prefix validity ends exactly at the first edited token. The appended notice leaves every original token resident.
Excludes: Semantic compliance with the notice, cache eviction, tokenization changes at edit boundaries, and the cost of editing.



Derivation: Subtract removed spans and add inserted spans to obtain total length. Subtract the unchanged prefix to obtain work requiring fresh prefill.

engine.solvers.context.PrefixLayoutBillModel()
Input bill of turns calls whose requests are ordered root, trunk, leaf.
With a volatile field first, no prefix is reused and every input token is billed at full price. Ordered by change rate, the first call is cold, each trunk rewrite prefills trunk and leaf, and every other call prefills only the leaf; reused tokens are billed at cached_fraction of the price. Assumes compatible cached state is retained; prices only input tokens.

Type

PrefixLayoutBillResult
Token counts, dimensionless reuse and cost ratios, and USD-valued total and per-call bills for the two layouts.






Equation: Total input is turns*(root + trunk + leaf). Fresh prefill is root + trunk + leaf + trunk_rewrites*(trunk + leaf) + (turns - 1 - trunk_rewrites)*leaf; cached input is the remainder.
Assumptions: The first call is cold. Compatible cached state remains available, and each trunk rewrite invalidates all following tokens.

>>> result.stable_cost < result.unstable_cost

engine.solvers.context.ProtectedFieldCheckModel()
Cost per accepted task with and without a protected-field check at each compaction.
Each of constraints is lost independently with loss_per_round in each of rounds; a lost constraint makes the task unacceptable, so acceptance is p_intact (1 - eps)^(n R). A check that detects detection of losses and repairs them leaves eps (1 - detection) per round and adds check_cost per round to the attempt.





Name
Description




solve
Compare acceptance cost with checks at context compactions.

    constraints,
    loss_per_round,
    rounds,
    acceptance_if_intact,
    attempt_cost,
    detection,
    check_cost_per_round,
    survival_floor,
    target_survival=None,
)

Name
Type
Description





ProtectedFieldCheckResult
Dimensionless survival and acceptance probabilities, USD-valued scalar costs, exposure counts, and optional maximum loss probability.






Equation: With N=constraints*rounds and loss e, survival is (1-e)**N. Checking changes e to e*(1-detection) and adds rounds*check_cost_per_round to attempt cost. Effective cost divides attempt cost by acceptance.
Assumptions: Losses are independent; all detected losses are repaired. Every constraint must remain intact, and checking has no other side effects.
Excludes: Correlated loss, imperfect repairs, false alarms, and measured quality improvements; detection and conditional acceptance are inputs.



Derivation: Multiply survival probabilities across constraint-round exposures, then multiply by conditional acceptance. Expected repeated-attempt cost follows the geometric identity implemented in physics.agents.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import ProtectedFieldCheckModel
>>> result = ProtectedFieldCheckModel().solve(2, 0.1, 3, 0.9, Q_(1, "USD"), 0.5, Q_(0.1, "USD"), 0.8)
>>> result.survival_checked > result.survival_unchecked
True

Position errors from a timing error and an angle error, for a target at distance.
A timestamp off by dt places the target v dt along the travel and, while turning at omega, misorients the view by omega dt, which at range is d omega dt sideways. An angle error theta moves the target d theta sideways (calc_lever_arm_error, small angle).

Type
Description





TimingAttitudeErrorResult
Translation and lateral errors in millimeters, timestamp-induced orientation error in milliradians, and an optional dimensionless share.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_lever_arm_error : Small-angle displacement.



Equation: translation = speed*timing_error; misorientation = yaw_rate* timing_error; timing lateral error = distance*misorientation; independent angle error produces distance*angle_error.
Assumptions: Translation and yaw remain constant over the timestamp offset. Angular errors are small; signs of supplied errors are retained.
Excludes: Error covariance, sensor fusion, acceleration, and a combined probabilistic error bound.



Derivation: Integrate constant velocity and angular velocity over the time offset, then multiply each angular error in radians by its lever arm.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = TimingAttitudeErrorModel().solve(Q_("1 m/s"), Q_("0 rad/s"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("10 ms"), Q_("0 rad"))
>>> r.timing_travel == Q_("10 mm") and r.angle_lateral == Q_("0 mm")
True

title: SingleAcceleratorLlmServiceScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
An LLM chat service on one accelerator: latency, KV residency, request rate, and token cost.
ServingModel gives TTFT and the weight footprint. TPOT combines the weight and request-cache transfer time with the solver’s ITL residual beyond its memory floor; that residual includes compute dominance as well as framework overhead. The KV reserve over cache bytes per token sets resident requests. Request rate is the smaller of prefill admission and residency turnover (Little’s law at the batch-one request time). The request-time calculation uses full-context TTFT; the separate ttft property uses prompt-only TTFT. Token billing counts prompt and output tokens.


Equation: ServingModel supplies prompt/full-context timing; request rate is min(prefill_rate/prompt_tokens, resident_requests/request_time).
Assumptions: Full-context cache size remains fixed throughout modeled decode; cache reserve and external admission rate are supplied assumptions.
Excludes: Queueing and dynamic batching. The ITL-minus-memory-floor residual may include compute cost, and request_time uses full-context TTFT rather than the prompt-only ttft property.



Derivation: the scenario composes mlsysim.physics.serving.calc_littles_law_rate, mlsysim.physics.transfer_time, mlsysim.solvers.ServingModel. Their contracts supply the underlying equations; property equations show the remaining unit conversions and accounting.

title: Sustainability Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

BatteryBudgetScenario: A continuous power_draw against a battery and a required runtime.
CarbonPricedPlacementScenario: A run of it_energy on fleet placed among regions with and without a carbon price.
CascadeEnergyScenario: An edge model on every input, escalating a fraction to a cloud model over a radio link.
CoolingScenario: Coolant flow that carries heat_load at temperature_rise.
DataMovementEnergyScenario: One weight of bytes_per_param used for flops_per_param FLOPs at stated per-op energies.
DemandReboundScenario: Per-unit energy scaled by a factor (or by a unit-price ratio) while volume scales by another.
DevelopmentSweepScenario: A sweep of candidates runs, each costing relative_cost of the final run.
DutyCycledPowerScenario: An always-on detector, a stage active a share of the time, and a full model run per event.
EmbodiedPaybackScenario: A replacement for device that does its work with saved_fraction less energy, on named grids.
EnergyPerInferenceScenario: Energy per inference across tiers: solver-derived device energies plus stated anchors.
FacilityPowerScenario: devices accelerators at device_power in racks shaped like rack, at pue.
GridPlacementScenario: One facility energy placed on each named grid, with an optional fractional energy cut.
OffloadEnergyScenario: Energy to send payload by radio against running the model locally.
OperationalCarbonScenario: Operational carbon = energy x PUE x grid intensity.
OutageScenario: A failure domain of failed_devices down for repair_time during a job on fleet.
PeriodicInferencePowerScenario: workload run once per period on hardware at its peak precision rate, idling between runs.
PowerTransientScenario: A barrier-aligned load step on hardware and across n_devices.
PueRetrofitScenario: A fixed IT load moved from pue_before to pue_after for period at an electricity price.
RepeatedWorkEnergyScenario: fleet’s accelerators at rated power, rolled back by each named interval.
RunFootprintScenario: A training run of device_hours on devices of device: energy, carbon, embodied carbon, water.
ServiceLifeExtensionScenario: A hardware service life extended from short_life to long_life.
ServingCrossoverScenario: Serving requests_per_day at energy_per_request against a one-time energy.
ThermalCeilingScenario: A model’s sustained power against a passively cooled device’s ceiling, before and after a reduction.
TokenEnergyScenario: Joules per generated token: node power over aggregate token rate, well used and poorly used.
WaterUseScenario: An IT load held for period at each named WUE.

engine.solvers.neural
Neural computation solvers: a dense network’s counts, and one training epoch’s time.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




DenseNetworkModel
Parameters, operations, bytes moved, and memory of a dense network at one batch size.


EpochOverheadModel
One training epoch of a small network: arithmetic and data movement against fixed per-operation overhead.





engine.solvers.neural.DenseNetworkModel()
Parameters, operations, bytes moved, and memory of a dense network at one batch size.
The network is its layer widths. Forward work counts each layer’s matrix multiply (2 B n_in n_out) and its bias add and activation (2 B n_out). Traffic assumes each layer runs as its own kernel: the weights are read once, the input and output cross memory once, and each hidden activation is written and read back. Training keeps every layer’s output for the backward pass and holds a gradient per parameter plus the optimizer’s state; inference keeps only the weights and the largest adjacent pair of activation buffers.
Literature Source: 1. Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline” (operations per byte moved). 2. Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams (1986), backpropagation (two products per layer).





Name
Description

    batch_size,
    bytes_per_value,
    optimizer_bytes_per_parameter,
    training_examples=None,
)

DenseNetworkResult
Parameter and FLOP counts, byte footprints, FLOP/byte intensity, and training/inference ratios. No hardware capacity or feasibility is tested.






mlsysim.physics.neural.calc_dense_forward_flops : Forward-work accounting. mlsysim.physics.neural.calc_training_state : Weight, gradient, optimizer bytes.



Equation: layer weights = n_in*n_out, biases = n_out, and forward work = 2*B*sum(n_in*n_out) + 2*B*sum(n_out). Training memory adds weights, gradients, optimizer state, and saved activations. Inference memory retains weights and the largest adjacent activation-buffer pair.
Assumptions: fully connected layers execute separately. Traffic includes weight reads plus layer inputs/outputs; hidden activations cross memory between kernels. Training-step FLOPs count matrix products, whereas the reported forward FLOPs also include bias and activation work.
Excludes: kernel fusion, reuse in caches, optimizer arithmetic, activation checkpointing, and device workspaces. Layer widths and batch size are cast to integers, so callers must supply integer counts rather than fractions.



Derivation: count the coefficients of each dense matrix and bias vector; a multiply-accumulate contributes two FLOPs. Saved tensors and state arrays are counted by element cardinality times representation size.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = DenseNetworkModel().solve([2, 3, 1], 2, Q_("4 byte"), Q_("8 byte"))
>>> result.parameters == (2 * 3 + 3) + (3 * 1 + 1)
True
>>> result.training_memory > result.inference_memory
True






engine.solvers.neural.EpochOverheadModel()
One training epoch of a small network: arithmetic and data movement against fixed per-operation overhead.
Work: steps x FLOPs per step at the attainable rate, the roofline’s min(peak, bandwidth x intensity) at the network’s batch intensity. Overhead: steps x operations launched per step x a fixed cost per operation, the framework’s dispatch on the host and dispatch plus a kernel launch on the accelerator. Energy: DRAM energy for the bytes behind one FLOP, against the energy of that FLOP.
Literature Source: 1. Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline”. 2. Horowitz (2014), “Computing’s energy problem” (per-op and per-byte energy).





Name
Description

Compare epoch work and fixed launch overhead on two devices.

    network_batch1,
    host,
    accelerator,
    precision,
    dispatch,
    launch,
    steps,
    dram_energy_per_byte,
    flop_energy,
)

Name
Type
Description





EpochOverheadResult
Per-device attainable FLOP/s, memory bandwidth, intensity ridge, work/overhead/total times in ms, and dimensionless speed and energy ratios. This result does not check memory residency.






mlsysim.physics.neural.calc_training_step_ops : Modeled launches per step.



Equation: rate = min(precision_peak, bandwidth*intensity); work_time = steps*training_step_flops/rate; overhead_time = steps*ops_per_step * per_operation_time. Host per-operation time is dispatch; accelerator time is dispatch + launch. Movement/arithmetic energy = energy_per_byte / (intensity*energy_per_flop).
Assumptions: a common intensity represents epoch work, and overhead adds serially to arithmetic time. Each step has the operation count returned by calc_training_step_ops for the layer count.
Excludes: overlap of launch and work, actual kernel traces, input loading, clock variation, and empirical power measurements.



Derivation: the slower of compute and byte transfer limits the attainable rate; dividing work by that rate gives time. Independent launch costs add per operation, and energy rates convert bytes/FLOP into an energy ratio.



>>> from mlsysim import Hardware, Q_
>>> network = DenseNetworkModel().solve([2, 3, 1], 1, Q_("4 byte"), Q_("8 byte"))
>>> result = EpochOverheadModel().solve(network, network, Hardware.Cloud.H100,
...     Hardware.Cloud.H100, "fp32", Q_("1 us"), Q_("0 us"), 1,
...     Q_("1 pJ/byte"), Q_("1 pJ/flop"))
>>> result.total_time["host"] == result.total_time["accelerator"]
True

Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/demonstrations.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A state space of state_components axes cut into bins per axis, against the records fleet robots log at log_rate for duration.


Equation: Cells=bins**sum(state_components); coverage upper bound=fleet*rate*duration/cells.
Assumptions: Uniform axis discretization and at most one newly occupied cell per recorded observation.
Excludes: Actual occupancy distribution, repeated-state correction, and proof that a grid represents task coverage.



Derivation: The Cartesian product of equally binned state axes contains bins raised to the summed dimension count. At most one new cell can be represented by each record, so records divided by cells is only an upper coverage bound.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.

title: LifecycleTcoScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Monthly lifecycle cost in four terms (training, inference, data, iteration), each counted once.


Equation: Total monthly cost sums the supplied category amounts; shares divide each category by the total.
Assumptions: Categories are mutually exclusive, exhaustive for the chosen accounting boundary, and total cost is positive.
Excludes: Capital discounting and unlisted lifecycle activities.



Derivation: Each monthly category is an explicitly supplied, nonoverlapping cost component. Adding those components gives total cost, division by total gives category shares, and comparison in a common currency/time unit identifies the largest component.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.StartupOneModelTco
>>> abs(sum(s.shares.values()) - 1) < 1e-12
True






Name
Description




dominant
Name of the category with the largest monthly USD contribution.


monthly



shares
Dimensionless category fractions of the total monthly cost.


total
Monthly USD cost summed across the declared lifecycle categories.









Name
Description




ratios_to
This budget’s terms (and total) over another’s.





engine.scenario_types.LifecycleTcoScenario.ratios_to(other)
This budget’s terms (and total) over another’s.
Equation: Divide each matching monthly category by the other scenario category; add total / other.total under the total key.




Type: Dict[str, Quantity].
Declared default: required.

Monthly USD cost summed across the declared lifecycle categories.
Equation: sum(monthly.values(), Q_(0, 'USD/month')).to('USD/month').

Dimensionless category fractions of the total monthly cost.

Equation: max(monthly, key=lambda k: monthly[k].to('USD/month').magnitude).

title: solvers.ScalingModel
text:
solvers.ScalingModel()
Analyzes the ‘Scaling Physics’ of model training (Chinchilla Laws).
This model determines the optimal model size (P) and dataset size (D) given a compute budget (C), following the compute-optimal training regime where D ≈ 20P.
Literature Source: 1. Hoffmann et al. (2022), “Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models.” 2. Kaplan et al. (2020), “Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models.” 3. McCandlish et al. (2018), “An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training.”





Name
Description




solve
Allocate a training compute budget between parameters and tokens.





solvers.ScalingModel.solve(compute_budget, target_model_size=None)
Allocate a training compute budget between parameters and tokens.











Name
Type
Description
Default




compute_budget
Quantity
Finite positive training work in FLOPs, or a finite positive duration interpreted as reference-H100 compute time at the declared sustained efficiency. Any compatible FLOP prefix is accepted and normalized before calculation.
required


target_model_size
Quantity
Finite positive fixed parameter count. If omitted, use the registered compute-optimal tokens-per-parameter ratio.
None














Name
Type
Description





ScalingResult
Modeled parameter and token counts, compute budget, and dimensionless tokens per parameter. The result does not include a quality estimate or a memory-feasibility decision.






Equation: C = k P D, where k is the registered compute coefficient. With D = r P, P = sqrt(C / (k r)); when P is fixed, D = C / (k P). A time input becomes C = duration * reference_peak * reference_MFU.
Assumptions: parameter-dominated dense training work and a constant registered optimal token ratio. The time conversion uses a declared reference accelerator rather than an arbitrary fleet supplied by a user.
Excludes: inference cost, data-quality variation, architecture-dependent loss prediction, attention work, and hardware memory capacity.



Hoffmann et al. (2022), “Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models.” https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556 (bibliography key: hoffmann2022chinchilla). The fixed-ratio allocation is the package’s simplified accounting form.



>>> result = ScalingModel().solve(Q_(1200000, "flop"))
>>> result.optimal_parameters.to("count").magnitude > 0
True
>>> result.optimal_tokens.to("count").magnitude > 0
True

A data loader feeding one accelerator over its host link.
workers loader processes each prepare prefetch_factor batches of batch_size samples. A sample is raw_sample bytes as decoded pixels and model_sample bytes as the tensor copied to the device; the accelerator consumes consume_rate samples a second. Copy times are bandwidth-only lower bounds; step_times are compute times a serial copy is compared with.

Assumptions: Constant consumption rate and ideal bandwidth for complete model-tensor copies.
Excludes: Worker scheduling, contention, and copy/compute overlap.

title: solvers.TopologyModel
text:
solvers.TopologyModel()
Models bisection bandwidth for different network topologies (Wall 10).
This model calculates the effective bandwidth available to collective communication operations based on the physical network topology. Different topologies trade cost against bisection bandwidth — the minimum bandwidth across any cut that divides the network in half.
Literature Source: 1. Leiserson (1985), “Fat-Trees: Universal Networks for Hardware-Efficient Supercomputing.” (Fat-tree bisection bandwidth.) 2. Kim et al. (2008), “Technology-Driven, Highly-Scalable Dragonfly Topology.” (Dragonfly topology model.) 3. Dally & Towles (2003), “Principles and Practices of Interconnection Networks.” (Torus and ring analysis.)





Name
Description




solve
Solve for effective network bandwidth under a given topology.





solvers.TopologyModel.solve(fabric, topology='fat_tree', num_nodes=64)
Solve for effective network bandwidth under a given topology.











Name
Type
Description
Default




fabric
NetworkFabric
The network fabric specification (link bandwidth, oversubscription).
required


topology
str
Network topology (‘fat_tree’, ‘dragonfly’, ‘torus_3d’, ‘ring’).
'fat_tree'


num_nodes
int
Number of nodes in the network.
64














Name
Type
Description





TopologyResult
Effective bandwidth, bisection fraction, and average hops.






Equation: effective bandwidth is link_bandwidth * beta / oversubscription; the reported bisection bandwidth multiplies it by num_nodes / 2. Ring beta is 2/N; three-dimensional torus beta is 2*N**(-1/3). Assumptions: positive node count and oversubscription, homogeneous links, and an aggregate bisection approximation. Other supported topologies use class-level beta and hop conventions; unknown names fall back to beta one. Excludes: routing simulation, packet contention, and physical cut-link counts. The absolute bisection output is normalized to a fat-tree reference cut; for a ring it counts one link-equivalent rather than two physical cut links.



Derivation: normalize cross-section link capacity by fleet size, then apply the declared oversubscription ratio to the shared capacity.



>>> from mlsysim import Systems
>>> result = TopologyModel().solve(Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_HDR,
...     topology="ring", num_nodes=8)
>>> result.bisection_bw_fraction == 2 / 8
True

title: OwnVsRentScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Owning gpus accelerators against renting them at rent_rate per GPU-hour for utilization of every hour, over years.
Owning pays the nodes, network, and facility up front, then a running cost per year: a fixed opex_per_year and staffing_per_year, plus electricity for power at pue and electricity_price. Electricity is charged every hour unless energy_scales_with_use, when it is drawn only while busy. A year is 8,760 hours and a month one twelfth of it, the book’s convention.


Equation: Ownership is upfront + years*annual_operation; rental is gpus*rate*annual_hours*utilization*years.
Assumptions: Constant prices, annual duration convention, divisible node sizing, and the declared utilization/power policy.
Excludes: Discounting, financing, residual resale value, price escalation, and utilization uncertainty.



Derivation: Initial purchases are paid once, whereas operating and rental charges repeat over the ownership horizon. Separating fixed annual costs from utilization-dependent electricity makes the break-even utilization algebra explicit; mlsysim.physics.economics.calc_ownership_breakeven_utilization and calc_rent_crossover perform the corresponding inversions.

>>> s = Scenarios.OwnVsRentH100Cluster1K
>>> s.owned_total.to("USD").magnitude > 0

Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/proposers.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One fresh evaluation of machine’s intent model on its application processor.
Each input left as None takes the machine’s deployed value: the weight precision, the input and action token counts, and the decoding mode. The sustained-bandwidth fraction and compute utilization are the machine’s.


Equation: evaluation = VlaEvaluationModel.solve(model, processor, selected precision and token counts, supplied efficiencies).
Assumptions: An omitted override takes its value from the machine configuration; compute and bandwidth efficiencies remain declared inputs.
Excludes: Scheduling and control guarantees beyond the underlying VLA model contract.



Derivation: This configuration forwards its stored inputs to mlsysim.solvers.VlaEvaluationModel.solve. The solver contract records the equations and their provenance.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
