title: engine.solvers.facility
text:
engine.solvers.facility
Facility solvers: power transients, coolant flow, and outage cost.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable.





Name
Description




CoolantFlowModel
Coolant flow that carries a heat load at a stated temperature rise.


OutageCostModel
Idle cost of a failure domain going down during a synchronous job.


PowerTransientModel
One accelerator’s load step and the ramp a synchronized cluster produces.





engine.solvers.facility.CoolantFlowModel()
Coolant flow that carries a heat load at a stated temperature rise.
m_dot = Q / (c_p dT), then volume flow from the coolant’s density. Water’s specific heat is about four times air’s and its density about 830 times, so it carries the same heat in thousands of times less volume.





Name
Description




solve
Calculate coolant mass and volume flow for a steady heat load.





engine.solvers.facility.CoolantFlowModel.solve(
    heat_load,
    temperature_rise,
    coolant='air',
)
Calculate coolant mass and volume flow for a steady heat load.











Name
Type
Description
Default




heat_load
Quantity
Nonnegative heat delivered to the coolant in W.
required


temperature_rise
Quantity
Positive inlet-to-outlet temperature difference in K.
required


coolant
str
Either “air” or “water”; default “air” selects its registered density and specific heat.
'air'














Name
Type
Description





CoolantFlowResult
Required mass flow in kg/s and volume flow in L/s.






mlsysim.physics.thermal.calc_coolant_mass_flow : Apply the sensible-heat energy balance.



Equation: mass_flow = heat_load / (specific_heat * temperature_rise); volume_flow = mass_flow / density.
Assumptions: Steady sensible heat transport and constant coolant properties from physics.constants.
Excludes: Pump or fan power, latent heat, pressure losses, and heat-exchanger effectiveness.



Derivation: The steady energy balance Q_dot = m_dot c_p delta_T sets mass flow; dividing by density converts mass flow to volume flow.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> a = CoolantFlowModel().solve(Q_(1, "kW"), Q_(10, "K"), "water")
>>> b = CoolantFlowModel().solve(Q_(2, "kW"), Q_(10, "K"), "water")
>>> b.mass_flow == 2 * a.mass_flow
True






engine.solvers.facility.OutageCostModel()
Idle cost of a failure domain going down during a synchronous job.
The direct cost counts only the devices in the failed domain. A synchronous job that cannot continue idles every device, and rolling back to the last checkpoint adds the lost work to the repair window.





Name
Description




solve
Price repair downtime for a failed domain and its synchronous job.





engine.solvers.facility.OutageCostModel.solve(
    failed_devices,
    job_devices,
    repair_time,
    device_hour_rate,
    rollback_times=None,
)
Price repair downtime for a failed domain and its synchronous job.











Name
Type
Description
Default




failed_devices
int
Nonnegative number of failed devices, no greater than job_devices.
required


job_devices
int
Nonnegative number of devices reserved by the job.
required


repair_time
Quantity
Nonnegative repair duration in hours or compatible time units.
required


device_hour_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative rental or opportunity-cost rate in USD/hour per device.
required


rollback_times
dict of str to Quantity
Named nonnegative lost-work durations added to repair time; None omits rollback scenarios.
None














Name
Type
Description





OutageCostResult
Direct failed-device cost, whole-job idle cost, and each rollback-adjusted job cost, as USD scalars.






Equation: direct_cost = failed_devices * rate * repair_hours; job_cost = job_devices  rate  repair_hours; rollback_cost[k] = job_devices * rate * (repair_hours + rollback_hours[k]).
Assumptions: The complete synchronous job is idle during repair, and every reserved device has the same hourly cost.
Excludes: Redundant operation, partial progress, revenue loss, and replacement equipment cost.



Derivation: Device-hours equal the number of reserved devices times unavailable hours. Multiplication by the hourly rate gives each cost.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = OutageCostModel().solve(1, 4, Q_(2, "hour"), Q_(3, "USD/hour"))
>>> r.job_cost == 4 * r.direct_cost
True






engine.solvers.facility.PowerTransientModel()
One accelerator’s load step and the ramp a synchronized cluster produces.
When a collective barrier releases every device from communication into dense arithmetic, each one steps from its communication-phase power toward its design power at once. On one device’s core rail the step is a current change dP / V, and the board loop’s inductance turns a fast edge into a voltage droop L dI/dt. Across the cluster the same step, aligned by the barrier, is a power ramp the facility supplies must follow.





Name
Description




solve
Calculate device voltage droop and a synchronized fleet power ramp.





engine.solvers.facility.PowerTransientModel.solve(
    high_power,
    low_power,
    rail_voltage,
    loop_inductance,
    rise_times,
    n_devices,
    ramp_window,
)
Calculate device voltage droop and a synchronized fleet power ramp.











Name
Type
Description
Default




high_power
Quantity
Power after the step in W; at least low_power.
required


low_power
Quantity
Power before the step in W; nonnegative.
required


rail_voltage
Quantity
Positive core supply voltage in V.
required


loop_inductance
Quantity
Nonnegative supply-loop inductance in H.
required


rise_times
dict of str to Quantity
Named positive current-rise times in seconds.
required


n_devices
int
Nonnegative number of synchronized devices.
required


ramp_window
Quantity
Positive facility ramp duration in seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





PowerTransientResult
Device step in W and A, droop in mV and voltage fractions, fleet step in kW, and ramp in GW/s.






mlsysim.physics.power.calc_rail_current_step : Compute current change from a power step. mlsysim.physics.power.calc_inductive_droop : Compute ideal inductive voltage droop.



Equation: dP = high_power - low_power; dI = dP / V; droop = L dI / dt; fleet ramp = n_devices dP / ramp_window.
Assumptions: All devices share one power step and change state together. Each rise time is a separate scenario.
Excludes: Regulator feedback, capacitance, parasitic resistance, and facility supply dynamics. A droop estimate is not a board safety assessment.



Derivation: Power P = VI gives the current change at fixed rail voltage; the ideal inductor relation V = L dI/dt gives droop magnitude. Summing identical load steps gives the fleet ramp.



>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> r = PowerTransientModel().solve(Q_(200, "W"), Q_(100, "W"),
...     Q_(1, "V"), Q_(1, "nH"), {"edge": Q_(1, "us")}, 2, Q_(1, "s"))
>>> r.current_step == Q_(100, "A")
True

title: physics.fine_tuning
text:
physics.fine_tuning
Fine-tuning on serialized trajectories: weighting, packing, and preference pairs.
Closed forms behind supervised and preference fine-tuning of a policy on recorded trajectories (added 2026-10-20). Each takes stated counts: selected target tokens per example, stored example lengths against a fixed buffer, or log-probability sums of two scored records. None models a trained network. The solvers in engine/solvers/fine_tuning.py compose them.





Name
Description




calc_example_average_share
Calculate a group’s share of an example-averaged loss.


calc_first_fit_decreasing
Pack example lengths using the first-fit-decreasing heuristic.


calc_preference_pair
Evaluate the DPO loss and coefficients for one preference pair.


calc_token_average_shares
Calculate each example’s share of a token-averaged loss.





physics.fine_tuning.calc_example_average_share(group_examples, total_examples)
Calculate a group’s share of an example-averaged loss.











Name
Type
Description
Default




group_examples
int
Number of records in the group, between zero and total_examples.
required


total_examples
int
Positive total number of records.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless fraction of equal-weight example losses assigned to the group.






Equation: share = group_examples / total_examples.
Assumptions: Each record contributes one mean loss, irrespective of its token count.
Excludes: Within-record loss variation and validation of group membership.
Splitting a trajectory into k records gives it k times the weight of one unsplit record when all record means receive equal weight.



Derivation: a group of k equal-weight records contributes k of N terms to the example average.



>>> calc_example_average_share(2, 8)
0.25




physics.fine_tuning.calc_first_fit_decreasing(lengths, capacity)
Pack example lengths using the first-fit-decreasing heuristic.











Name
Type
Description
Default




lengths
iterable of int
Nonnegative example lengths in tokens, each no larger than capacity.
required


capacity
int
Positive token capacity of each buffer.
required














Name
Type
Description





list of int
Token load of each allocated buffer, in buffer-creation order.






Equation: Sort lengths in descending order; place each length n in the first buffer whose current load plus n does not exceed capacity.
Assumptions: Examples cannot be split and buffer capacities are identical.
Excludes: Optimal bin packing, sequence-boundary overhead, and attention masking.



Derivation: this is the explicit first-fit-decreasing packing procedure, a heuristic rather than a claim of optimal allocation.



>>> calc_first_fit_decreasing([6, 4, 3, 3], 10)
[10, 6]




physics.fine_tuning.calc_preference_pair(
    policy_preferred,
    reference_preferred,
    policy_dispreferred,
    reference_dispreferred,
    beta,
)
Evaluate the DPO loss and coefficients for one preference pair.











Name
Type
Description
Default




policy_preferred
float
Policy log-probability sum for the preferred record, in natural-log units.
required


reference_preferred
float

site’s unloaded permission tick with a share of it slowed slowdown times.
The tick may stretch to bound (default the declared WCET); the break-even share is (bound / unloaded - 1) / (slowdown - 1) (calc_stall_share_breakeven).

title: solvers.SeriesFailureModel
text:
solvers.SeriesFailureModel()
Failure interval of a synchronous job built from heterogeneous components.
Any single component failure stops the job, so failure rates add (a series system with independent, exponentially distributed failures). Each component is stated per node, with its MTTF and its count per node; its share per device is count / devices_per_node / MTTF. A redundant part that cannot fail the node singly (an N+M power supply) enters with count 0. Added 2026-10-20.





Name
Description




solve
Aggregate heterogeneous component hazards for a synchronous job.





solvers.SeriesFailureModel.solve(
    n_devices,
    devices_per_node,
    component_mttf,
    per_node,
)
Aggregate heterogeneous component hazards for a synchronous job.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_devices
int
Positive accelerator count in the job.
required


devices_per_node
int
Positive accelerator count per node.
required


component_mttf
dict of str to Quantity
Positive component MTTFs in hours or compatible units.
required


per_node
dict of str to int
Nonnegative component counts per node, with the same keys as component_mttf. Use zero for parts whose single failure cannot stop the node.
required














Name
Type
Description





SeriesFailureResult
Per-device component rates, total device and system rates in inverse hours, MTBF in hours, and failures per day.






Equation: component_rate[k] = per_node[k] / (devices_per_node * MTTF[k]); system_rate = n_devices * sum(component_rate); MTBF = 1/system_rate.
Assumptions: Independent exponential component failures; any included component failure stops the entire job. At least one component rate must be positive.
Excludes: Fault correlation, shared infrastructure, and explicit redundant failure combinations.



Derivation: Summing independent exponential hazards gives the series-system rate. Per-node rates are divided by devices per node and multiplied by the job’s device count.



>>> r = SeriesFailureModel().solve(8, 4, {"gpu": Q_(100, "hour")}, {"gpu": 4})
>>> r.mtbf == Q_(12.5, "hour")
True

title: solvers.StereoDepthErrorModel
text:
solvers.StereoDepthErrorModel()
One-sigma stereo depth error against range, and where it spends each clearance.
sigma_z = z^2 sigma_d / (f b) grows with squared range; the range at which one sigma equals a clearance C is sqrt(C f b / sigma_d). Adding one sigma to a clearance kept along the viewing ray is the shortcut inset; an unmodeled baseline change db biases depth by z db / b.





Name
Description




solve
Propagate stereo disparity uncertainty into range-dependent depth error.





solvers.StereoDepthErrorModel.solve(
    baseline,
    focal_length_px,
    disparity_sigma_px,
    near_range,
    far_range,
    target_range,
    ray_clearance,
    loc_allowance,
    side_clearance,
    baseline_change,
    bias_range,
)
Propagate stereo disparity uncertainty into range-dependent depth error.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive camera separation, in length units.
required


focal_length_px
float
Positive rectified-camera focal length, in pixels.
required


disparity_sigma_px
float
Positive disparity standard deviation, in pixels.
required


near_range
Quantity
Positive near comparison depth, in length units.
required


far_range
Quantity
Positive far comparison depth, in length units.
required


target_range
Quantity
Positive depth of the target whose uncertainty is reported.
required


ray_clearance
Quantity
Nonnegative clearance added to one standard deviation along the ray.
required


loc_allowance
Quantity
Positive localization allowance used to invert the uncertainty equation.
required


side_clearance
Quantity
Positive second error allowance used for range comparisons.
required


baseline_change
Quantity
Nonnegative magnitude of unmodeled baseline change.
required


bias_range
Quantity
Positive depth at which baseline-change bias is evaluated.
required














Name
Type
Description





StereoDepthErrorResult
One-sigma errors, clearance-plus-sigma insets, and baseline bias in millimeters; inverse-error ranges in meters; dimensionless growth ratios. One sigma is not a guaranteed containment interval.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_depth_sigma : Disparity propagation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_range_for_sigma : Inverse error relation. mlsysim.physics.robotics.sensing.calc_stereo_baseline_bias : Baseline sensitivity.



Equation: sigma_z = z**2*sigma_d/(f*b); z_at_allowance = sqrt(allowance*f*b/sigma_d); baseline bias = bias_range*baseline_change/b. The near and far insets add ray_clearance to their respective sigma_z.
Assumptions: Rectified pinhole stereo, small disparity errors, fixed f and b, and the same disparity variance across all evaluated depths.
Excludes: Occlusions, matching outliers, lens/calibration covariance, correlated errors, and any claimed collision-risk probability.



Derivation: Differentiate z=f*b/disparity with respect to disparity to propagate one standard deviation; invert that expression for a chosen error allowance. Baseline enters linearly at fixed disparity.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> r = StereoDepthErrorModel().solve(Q_("0.1 m"), 1000, 1, Q_("1 m"), Q_("2 m"), Q_("1 m"), Q_("1 mm"), Q_("10 mm"), Q_("20 mm"), Q_("0 mm"), Q_("1 m"))
>>> r.sigma_far == 4 * r.sigma_near and r.baseline_bias == Q_("0 mm")
True

title: TensorParallelSpeedupScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Stated per-layer compute split tp_size ways, plus the AllReduces each layer adds.


Equation: T_parallel_layer=sum(T_serial_phase)/tp_size+collectives_per_layer*T_allreduce.
Assumptions: Ideal equal compute partition and identical layers; all collective costs serialize with compute.
Excludes: Communication overlap, load imbalance, and capacity checks.



Derivation: The ideal partition assumption divides each serial compute phase by the tensor-parallel degree. Collectives add serial delays, so their count times per-collective time is added to the compute sum.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.

>>> scenario = Scenarios.Llama2_70BPrefillTensorParallel8
>>> round(scenario.speedup, 6)
6.896552

title: CorpusRepetitionScenario
text:
Data scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/data.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A training run (ClusterTrainingTimeScenario) set against the unique tokens of its workload’s own corpus.
The corpus holds training_dataset_size / bytes_per_token unique tokens. The run processes training_ops / (flops_per_param_token x parameters) tokens, so it passes over the corpus that many times. A compute-optimal fit asks for tokens_per_param training tokens per parameter.


Equation: passes is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: The run uses fixed per-parameter token FLOPs, corpus bytes per token, and board power.
Excludes: Data-quality effects, changing utilization, and measured energy or compute-optimal quality.



Derivation: The scenario binds declared inputs to calc_compute_optimal_allocation. Those implementations document their derivations and sources.

title: LittlesLawScenario
text:
Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Requests in flight at arrival_rate, and replicas sized from a batch service time.


Equation: N=lambda*T; replica capacity=B/S; provisioned replicas=ceil(lambda/(u*capacity)).
Assumptions: Stationary mean rates and identical replica service times; replica properties require all optional sizing fields.
Excludes: Burst distributions and tail-latency guarantees.



Implementation references: mlsysim.physics.serving.calc_littles_law_occupancy. These helper contracts state the source assumptions; the scenario binds their inputs and derives the displayed ratios and budgets.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.VisionServingLittlesLaw
>>> round(scenario.in_flight, 6)
100.0

Description




arrival_rate



batch_service_time



batch_size



executing_positions
Total batch slots in the provisioned replicas: replicas_needed * batch_size; a count, not mean occupancy.


in_flight
Mean outstanding request count from Little’s law, arrival_rate * time_in_system; delegates to calc_littles_law_occupancy.


mean_executing
Mean busy batch positions under the fixed service-time approximation: arrival_rate * batch_service_time, dimensionless.


replica_throughput
Saturated capacity of one replica in 1/s: batch_size / batch_service_time; requires both optional fields.


replicas_needed
Integer replica count allowing the declared utilization headroom; ceiling of demand divided by target-utilization capacity.


service_utilization
Offered load divided by provisioned saturated capacity; dimensionless and distinct from the input utilization target.

title: HostDispatchScenario
text:
Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
The host’s work to issue one eager step against device_time of accelerator work.
The step has blocks blocks of ops_per_block Python-level operations, each paying dispatch, and launches_per_block kernels per block (default: one per operation), each paying launch. The model is additive with no host-device overlap: the overhead ratio is host time over device time, and above 1 the host takes more than half of the step.


Equation: Host time is operation_count*dispatch + launch_count*launch; the additive step includes device_time.
Assumptions: Constant overhead per event and serial host/device timing.
Excludes: Asynchronous overlap, graph capture, and measured interpreter or driver behavior.



Derivation: Serial event accounting adds dispatch cost once per Python operation and launch cost once per kernel launch. Adding device work then gives the assumed serial step; removing the entire host term defines a ceiling rather than a predicted optimization gain.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.Gpt2XlEagerDecodeDispatch
>>> s.host_time == s.dispatch_time+s.launch_time
True

Description

device_time



dispatch



dispatch_time
Total Python-side dispatch time in microseconds.


host_share
Host time as a share of the serial step, host plus device.


host_time
Serial dispatch-plus-launch time in microseconds.


launch



launch_ratio
Kernel launches alone over device time.


launch_time
Total kernel-launch overhead in microseconds.


launches
Kernel launch count across blocks; defaults to one launch per operation.


launches_per_block



operations
Count of Python-level operations across all blocks.


ops_per_block



overhead_ratio

per_op_cost

Equation: per = ops_per_block if launches_per_block is None else launches_per_block; blocks * per.

Serial step over device time: the most removing all host work could gain.
Equation: ((host_time + device_time) / device_time).to('').magnitude.

title: CounterfactualSearchScenario
text:
Agents scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/agents.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Replay paths that blame for a failure must search: a whole horizon, or one checked window.


Equation: Leaf paths number branching**depth; serial replay time is checked-window path count times time per path.
Assumptions: Every step has the same branching factor and each full path is replayed separately.
Excludes: Pruning, shared prefixes, parallel replay, and proof that a replay identifies causal responsibility.



Derivation: Leaf paths number branching**depth; serial replay time is checked-window path count times time per path. This is declared scenario accounting rather than a fitted empirical law.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.CheckedWindowBlameSearch
>>> value = scenario.full_paths
>>> round(float(value), 3)
1.2676506002282294e+30

Description




branching



full_exponent
Base-ten logarithm of full leaf-path count, dimensionless.


full_paths
Leaf-path count for fixed branching at every step of the full horizon.


horizon



replay_time



window



window_paths
Leaf-path count within the shorter checked replay window.


window_search_time
Serial minutes to replay every checked-window path at constant per-path duration.

Equation: branching ** horizon.



engine.scenario_types.CounterfactualSearchScenario.full_exponent
Base-ten logarithm of full leaf-path count, dimensionless.
Equation: _math.log10(full_paths).

Leaf-path count within the shorter checked replay window.
Equation: branching ** window.



engine.scenario_types.CounterfactualSearchScenario.window_search_time
Serial minutes to replay every checked-window path at constant per-path duration.
Equation: (window_paths * replay_time).to('minute').

title: engine.solvers.security
text:
engine.solvers.security
Agent-security solvers: injection exposure and defense evaluation (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated rates and episode counts: how often a task meets attacker text given how much untrusted content it reads, the same exposure counted in turns, and attack success against benign acceptance for two policies run on equal cohorts. None models an adaptive attacker or correlated payloads.





Name
Description




InjectionExposureModel
Per-task exposure to injected payloads across workloads that read different volumes.


PolicyComparisonModel
Two policies on equal, separate attacked and benign cohorts.





engine.solvers.security.InjectionExposureModel()
Per-task exposure to injected payloads across workloads that read different volumes.
Pr(exp) = 1 - (1 - q)^n,   linear estimate q n,
behind a screen that misses a fraction m:  1 - (1 - q m)^n
Reads are independent; a payload is counted once it is read, whatever it asks.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate independent payload exposure across read volumes.





engine.solvers.security.InjectionExposureModel.solve(
    payload_fraction,
    reads,
    miss_rate,
    cohort,
)
Estimate independent payload exposure across read volumes.











Name
Type
Description
Default




payload_fraction
float
Probability a read contains an injected payload, in [0, 1].
required


reads
Dict[str, int]
Workload names mapped to nonnegative counts of untrusted reads per task.
required


miss_rate
float
Fraction of payloads missed by a screen, in [0, 1].
required


cohort
int
Nonnegative task count used to report expected exposed tasks.
required














Name
Type
Description





InjectionExposureResult
Dimensionless exposure probabilities, a linear approximation, screened probabilities, and expected exposed-task counts.






Equation: For payload fraction q and n reads, exposure is 1-(1-q)**n. Screening replaces q by q*miss_rate. The small-exposure approximation is n*q.
Assumptions: Reads are independent and have constant payload prevalence. The screen has a fixed miss probability; a read counts as exposure whether or not the payload affects the agent.
Excludes: Adaptive attackers, correlated documents, execution of injected instructions, and any security guarantee. The linear approximation can exceed one.



Derivation: Exposure is the complement of no payload in any independent read. Multiplying by cohort size gives an expected count; physics.agents.calc_injection_exposure computes the probability.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import InjectionExposureModel
>>> result = InjectionExposureModel().solve(0.01, {"small": 1, "large": 10}, 0.5, 100)
>>> result.screened["large"] < result.exposure["large"]
True






engine.solvers.security.PolicyComparisonModel()
Two policies on equal, separate attacked and benign cohorts.
lower = confirmed / attacked,  upper = (confirmed + unresolved) / attacked
reduction = 1 - candidate / baseline   (observed, both upper, least favorable)
p_acc = accepted benign / benign,  C_eff = C_attempt / p_acc
Unresolved episodes count as harm in the upper rate; the least favorable reduction sets the candidate’s upper rate against the baseline’s lower. At equal attempt cost, C_eff rises by p_acc(baseline) / p_acc(candidate) - 1.





Name
Description




solve
Compare observed attack bounds and benign acceptance for two policies.





engine.solvers.security.PolicyComparisonModel.solve(
    attacked,
    benign,
    baseline,
    candidate,
    attempt_cost=None,
)
Compare observed attack bounds and benign acceptance for two policies.











Name
Type
Description
Default




attacked
int
Positive attacked-cohort size, identical for the two policies.
required


benign
int
Positive benign-cohort size, identical for the two policies.
required


baseline
Dict[str, int]
Nonnegative counts keyed confirmed, unresolved, accepted_benign, and false_block; counts must respect their cohort sizes.
required


candidate
Dict[str, int]
Same count schema and cohort denominators as baseline.
required


attempt_cost
float
Nonnegative common cost per attempt in a consistent currency unit; None omits priced outputs.
None














Name
Type
Description





PolicyComparisonResult
Dimensionless harm bounds, reductions, acceptance and cost rise; count differences; optional costs in the supplied cost unit.






Equation: Lower harm is confirmed/attacked and upper harm is (confirmed+unresolved)/attacked. Least-favorable reduction compares candidate upper to baseline lower. Effective cost is attempt_cost/benign_acceptance.
Assumptions: Cohorts have the stated common sizes. Baseline harm denominators and candidate benign acceptance are positive for ratios. Unresolved outcomes count as harm only in the upper bound.
Excludes: Sampling uncertainty, causal attribution, differing cohort difficulty, adaptive attackers, and a security certification.



Derivation: Divide observed outcome counts by their cohort denominators; setting unresolved outcomes to none or all harmful gives bounds. Equal attempt costs leave the inverse acceptance ratio as the cost multiplier.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import PolicyComparisonModel
>>> base = {"confirmed": 4, "unresolved": 1, "accepted_benign": 9, "false_block": 1}
>>> candidate = {"confirmed": 2, "unresolved": 1, "accepted_benign": 8, "false_block": 2}
>>> result = PolicyComparisonModel().solve(10, 10, base, candidate)
>>> result.candidate_lower <= result.candidate_upper
True

A week of raw captures against compressed model updates sent at named round cadences.


Equation: Update bytes=update_params*update_bits_per_param/bits_per_byte; weekly traffic=rounds*update_bytes.

text:
physics.quantities
Quantity-first formula helpers for LEGO cells — return Pint quantities, never strings.





Name
Description




carbon_from_energy
Convert energy consumption to emissions mass.


compute_time
Calculate duration from operation count and sustained rate.


energy_from_power
Integrate constant power over a duration.


memory_from_params
Convert parameter count and storage width to weight bytes.


token_throughput
Calculate average token rate over an interval.


transfer_time
Calculate streaming duration from payload and bandwidth.





physics.quantities.carbon_from_energy(energy, carbon_intensity)
Convert energy consumption to emissions mass.











Name
Type
Description
Default




energy
Quantity
Nonnegative energy; converted internally to kWh.
required


carbon_intensity
Quantity
Nonnegative mass per unit energy, such as g/kWh; caller specifies whether mass denotes CO2 or CO2e.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Emissions mass in kilograms.






Equation: m = E CI.
Assumptions: One intensity represents the entire energy-consumption interval.
Excludes: Embodied emissions, temporal grid variation, and overhead outside the supplied energy.



Derivation: Carbon intensity is emissions mass divided by energy. Multiplying consumed energy by the corresponding intensity cancels the energy unit and leaves emissions mass.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> carbon_from_energy(Q_(2, "kWh"), Q_(500, "g/kWh")) == Q_(1, "kg")
True




physics.quantities.compute_time(work, throughput)
Calculate duration from operation count and sustained rate.











Name
Type
Description
Default




work
Quantity
Nonnegative operation count, with units compatible with throughput.
required


throughput
Quantity
Positive sustained rate of those operations per unit time.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Computation duration in seconds.






Equation: t = work / throughput.
Assumptions: The supplied rate applies throughout the workload.
Excludes: Memory limits, launch overhead, and changes in utilization.



Derivation: Sustained throughput is completed operation count per unit time. Dividing the required count by this rate cancels the operation unit and leaves elapsed time.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> compute_time(Q_(4, "flop"), Q_(2, "flop/s")) == Q_(2, "s")
True




physics.quantities.energy_from_power(power, duration)
Integrate constant power over a duration.











Name
Type
Description
Default




power
Quantity
Nonnegative constant power in watt-compatible units.
required


duration
Quantity
Nonnegative elapsed time.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Energy in joules.






Equation: E = P t.
Assumptions: Power is constant, or represents the correct time-average for the interval.
Excludes: Time-varying power integration and facility overhead not already in power.



Derivation: Integrate constant power P over time: E = integral(P dt) = P t.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> energy_from_power(Q_(2, "W"), Q_(3, "s")) == Q_(6, "J")
True




physics.quantities.memory_from_params(parameters, bytes_per_param)
Convert parameter count and storage width to weight bytes.











Name
Type
Description
Default




parameters
Quantity
Nonnegative parameter count in param-compatible units.
required


bytes_per_param
Quantity
Nonnegative storage width in byte/param units.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Weight storage in bytes.






Equation: M = P b.
Assumptions: Every parameter has the same supplied storage width.
Excludes: Activations, gradients, optimizer state, KV cache, metadata, and alignment.



Derivation: Each stored parameter occupies the supplied byte width. Multiplying the parameter count by bytes per parameter cancels the parameter unit and leaves stored bytes.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> memory_from_params(Q_(3, "param"), Q_(2, "byte/param")) == Q_(6, "byte")
True




physics.quantities.token_throughput(tokens, duration)
Calculate average token rate over an interval.











Name
Type
Description
Default




tokens
Quantity
Nonnegative token count in count-compatible units.
required


duration
Quantity
Positive elapsed time.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Average rate in count/second.






Equation: r = N_tokens / t.
Assumptions: The count and interval describe the same work; the caller defines prompt or output tokens.
Excludes: Instantaneous rate, latency quantiles, and separation of prefill from decode.



Derivation: Average throughput is the count of completed items divided by their observation interval. Using token count and elapsed time gives tokens per second.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> token_throughput(Q_(6, "count"), Q_(2, "s")) == Q_(3, "count/s")
True




physics.quantities.transfer_time(payload, bandwidth)
Calculate streaming duration from payload and bandwidth.











Name
Type
Description
Default




payload
Quantity
Nonnegative payload in byte-compatible units.
required


bandwidth
Quantity
Positive sustained byte rate, such as GB/s.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Streaming duration in seconds.






Equation: t = payload / bandwidth.
Assumptions: The supplied bandwidth is constant and available to this transfer.
Excludes: Per-message latency, protocol headers, queueing, and contention.



Derivation: Sustained bandwidth is transferred bytes per unit time. Dividing payload bytes by this rate cancels the byte unit and leaves transfer duration.



>>> from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
>>> transfer_time(Q_(4, "GB"), Q_(2, "GB/s")) == Q_(2, "s")
True

title: solvers.NetworkRooflineModel
text:
solvers.NetworkRooflineModel()
Analyzes the Distributed Performance Bounds (The Network Wall).
This model elevates the single-node Roofline analysis to the fleet scale. It calculates the Communication Intensity (CI) of a workload and identifies if the fleet is Compute-Bound (Wall 1) or Network-Bound (Wall 2).
Literature Source: 1. Williams et al. (2009), “Roofline Model.” (Theoretical basis) 2. Ghose et al. (2019), “A Survey of Communication-Efficient Distributed Training.”





Name
Description




solve
Solve for the fleet-scale performance bound (network roofline).





solvers.NetworkRooflineModel.solve(
    model,
    fleet,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
)
Solve for the fleet-scale performance bound (network roofline).
Models one data-parallel training step as two independent ceilings — compute and gradient synchronization — and takes the slower as the binding latency (ideal overlap is assumed, so this is a lower-bound model). The conventions used:

communication intensity CI = training_ops / sync_bytes [FLOP/byte], with training_ops = 6 * P FLOPs per sample (Kaplan/Chinchilla forward+backward convention) and sync_bytes = 2 * P * bytes_per_param (ring all-reduce moves roughly 2x the gradient volume);
network ridge = fleet_peak_FLOPS / bisection_BW [FLOP/byte], the CI above which the fleet is compute-bound.












Name
Type
Description
Default




model
Workload
Workload with a parameter count (required).
required


fleet
Fleet
The cluster; supplies total accelerators, per-accelerator FLOPS, and fabric bandwidth / oversubscription ratio.
required


precision
str
Numerical precision; sets bytes per parameter and the FLOPS entry.
'fp16'


efficiency
float
Software efficiency factor in (0, 1] applied to fleet peak FLOPS.
0.5














Name
Type
Description





PerformanceProfile
latency_compute holds the compute ceiling, latency_memory the network ceiling (both in ms); bottleneck is ‘Network’ or ‘Compute’; arithmetic_intensity carries CI.






Equation: T = max(6P / (eta * fleet_peak), 2P*b / bisection_BW), where P is parameter count and b is bytes per gradient element. CI = 6P / (2P*b); the reported ridge uses fleet peak without eta.
Assumptions: one normalized training sample, uniform data-parallel replicas, and ideal overlap between the two independent ceilings. Excludes: batch/sequence scaling, ring startup latency, optimizer state, capacity checks, and pipeline bubbles. feasible=True does not check whether training state fits; the stored footprint is sync traffic.



Williams, Waterman, and Patterson (2009), “Roofline.” https://doi.org/10.1145/1498765.1498785 (bibliography key: williams2009). Derivation: replace memory traffic and its rate by gradient traffic and fabric bisection rate; the 2P*b traffic is an approximate ring volume.



>>> from mlsysim import Models, Systems
>>> from mlsysim.solvers import NetworkRooflineModel
>>> r = NetworkRooflineModel().solve(Models.Language.Llama3_8B, Systems.Clusters.Research_256)
>>> bool(r.latency >= r.latency_compute and r.latency >= r.latency_memory)
True

An extractor that needs extraction_queries answers from a priced API, under three billing regimes: pay per query, a paid tier capped per day, and a lifetime per-principal allowance after which every query is billed at the per-query price.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Retraining a model whose accuracy decays as drift fits it, serving query_rate queries worth value_per_query per unit accuracy, at run_cost a run. footprint and accelerator_price price the compute share of a run; compared_intervals and scheduled_interval are cadences to compare with the optimum.


Equation: Average cost combines run_cost/interval with staleness_slope*interval/2; the optimum balances these terms.

title: solvers.OrchestrationModel
text:
solvers.OrchestrationModel()
Analyzes Cluster Orchestration and Queueing (Little’s Law).
Caveat: This model uses a pedagogical M/D/1 queue (single server, deterministic service) to establish macroscopic wait-time bounds for dedicated, monolithic cluster workloads. For detailed multi-tenant job packing and preemption, a discrete-event M/G/c scheduler simulation would be required.
This model simulates the ‘Wait Wall’ in shared research clusters, calculating job completion times and researcher wait times based on cluster utilization and arrival rates.
Literature Source: 1. Little (1961), “A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW.” 2. Barroso et al. (2018), “The Datacenter as a Computer” (Cluster Mgmt). 3. Jeon et al. (2019), “Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters.”





Name
Description




solve
Estimate waiting time for a whole-fleet M/D/1 queue.





solvers.OrchestrationModel.solve(
    fleet,
    arrival_rate_jobs_per_day,

Dimensionless utilization, mean waiting time in days, queue length in jobs, and is_stable. Waiting time and queue length are infinite when utilization is at least one.






Equation: mu = 1 / service_days; rho = arrival_rate / mu; Wq = rho / (2 mu (1-rho)); Lq = rho^2 / (2(1-rho)) for rho < 1.

True

title: PartitionScreenScenario
text:
Agents scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/agents.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A fixed partition screened over worker counts: (1 - p) + p / N + c (N - 1) of the serial time.
The best count is the integer that minimizes elapsed time under the ceiling max_workers; no count beats 1 / (1 - p), and the continuous optimum sits at sqrt(p / c).


Equation: The calculation members below define elapsed, best_workers, best_time, best_speedup, speedup_cap, continuous_best.
Assumptions: The parallel share divides evenly across workers and each extra worker adds the same coordination fraction.
Excludes: Overhead changing with topology, data skew, or a nonlinear worker count.



Derivation: A fixed partition screened over worker counts: (1 - p) + p / N + c (N - 1) of the serial time. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.RepairPartitionScreen
>>> value = case.best_workers
>>> print(value)
6






Name
Description




best_speedup
Dimensionless serial-to-best-parallel speedup, reciprocal normalized elapsed time.


best_time
Smallest normalized elapsed time in the enumerated search.


best_workers
Worker count minimizing normalized elapsed time within the configured search ceiling.


continuous_best
Unconstrained continuous optimum sqrt(parallel fraction / per-worker overhead); not an integer search result.


elapsed
Normalized elapsed time by integer worker count via calc_partition_elapsed.


max_workers



overhead_per_extra_worker



parallel_fraction



speedup_cap
Amdahl ceiling with coordination removed, one over the serial fraction.

Agents scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/agents.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Fresh continuations from one saved prefix under several branches, counted by outcome; the Wilson bound a clean branch leaves and the clean runs a target_bound needs.


Equation: clean_runs_for_target is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: Each branch has a nonempty binomial outcome sample and the confidence target is supplied.
Excludes: Dependence between trials, multiple-comparison corrections, and evidence for unobserved branches.



Derivation: The scenario binds declared inputs to calc_wilson_clean_runs, calc_wilson_interval. Those implementations document their derivations and sources.

Data scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/data.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
accelerators copies of hardware training workload at sustained_rate samples a second each, fed from supply with encoded_sample bytes stored per sample and decoded_sample bytes after decode.
The arithmetic ceiling is peak FLOP/s over the training FLOPs of one sample (training_flops_factor times the forward pass). Demand is rate times bytes per sample; the feeding loss is the share of the training rate a slower supply removes (DataModel). worker_rate is what one host loader worker decodes and augments a second; host_decode_cap is where adding workers stops helping because the host’s cores run out.


Equation: sample ceiling = peak arithmetic / training FLOPs per sample; bandwidth demand = samples per second * bytes per sample.
Assumptions: Forward work and training multiplier define the arithmetic estimate; rates and encoded/decoded sample sizes refer to the same workload.
Excludes: Host-contention scaling, asynchronous pipeline transients, and automatic enforcement of the optional host decode cap.

title: CorrelatedReviewersScenario
text:
Agents scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/agents.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Reviewers who each falsely approve with the same marginal rate, independent or correlated.
The correlated model draws one propensity per candidate from a beta law with the stated mean and pairwise correlation; reviewers err independently given it (a beta-binomial). The beta mass above one half floors the majority error of any panel size.


Equation: The calculation members below define shape, independent_majority, correlated_majority, independent_unanimous, correlated_unanimous, unanimous_ratio, floor, panels.
Assumptions: Conditional reviewer errors are independent given a shared beta-distributed propensity; panel sizes are odd.
Excludes: Evidence that this correlation model describes a particular reviewer population.



Derivation: Reviewers who each falsely approve with the same marginal rate, independent or correlated. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios

>>> value = case.unanimous_ratio
>>> print(f"{value:.3g}")
122

title: solvers.TailLatencyModel
text:
solvers.TailLatencyModel()
Analyzes queueing delays and P99 tail latency for deployed inference models.
Models inference servers as M/M/c queues to determine if the deployment can sustain the target arrival rate while meeting strict SLA latency bounds.
Approximations (deliberate, pedagogical): - p50_latency/p99_latency add the WAIT-time quantile to the MEAN service time. The true quantile of sojourn time (wait + service) is generally larger, because service time has its own variance. - Kingman’s (cv^2 + 1)/2 factor is derived for the MEAN wait (M/G/1); applying it to the P50/P99 wait quantiles is a further heuristic. Quote these fields as model estimates, not exact M/G/c percentiles.
Literature Source: 1. Dean & Barroso (2013), “The Tail at Scale.”





Name
Description




solve
Solve for P50 and P99 tail latencies under variable load.





solvers.TailLatencyModel.solve(
    arrival_rate_qps,
    service_latency_ms,
    num_replicas=1,
    service_time_cv=1.0,
)
Solve for P50 and P99 tail latencies under variable load.











Name
Type
Description
Default




arrival_rate_qps
float
Request arrival rate in queries per second.
required


service_latency_ms
float
Mean service time per request in milliseconds.
required


num_replicas
int
Positive integer number of server replicas (c in M/M/c).
1


service_time_cv
float
Coefficient of variation of service time (default 1.0 = exponential). When CV != 1, applies Kingman’s M/G/1 correction factor (cv^2 + 1) / 2 to queue wait times, approximating M/G/c behavior.
1.0














Name
Type
Description





TailLatencyResult
Estimated P50/P99 service-plus-wait times in milliseconds, utilization, stability, and a dimensionless ratio of P99 wait to five service times. Unstable queues have infinite waits; the ratio is not a probability.






mlsysim.physics.serving.calc_queue_latency_mmc : Erlang-C wait quantiles.



Equation: mu = 1000/service_latency_ms and rho = arrivals/(c*mu). Erlang-C wait quantiles are multiplied by (CV^2+1)/2, then the mean service duration is added to each quantile.
Assumptions: nonnegative arrivals, positive mean service time, positive replica count, Poisson arrivals, and identical replicas. CV must be nonnegative; CV=1 gives the exponential-service queue approximation. Excludes: true convolution of service and wait distributions, bursty arrivals, heterogeneous servers, and scheduler dynamics. The CV correction is an approximation for multiple servers, not an exact M/G/c quantile.



Derivation: compose the Erlang-C queue-wait quantile with a fixed mean service time. The variability multiplier extends a mean-wait correction to quantiles as a modeling approximation.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import TailLatencyModel
>>> r = TailLatencyModel().solve(arrival_rate_qps=1, service_latency_ms=10)
>>> bool(r.is_stable and r.p99_latency >= r.p50_latency)
True

title: LayerStackScenario
text:
Training scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/training.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Weight-only count of a network built from convolution and dense layers, input first (biases omitted).
A multilayer perceptron has no convolution layers; a small CNN ends in a dense classifier head. (The full forward and training costs of a dense network belong to the neural-computation solvers; this counts weights.)


Equation: Total weights are the sum of convolution and dense matrix counts; the dense share divides its subtotal by the total.
Assumptions: A nonempty dense-layer sequence with compatible widths and positive total weight count.
Excludes: Biases, activation state, and training work; use neural solvers for those costs.



Derivation: Convolution filters and dense matrices are disjoint parameter sets, so their counts add. Dividing the dense subtotal by the combined count expresses its share. Biases are omitted consistently from both numerator and denominator.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.MnistMlpLayerStack
>>> s.weights == s.conv_weights + s.dense_weights
True

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Relative capacity N / (1 + sigma (N - 1) + kappa N (N - 1)) over integer worker counts.


Equation: The calculation members below define capacity, best_workers, peak_capacity, continuous_peak, retrograde_threshold, first_slower.
Assumptions: Contention and coherency coefficients define the stated USL capacity curve over positive worker counts.
Excludes: Fitting coefficients to measurements or extrapolation guarantees outside the selected range.



Derivation: Relative capacity N / (1 + sigma (N - 1) + kappa N (N - 1)) over integer worker counts. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.RepairPartitionScalability
>>> value = case.best_workers
>>> print(value)
6

Description

Integer count maximizing relative capacity within the search limit.


capacity
Relative capacity by integer worker count via calc_universal_scalability_law.


coherency



contention



continuous_peak
Continuous optimum via calc_usl_optimal_concurrency, distinct from integer search.


first_slower
First enumerated count above one with capacity below baseline, or None if absent.


peak_capacity
Largest dimensionless relative capacity among enumerated worker counts.


retrograde_threshold
Worker threshold above which USL capacity falls below the one-worker baseline.

Worker threshold above which USL capacity falls below the one-worker baseline.

Equation: (1 - contention) / coherency.

First enumerated count above one with capacity below baseline, or None if absent.
The smallest count above one whose capacity is below one worker’s.
Equation: next((n for n, c in capacity.items() if n > 1 and c < 1), None).

title: TwoProportionTestScenario
text:
Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A two-arm test sized to detect an absolute lift on a baseline_rate at the normal quantiles z_alpha and z_beta, on daily_requests split between arms.
family_size uncorrected tests at significance give the familywise error.


Equation: The normal planning approximation uses 2*p*(1-p)*(z_alpha+z_beta)**2/lift**2 per arm.
Assumptions: Independent Bernoulli samples, equal arms, a nonzero lift, and declared normal quantiles.
Excludes: Sequential peeking, correlated samples, and multiplicity correction; familywise_error assumes independent tests.



Derivation: Delegates sample planning to mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_sample_size and detectable lift to calc_two_proportion_detectable_lift. Their equal-arm normal approximation combines two Bernoulli variances with significance/power quantiles. The familywise error uses the complement of all independent tests avoiding a false rejection.



>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> s = Scenarios.CtrLiftExperiment
>>> s.total == 2*s.per_variant
True

Data scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/data.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A curriculum that reaches target in curriculum_epochs against baseline_epochs shuffled, with an optional linear warmup of warmup_epochs (epoch j serves j/W of the data).


Equation: epoch_reduction is the worked quantity; each property below states its equation and units.
Assumptions: Epoch counts are supplied and warmup epoch j uses j/W of a full dataset.
Excludes: Predicting curriculum convergence, fractional-epoch scheduling, and data-selection overhead.



Derivation: The equations below follow the stated counts, geometric relations, or accounting definitions; scenario inputs are supplied assumptions or observations, not fitted predictions.



Execute the registered worked inputs; this is a modeled calculation.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.Cifar10LinearCurriculum
>>> value = case.epoch_reduction
>>> round(value, 3)
0.233

curriculum_epochs

warmup_epochs



warmup_samples

Dimensionless fraction of full-data warmup work actually served.

title: engine.solvers.acceptance
text:
engine.solvers.acceptance
Agent evaluation solvers: what a set of graded trials supports about a configuration.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on stated trial counts, verdicts, and costs: the acceptance rate when some trials never resolve; a grader’s error rates against a reference assessment; how tasks and repeated runs share an evaluation budget; Wald and Wilson intervals; the task counts a precision or detection target needs; a paired candidate-against-baseline comparison (Newcombe’s method 10, McNemar’s exact test, and the variance pairing removes); the within-model spread of a leaderboard across scaffolds and the neighboring ranks it cannot separate; repeated runs of one task against new tasks; batch and sequential selection under one candidate cap; and the summary of a paired repeated-run evaluation. Repeated-run consistency over k recurrences is horizon compounding (HorizonCompoundingModel).





Name
Description




BinomialIntervalsModel
Wald and Wilson intervals for several success counts out of trials.


CappedSelectionCostModel
Batch against sequential selection of up to cap candidates under an exact checker.


PairedComparisonModel
A candidate against a baseline, one trial of each on the same tasks.


ProportionPlanningModel
How many independent tasks a precision or a detection target needs.


TaskMixConsistencyModel
All-pass probability of k runs: one task repeated against k new tasks.





engine.solvers.acceptance.BinomialIntervalsModel()
Wald and Wilson intervals for several success counts out of trials.
Wald collapses to zero width at x = 0 and leaves [0, 1] near the boundaries; Wilson keeps a nonzero width and stays inside, and the two nearly coincide near one half. The Wilson upper limit at x = 0 is z^2 / (n + z^2).





Name
Description




solve
Compare Wald and Wilson intervals for specified success counts.





engine.solvers.acceptance.BinomialIntervalsModel.solve(
    trials,
    successes,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Compare Wald and Wilson intervals for specified success counts.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trials
int
Positive number of independent Bernoulli trials shared by each count.
required


successes
Sequence[int]
Success counts from zero through trials, inclusive.
required


confidence
float
Central confidence probability in (0, 1); default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





BinomialIntervalsResult
Dimensionless critical value and interval endpoints keyed by success count.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_wald_interval : Uncorrected normal interval for a binomial rate. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_wilson_interval : Score interval that handles boundary success counts.



Equation: Wald uses p +/- z sqrt(p(1-p)/n); Wilson inverts the binomial score test. The normal quantile z is shared by both.
Assumptions: Each count represents independent trials with a common success probability.
Excludes: Repeated-task dependence, multiple-comparison correction, and exact coverage guarantees for the Wald approximation.



Wilson (1927), Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference. https://www.jstor.org/stable/2276774 The solver composes the two interval functions without changing their formulas.



>>> result = BinomialIntervalsModel().solve(10, [0, 5])
>>> result.wald[0] == (0.0, 0.0) and result.wilson[0][1] > 0
True






engine.solvers.acceptance.CappedSelectionCostModel()
Batch against sequential selection of up to cap candidates under an exact checker.
Both policies return a passing candidate with q = 1 - (1 - p)^cap. The batch generates and checks all cap; sequential selection stops at the first pass and starts q / p candidates on average. Charging every initiated trial to the accepted ones gives cap c / q against (c / p), where c is generation plus checking: sequential cost per accepted task does not depend on the cap, and only p lowers it.





Name
Description




solve
Compare batch and early-stopping selection under one candidate cap.





engine.solvers.acceptance.CappedSelectionCostModel.solve(
    pass_rate,
    cap,
    generation_cost,
    check_cost,
)
Compare batch and early-stopping selection under one candidate cap.











Name
Type
Description
Default




pass_rate
float
Independent candidate acceptance probability in (0, 1].
required


cap
int
Positive maximum candidates per task.
required


generation_cost
Quantity
Nonnegative generation cost per candidate, convertible to USD.
required


check_cost
Quantity
Nonnegative exact-checker cost per candidate, convertible to USD; total unit cost must be positive.
required














Name
Type
Description





CappedSelectionCostResult
Dimensionless availability and counts; trial and accepted-task costs in USD.






mlsysim.physics.agents.calc_independent_success : Probability that at least one independent candidate passes.



Equation: q = 1 - (1-p)^cap; E[N_sequential] = q/p; batch cost per acceptance = cap*c/q and sequential cost per acceptance = c/p.
Assumptions: Independent identically distributed candidates, an exact checker, constant generation/check costs, and immediate stopping after acceptance.
Excludes: Parallel latency, checker errors, correlated candidates, and a feasible interpretation of the doubled-rate counterfactual when 2p exceeds one.



Derivation: sum the truncated geometric survival probabilities for expected starts and divide total trial cost by probability of acceptance.



>>> result = CappedSelectionCostModel().solve(0.25, 4, 1 * USD, 0.1 * USD)
>>> result.batch_per_accepted > result.sequential_per_accepted
True






engine.solvers.acceptance.PairedComparisonModel()
A candidate against a baseline, one trial of each on the same tasks.
Only discordant pairs move the difference; Newcombe’s method 10 gives its interval, and a noninferiority gate needs the lower limit above -tolerance. Lower half-widths shrink as 1 / sqrt(n), so the pairs that center the expected lower limit on the margin are n [(delta - lower) / (delta + tolerance)]^2 (even odds of clearing), and a true gain of zero needs the half-width inside the tolerance itself. The paired outcome has variance d - delta^2 per pair against p_c (1 - p_c) + p_b (1 - p_b) for two independent arms. McNemar’s exact test answers the separate equality question.





Name
Description




solve
Evaluate paired binary outcomes and approximate further sample needs.





engine.solvers.acceptance.PairedComparisonModel.solve(
    both,
    candidate_only,
    baseline_only,
    neither,
    tolerance,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Evaluate paired binary outcomes and approximate further sample needs.











Name
Type
Description
Default




both
int
Nonnegative number of tasks accepted by both configurations.
required


candidate_only
int
Nonnegative number accepted only by the candidate.
required


baseline_only
int
Nonnegative number accepted only by the baseline.
required


neither
int
Nonnegative number accepted by neither; total pairs must be positive.
required


tolerance
float
Positive noninferiority margin in probability units. The observed gain plus tolerance and both variance denominators must be nonzero.
required


confidence
float
Central interval probability in (0, 1); default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





PairedComparisonResult
Rates, interval endpoints, p-value, variance ratios, Boolean gates, and approximate integer pair counts.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_newcombe_paired_difference : Paired difference with the method-10 score interval. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_mcnemar_exact_two_sided : Exact equality test using discordant pair counts.



Equation: delta = (candidate_only - baseline_only)/n; paired variance = discordant_fraction - delta^2. Newcombe method 10 supplies the interval. Planning scales n by squared current-width/target-width ratios.
Assumptions: Independent task pairs and stable population rates. Both methods observe the same tasks. The projected sample counts use inverse-square-root interval-width scaling.
Excludes: Sequential testing, task clusters, zero-variance degenerate cases, and a power guarantee for the projected pair counts.



Newcombe (1998), Improved confidence intervals for the difference between binomial proportions based on paired data. https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19981130)17:22%3C2635::AID-SIM954%3E3.0.CO;2-C The additional sample projection is a solver approximation, not the interval method.



>>> result = PairedComparisonModel().solve(50, 20, 10, 20, 0.05)
>>> result.candidate_rate > result.baseline_rate and result.pairs == 100
True






engine.solvers.acceptance.ProportionPlanningModel()
How many independent tasks a precision or a detection target needs.
One rate: the normal half-width z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) shrinks as 1 / sqrt(n), and ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / h^2) tasks reach a half-width h. Two independent arms at average rate p: about 2 (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 p (1 - p) / delta^2 tasks per arm detect a difference delta, so halving delta quadruples the count. The detection quantiles are the rounded planning values the caller states.





Name
Description




solve
Plan independent trial counts from precision and detection targets.





engine.solvers.acceptance.ProportionPlanningModel.solve(
    rate,
    planning_tasks,
    target_half_width,
    differences,
    z_alpha,
    z_beta,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Plan independent trial counts from precision and detection targets.











Name
Type
Description
Default

float
Planning success probability strictly between zero and one.
required


planning_tasks
int
Positive number of independent tasks in the proposed evaluation.
required


target_half_width
float
Positive target half-width in probability units.
required


differences
Sequence[float]
Positive differences in probabilities to detect between independent arms.
required


z_alpha
float
Positive normal critical value selected for the detection significance level.
required


z_beta
float
Positive normal quantile selected for the desired detection power.
required


confidence
float
Central probability for the single-rate interval; default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





ProportionPlanningResult
Dimensionless interval widths and integer sample counts, including counts per arm.






mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_proportion_half_width : Normal standard-error half-width for one proportion. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_samples_for_half_width : Invert a requested one-rate interval half-width. mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_sample_size : Equal-arm normal-approximation detection planning.



Equation: h = z sqrt(p(1-p)/n); n_target = ceil(z^2 p(1-p)/h^2). Two-arm planning uses ceil(2(z_alpha+z_beta)^2 p(1-p)/delta^2).
Assumptions: Independent Bernoulli tasks; the planning rate is supplied, not estimated by this solver. The Wilson comparison rounds rate times planning_tasks to a whole success count.
Excludes: Clustered tasks, paired-arm gains, attrition, and exact power calculations.



Derivation: solve the normal-approximation standard error for the sample count. The two-arm expression adds equal independent Bernoulli variances. The Wilson comparison is implemented by calc_wilson_interval.



>>> result = ProportionPlanningModel().solve(0.5, 100, 0.1, [0.1, 0.2], 1.96, 0.84)
>>> result.per_arm[0.1] > result.per_arm[0.2]
True






engine.solvers.acceptance.TaskMixConsistencyModel()
All-pass probability of k runs: one task repeated against k new tasks.
Repeating one randomly drawn task passes every run with E[p_i^k]; k independently drawn tasks all pass with (E[p_i])^k, which Jensen’s inequality places at or below it, strictly when task difficulty varies and k >= 2. Task types are equally weighted.





Name
Description




solve
Compare all-pass probabilities for repeated versus newly sampled tasks.





engine.solvers.acceptance.TaskMixConsistencyModel.solve(
    task_pass_rates,
    repetitions,
)
Compare all-pass probabilities for repeated versus newly sampled tasks.











Name
Type
Description
Default




task_pass_rates
Sequence[float]
Nonempty sequence of per-task success probabilities in [0, 1].
required


repetitions
int
Positive number of runs in each all-pass event.
required














Name
Type
Description





TaskMixConsistencyResult
Dimensionless mean rate and all-pass probabilities under the two sampling policies.






Equation: same_task_all = mean(p_i^k); new_tasks_all = mean(p_i)^k.
Assumptions: Task types have equal weight; runs are independent conditional on their task type. New tasks are sampled independently with replacement.
Excludes: State carried across runs, correlated failures, and empirical uncertainty in task rates.



Derivation: condition on task type before multiplying conditional pass probabilities; average the conditional products for repeated tasks.



>>> result = TaskMixConsistencyModel().solve([0.2, 0.8], 2)
>>> result.same_task_all > result.new_tasks_all
True










Name
Description




z_for_confidence
Return the standard-normal critical value for a two-sided interval.

Wald and Wilson intervals for several success counts out of trials.

engine.solvers.acceptance.CappedSelectionCostModel()
Batch against sequential selection of up to cap candidates under an exact checker.
Both policies return a passing candidate with q = 1 - (1 - p)^cap. The batch generates and checks all cap; sequential selection stops at the first pass and starts q / p candidates on average. Charging every initiated trial to the accepted ones gives cap c / q against (c / p), where c is generation plus checking: sequential cost per accepted task does not depend on the cap, and only p lowers it.

Equation: q = 1 - (1-p)^cap; E[N_sequential] = q/p; batch cost per acceptance = cap*c/q and sequential cost per acceptance = c/p.
Assumptions: Independent identically distributed candidates, an exact checker, constant generation/check costs, and immediate stopping after acceptance.
Excludes: Parallel latency, checker errors, correlated candidates, and a feasible interpretation of the doubled-rate counterfactual when 2p exceeds one.

engine.solvers.acceptance.PairedComparisonModel()
A candidate against a baseline, one trial of each on the same tasks.
Only discordant pairs move the difference; Newcombe’s method 10 gives its interval, and a noninferiority gate needs the lower limit above -tolerance. Lower half-widths shrink as 1 / sqrt(n), so the pairs that center the expected lower limit on the margin are n [(delta - lower) / (delta + tolerance)]^2 (even odds of clearing), and a true gain of zero needs the half-width inside the tolerance itself. The paired outcome has variance d - delta^2 per pair against p_c (1 - p_c) + p_b (1 - p_b) for two independent arms. McNemar’s exact test answers the separate equality question.

engine.solvers.acceptance.ProportionPlanningModel()
How many independent tasks a precision or a detection target needs.
One rate: the normal half-width z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) shrinks as 1 / sqrt(n), and ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / h^2) tasks reach a half-width h. Two independent arms at average rate p: about 2 (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 p (1 - p) / delta^2 tasks per arm detect a difference delta, so halving delta quadruples the count. The detection quantiles are the rounded planning values the caller states.

title: Statistics Scenarios
text:
Scenario contracts

AccuracyFrontierScenario: A hypothetical accuracy-against-disparity frontier, floor + span (1 - exp(-rate x)), with named candidate disparities on it.
AgreementDriftScenario: A labeling campaign’s kappa at a baseline and again after elapsed.
AnnotatorAgreementScenario: Two independent annotators with the same label mix class_shares: chance agreement, and Cohen’s kappa at an observed_agreement.
ArgumentConfidenceScenario: A stipulated safety argument: premises required premises at premise_confidence each, and a claim carried by legs independent legs at leg_confidence each.
ArmComparisonScenario: Two policies run arm_runs times each, with successes_a and successes_b successes; Fisher’s exact test, and the runs per arm that separate p_high from p_low two-sided at alpha with power.
AutomationBiasScenario: A human reviews an AI’s output; the human accepts miss_acceptance of the AI’s misses.
BiasFeedbackScenario: A gap passed at launch, refit from the next audit, iterated over retraining cycles: gap(k) = launch_gap * factor^k against a release gate (all in percentage points).
BinShareShiftScenario: A feature binned at the training quantiles: training shares against recent shares, scored by PSI.
BinomialIntervalsScenario: Several success counts out of one number of independent tasks.
CappedSelectionCostScenario: Candidates for one fixed task, an exact checker, and a cap on candidates.
CertifiedRadiusScenario: Binary randomized smoothing at noise noise_sd, against an l-infinity budget on one input.
ClosedLoopCampaignScenario: clean_runs failure-free closed-loop trials of a frozen policy in one cell of table on site, each run long with an automated reset, bounded at one-sided confidence.
ConfidenceRegimesScenario: Stipulated proposer confidence against task success in several operating regimes.
ConstraintAccuracyCostScenario: Accuracy before and after a fairness constraint (percent), with the policy’s stated rates.
CrashRateDenominatorScenario: A reported before-and-after crash rate and the same comparison on the cohort whose exposure is complete (rates per million miles).
DetectionDelayLossScenario: A fault that cuts quality_drop of annual_value until it is detected, found after slow_detection or fast_detection, incidents_per_year times a year.
DriftConfirmationScenario: Labeled outcomes that confirm a drop of drop from baseline_accuracy.
EfficiencyClaimGapScenario: A datasheet operating point against a sustained one: operations per watt at each, and their ratio.
EqualOpportunityPriceScenario: Utility per applicant of raising group’s TPR to reference_group’s by moving its threshold, when that move raises its FPR by fpr_increase: a repaid loan earns repay_margin, a default loses default_loss (both USD).
ExplanationLogScenario: Logging an explanation with every prediction: predictions_per_day for days_per_month, each a map_size_low to map_size_high attribution map (or tabular attributions of attribution_bytes_low to attribution_bytes_high per feature).
ExplorationExposureScenario: A ranking service showing slots_per_user items a day to daily_users from a catalog of catalog_items, with explore_share of slots served by randomized exploration.
FalseAlarmBudgetScenario: One detection window every window, listening_per_day of each day, over horizon.
FloatBitFlipScenario: One stored binary32 value with bit flipped_bit flipped (bit 30 is the top exponent bit).
GaussianDriftScenario: A continuous feature fitted as a normal at reference and now: KL divergence of the reference from the current fit.
GroupConfusionScenario: Binary decisions for two or more groups as confusion counts {group: {tp, fp, fn, tn}}.
HazardExposureScenario: Failure-free exposure that bounds each of rates (constant hazards per hour) at one-sided confidence, against what rigs rigs or one rig over rig_time accumulate.
HostAcceleratorBoardScenario: One board, a host CPU and an attached accelerator: model-only and end-to-end latency, active energy.
InlineOverheadScenario: A safeguard added inline to a request path of base_latency, costing overhead_low to overhead_high (fractions of the base) per request.
InterventionCampaignScenario: interventions interventions in missions supervised runs of mission: burden per hour and per kilometer, and an exact two-sided 1 - alpha interval on the rate.
KsDriftScenario: A two-sample K-S drift test of n_reference training against n_current recent values of one feature.
LaplaceMeanReleaseScenario: The mean of a public roster of group_size values in [0, value_range] released under epsilon-DP by one Laplace draw on the sum (replace-one adjacency).
MeanShiftTestScenario: A feature mean that moves from reference_mean to observed_mean over n_samples requests.
MeanVersusTailScenario: A benchmark’s mean latency against a production tail stated as a range.
MembershipAuditScenario: A membership-inference audit on the ROC plane against the ceiling a pure epsilon-DP release allows; the audit curve FPR + a FPR (1 - FPR) is illustrative.
MissionExposureScenario: Failure-free missions of mission at machine’s drive limit, with reset between them, that bound hazard_rate at one-sided confidence; and the exposure a relaxed target of one failure per relaxed_mtbf needs.
MonitorFleetAlertScenario: models x metrics_per_model monitors checked every check_interval at a per-check false_positive_rate on a stable process; dedup_share of crossings are merged away.
PairedComparisonScenario: One candidate and one baseline trial on each sampled task, outcomes kept in pairs.
PreferenceLabelBudgetScenario: Human preference labels for a reward model: comparisons_low to comparisons_high at price_low to price_high per comparison.
ProportionGapTestScenario: An observed gap between two rates, rate_a and rate_b, on n_per_group decisions each.
ProportionPlanningScenario: Planning targets for one acceptance rate and for two independent arms.
ProportionSampleSizeScenario: Samples that pin a pass fraction rate to within half_width at confidence: z^2 p (1 - p) / m^2.
ProxyMetricLatencyScenario: A search-width change that buys an offline metric gain with latency, against a serving budget.
QuantizedAcceptanceGatesScenario: A float model and its quantized copy against acceptance gates set before compression.
RetrainingIntervalScenario: Retraining a model whose accuracy decays as drift fits it, serving query_rate queries worth value_per_query per unit accuracy, at run_cost a run. footprint and accelerator_price price the compute share of a run; compared_intervals and scheduled_interval are cadences to compare with the optimum.
RoadExposureScenario: Miles-to-demonstrate requirements per event class (zero failures, precision, improvement), in millions of miles at human benchmark rates per 100 million miles, against one dated fleet_miles total (millions) at one-sided confidence.
SameTestSetAccuracyComparisonScenario: Two models scored on the same n_samples test items: independent-set interval and McNemar’s limit.
SampledDecisionMonitorScenario: Per-group metric monitoring of a decision service at request_rate.
SegmentAccuracyScenario: Accuracy measured separately on each traffic segment; traffic_shares and accuracies are keyed by segment name.
SequentialTestScenario: Wald’s SPRT between an unacceptable failure rate p_unacceptable and an acceptable one p_acceptable at error rates alpha and beta; the score after trace_clean_runs clean runs and one failure; and the fixed zero-failure test for success 1 - p_unacceptable at the same alpha.
ShardedUnlearningScenario: Exact unlearning by sharded retraining (SISA) against a full retrain of workload.
StrongScalingPairScenario: The same fixed job on base_devices and on scaled_devices: speedup, ideal time, and efficiency.
SubgroupEvaluationBudgetScenario: The labeled data a per-group evaluation needs: one group’s rate within half_width at confidence (worst case rate 0.5), the collection random sampling needs to reach a target_per_group from a group of group_share, and the per-group count that pins a gap between two equal-size groups to gap_half_width.
TaskMixConsistencyScenario: Equally weighted task types and a number of runs that must all pass.
TwoProportionTestScenario: A two-arm test sized to detect an absolute lift on a baseline_rate at the normal quantiles z_alpha and z_beta, on daily_requests split between arms.
ZeroEventExposureScenario: Exposure needed, with zero events observed, to bound a rate of budget per horizon at one-sided confidence, and the size of recording that exposure at sample_rate.

title: BiasFeedbackScenario
text:
Statistics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/statistics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A gap passed at launch, refit from the next audit, iterated over retraining cycles: gap(k) = launch_gap * factor^k against a release gate (all in percentage points).


Equation: Disparity compounds as launch_gap*factor**cycles; factor is fitted from the next audit and the gate-crossing index is rounded upward.
Assumptions: One constant multiplicative factor represents each retraining cycle; gap and gate use matching percentage-point units.
Excludes: A causal feedback model, saturation, sampling uncertainty, and assurance that the fitted factor persists.



Derivation: the scenario composes mlsysim.physics.fairness.calc_cycles_to_gate, mlsysim.physics.fairness.calc_feedback_disparity. Their contracts supply the underlying equations; property equations show the remaining unit conversions and accounting.
