title: SpotEffectiveCostScenario
text:
Economics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/economics.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Spot capacity priced per hour of retained progress.
Each interruption bills checkpoint_overhead + restart_overhead that retain no progress, once per retained_interval of progress, so the effective price is the spot price times billed time over retained time.


Equation: effective price = spot price * (retained time + checkpoint time + restart time) / retained time.
Assumptions: The same interruption overhead accompanies every positive retained- progress interval.
Excludes: Interruption distributions, unavailable replacement capacity, and nonlinear recovery work.



Derivation: effective price = spot price * (retained time + checkpoint time + restart time) / retained time. The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.



The named scenario supplies illustrative inputs; the output is calculated.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.SpotInterruptionEffectiveCost
>>> round(float(case.nominal_discount), 3)
0.65

Description




billed_over_retained
Billed time per unit of useful progress, a dimensionless multiplier; retained time


checkpoint_overhead



effective_cost_ratio
Effective spot price divided by on-demand price, a dimensionless cost ratio.


effective_rate
USD per device-hour of retained progress, including the interruption time


effective_savings
Fraction of on-demand cost saved after overhead; negative values mean spot costs


lost_per_interruption
Minutes billed for checkpoint and restart without retaining additional progress.


nominal_discount
Fractional price reduction before interruption overhead, relative to on-demand

restart_overhead



retained_interval

title: physics.reliability
text:
physics.reliability
Reliability, checkpointing, and availability models.





Name
Description




calc_all_up_availability
Calculate availability when every component must be up.


calc_availability_stacked
Calculate availability when any replica can serve.


calc_checkpoint_stride
Find a continuous checkpoint stride balancing pause and rework.


calc_checkpoint_waste
Estimate the wall-time fraction lost to saves and rework.


calc_downtime
Calculate expected downtime over a steady-state interval.


calc_error_budget_spent
Calculate the share of an error budget consumed by a burn.


calc_failure_probability
Calculate the chance of at least one failure during a job.


calc_group_commit_waits
Separate per-record flush work from group-commit wait time.


calc_mtbf_cluster
Combine component MTBFs for a homogeneous series system.


calc_mtbf_node
Combine heterogeneous component hazards into node MTBF.


calc_probe_detection_window
Bound crash-to-removal delay for periodic health probes.


calc_snapshot_write_volume
Compare accumulated bytes in full snapshots and deltas.


calc_step_event_probability
Calculate event exposure across device-hours in one step.


calc_stride_overhead
Estimate checkpoint and expected-rework overhead per turn.


calc_young_daly_interval
Estimate the first-order checkpoint interval that minimizes lost work.





physics.reliability.calc_all_up_availability(availability, n_components)
Calculate availability when every component must be up.











Name
Type
Description
Default




availability
float
Per-component steady-state availability in [0, 1].
required


n_components
int
Number of required components, at least one.
required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless joint availability.






Equation: A_all = availability**n_components.
Assumptions: Independent and identically available components; every component is required.
Excludes: Redundancy, common-cause failures, and partial-service operation.



Derivation: Independence turns the intersection of all component-up events into the product of their individual probabilities.



>>> calc_all_up_availability(0.9, 2) < calc_all_up_availability(0.9, 1)
True




physics.reliability.calc_availability_stacked(single_availability, n_replicas)
Calculate availability when any replica can serve.











Name
Type
Description
Default




single_availability
float
Per-replica steady-state availability in [0, 1].
required


n_replicas
int
Positive count of interchangeable replicas.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless probability that at least one replica is available.






Equation: A = 1 - (1 - single_availability)**n_replicas.
Assumptions: Replica availability events are independent and any available replica suffices.
Excludes: Common-cause outages, load capacity, failover delay, and replication lag.



Derivation: All replicas are unavailable with probability (1-a)**n; complementing that event gives the at-least-one-up probability.



>>> calc_availability_stacked(0.9, 2) > calc_availability_stacked(0.9, 1)
True




physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_stride(pause, crash_rate, lost_turn_cost)
Find a continuous checkpoint stride balancing pause and rework.











Name
Type
Description
Default




pause
Quantity or float
Nonnegative checkpoint pause; bare numbers are seconds.
required


crash_rate
float
Positive expected crashes per turn.
required


lost_turn_cost
Quantity or float
Positive recovery cost per lost turn; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Optimal continuous stride in turns; not rounded to an integer policy.






Equation: k_star = sqrt(2*pause/(crash_rate*lost_turn_cost)).
Assumptions: A checkpoint every k turns costs pause/k per turn; crashes lose k/2 turns on average.
Excludes: Integer scheduling, restart costs independent of lost turns, and correlated crashes.



Young (1974), “A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval.” https://doi.org/10.1145/361147.361115 (bibliography key: young1974). Derivation: Differentiate pause/k + crash_rate*lost_turn_cost*k/2 with respect to the continuous stride k and set the derivative to zero.



>>> stride = calc_checkpoint_stride(1, 0.01, 1)
>>> optimum = calc_stride_overhead(1, stride, 0.01, 1)
>>> optimum < calc_stride_overhead(1, stride * 2, 0.01, 1)
True




physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_waste(write_time, interval, mtbf)
Estimate the wall-time fraction lost to saves and rework.











Name
Type
Description
Default




write_time
Quantity or float
Nonnegative duration of one blocking checkpoint; bare numbers are seconds.
required


interval
Quantity or float
Positive spacing between checkpoints; bare numbers are seconds.
required


mtbf
Quantity or float
Positive mean time between failures; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless first-order waste; values above one signal an unsuitable regime, not a capped fraction.






Equation: W = write_time / interval + interval / (2 * mtbf).
Assumptions: Rare independent failures and uniformly distributed failure position within an interval. Saves block useful work.
Excludes: Restart overhead, lost checkpoint writes, overlapping saves, and higher-order interactions.
At the minimizing Young interval, the save and rework contributions are equal. This is an approximation to wasted wall time rather than a simulation of failure and restart events.



Young (1974), “A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval.” https://doi.org/10.1145/361147.361115 (bibliography key: young1974).



>>> tau = calc_young_daly_interval(10, 10000)
>>> optimum = calc_checkpoint_waste(10, tau, 10000)
>>> optimum < calc_checkpoint_waste(10, tau * 2, 10000)
True




physics.reliability.calc_downtime(availability, interval)
Calculate expected downtime over a steady-state interval.











Name
Type
Description
Default




availability
float
Steady-state fraction of time available in [0, 1].
required


interval
Quantity or float
Nonnegative observation duration; returned time retains its units or implicit unit.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity or float
Expected downtime in the same time unit as interval.






Equation: downtime = (1 - availability) * interval.
Assumptions: The availability fraction applies throughout the observation interval.
Excludes: Outage clustering, recovery trajectories, and downtime quantiles.



Derivation: Multiplying total observation time by its unavailable fraction gives expected time down.



>>> calc_downtime(1.0, 24 * ureg.hour).m_as("hour")
0.0




physics.reliability.calc_error_budget_spent(burn_rate, window, budget_period)
Calculate the share of an error budget consumed by a burn.











Name
Type
Description
Default




burn_rate
float
Nonnegative rate relative to the rate that exhausts the budget over budget_period.
required


window
Quantity
Nonnegative duration of sustained burn, with time units.
required


budget_period
Quantity
Positive duration of the complete error-budget period.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless budget share; may exceed one after overspending.






Equation: share = burn_rate * window / budget_period.
Assumptions: Constant burn rate across the window and a fixed budget-period definition.
Excludes: Traffic weighting changes, rolling-window edge effects, and alerting policy.



Google, “Alerting on SLOs,” The Site Reliability Workbook. https://sre.google/workbook/alerting-on-slos/



>>> calc_error_budget_spent(1, 1 * ureg.day, 1 * ureg.day)
1.0




physics.reliability.calc_failure_probability(mtbf, job_duration)
Calculate the chance of at least one failure during a job.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mtbf
Quantity or float
Positive mean time between failures; supply a time quantity or a bare number.
required


job_duration
Quantity or float
Nonnegative duration; supply a time quantity if MTBF has units, otherwise use the same implicit time unit.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Failure probability in [0, 1], subject to floating-point rounding.






Equation: P = 1 - exp(-job_duration / mtbf).
Assumptions: Constant Poisson failure rate 1/MTBF, independent of job age. Both inputs are quantities or both are bare numbers.
Excludes: Aging hazards, correlated failures, and recovery or retry costs.
Mixing a bare number with a quantity raises TypeError because its implied unit would be ambiguous. For short jobs, the probability approaches T/MTBF.



Derivation: A constant-hazard lifetime survives duration T with probability exp(-T/MTBF); the complement is the probability of at least one failure.



>>> calc_failure_probability(1000, 0)
0.0
>>> calc_failure_probability(1000, 20) > calc_failure_probability(1000, 10)
True




physics.reliability.calc_group_commit_waits(batch_timer, flush_time, batch_size)
Separate per-record flush work from group-commit wait time.











Name
Type
Description
Default




batch_timer
Quantity or float
Nonnegative collection window after the first arrival; bare numbers are seconds.

physics.reliability.calc_stride_overhead(
    pause,
    stride,
    crash_rate,
    lost_turn_cost,
)
Estimate checkpoint and expected-rework overhead per turn.











Name
Type
Description
Default




pause
Quantity or float
Nonnegative pause per checkpoint; bare numbers are seconds.
required

float
Positive number of turns between checkpoints.
required


crash_rate
float
Nonnegative expected crashes per turn.
required


lost_turn_cost
Quantity or float
Nonnegative recovery cost per lost turn; bare numbers are seconds.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Expected overhead per turn in seconds.

>>> calc_stride_overhead(2, 4, 0, 1) * 4 == 2 * ureg.second
True




physics.reliability.calc_young_daly_interval(checkpoint_cost_s, mtbf_s)
Estimate the first-order checkpoint interval that minimizes lost work.











Name
Type
Description
Default




checkpoint_cost_s
Quantity or float
Positive write time delta; bare numbers are seconds.
required


mtbf_s
Quantity or float
Positive system mean time between failures; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Interval in seconds; not rounded to a scheduling quantum.






Equation: tau = sqrt(2 * delta * MTBF), from minimizing delta/tau + tau/(2*MTBF).
Assumptions: Failures arrive independently and rework averages half an interval; delta is small relative to MTBF.
Excludes: Restart time, correlated failures, asynchronous checkpointing, and higher-order terms.
This implements the Young form, despite the historical function name. When delta >= 2*MTBF it warns but still returns the first-order result; the caller must not treat that out-of-regime value as an achievable schedule.



Young (1974), “A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval.” https://doi.org/10.1145/361147.361115 (bibliography key: young1974). Daly (2006), “A higher order estimate of the optimum checkpoint interval for restart dumps.” https://doi.org/10.1016/j.future.2004.11.016 (bibliography key: daly2006).



>>> baseline = calc_young_daly_interval(10, 10000)
>>> longer = calc_young_daly_interval(40, 10000)
>>> math.isclose(longer.m_as("s"), 2 * baseline.m_as("s"))
True

required

required









Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless joint availability.






Equation: A_all = availability**n_components.

Excludes: Redundancy, common-cause failures, and partial-service operation.

Dimensionless probability that at least one replica is available.

physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_stride(pause, crash_rate, lost_turn_cost)
Find a continuous checkpoint stride balancing pause and rework.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity or float
Nonnegative checkpoint pause; bare numbers are seconds.
required


crash_rate
float
Positive expected crashes per turn.
required


lost_turn_cost
Quantity or float
Positive recovery cost per lost turn; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Optimal continuous stride in turns; not rounded to an integer policy.






Equation: k_star = sqrt(2*pause/(crash_rate*lost_turn_cost)).
Assumptions: A checkpoint every k turns costs pause/k per turn; crashes lose k/2 turns on average.
Excludes: Integer scheduling, restart costs independent of lost turns, and correlated crashes.

Estimate the wall-time fraction lost to saves and rework.

Type
Description
Default

Quantity or float
Nonnegative duration of one blocking checkpoint; bare numbers are seconds.
required

Quantity or float
Positive spacing between checkpoints; bare numbers are seconds.
required

Quantity or float
Positive mean time between failures; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description

Dimensionless first-order waste; values above one signal an unsuitable regime, not a capped fraction.

>>> optimum = calc_checkpoint_waste(10, tau, 10000)
>>> optimum < calc_checkpoint_waste(10, tau * 2, 10000)
True

Estimate the first-order checkpoint interval that minimizes lost work.











Name
Type
Description
Default




checkpoint_cost_s
Quantity or float
Positive write time delta; bare numbers are seconds.
required


mtbf_s
Quantity or float
Positive system mean time between failures; bare numbers are seconds.
required














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Interval in seconds; not rounded to a scheduling quantum.






Equation: tau = sqrt(2 * delta * MTBF), from minimizing delta/tau + tau/(2*MTBF).
Assumptions: Failures arrive independently and rework averages half an interval; delta is small relative to MTBF.
Excludes: Restart time, correlated failures, asynchronous checkpointing, and higher-order terms.
This implements the Young form, despite the historical function name. When delta >= 2*MTBF it warns but still returns the first-order result; the caller must not treat that out-of-regime value as an achievable schedule.



Young (1974), “A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval.” https://doi.org/10.1145/361147.361115 (bibliography key: young1974). Daly (2006), “A higher order estimate of the optimum checkpoint interval for restart dumps.” https://doi.org/10.1016/j.future.2004.11.016 (bibliography key: daly2006).



>>> baseline = calc_young_daly_interval(10, 10000)
>>> longer = calc_young_daly_interval(40, 10000)
>>> math.isclose(longer.m_as("s"), 2 * baseline.m_as("s"))
True

title: physics.context
text:
physics.context
Context engineering: the equations behind what one agent request carries.
Pure arithmetic on serialized token counts (added 2026-10-20). A request is budgeted by role against the window, laid out in zones ordered by change rate so a serving engine can reuse its prefix, compacted between two watermarks, and edited when a write supersedes an observation. One attention head’s softmax gives the first-order cost of every admitted token. The solvers in engine/solvers/context.py compose these.





Name
Description




calc_compaction_cycle
Return turns between two context-compaction watermarks.


calc_equivalent_key_count
Return an equal-normalizer count at a reference logit.


calc_observation_budget
Return the token budget remaining for observations.


calc_softmax_target_weight
Return a target key’s softmax weight against grouped competitors.


calc_turns_that_fit
Return the number of complete observation turns that fit.


calc_zoned_prefill_tokens
Count uncached input tokens in a root-trunk-leaf trajectory.





physics.context.calc_compaction_cycle(trigger, target, tokens_per_turn)
Return turns between two context-compaction watermarks.











Name
Type
Description
Default




trigger
int
Token count at which compaction fires; greater than target.
required


target
int
Token count immediately after compaction; nonnegative.
required


tokens_per_turn
int
Fixed tokens appended per turn; positive.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Turns until the first request reaches or exceeds the trigger.






Equation: n_cycle = ceil((trigger - target) / tokens_per_turn).
Assumptions: Compaction resets exactly to target and observations append at a fixed rate.
Excludes: Compaction latency, information loss, and variable-size observations.



Derivation: Solve target + n*tokens_per_turn >= trigger for the smallest integer n.



>>> calc_compaction_cycle(100, 40, 20) == 3
True




physics.context.calc_equivalent_key_count(count, logit, reference_logit)
Return an equal-normalizer count at a reference logit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




count
int
Number of original keys; nonnegative.
required


logit
float
Dimensionless score shared by the original keys.
required


reference_logit
float
Dimensionless score assigned to equivalent keys.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Equivalent key count; fractional counts represent normalizer mass.






Equation: n_equivalent = count * exp(logit - reference_logit).
Assumptions: Logits are fixed and their exponential difference is representable.
Excludes: Integer rounding and changes in attention scores induced by the input.



Derivation: Solve n_equivalent exp(reference_logit) = count exp(logit) for the equivalent count.



>>> calc_equivalent_key_count(4, 2.0, 2.0) == 4
True




physics.context.calc_observation_budget(window, output_reserve, fixed_tokens)
Return the token budget remaining for observations.











Name
Type
Description
Default




window
int
Total context-window capacity in tokens; nonnegative.
required


output_reserve
int
Tokens reserved for the generated reply; nonnegative.
required


fixed_tokens
int
Serialized system, tool, and persistent-state tokens; nonnegative.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Available observation tokens; a negative result denotes overcommitment.






Equation: S_obs = window - output_reserve - fixed_tokens.
Assumptions: All three counts refer to the same tokenizer and request.
Excludes: Tokenizer estimation, KV capacity, and truncation; negative budgets are not clamped.



Derivation: Subtract disjoint reservations from a finite token capacity.



>>> calc_observation_budget(100, 20, 30) == 100 - 20 - 30
True




physics.context.calc_softmax_target_weight(target_logit, competitors)
Return a target key’s softmax weight against grouped competitors.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_logit
float
Dimensionless target score; its exponential must be representable.
required


competitors
iterable of tuple
Pairs of nonnegative key counts and dimensionless logits.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Normalized target weight, between zero and one for valid inputs.






Equation: a = exp(z_t) / (exp(z_t) + sum_j n_j exp(z_j)).
Assumptions: Competitor keys in each group share a fixed logit; there is one target key.
Excludes: Learned changes to logits, multihead aggregation, and overflow-stable softmax.
Adding keys at fixed logits increases the normalizer and reduces target weight.



Derivation: Expand the softmax denominator by repeated equal-logit terms; each group contributes n_j exp(z_j).



>>> calc_softmax_target_weight(0.0, [(1, 0.0)]) == 0.5
True




physics.context.calc_turns_that_fit(observation_budget, tokens_per_turn)
Return the number of complete observation turns that fit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




observation_budget
int
Available observation capacity in tokens; nonnegative.
required


tokens_per_turn
int
Fixed serialized tokens appended per turn; positive.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Number of whole turns admitted by the token budget.






Equation: turns = floor(observation_budget / tokens_per_turn).
Assumptions: Every turn contributes the same token count and existing state stays fixed.
Excludes: Partial turns, variable-length observations, and context compaction.



Derivation: Integer division counts complete equal-sized groups within a capacity.



>>> calc_turns_that_fit(100, 30) == 100 // 30
True




physics.context.calc_zoned_prefill_tokens(
    turns,
    root,
    trunk,
    leaf,
    trunk_rewrites,
)
Count uncached input tokens in a root-trunk-leaf trajectory.











Name
Type
Description
Default




turns
int
Number of calls in the trajectory; at least one.
required


root
int
Invariant leading-prefix size in tokens; nonnegative.
required


trunk
int
Less frequently changed middle-prefix size in tokens; nonnegative.
required


leaf
int
Per-call changing suffix size in tokens; nonnegative.
required


trunk_rewrites
int
Calls after the first that rewrite the trunk; from zero to turns - 1.
required














Name
Type
Description





int
Total tokens prefilling uncached input across all calls.






Equation: total = root + trunk + leaf + R*(trunk + leaf) + (H - 1 - R)*leaf.
Assumptions: The first call is cold; matching root and trunk prefixes remain cached for subsequent calls.
Excludes: Eviction, cache lookup overhead, output tokens, and partial trunk-prefix reuse.



Derivation: Partition calls into one cold call, R trunk rewrites, and H - 1 - R leaf-only updates.



>>> calc_zoned_prefill_tokens(3, 10, 20, 5, 1) == (10 + 20 + 5) + (20 + 5) + 5
True

text:
physics.robotics.assurance
Statistical release gates, Clopper-Pearson bounds, and fleet hazard rates.





Name
Description




calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound
Invert a binomial tail for a one-sided success lower limit.


calc_clopper_pearson_zero_failure_bound
Compute a one-sided success-probability bound after no failures.


calc_empirical_testing_exposure
Compute zero-event exposure for a one-sided Poisson rate bound.


calc_rule_of_three_bound
Approximate a failure upper limit after failure-free trials.


calc_rule_of_three_trials
Invert the rounded rule of three for a success target.


calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate
Combine residual brain hazards with a shield failure rate.


calc_zero_failure_mission_count
Estimate failure-free missions needed for a hazard-rate target.

Compute a Poisson upper event-rate estimate per failure-free trial.


calc_zero_failure_sample_size
Size an all-success sample for a binomial lower confidence limit.





physics.robotics.assurance.calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound(
    successes,
    trials,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Invert a binomial tail for a one-sided success lower limit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




successes
int
Observed successes from zero through trials inclusive.
required


trials
int
Positive total Bernoulli-trial count.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence in (0, 1), default 0.95; caller must supply a valid probability.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





float
Lower success-probability limit; zero when no successes were observed.






Equation: Find p with sum(comb(n,j)*p**j*(1-p)**(n-j), j=k..n) = 1-confidence.
Assumptions: Independent trials with one common probability; the numerical solve uses fixed bisection iterations.
Excludes: Dependence, changing success rates, numerical guarantees for arbitrarily large counts, and safety certification.
Solves P(X >= k | n, p) = 1 - C for p by bisection, X ~ Binomial(n, p). At k = n it reduces to (1 - C)^(1/n), the zero-failure bound.
Source: Clopper and Pearson, “The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial,” Biometrika 26(4), 1934.



Derivation: Invert the binomial upper tail as in Clopper and Pearson, Biometrika 26(4), 1934; this is a one-sided interval endpoint.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> assert calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound(0, 10) == 0.0
>>> assert 0 < calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound(8, 10) < 0.8




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_clopper_pearson_zero_failure_bound(
    n_trials,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Compute a one-sided success-probability bound after no failures.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_trials
int
Positive number of independent successful Bernoulli trials.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence in (0, 1), default 0.95; caller must supply a valid probability.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





float
Dimensionless lower confidence limit on success probability.






Equation: success_lower = (1 - confidence)**(1 / n_trials).
Assumptions: Independent trials with a common success probability and no observed failures.
Excludes: Distribution shift, trial dependence, and a deterministic reliability guarantee.
Equation: p_L = (1 - C)^(1 / n)



Derivation: For all-success binomial trials P(X=n) = p**n; invert this tail at 1-confidence, the Clopper-Pearson endpoint.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_clopper_pearson_zero_failure_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> low = calc_clopper_pearson_zero_failure_bound(10)
>>> high = calc_clopper_pearson_zero_failure_bound(20)
>>> assert 0 < low < high < 1




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_empirical_testing_exposure(
    target_hazard_rate,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Compute zero-event exposure for a one-sided Poisson rate bound.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_hazard_rate
Quantity or float
Positive target event rate; plain floats mean events per hour.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence in (0, 1), default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Required modeled failure-free operating exposure in hours.






Equation: exposure = -log(1 - confidence) / target_hazard_rate.
Assumptions: A homogeneous Poisson process and complete event observation over accumulated exposure.
Excludes: Nonstationary hazards, dependent exposure, unobserved failures, and safety certification.
Under a Poisson failure arrival process with constant rate lambda, the probability of observing zero failures over total exposure duration T is P(0) = exp(-lambda * T). To claim lambda <= lambda_target at statistical confidence C = 1 - alpha: exp(-lambda_target * T) <= 1 - C ==> T >= -ln(1 - C) / lambda_target
For 95% confidence (C = 0.95): -ln(0.05) ≈ 2.99573 ==> T ≈ 3.0 / lambda_target
Source: Littlewood and Wright, “Some Conservative Stopping Rules for Testing Software”, IEEE TSE, 1997; Kalbfleisch and Prentice, The Statistical Analysis of Failure Time Data, Wiley, 2002.



Derivation: Invert the zero-count likelihood exp(-rate*exposure) at the one-sided tail probability. Existing Littlewood-Wright and Kalbfleisch-Prentice citations give reliability-testing context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_empirical_testing_exposure
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> a = calc_empirical_testing_exposure(1 / ureg.hour)
>>> b = calc_empirical_testing_exposure(2 / ureg.hour)
>>> assert a == 2 * b




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_rule_of_three_bound(n_trials)
Approximate a failure upper limit after failure-free trials.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_trials
int
Positive count of independent failure-free trials.
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Rounded Poisson upper limit 3/n, approximately at 95 percent one-sided confidence; not clipped to one.






Equation: upper = 3 / n_trials.
Assumptions: Rare independent failures with equal trial exposure; the numerator rounds -log(0.05).
Excludes: Exact binomial inference, small-sample probability clipping, and changing hazards.
The rounded form of calc_zero_failure_rate_upper_bound; it overstates the exact limit slightly. Source: Hanley and Lippman-Hand, JAMA 249(13), 1983.



Derivation: Round the zero-event Poisson numerator -log(0.05) to three; Hanley and Lippman-Hand, JAMA 249(13), 1983.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_rule_of_three_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> assert calc_rule_of_three_bound(30) == 3 / 30




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_rule_of_three_trials(target_lower_bound)
Invert the rounded rule of three for a success target.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_lower_bound
float
Desired lower success-probability limit in (0, 1).
required














Name
Type
Description





float
Unrounded trial-count estimate; callers needing an integer must round upward.






Equation: trials = 3 / (1-target_lower_bound).
Assumptions: The rare-failure Poisson approximation and a rounded 95-percent numerator.
Excludes: Exact binomial sizing, observed failures, and certification.



Derivation: Set the rule-of-three failure upper limit to 1-target_lower_bound and solve for the number of trials.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_rule_of_three_trials
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> lo = calc_rule_of_three_trials(0.5)
>>> hi = calc_rule_of_three_trials(0.75)
>>> assert hi == 2 * lo




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate(
    brain_hazard_rate,
    shield_coverage,
    shield_hw_failure_rate=None,
)
Combine residual brain hazards with a shield failure rate.











Name
Type
Description
Default




brain_hazard_rate
Quantity
Positive unshielded event rate in inverse time.
required


shield_coverage
float
Fraction of brain hazards intercepted, in [0, 1].
required


shield_hw_failure_rate
Quantity
Nonnegative additive hardware hazard rate; None means zero.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled total hazardous-event rate per hour.






Equation: system_rate = brain_rate*(1-shield_coverage) + hardware_rate.
Assumptions: Coverage is a stable fraction of hazardous events and the hardware contribution is additive.
Excludes: Common-cause failures, dependence, hazard severity, and proof of shield coverage.
Equation: p_sys = p_brain * (1 - c_shield) + p_hw



Derivation: Partition brain events into intercepted and residual events, then add the stipulated hardware-event stream.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> rate = calc_shielded_system_hazard_rate(1 / ureg.hour, 1.0)
>>> assert rate.magnitude == 0




physics.robotics.assurance.calc_zero_failure_mission_count(
    target_hazard_rate,
    mission_time,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Estimate failure-free missions needed for a hazard-rate target.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_hazard_rate
Quantity
Positive assumed constant hazard rate in inverse time.
required


mission_time
Quantity
Positive duration per mission; rate times duration must lie in (0, 1) and should be small.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence in (0, 1), default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





float
Unrounded failure-free mission count; round upward for a whole-mission plan.






Equation: missions = log(1-confidence) / log(1-target_hazard_rate*mission_time).

n = ln(1 - C) / ln(1 - lambda t)
Unrounded; at small lambda t it approaches the exposure wall divided by t.

>>> assert n > 0

    successes,
    trials,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Invert a binomial tail for a one-sided success lower limit.

Equation: Find p with sum(comb(n,j)*p**j*(1-p)**(n-j), j=k..n) = 1-confidence.
Assumptions: Independent trials with one common probability; the numerical solve uses fixed bisection iterations.
Excludes: Dependence, changing success rates, numerical guarantees for arbitrarily large counts, and safety certification.
Solves P(X >= k | n, p) = 1 - C for p by bisection, X ~ Binomial(n, p). At k = n it reduces to (1 - C)^(1/n), the zero-failure bound.
Source: Clopper and Pearson, “The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial,” Biometrika 26(4), 1934.



Derivation: Invert the binomial upper tail as in Clopper and Pearson, Biometrika 26(4), 1934; this is a one-sided interval endpoint.

>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> assert calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound(0, 10) == 0.0
>>> assert 0 < calc_clopper_pearson_lower_bound(8, 10) < 0.8

physics.robotics.assurance.calc_empirical_testing_exposure(
    target_hazard_rate,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Compute zero-event exposure for a one-sided Poisson rate bound.











Name
Type
Description
Default




target_hazard_rate
Quantity or float
Positive target event rate; plain floats mean events per hour.
required


confidence
float
One-sided confidence in (0, 1), default 0.95.
0.95














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Required modeled failure-free operating exposure in hours.






Equation: exposure = -log(1 - confidence) / target_hazard_rate.
Assumptions: A homogeneous Poisson process and complete event observation over accumulated exposure.
Excludes: Nonstationary hazards, dependent exposure, unobserved failures, and safety certification.
Under a Poisson failure arrival process with constant rate lambda, the probability of observing zero failures over total exposure duration T is P(0) = exp(-lambda * T). To claim lambda <= lambda_target at statistical confidence C = 1 - alpha: exp(-lambda_target * T) <= 1 - C ==> T >= -ln(1 - C) / lambda_target
For 95% confidence (C = 0.95): -ln(0.05) ≈ 2.99573 ==> T ≈ 3.0 / lambda_target
Source: Littlewood and Wright, “Some Conservative Stopping Rules for Testing Software”, IEEE TSE, 1997; Kalbfleisch and Prentice, The Statistical Analysis of Failure Time Data, Wiley, 2002.



Derivation: Invert the zero-count likelihood exp(-rate*exposure) at the one-sided tail probability. Existing Littlewood-Wright and Kalbfleisch-Prentice citations give reliability-testing context.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.assurance import calc_empirical_testing_exposure
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> a = calc_empirical_testing_exposure(1 / ureg.hour)
>>> b = calc_empirical_testing_exposure(2 / ureg.hour)
>>> assert a == 2 * b

physics.robotics.actuation.calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(
    effective_length,
    gravity=None,
    theta_0=None,
    theta_fall=None,
)
Calculate characteristic instability timescale or fall duration for an inverted pendulum.











Name
Type
Description
Default




effective_length
Quantity
Center-of-mass height or pendulum leg length L (e.g. meter).
required


gravity
Quantity
Gravitational acceleration g (defaults to 9.80665 m/s^2).
None


theta_0
Quantity or float
Initial angular perturbation from vertical (e.g. radians or degrees).
None


theta_fall
Quantity or float
User-selected fall angle greater than theta_0; it is not a certified recovery threshold.
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Characteristic timescale or fall duration in seconds.






Equation:
Models bipedal/humanoid balance dynamics under gravity. The linearized dynamics d^2 theta / dt^2 = (g / L) * theta yield the characteristic natural timescale: tau_0 = sqrt(L / g)
If initial perturbation theta_0 and fall threshold theta_fall are given: t_fall = tau_0 * ln(2 * theta_fall / theta_0)
Assumptions: The pendulum has positive length and gravity. The optional fall estimate assumes a small initial angle, zero angular velocity, and a much larger final angle.
Excludes: Nonlinear large-angle motion, active balancing, and a proof that the chosen angle implies irrecoverability.



The linear inverted pendulum has natural frequency omega_0 = sqrt(g / h), so tau_0 = sqrt(L / g) (Caron, “Biped Stabilization by Linear Feedback of the Variable-Height Inverted Pendulum Model”, arXiv:1909.07732, Sec. II). The t_fall expression is derived here, not taken from a published model. With zero initial angular velocity the linearized solution is theta(t) = theta_0 * cosh(t / tau_0), so t = tau_0 * acosh(theta_fall / theta_0), and ln(2x) approximates acosh(x) for x >> 1 (it overestimates by about 5% at x = 2). The small-angle linearization also loses accuracy as theta_fall grows.
Derivation: The linearized equation has timescale sqrt(L/g); replacing acosh(theta_f/theta_0) by log(2 theta_f/theta_0) gives the optional approximation.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(ureg('1 m')).check('[time]')
True

)

Default

When an unblended trajectory transition injects an acceleration discontinuity delta_accel across a discrete boundary, the transmission’s reflected rotor inertia amplifies the required inertial reaction torque at the output joint.

Derivation: Multiply the gear-reflected inertia N squared J by the acceleration jump.

>>> calc_voltage_droop(ureg('2 A'), ureg('1 ohm')) == ureg('2 V')
True

physics.robotics.actuation.calc_alpha_power_gate_delay_stretch(
    nominal_voltage,
    drooped_voltage,
    threshold_voltage=None,
    alpha=1.3,
)
Estimate CMOS gate delay stretch using the alpha-power approximation.











Name
Type
Description
Default




nominal_voltage
Quantity
Nominal rail voltage in V, above threshold in the intended regime.
required


drooped_voltage
Quantity
Drooped rail voltage in V; must exceed threshold.
required


threshold_voltage
Quantity
Threshold in V; None selects the assumed 0.42 V default.
None


alpha
float
Dimensionless alpha-power exponent; assumed default is 1.3.
1.3














Name
Type
Description





dict
Dimensionless stretch_ratio and delay_expansion_percent relative to nominal delay.






Equation:
Sakurai-Newton Alpha-Power Law: stretch_ratio = (V_droop / V_nom) * ((V_nom - V_th) / (V_droop - V_th))^alpha
Assumptions: Both rail voltages exceed the threshold in the intended regime; threshold defaults to an assumed 0.42 V and exponent alpha to an assumed 1.3.
Excludes: Process-specific calibration, frequency control, temperature dependence, and behavior at or below threshold.



Derivation: Under the alpha-power approximation delay is proportional to V/(V-V_th)**alpha; divide drooped delay by nominal delay.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_alpha_power_gate_delay_stretch
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_alpha_power_gate_delay_stretch(ureg('1 V'), ureg('1 V'))['stretch_ratio'] == 1.0
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_coasting_contact_peak_force(
    contact_velocity,
    effective_mass,
    contact_stiffness,
    preload_force,
)
Calculate peak spring force after drive removal at a contact tripwire.











Name
Type
Description
Default




contact_velocity
Quantity
Positive relative approach speed in m/s.
required


effective_mass
Quantity
Positive robot-side effective mass in kg.
required


contact_stiffness
Quantity
Positive linear contact stiffness in N/m.
required


preload_force
Quantity
Initial spring-force magnitude in N, nonnegative in the intended model.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Peak elastic contact force in N.






Equation:
Energy balance from the tripwire, where the spring already carries preload_force: F0^2 / (2k) + m v^2 / 2 = F_peak^2 / (2k) => F_peak = sqrt(F0^2 + k m v^2)
With preload_force zero this is the unbraked transient force v sqrt(k m) (calc_transient_impact_force). Added 2026-10-20.
Assumptions: After drive removal, a positive effective mass and approach speed compress a positive linear spring with a nonnegative preload magnitude.
Excludes: Damping, residual drive torque, nonlinear contact, and safety certification.



Derivation: Conserve initial spring energy plus kinetic energy to obtain F_peak squared = F0 squared + k m v squared.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_coasting_contact_peak_force
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_coasting_contact_peak_force(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 kg'), ureg('1 N/m'), ureg('0 N')) == ureg('1 N')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_contact_force(stiffness, displacement)
Calculate linear Hookean elastic contact force upon unconstrained impact.











Name
Type
Description
Default




stiffness
Quantity
Positive linear spring stiffness in N/m.
required


displacement
Quantity
Nonnegative compression in m.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Elastic force in N.






Equation: F = k * delta_x
Assumptions: The spring is linear with positive stiffness and nonnegative compression.
Excludes: Damping, nonlinear material response, and dynamic impact trajectory.



Derivation: Hooke’s law gives force as stiffness times displacement.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_contact_force
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_contact_force(ureg('100 N/m'), ureg('0.01 m')) == ureg('1 N')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_contact_yield_deadline(
    yield_force,
    stiffness,
    approach_velocity,
)
Calculate the constant-speed contact deadline at a force threshold.











Name
Type
Description
Default




yield_force
Quantity
Maximum permissible mechanical shock / yield force (e.g. N).
required


stiffness
Quantity
Contact environment stiffness (e.g. N/m).
required


approach_velocity
Quantity
Tool-center-point approach velocity (e.g. m/s).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Deadline duration in milliseconds.






Equation:
For an arm approaching a rigid fixture of stiffness k at constant velocity v, contact force rises as F(t) = k * v * t. To prevent structural damage (F <= F_yield): t_deadline = F_yield / (k * v)
Assumptions: Positive approach speed stays constant while a positive linear stiffness accumulates force from zero.
Excludes: Braking after detection, damping, initial preload, and safety certification.



Derivation: Substitute compression v t into Hooke’s law and solve k v t = F_yield.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_contact_yield_deadline
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_contact_yield_deadline(ureg('10 N'), ureg('100 N/m'), ureg('1 m/s')).check('[time]')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_inductive_voltage_droop(
    loop_inductance,
    current_slew_rate,
)
Calculate inductive voltage drop during a current transient.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Positive loop inductance in H.
required


current_slew_rate
Quantity
Positive current slew in A/s.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Inductive voltage drop in V.






Equation: Delta_V_ind = L * (dI / dt)
Assumptions: A positive lumped loop inductance experiences a positive current slew.
Excludes: Resistive droop, decoupling capacitance, and distributed PDN resonances.



Derivation: The ideal inductor terminal relation is voltage L times the time derivative of current.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_inductive_voltage_droop
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_inductive_voltage_droop(ureg('1 H'), ureg('1 A/s')) == ureg('1 V')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(
    effective_length,
    gravity=None,
    theta_0=None,
    theta_fall=None,
)
Calculate characteristic instability timescale or fall duration for an inverted pendulum.











Name
Type
Description
Default




effective_length
Quantity
Center-of-mass height or pendulum leg length L (e.g. meter).
required


gravity
Quantity
Gravitational acceleration g (defaults to 9.80665 m/s^2).
None


theta_0
Quantity or float
Initial angular perturbation from vertical (e.g. radians or degrees).
None


theta_fall
Quantity or float
User-selected fall angle greater than theta_0; it is not a certified recovery threshold.
None














Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Characteristic timescale or fall duration in seconds.






Equation:
Models bipedal/humanoid balance dynamics under gravity. The linearized dynamics d^2 theta / dt^2 = (g / L) * theta yield the characteristic natural timescale: tau_0 = sqrt(L / g)
If initial perturbation theta_0 and fall threshold theta_fall are given: t_fall = tau_0 * ln(2 * theta_fall / theta_0)
Assumptions: The pendulum has positive length and gravity. The optional fall estimate assumes a small initial angle, zero angular velocity, and a much larger final angle.
Excludes: Nonlinear large-angle motion, active balancing, and a proof that the chosen angle implies irrecoverability.



The linear inverted pendulum has natural frequency omega_0 = sqrt(g / h), so tau_0 = sqrt(L / g) (Caron, “Biped Stabilization by Linear Feedback of the Variable-Height Inverted Pendulum Model”, arXiv:1909.07732, Sec. II). The t_fall expression is derived here, not taken from a published model. With zero initial angular velocity the linearized solution is theta(t) = theta_0 * cosh(t / tau_0), so t = tau_0 * acosh(theta_fall / theta_0), and ln(2x) approximates acosh(x) for x >> 1 (it overestimates by about 5% at x = 2). The small-angle linearization also loses accuracy as theta_fall grows.
Derivation: The linearized equation has timescale sqrt(L/g); replacing acosh(theta_f/theta_0) by log(2 theta_f/theta_0) gives the optional approximation.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(ureg('1 m')).check('[time]')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_kinetic_energy(mass, velocity)
Calculate kinetic energy of a translating body.











Name
Type
Description
Default




mass
Quantity
Total mass of the body (e.g. kg).
required


velocity
Quantity
Translational velocity (e.g. m/s).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Kinetic energy in Joules.






Equation: E_k = 0.5 * m * v^2
Assumptions: A translating point mass has nonrelativistic speed; mass is positive and speed is nonnegative.
Excludes: Rotation, deformation, and dissipated energy.



OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 7.2, Eq. 7.6.
Derivation: Integrating Newtonian work m v dv from rest gives m v squared divided by two.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_kinetic_energy
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_kinetic_energy(ureg('2 kg'), ureg('3 m/s')).check('[energy]')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_passive_compliance_stiffness_bound(
    force_limit,
    tripwire_force,
    detection_speed,
    response_latency,
    arm_deceleration,
)
Largest series stiffness that keeps a driven contact under a force limit after the tripwire.











Name
Type
Description
Default




force_limit
Quantity
Force ceiling in N.
required


tripwire_force
Quantity
Force at tripwire detection in N.
required


detection_speed
Quantity
Positive contact approach speed in m/s.
required


response_latency
Quantity
Nonnegative delay before braking in s.
required


arm_deceleration
Quantity
Positive constant braking deceleration in m/s^2.
required














Name
Type
Description





tuple of Quantity
Stiffness bound in N/m and driven stroke in mm; nonpositive stiffness indicates no positive force headroom.






Equation:
After the tripwire the arm keeps driving for the response latency, then stops at arm_deceleration; the stroke it drives is s = v t_r + v^2 / (2 a), and the force rises by k s on top of the tripwire force: F_trip + k s <= F_limit <=> k <= (F_limit - F_trip) / (v t_r + v^2 / (2 a))
Returns (stiffness bound, driven stroke). Added 2026-10-20.
Assumptions: The arm keeps a positive speed during a nonnegative delay, then brakes at positive constant deceleration; a usable bound requires force_limit greater than tripwire_force.
Excludes: Jerk ramps, damping, controller tracking error, and certification. The implementation returns a nonpositive stiffness when no force headroom remains.



Derivation: Add latency travel and constant-deceleration braking travel, then divide force headroom by that stroke.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_passive_compliance_stiffness_bound
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_passive_compliance_stiffness_bound(ureg('10 N'), ureg('1 N'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 s'), ureg('1 m/s**2'))[0].check('[force]/[length]')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_quasistatic_spill_acceleration(
    inner_radius,
    freeboard,
    gravity=None,
)
Calculate the steady-tilt acceleration ceiling for an open vessel.











Name
Type
Description
Default




inner_radius
Quantity
Positive vessel inner radius in m.
required


freeboard
Quantity
Positive liquid-to-rim height in m.
required


gravity
Quantity
Positive gravitational acceleration in m/s^2; None uses standard gravity.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Steady-tilt acceleration ceiling in m/s^2.






Equation: tan(theta) = a / g ; wall rise = R a / g ; a_max = g h_f / R
Under steady acceleration the free surface settles perpendicular to the effective gravity. Sloshing overshoots this steady tilt, so the bound is necessary, not sufficient.
Assumptions: A positive-radius open vessel has positive freeboard and reaches a steady free- surface tilt under positive gravity.
Excludes: Transient slosh, viscosity, vessel shape details, and a sufficient no-spill guarantee.



Hydrostatics of a uniformly accelerated liquid gives a free surface normal to effective gravity. Container slosh is discussed by Mayer and Krechetnikov 2012, “Walking with coffee: why does it spill?”, Phys. Rev. E 85, 046117.
Derivation: The free surface is perpendicular to effective gravity, so wall rise R a/g reaches freeboard h at a = g h/R.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_quasistatic_spill_acceleration
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_quasistatic_spill_acceleration(ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 m'), ureg('1 m/s**2')) == ureg('1 m/s**2')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_quintic_blend_duration(
    delta_torque,
    max_allowable_jerk,
)
Compute minimum blend duration for quintic polynomial trajectory to bound torque jerk.











Name
Type
Description
Default




delta_torque
Quantity
Signed torque change in N m; the magnitude sets duration.
required


max_allowable_jerk
Quantity
Positive torque-rate ceiling in N m/s, not angular jerk.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Required smoothstep duration in ms.






Equation: tau_blend >= (1.875 * |Delta_tau|) / jerk_max
Assumptions: The torque command follows a fixed-endpoint quintic smoothstep; the positive rate limit is a torque rate, despite the legacy jerk parameter name.
Excludes: Mechanical angular jerk, actuator tracking error, and time optimality among other trajectory families.



Derivation: The peak derivative of 10 s cubed - 15 s fourth + 6 s fifth is 1.875; divide peak scaled torque slope by the allowed torque rate.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_quintic_blend_duration
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_quintic_blend_duration(ureg('0 N*m'), ureg('1 N*m/s')) == ureg('0 ms')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_reduced_mass(mass_a, mass_b)
Calculate the two-body reduced mass of a collision.





Name
Type
Description
Default




mass_a
Quantity
Positive first-body mass in kg.
required


mass_b
Quantity
Positive second-body mass in kg.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Reduced mass in kg.






Equation: mu = (1/m_a + 1/m_b)^-1
When one body cannot recoil (m_b -> infinity, a clamped contact), mu -> m_a.
Assumptions: Both masses are positive and free to recoil in a one-dimensional two-body collision.
Excludes: Rotational inertia coupling, constraints, and contact compliance.



ISO/TS 15066:2016 Annex A, transient-contact model (content carried into ISO 10218-2:2025), as reproduced in Kirschner et al. 2022, eq. 2 (arXiv:2203.02706).
Derivation: In the relative coordinate, inverse effective mass is the sum of the two inverse masses.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_reduced_mass
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_reduced_mass(ureg('2 kg'), ureg('2 kg')) == ureg('1 kg')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_reflected_inertia(gear_ratio, rotor_inertia)
Calculate reflected rotor inertia felt at the actuator output shaft.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gear_ratio
float
Transmission reduction ratio N (>= 1.0).
required


rotor_inertia
Quantity
Unloaded rotor moment of inertia (e.g. kg * m^2).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Reflected inertia in kg * m^2.






Equation: J_reflected = N^2 * J_rotor
Assumptions: The ideal gear reduction has ratio at least one and a rigid rotor.
Excludes: Gear compliance, efficiency losses, and load inertia.



Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics, Cambridge University Press, 2017, Sec. 8.9.2 (“Apparent Inertia”), where G^2 * I_rotor is the rotor’s apparent (often called reflected) inertia for gear ratio G.
Derivation: Equate rotor kinetic energy to output-shaft kinetic energy with rotor speed N times output speed.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_reflected_inertia
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_reflected_inertia(2, ureg('1 kg*m**2')) == 4 * ureg('1 kg*m**2')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_seam_acceleration_torque_jump(
    gear_ratio,
    rotor_inertia,
    delta_accel,
)
Calculate the impulsive torque spike at an actuator seam transition.











Name
Type
Description
Default




gear_ratio
float
Transmission reduction ratio N (>= 1.0).
required


rotor_inertia
Quantity
Unloaded rotor moment of inertia (e.g. kg * m^2).
required


delta_accel
Quantity
Discontinuous acceleration step across the seam (e.g. rad / s^2).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Peak reaction torque spike in Newton-meters.






When an unblended trajectory transition injects an acceleration discontinuity delta_accel across a discrete boundary, the transmission’s reflected rotor inertia amplifies the required inertial reaction torque at the output joint.
Equation: tau_spike = J_reflected * delta_accel = (N^2 * J_rotor) * delta_accel
Assumptions: A positive rotor inertia is reflected through an ideal reduction; the acceleration jump is nonnegative.
Excludes: Link/load inertia, friction, gear compliance, and finite controller response.



The torque relation tau = I * alpha (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 10.7, Eq. 10.25) applied to the rotor’s apparent (reflected) inertia G^2 * I_rotor (Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics, Cambridge University Press, 2017, Sec. 8.9.2). Link inertia, load, friction, and gear compliance are omitted, so this is the reflected-rotor share of the spike; treating the seam as an instantaneous acceleration step is a modeling assumption.
Derivation: Multiply the gear-reflected inertia N squared J by the acceleration jump.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_seam_acceleration_torque_jump
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_seam_acceleration_torque_jump(2, ureg('1 kg*m**2'), ureg('1 rad/s**2')).check('[force]*[length]')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_smoothstep_blend_window(change, rate_limit)
Shortest window of a fixed-endpoint quintic smoothstep whose peak rate stays at a limit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




change
Quantity
Signed command change; its units must match rate_limit times seconds.
required


rate_limit
Quantity
Positive allowed command rate in change-units per second.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Window in seconds.






Equation: T >= 1.875 |Delta u| / rate_max
The smoothstep alpha(s) = 10 s^3 - 15 s^4 + 6 s^5 has peak slope d alpha / ds = 30/16 = 1.875 at s = 1/2, so a change Delta u spread over T peaks at 1.875 Delta u / T. Unit-generic form of calc_quintic_blend_duration: an acceleration change against a jerk bound, or a torque change against a torque-rate ceiling (added 2026-10-20).
Assumptions: The change has units compatible with a positive rate limit times time; a quintic fixed-endpoint smoothstep is used.
Excludes: Tracking error, other profile shapes, and dynamic feasibility beyond the rate ceiling.



Derivation: The quintic smoothstep peak slope is 1.875; scaling by absolute change and dividing by rate gives the required window.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_smoothstep_blend_window
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_smoothstep_blend_window(ureg('0 m/s**2'), ureg('1 m/s**3')) == ureg('0 s')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_transient_contact_speed_limit(
    force_limit,
    effective_mass,
    contact_stiffness,
    human_mass=None,
)
Calculate the highest contact speed whose transient peak force stays at a force limit.











Name
Type
Description
Default




force_limit
Quantity
Force ceiling in N.
required


effective_mass
Quantity
Positive robot-side effective mass in kg.
required


contact_stiffness
Quantity
Positive linear contact stiffness in N/m.
required


human_mass
Quantity
Positive recoiling-body mass in kg; None uses the robot mass alone.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled contact-speed ceiling in m/s.






Equation: v_max = F_max / sqrt(k * m)
The inverse of calc_transient_impact_force: human_mass=None gives the clamped case (m = m_eff); a human_mass gives the free, recoiling case (m = mu, the two-body reduced mass).
Assumptions: Positive force limit, effective mass, and linear stiffness describe the same elastic model as calc_transient_impact_force.
Excludes: Damping, control response, biological variability, and certification of a safe operating speed.



ISO/TS 15066:2016 Annex A (carried into ISO 10218-2:2025), as used for v_rel,max in Kirschner et al. 2022 (arXiv:2203.02706).
Derivation: Solve the elastic energy equation F = v sqrt(k m) for v.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_transient_contact_speed_limit
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_transient_contact_speed_limit(ureg('1 N'), ureg('1 kg'), ureg('1 N/m')) == ureg('1 m/s')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_transient_impact_force(
    contact_velocity,
    effective_mass,
    contact_stiffness,
    human_mass=None,
)
Calculate peak unbraked transient impact force on an elastic body.











Name
Type
Description
Default




contact_velocity
Quantity
Positive relative approach speed in m/s.
required


effective_mass
Quantity
Positive robot-side effective mass in kg.
required


contact_stiffness
Quantity
Positive linear contact stiffness in N/m.
required


human_mass
Quantity
Positive recoiling-body mass in kg; None uses the robot mass alone.
None









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Modeled peak elastic force in N.






Equation: F_peak = v * sqrt(k * m)
With human_mass=None the robot-side effective_mass acts alone (m = m_eff), the clamped (quasi-static) case in which the body part cannot recoil. With human_mass given, the free body part recoils and the two-body reduced mass acts: m = mu = (1/m_eff + 1/m_H)^-1.
Assumptions: A positive approach speed loads a positive linear stiffness without braking; optional human mass gives free recoil, otherwise the contacted body is clamped.
Excludes: Damping, geometry-dependent stiffness, active control, injury prediction, and safety certification.



ISO/TS 15066:2016 Annex A energy model F = v * sqrt(mu * k) (content carried into ISO 10218-2:2025), as reproduced in Kirschner et al. 2022, eqs. 1-2 (arXiv:2203.02706).
Derivation: Equate relative kinetic energy m v squared/2 with spring energy F squared/(2 k).



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_transient_impact_force
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_transient_impact_force(ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 kg'), ureg('1 N/m')) == ureg('1 N')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_tripwire_contact_force_accumulation(
    tripwire_force,
    contact_stiffness,
    penetration_velocity,
    loop_latency,
)
Calculate contact force at brake-command onset after a tripwire breach.











Name
Type
Description
Default




tripwire_force
Quantity
Force at tripwire detection in N.
required


contact_stiffness
Quantity
Positive linear contact stiffness in N/m.
required


penetration_velocity
Quantity
Positive continued penetration speed in m/s.
required


loop_latency
Quantity
Positive response delay in s.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Contact force at brake-command onset in N.






Equation: F_lat = F_trip + k * v * t_lat
Assumptions: Positive speed remains constant during a positive loop delay after a positive tripwire threshold; stiffness is linear and positive.
Excludes: Braking travel after command onset, damping, and contact safety certification.



Derivation: Add the spring-force increment k times additional penetration v t to the tripwire force.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_tripwire_contact_force_accumulation
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_tripwire_contact_force_accumulation(ureg('1 N'), ureg('1 N/m'), ureg('1 m/s'), ureg('1 s')) == ureg('2 N')
True




physics.robotics.actuation.calc_voltage_droop(current, internal_resistance)
Calculate DC bus voltage droop across internal battery and cable resistance.











Name
Type
Description
Default




current
Quantity
Total instantaneous draw current across actuators and compute (e.g. Amperes).
required


internal_resistance
Quantity
Combined battery internal DC resistance and harness resistance (e.g. Ohms).
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Voltage droop in Volts.






Equation: Delta_V = I * R_internal
Assumptions: Current is nonnegative and a positive lumped DC resistance describes the path.
Excludes: Inductance, capacitance, and frequency-dependent impedance.



Ohm’s law, V = I * R (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, Sec. 9.3).
Derivation: Ohm’s law applied to the series resistance gives I R.



>>> from mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation import calc_voltage_droop
>>> from mlsysim.core.units import ureg
>>> calc_voltage_droop(ureg('2 A'), ureg('1 ohm')) == ureg('2 V')
True

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
An optimization costing implementation_cost that cuts a monthly_bill by reduction.


Equation: Monthly saving is bill*reduction; payback is implementation_cost/monthly_saving.
Assumptions: A sustained positive saving and constant monthly bill.

Serving scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/serving.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
A compiled decode step and the executions that repay its build.
The eager step splits into shares (matrix multiplies, element-wise kernels, launch overhead); compilation removes removed[k] of each share. A build is repaid after build / saved_per_token tokens; shared by replicas it is repaid in a fraction of that time, and rebuilt by each it costs replicas x gpus_per_replica x build.

Excludes: Compiler-specific prediction, overlap between removed components, and build- cache invalidation.

Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
tables embedding tables of rows rows, each width values wide, against hardware.


Equation: Row bytes are width*value_width; total storage multiplies by rows and table count.
Assumptions: Fully allocated equal-shaped tables and labeled memory capacity.
Excludes: Index metadata, replicas, allocator reserve, and cached or compressed tables.

Optimization scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/optimization.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Amdahl’s law with a path gain set by two rates: fraction of the baseline time runs accelerated_rate / baseline_rate times faster.
The rates may be operation rates (a compute-bound path) or bandwidths (a bandwidth-bound path); only their ratio enters.


Equation: The calculation members below define gain, speedup, ceiling.
Assumptions: The accelerated fraction is baseline elapsed-time share; the two rates measure compatible work.
Excludes: Changes to the unaccelerated path, contention, and overlap.



Derivation: Amdahl’s law with a path gain set by two rates: fraction of the baseline time runs accelerated_rate / baseline_rate times faster. Each member records the corresponding algebra or named physics function.



Evaluate the named configuration and display a modeled result.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> case = Scenarios.ResNet50InferenceH100OverServerCpu
>>> value = case.speedup
>>> print(f"{value:.3g}")
18.6

Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/proposers.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
One backbone priced at several weight formats against measurements of the same formats.
formats maps a label to its evaluation scenario; measured and scores map the same labels to a measured latency and a task score. group_size, scale_bits, and weight_bits price the per-group scale overhead of the deployed format.


Equation: relative gap = (modeled - measured latency) / measured latency; scale overhead = scale bits / (group size * weight bits).
Assumptions: Every label names the same workload and hardware configuration across modeled and measured mappings; group size and bit widths are positive.
Excludes: A universal quantization speedup, statistical uncertainty in measurements, and automatic quality validation.



Derivation: relative gap = (modeled - measured latency) / measured latency; scale overhead = scale bits / (group size * weight bits). The individual properties state units and intermediate accounting; this class introduces no fitted coefficient.

title: ImitationBoundScenario
text:
Robotics scenarios · Implementation: mlsysim/engine/scenario_definitions/robotics/demonstrations.py.
Construct this scenario with keyword inputs. The fields below show the types and defaults declared by this class.
Worst-case imitation cost over one episode at control_rate with per-step error per_step_error: open loop, behavioral cloning, and aggregation with recoverability u.


Equation: Cloning scales as horizon**2*error; aggregation uses recoverability*horizon*error; capped values cannot exceed horizon.
Assumptions: Per-step loss is bounded by one and the supplied error/recoverability satisfy the cited helper assumptions.
Excludes: Empirical rollout measurement or guarantees for policies outside those assumptions.



Implementation references: mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_behavior_cloning_cost_bound, mlsysim.physics.statistics.calc_dagger_cost_bound. These helper contracts state the source assumptions; the scenario binds their inputs and derives the displayed ratios and budgets.



The named registry scenario supplies the stated inputs; this is a modeled calculation, not a new measurement.
>>> from mlsysim import Scenarios
>>> scenario = Scenarios.ImitationBoundsFiveSecondEpisode
>>> round(scenario.cloning_capped, 6)
250.0






Name
Description




aggregation
Recoverability-scaled linear bound from calc_dagger_cost_bound; not a guarantee for arbitrary learned policies.


aggregation_capped
Dataset-aggregation cost bound capped at the same horizon maximum.


capped_gap
Dimensionless ratio of capped cloning and aggregation bounds; requires nonzero aggregation cost.


cloning
Uncapped quadratic imitation bound from calc_behavior_cloning_cost_bound; not an empirical rollout error count.


cloning_capped
Behavior-cloning cost bound capped at the episode’s maximum unit loss per step.


cloning_over_maximum
Uncapped cloning bound divided by the maximum horizon loss; values above one indicate a vacuous bound.


control_rate



episode



horizon



horizon_steps
Episode decision count; uses explicit horizon when supplied, otherwise rounds episode duration times control rate.


matching_error
Per-step cloning error needed for its quadratic bound to equal the capped aggregation cost: aggregation_capped / horizon_steps**2.


open_loop
Linear count of expected errors without compounding: horizon times per-step error; a comparison baseline.


per_step_error



recoverability



saturation_horizon
Horizon at which the uncapped quadratic cloning bound reaches the maximum cumulative loss: reciprocal of positive per-step error.


vacuous_error
Per-step error threshold at which the quadratic bound reaches horizon loss: 1 / horizon_steps.

Declared default: None.

Declared default: None.

title: engine.solvers.trajectory
text:
engine.solvers.trajectory
Trajectory-planning solvers: joint rates, handoff deadlines, seams, swings, and jerk-limited stops.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.robotics (the two-link Jacobian and damped least squares, the S-curve and polynomial stops, the seam torque step, the spill bound); these models compose them for one stated arm, joint, base, or mission, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




BrakingBlendModel
A bumpless transfer from cruise into braking, beside the step and the resident stop.


ChunkReplacementModel
Replacement latency, capture to admission, against the renewal period and the lease.


DynamicWindowModel
The dynamic window of a base over one renewal, and the classical admissibility test.


HandoffExposureModel
A per-handoff deadline budget read across a mission of K handoffs.


JerkLimitedStopModel
A delayed jerk-limited (S-curve) stop, beside the constant and polynomial stops it replaces.


SeamBridgeModel
A velocity gap at a chunk seam, closed in one servo tick or by a quintic bridge.


ShoulderSwingModel
The loaded shoulder: holding torque, effective inertia, and a rest-to-rest swing.


SpillLimitedStopModel
The stop of a machine carrying an open container, whose liquid caps the deceleration.


StaleAnchorModel
How far a moving reference runs past a pose sampled when a replacement was requested.


TrajectoryDeadlinesModel
The deadlines a trajectory record carries, and the cruise charged before its stop begins.


TwoLinkJointRateModel
Joint rates a tool speed asks of a planar two-link arm, exact and damped.





engine.solvers.trajectory.BrakingBlendModel()
A bumpless transfer from cruise into braking, beside the step and the resident stop.
At a change of authority the enforcer may blend the base’s command from cruise to the braking deceleration a with the fixed-endpoint quintic smoothstep. Its slope peaks at 1.875, so under the resident stop’s jerk bound j the window is T = 1.875 a / j (calc_smoothstep_blend_window), rounded up to whole permission ticks. The same change taken in one tick asks a jerk of a / tick. During the blend the speed falls by a T / 2 and the base travels v0 T - a T^2 / 7 (calc_smoothstep_braking_blend); full braking follows. The blended stop is set against an ideal step (v0^2 / 2a) and the resident S-curve stop; the reserve a blend uses is the largest growth of travel plus resident stop over its ticks (calc_blend_reserve_use). An arm joint’s torque change under a torque-rate ceiling gives its own window the same way (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




solve
Account for travel and reserve consumed while blending into braking.





engine.solvers.trajectory.BrakingBlendModel.solve(
    speed,
    deceleration,
    jerk,
    tick,
    torque_change=None,
    torque_rate_limit=None,
)
Account for travel and reserve consumed while blending into braking.











Name
Type
Description
Default

required


deceleration
Quantity

required


jerk
Quantity
Positive permitted jerk magnitude, in meters per second cubed.
required

Positive permission/control tick used to round budgets and sample reserve use.
required

None

None

Type
Description

Blend window and rounded budget, travel distances and reserve use in length units, and optional arm blend timing. The actual blend uses the unrounded window; tick rounding supplies its budget.






mlsysim.physics.robotics.actuation.calc_smoothstep_blend_window : Scale the smoothstep derivative to a rate ceiling. mlsysim.physics.robotics.stopping.calc_smoothstep_braking_blend : Integrate speed and travel while acceleration is blended.



Equation: T = 1.875*deceleration/jerk, exit speed = speed-deceleration*T/2, and blend travel = speed*T-deceleration*T**2/7. Constant braking follows the blend.
Assumptions: A fixed-endpoint quintic smoothstep reaches the requested deceleration without reversal. Reserve use is sampled at permission ticks.
Excludes: Actuator lag, changing traction, obstacles, continuous-time reserve maximization, and a safety guarantee.



Derivation: The quintic smoothstep has maximum normalized slope 1.875. Scaling its slope by acceleration change and dividing by the jerk ceiling gives the shortest modeled window; integrating gives speed and travel.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import BrakingBlendModel
>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = BrakingBlendModel().solve(
...     speed=Q_('2 m/s'),
...     deceleration=Q_('1 m/s^2'),
...     jerk=Q_('10 m/s^3'),
...     tick=Q_('1 ms'),
... )
>>> result.blended_stop > result.step_stop
True

Replacement latency, capture to admission, against the renewal period and the lease.
L = observation age at dispatch + the dispatch-to-admission allocation; the inference pass and whole-plan validation sit inside the allocation. Admitting one plan every renewal period with L longer than that period keeps ceil(L / T_renew) requests in flight.

Assumptions: Requests arrive periodically and experience the stated fixed capture-to-admission latency.

engine.solvers.trajectory.DynamicWindowModel()
The dynamic window of a base over one renewal, and the classical admissibility test.
Speeds reachable in the next window differ from the current one by at most a_max x window. The dynamic window approach admits an arc whose speed satisfies v <= sqrt(2 d a_b), a constant-deceleration stop within the distance d to the nearest obstacle (Fox, Burgard, and Thrun 1997, eq. 14), with no pre-brake delay, jerk ramps, or margins.





Name
Description




solve
Compare reachable speed change with a constant-deceleration stop ceiling.

    max_acceleration,
    window,
    clear_distance,
    deceleration,
    drive_limit,
)
Compare reachable speed change with a constant-deceleration stop ceiling.











Name
Type
Description
Default

Quantity
Nonnegative acceleration magnitude, in meters per second squared.
required

Quantity
Nonnegative duration over which reachable speed change is evaluated.
required

required

required

required














Name
Type
Description





DynamicWindowResult
Reachable speed-window half-width and admissible speed in meters per second, plus whether the admissible speed is strictly greater than the drive rating.






Equation: Half-width = max_acceleration*window; admissible_speed = sqrt(2*clear_distance*deceleration).
Assumptions: Constant acceleration over the renewal window and immediate constant-deceleration braking along an already selected arc.
Excludes: Pre-brake latency, jerk limits, margins, moving obstacles, and trajectory search.



Derivation: Integrate constant acceleration to obtain the reachable speed increment. Rearranging stopping distance v**2/(2*a) <= distance gives the admissibility ceiling.



>>> from mlsysim.solvers import DynamicWindowModel
>>> from mlsysim import Q_
>>> result = DynamicWindowModel().solve(
...     max_acceleration=Q_('1 m/s^2'),
...     window=Q_('0.1 s'),
...     clear_distance=Q_('1 m'),
...     deceleration=Q_('2 m/s^2'),
...     drive_limit=Q_('1 m/s'),
... )
>>> result.admits_drive_limit
True






engine.solvers.trajectory.HandoffExposureModel()
A per-handoff deadline budget read across a mission of K handoffs.
With independent misses at probability p, all K handoffs are on time with probability (1 - p)^K and p K are late on average. Holding a mission budget eps_M by the union bound leaves each handoff eps_M / K, the quantile 1 - eps_M / K, deeper than p by the ratio p K / eps_M.





Name
Description




solve
Translate repeated deadline misses into a mission exposure budget.
